title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
嘉靖十年例應鄉試取士禮
部以湖廣考試官請
上命給事中臣王禎行人臣朱隆
禧行矣未幾臣隆禧弗果至
禮部復以請
上命行人臣謙往時盖七月十二
===
日也臣受
命祗懼嚴程以進越十有三日入
湖境則聞臣禎又弗果至矣
益為惕然初湖中但知二臣
者之去而不知臣之来也自
鎮守太監臣潘真巡撫右副
都御史臣凌相以下咸慮焉
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序

嘉靖十年，例應鄉試取士，禮部以湖廣考試官請。上命給事中臣王禎、行人臣朱隆禧行矣。未幾，臣隆禧弗果至，禮部復以請。上命行人臣謙往，時盖七月十二日也。臣受命祗懼，嚴程以進。越十有三日，入湖境，則聞臣禎又弗果至矣，益為惕然。初，湖中但知二臣者之去，而不知臣之来也。自鎮守太監臣潘真、巡撫右副都御史臣凌相以下，咸慮焉。
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the tenth year of Jiajing [1531], the Provincial Examination for selecting men for service was due to be held according to established practice. The Ministry of Rites requested the appointment of Examiners for Huguang. His Majesty commanded his servants Wang Zhen, Supervising Secretary, and Zhu Longxi, Messenger, to proceed there. Before long, however, his servant Longxi proved unable to arrive, and the Ministry of Rites submitted another request. His Majesty commanded me, his servant Qian, a Messenger, to go. It was then the twelfth day of the seventh month. Receiving the command with reverence and trepidation, I pressed forward on a strict travel schedule. Thirteen days later, I entered Huguang, only to hear that his servant Zhen, too, had been unable to arrive. I became still more apprehensive. At first, those in Huguang knew only that the two officials had set out, and did not know that I was coming. From his servant Pan Zhen, the eunuch Grand Director serving as Regional Defender, and his servant Ling Xiang, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-chief, on down, all were concerned.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
顯陵督理大工內官監太監臣傅
平工部左侍郎臣黎奭撫治
鄖陽右副都御史臣潘旦巡
撫南贛右副都御史臣陶諧
清戎御史臣陸琳慮亦如之
若郎中臣劉佐臣張淑主事
臣華察行人臣李遂錦衣衛
===
千戶臣李鵬皆奉
命而蒞兹土者亦與厥慮臣至則
皆喜曰来何速哉事其濟乎
其尤深喜者監臨官巡按監
察御史臣組提調官右布政
使臣鐸左參議臣日休監試
官按察使臣峨副使臣錫也
punctuated: 顯陵督理大工內官監太監臣傅平、工部左侍郎臣黎奭、撫治鄖陽右副都御史臣潘旦、巡撫南贛右副都御史臣陶諧、清戎御史臣陸琳，慮亦如之。若郎中臣劉佐、臣張淑，主事臣華察，行人臣李遂，錦衣衛千戶臣李鵬，皆奉命而蒞兹土者，亦與厥慮。臣至，則皆喜曰：「来何速哉！事其濟乎！」其尤深喜者，監臨官巡按監察御史臣組，提調官右布政使臣鐸、左參議臣日休，監試官按察使臣峨、副使臣錫也。
translation_en:
… The same concerns were shared by your servants Fu Ping, Eunuch Director of the Directorate of Palace Domestic Service, supervising the major construction works at Xianling; Li Shi, Left Vice Minister of Works; Pan Dan, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief charged with pacifying and administering Yunyang; Tao Xie, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of southern Jiangxi; and Lu Lin, Investigating Censor charged with reorganizing the military. Your servants Liu Zuo and Zhang Shu, bureau directors; Hua Cha, a bureau secretary; Li Sui, a messenger; and Li Peng, a battalion commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard—all of whom had come to this region under imperial orders—also shared these concerns.

When I arrived, they all rejoiced, saying, “How quickly you have come! Now perhaps the undertaking will succeed!” Especially delighted were your servants Zu, the Supervising Official and Regional Inspector serving as an Investigating Censor; Duo, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Rixiu, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner, the Proctors; and E, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Xi, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, the examination monitors.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其叅政臣黃焯臣劉棟叅議
臣胡德臣鄺灝副使臣文明
臣朱珮臣陳卿僉事臣周佐
臣孟居仁臣毛紹元臣陳嘉
言都指揮臣王表臣周邦簡
臣陳曉罔不欣然樂相其事
若副使臣李顯右叅議臣張
===
天性則先期入
賀矣維時先綜理試事巡按監
察御史臣劉濂暨左布政使
今陞太僕寺卿臣盛儀所聘
同考試官教授臣克昌臣嘉
秀臣汶學正臣燦臣登教諭
臣文昌臣河臣畿臣士奎等
punctuated:
其叅政臣黃焯、臣劉棟，叅議臣胡德、臣鄺灝，副使臣文明、臣朱珮、臣陳卿，僉事臣周佐、臣孟居仁、臣毛紹元、臣陳嘉言，都指揮臣王表、臣周邦簡、臣陳曉，罔不欣然樂相其事。若副使臣李顯、右叅議臣張天性，則先期入賀矣。
維時，先綜理試事巡按監察御史臣劉濂暨左布政使今陞太僕寺卿臣盛儀所聘同考試官，教授臣克昌、臣嘉秀、臣汶，學正臣燦、臣登，教諭臣文昌、臣河、臣畿、臣士奎等，
translation_en:
The Administration Vice Commissioners Huang Zhuo and Liu Dong; the Administration Assistant Commissioners Hu De and Kuang Hao; the Surveillance Vice Commissioners Wenming, Zhu Pei, and Chen Qing; the Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Zhou Zuo, Meng Juren, Mao Shaoyuan, and Chen Jiayan; and the Regional Military Commissioners Wang Biao, Zhou Bangjian, and Chen Xiao—all were pleased and glad to assist in the undertaking. As for Surveillance Vice Commissioner Li Xian and Right Administration Assistant Commissioner Zhang Tianxing, they had already gone to court ahead of the appointed time to offer congratulations.
At this time, the Associate Examiners engaged by Regional Inspector Liu Lian, who had previously overseen examination affairs, and Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Sheng Yi, now promoted to Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud—Professors Kechang, Jiaxiu, and Wen; School Instructors Can and Deng; and Instructors Wenchang, He, Ji, Shikui, and others…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
畢集乃合提學副使臣崔桐
所取士二千七百有奇三試
之遵
制額得士八十五人并錄其文之
優者以
獻臣不佞敢颺言于衆曰湖南
山川之美甲天下然自開闢
===
===
以来至于
今日而
大聖人始作何也蓋天地至精至
粹之氣乆于積泓于蓄故其
發也昌以大是氣也一鍾之
冀北而堯舜者出以開百有
餘年之帝治再鍾之岐周而
punctuated: 畢集，乃合提學副使臣崔桐所取士二千七百有奇，三試之，遵制額得士八十五人，并錄其文之優者以獻。臣不佞，敢颺言于衆曰：「湖南山川之美甲天下，然自開闢以来，至于今日，而大聖人始作，何也？蓋天地至精至粹之氣，乆于積，泓于蓄，故其發也昌以大。是氣也，一鍾之冀北，而堯舜者出，以開百有餘年之帝治；再鍾之岐周，而
translation_en: …all assembled. They then gathered the more than 2,700 candidates selected by your servant Cui Tong, Vice Commissioner for Education, and examined them in three sessions. In accordance with the prescribed quota, they selected eighty-five men and also compiled their outstanding compositions for presentation to the throne. Your servant, though lacking in ability, ventured to proclaim to the assembled company: “The beauty of Hunan’s mountains and rivers ranks first under Heaven. Yet why, from the creation of the world down to this day, has a great sage arisen only now? It is because the most refined and pure vital energy of Heaven and Earth accumulates over a long time and is stored in profound depths; thus, when it manifests itself, it does so with flourishing grandeur. This vital energy first concentrated in northern Ji, and Yao and Shun emerged to inaugurate more than a hundred years of imperial rule. It concentrated a second time in the Zhou homeland at Qi, and…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
文武者出以開八百餘年之
王業鍾之淮甸則
聖祖興焉億萬年鴻基茲啓矣鍾
之湖南而我
大聖人作豈非無疆之休乎然其
間亦必有附是間氣而挺生
於若地者為之名世故元凱
冀産周召岐英而我
朝開國功臣又皆淮之豪傑也
則夫
今日獨無若人者奮於湖南乎
矧
天降甘露瑞諸物也瑞諸物未有
不瑞諸人者也
punctuated: 文武者出，以開八百餘年之王業。鍾之淮甸，則聖祖興焉，億萬年鴻基茲啓矣；鍾之湖南，而我大聖人作，豈非無疆之休乎？然其間亦必有附是間氣而挺生於若地者，為之名世。故元凱冀産，周召岐英，而我朝開國功臣又皆淮之豪傑也。則夫今日獨無若人者奮於湖南乎？矧天降甘露，瑞諸物也；瑞諸物，未有不瑞諸人者也。
translation_en: …Kings Wen and Wu emerged, inaugurating a royal enterprise lasting more than eight hundred years. When this vital energy concentrated in the Huai region, our sagely founding ancestor arose, and the vast foundation for countless ages was thereby laid. When it concentrated in Hunan, our great sage arose: was this not a blessing without bounds? Yet there must also have been men who partook of this exceptional vital energy and emerged outstanding in such places, becoming renowned in their age. Thus the Yuan and Kai worthies were natives of Ji, and the Dukes of Zhou and Shao were the outstanding men of Qi; the meritorious founders of our dynasty, too, were all heroes of the Huai region. Could it be that today alone no such men will rise in Hunan? Moreover, Heaven has sent down sweet dew, an auspicious sign manifested in things. Never has an auspicious sign been manifested in things without also being manifested in men.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
天於湖南其亦不靳若人也已維
兹辛卯黃帝之曆伊起也建
酉之月日月會於壽星是蒼
龍宿之首也抑時必有非常
之士應
大聖人求焉求而得非常之士則
曰元凱曰周召者為時庸矣
===
然臣懼以一己目力而欲悉
搜人材於無遺亦殆矣所幸
諸執事者盡心殫力以克成
之諸執事亦曰懼哉閱卷貴
詳校才貴精取士貴當難乎
其庸力也殆益懼哉臣廼喜
曰均是懼也諸士子聞之必
punctuated:
天於湖南，其亦不靳若人也已。維兹辛卯，黃帝之曆伊起也。建酉之月，日月會於壽星，是蒼龍宿之首也。抑時必有非常之士應大聖人求焉。求而得非常之士，則曰元凱、曰周召者，為時庸矣。

然臣懼以一己目力，而欲悉搜人材於無遺，亦殆矣。所幸諸執事者盡心殫力，以克成之。諸執事亦曰：「懼哉！閱卷貴詳，校才貴精，取士貴當，難乎其庸力也，殆益懼哉！」臣廼喜曰：「均是懼也，諸士子聞之必
translation_en:
Heaven surely will not begrudge Hunan such men. This xinmao year is the starting point of the Yellow Emperor’s calendar [?]. In the month designated by you, the sun and moon meet in Shouxing, the first of the Azure Dragon’s celestial lodges. Surely at this time there must be extraordinary scholars who answer the call of the great sage ruler. If his search yields extraordinary scholars, men comparable to the Yuan and Kai, or to the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, will be employed in the service of the age.

Yet I, your servant, fear that to rely upon my own discernment alone and hope to discover every talented man without omission is a precarious undertaking. Fortunately, all the officials concerned have devoted their minds and exhausted their strength to accomplish it. They too said: “How daunting! In reading examination papers, thoroughness is essential; in assessing talent, precision; in selecting scholars, sound judgment. How difficult it is to apply our efforts! We have still greater cause for apprehension!” I, your servant, then said with delight: “We all share this apprehension. When the candidates hear of it, they will surely …”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
將自奮為
大聖人之名臣罔俾諸賢專美於
前
行人司行人徐謙謹序
punctuated:
將自奮為大聖人之名臣，罔俾諸賢專美於前。

行人司行人徐謙謹序。
translation_en:
…will strive to become renowned ministers of our great sage sovereign, not allowing the worthies of earlier times alone to enjoy such distinction.

Preface respectfully composed by Xu Qian, Messenger in the Office of Messengers.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖十年湖廣鄕試
監臨官
巡按湖廣監察御史倪組〔維朱福建閩縣人丙戌進士〕
提調官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司右布政使胡鐸〔時振浙江餘姚縣人乙丑進士〕
湖廣等處承宣布政使司左參議郭曰休〔德夫福建莆田縣人辛巳進士〕
監試官
湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使張峨〔蜀望四川成都前衞人甲戌進士〕
湖廣等處提刑按察司副使李錫〔晉卿山東臨邑縣人甲戌進士〕
===
考試官
行人司行人徐謙〔子恭四川富順縣人乙丑進士〕
同考試官
直隸揚州府儒學敎授陳克昌〔德貽浙江仁和縣人丙戌進士〕
江西饒州府儒學敎授張嘉秀〔文英浙江海塩縣人乙丑進士〕
浙江杭州府儒學敎授唐汶〔源魯福建建寧右衞人辛酉貢士〕
直隸廬州府六安州儒學學正區燦〔暉卿廣東番禺縣人丙子貢士〕
山西遼州儒學學正劉登〔進之陝西西安後衞人乙酉貢士〕
浙江杭州府臨安縣儒學敎諭陳文昌〔希周福建福清縣人庚午貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖十年湖廣鄕試。

監臨官：巡按湖廣監察御史倪組〔維朱，福建閩縣人，丙戌進士〕。

提調官：湖廣等處承宣布政使司右布政使胡鐸〔時振，浙江餘姚縣人，乙丑進士〕。湖廣等處承宣布政使司左參議郭曰休〔德夫，福建莆田縣人，辛巳進士〕。

監試官：湖廣等處提刑按察司按察使張峨〔蜀望，四川成都前衞人，甲戌進士〕。湖廣等處提刑按察司副使李錫〔晉卿，山東臨邑縣人，甲戌進士〕。

考試官：行人司行人徐謙〔子恭，四川富順縣人，乙丑進士〕。

同考試官：直隸揚州府儒學敎授陳克昌〔德貽，浙江仁和縣人，丙戌進士〕。江西饒州府儒學敎授張嘉秀〔文英，浙江海塩縣人，乙丑進士〕。浙江杭州府儒學敎授唐汶〔源魯，福建建寧右衞人，辛酉貢士〕。直隸廬州府六安州儒學學正區燦〔暉卿，廣東番禺縣人，丙子貢士〕。山西遼州儒學學正劉登〔進之，陝西西安後衞人，乙酉貢士〕。浙江杭州府臨安縣儒學敎諭陳文昌〔希周，福建福清縣人，庚午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Huguang Provincial Examination of the tenth year of Jiajing (1531).

Supervising Official: Ni Zu, Investigating Censor inspecting Huguang, courtesy name Weizhu, was from Min County, Fujian, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingxu year.

Proctors: Hu Duo, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Huguang, courtesy name Shizhen, was from Yuyao County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year. Guo Yuexiu, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of Huguang, courtesy name Defu, was from Putian County, Fujian, and was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.

Examination Supervisors: Zhang E, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang, courtesy name Shuwang, was from Chengdu Front Guard, Sichuan, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year. Li Xi, Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang, courtesy name Jinqing, was from Linyi County, Shandong, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Examiner: Xu Qian, Messenger in the Messenger Office, courtesy name Zigong, was from Fushun County, Sichuan, and was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Associate Examiners: Chen Kechang, Professor at the Confucian School of Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Deyi, was from Renhe County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Zhang Jiaxiu, Professor at the Confucian School of Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Wenying, was from Haiyan County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the yichou year.

Tang Wen, Professor at the Confucian School of Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Yuanlu, was from Jianning Right Guard, Fujian, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the xinyou year.

Ou Can, Instructor at the Confucian School of Liu’an Subprefecture, Luzhou Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Huiqing, was from Panyu County, Guangdong, and was a tribute student of the bingzi year.

Liu Deng, Instructor at the Confucian School of Liaozhou Subprefecture, Shanxi, courtesy name Jinzhi, was from Xi’an Rear Guard, Shaanxi, and was a tribute student of the yiyou year.

Chen Wenchang, Instructor at the Confucian School of Lin’an County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Xizhou, was from Fuqing County, Fujian, and was a tribute student of the gengwu year.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
山東兖州府滕縣儒學教諭黃河〔汝清直隸通州人壬午貢士〕
河南開封府杞縣儒學教諭徐璣〔子美浙江鄞縣人丙子貢士〕
山東登州府寧海州文登縣儒學教諭韓奎〔文徵直隸豐縣人戊子貢士〕
印卷官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷茹鳴金〔行父直隸無錫縣人乙卯貢士〕
湖廣等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷楊敷頤〔養正雲南太和縣人辛酉貢士〕
收掌試卷官
武昌府知府仲選〔思舜直隸沭陽縣人辛巳進士〕
衡州府知府章僑〔處仁浙江蘭谿縣人丁丑進士〕
===
永州府知府汪漢〔淵之直隸懷寧縣人癸未進士〕
受卷官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司照磨所添註照磨王納言〔惟允河南信陽衛籍襄城縣人巳丑進士〕
岳州府知府蕭晚〔啓旦江西吉水縣人辛巳進士〕
荆州府同知李章〔民俊四川長壽縣人辛巳進士〕
襄陽府通判顧瑛〔德華直隸太倉州人戊午貢士〕
荆州府潜江縣知縣周洪範〔伯陳四川漢州人巳丑進士〕
彌封官
襄陽府推官張鈇〔德威山東冠縣人巳丑進士〕
punctuated:
山東兖州府滕縣儒學教諭黃河〔汝清，直隸通州人，壬午貢士〕。河南開封府杞縣儒學教諭徐璣〔子美，浙江鄞縣人，丙子貢士〕。山東登州府寧海州文登縣儒學教諭韓奎〔文徵，直隸豐縣人，戊子貢士〕。

印卷官：湖廣等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷茹鳴金〔行父，直隸無錫縣人，乙卯貢士〕。湖廣等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷楊敷頤〔養正，雲南太和縣人，辛酉貢士〕。

收掌試卷官：武昌府知府仲選〔思舜，直隸沭陽縣人，辛巳進士〕。衡州府知府章僑〔處仁，浙江蘭谿縣人，丁丑進士〕。永州府知府汪漢〔淵之，直隸懷寧縣人，癸未進士〕。

受卷官：湖廣等處承宣布政使司照磨所添註照磨王納言〔惟允，河南信陽衛籍，襄城縣人，巳丑進士〕。岳州府知府蕭晚〔啓旦，江西吉水縣人，辛巳進士〕。荆州府同知李章〔民俊，四川長壽縣人，辛巳進士〕。襄陽府通判顧瑛〔德華，直隸太倉州人，戊午貢士〕。荆州府潜江縣知縣周洪範〔伯陳，四川漢州人，巳丑進士〕。

彌封官：襄陽府推官張鈇〔德威，山東冠縣人，巳丑進士〕。
translation_en:
Huang He, courtesy name Ruqing, was Instructor of the Confucian School of Teng County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A native of Tongzhou, Zhili, he was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the renwu year.
Xu Ji, courtesy name Zimei, was Instructor of the Confucian School of Qi County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A native of Yin County, Zhejiang, he was a tribute scholar of the bingzi year.
Han Kui, courtesy name Wenzheng, was Instructor of the Confucian School of Wendeng County, Ninghai Subprefecture, Dengzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A native of Feng County, Zhili, he was a tribute scholar of the wuzi year.

Officials for Printing Examination Papers:
Ru Mingjin, courtesy name Xingfu, was Registrar in the Registry of the Huguang Provincial Administration Commission. A native of Wuxi County, Zhili, he was a tribute scholar of the yimao year.
Yang Fuyi, courtesy name Yangzheng, was Registrar in the Registry of the Huguang Provincial Surveillance Commission. A native of Taihe County, Yunnan, he was a tribute scholar of the xinyou year.

Officials for Collecting and Safekeeping Examination Scripts:
Zhong Xuan, courtesy name Sishun, was Prefect of Wuchang. A native of Shuyang County, Zhili, he was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the xinsi year.
Zhang Qiao, courtesy name Churen, was Prefect of Hengzhou. A native of Lanxi County, Zhejiang, he was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.
Wang Han, courtesy name Yuanzhi, was Prefect of Yongzhou. A native of Huaining County, Zhili, he was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Officials for Receiving Examination Scripts:
Wang Nayan, courtesy name Weiyun, was a supernumerary Record Keeper in the Records Office of the Huguang Provincial Administration Commission. Registered with Xinyang Guard, Henan, and a native of Xiangcheng County, he was a metropolitan graduate of the year transcribed as “sichou” [?].
Xiao Wan, courtesy name Qidan, was Prefect of Yuezhou. A native of Jishui County, Jiangxi, he was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.
Li Zhang, courtesy name Minjun, was Vice Prefect of Jingzhou. A native of Changshou County, Sichuan, he was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.
Gu Ying, courtesy name Dehua, was Assistant Prefect of Xiangyang. A native of Taicang Subprefecture, Zhili, he was a tribute scholar of the wuwu year.
Zhou Hongfan, courtesy name Bochen, was Magistrate of Qianjiang County, Jingzhou Prefecture. A native of Hanzhou, Sichuan, he was a metropolitan graduate of the year transcribed as “sichou” [?].

Officials for Sealing Candidates’ Identifying Information:
Zhang Fu, courtesy name Dewei, was Prefectural Judge of Xiangyang. A native of Guan County, Shandong, he was a metropolitan graduate of the year transcribed as “sichou” [?].

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
武昌府興國州知州楊祐〔汝承浙江錢塘縣人已丑進士〕
荆州府石首縣知縣張溪〔伯清直隸壽州人已丑進士〕
黃州府麻城縣知縣陳子文〔在中福建閩縣人已丑進士〕
襄陽府南漳縣知縣袁載〔安道浙江慈谿縣人癸未進士〕
岳州府巴陵縣知縣江滿〔謙之江西進賢縣人已丑進士〕
謄錄官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司照磨所添註照磨薛甲〔應登直隸江陰縣人已丑進士〕
寶慶府推官竇一桂〔元芳山西武鄉縣人丙戌進士〕
長沙府推官卞偉〔子充四川宜賓縣人已丑進士〕
===
荆州府歸州知州趙章〔達卿四川合州人辛巳進士〕
荆州府夷陵州知州石萬鈞〔汝重四川眉州人辛酉貢士〕
黃州府黃陂縣知縣林東海〔世觀福建莆田縣人已丑進士〕
對讀官
德安府推官饒中〔性甫河南固始縣人已丑進士〕
黃州府蘄州同知趙廷松〔子後浙江樂清縣人癸未進士〕
武昌府蒲圻縣知縣吳本固〔道深河南商城縣人已丑進士〕
長沙府瀏陽縣知縣陳鯨〔石卿浙江慈谿縣人丙戌進士〕
荆州府枝江縣知縣高自卑〔大德四川内江縣人癸酉貢士〕
punctuated:
武昌府興國州知州楊祐〔汝承，浙江錢塘縣人，已丑進士〕。荆州府石首縣知縣張溪〔伯清，直隸壽州人，已丑進士〕。黃州府麻城縣知縣陳子文〔在中，福建閩縣人，已丑進士〕。襄陽府南漳縣知縣袁載〔安道，浙江慈谿縣人，癸未進士〕。岳州府巴陵縣知縣江滿〔謙之，江西進賢縣人，已丑進士〕。

謄錄官：
湖廣等處承宣布政使司照磨所添註照磨薛甲〔應登，直隸江陰縣人，已丑進士〕。寶慶府推官竇一桂〔元芳，山西武鄉縣人，丙戌進士〕。長沙府推官卞偉〔子充，四川宜賓縣人，已丑進士〕。荆州府歸州知州趙章〔達卿，四川合州人，辛巳進士〕。荆州府夷陵州知州石萬鈞〔汝重，四川眉州人，辛酉貢士〕。黃州府黃陂縣知縣林東海〔世觀，福建莆田縣人，已丑進士〕。

對讀官：
德安府推官饒中〔性甫，河南固始縣人，已丑進士〕。黃州府蘄州同知趙廷松〔子後，浙江樂清縣人，癸未進士〕。武昌府蒲圻縣知縣吳本固〔道深，河南商城縣人，已丑進士〕。長沙府瀏陽縣知縣陳鯨〔石卿，浙江慈谿縣人，丙戌進士〕。荆州府枝江縣知縣高自卑〔大德，四川内江縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Yang You, Magistrate of Xingguo Subprefecture in Wuchang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Rucheng and was from Qiantang County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the jichou year [?].

Zhang Xi, Magistrate of Shishou County in Jingzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Boqing and was from Shouzhou, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year [?].

Chen Ziwen, Magistrate of Macheng County in Huangzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zaizhong and was from Min County, Fujian. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year [?].

Yuan Zai, Magistrate of Nanzhang County in Xiangyang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Andao and was from Cixi County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Jiang Man, Magistrate of Baling County in Yuezhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Qianzhi and was from Jinxian County, Jiangxi. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year [?].

Transcription Officials

Xue Jia was an additionally appointed Examiner of Documents in the Documents Examination Office of the Huguang Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Yingdeng, and he was from Jiangyin County, Zhili; he was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year [?].

Dou Yigui, Prefectural Judge of Baoqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yuanfang and was from Wuxiang County, Shanxi. He was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Bian Wei, Prefectural Judge of Changsha Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zichong and was from Yibin County, Sichuan. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year [?].

Zhao Zhang, Magistrate of Guizhou Subprefecture in Jingzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Daqing and was from Hezhou, Sichuan. He was a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.

Shi Wanjun, Magistrate of Yiling Subprefecture in Jingzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ruzhong and was from Meizhou, Sichuan. He was a tribute student (gongshi) of the xinyou year.

Lin Donghai, Magistrate of Huangpi County in Huangzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shiguan and was from Putian County, Fujian. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year [?].

Proofreading Officials

Rao Zhong, Prefectural Judge of De'an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Xingfu and was from Gushi County, Henan. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year [?].

Zhao Tingsong, Vice Magistrate of Qizhou Subprefecture in Huangzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zihou and was from Yueqing County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

Wu Bengu, Magistrate of Puqi County in Wuchang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Daoshen and was from Shangcheng County, Henan. He was a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year [?].

Chen Jing, Magistrate of Liuyang County in Changsha Prefecture, had the courtesy name Shiqing and was from Cixi County, Zhejiang. He was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Gao Zibei, Magistrate of Zhijiang County in Jingzhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Dade and was from Neijiang County, Sichuan. He was a tribute student of the guiyou year.

[The transcription repeatedly gives 已丑, apparently for the cyclical designation 己丑, jichou.]

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:

武昌左衞指揮僉事彭意〔克誠直隸舒城縣人〕
武昌左衞署指揮僉事劉閑〔大方湖廣蒲圻縣人〕
武昌衞中千戶所正千戶晉表〔國章河南靈寳縣人〕
===
武昌左衞右千戶所正千戶彭綬〔廷章直隸臨淮縣人〕
搜檢官
武昌衞指揮使王堂〔道升山後人〕
武昌衞指揮同知賀恩〔克承湖廣麻城縣人〕
武昌左衞指揮僉事余學〔希賢湖廣黃岡縣人〕
武昌左衞指揮僉事胡綸〔大中直隸臨淮縣人〕
武昌衞左千戶所副千戶徐節〔子山直隸壽州人〕
武昌衞中千戶所副千戶瞿能〔國才直隸盱眙縣人〕
武昌左衞左千戶所副千戶葛方〔汝春直隸宣城縣人〕
punctuated:
靖州綏寧縣知縣應𤋮〔天監，浙江永康縣人，庚午貢士〕。

武昌衞指揮使王言〔汝綸，直隸含山縣人〕。武昌衞指揮使滿容〔汝德，直隸定遠縣人〕。武昌衞指揮同知黃經〔世常，福建連江縣人〕。武昌左衞指揮僉事張秀〔繼實，直隸大興縣人〕。武昌左衞指揮僉事彭意〔克誠，直隸舒城縣人〕。武昌左衞署指揮僉事劉閑〔大方，湖廣蒲圻縣人〕。武昌衞中千戶所正千戶晉表〔國章，河南靈寳縣人〕。武昌左衞右千戶所正千戶彭綬〔廷章，直隸臨淮縣人〕。

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
武昌左衞左千戸所副千戸孫元〔體仁直隸定遠縣人〕
供給官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司照磨所檢校楊梅〔濟川山東安東衞人監生〕
武昌府通判雙桂〔月卿四川寧川衞人癸酉貢士〕
武昌府江夏縣知縣葉宗傑〔千才廣西靈川縣人已卯貢士〕

辰州府溆浦縣龍潭巡檢司巡檢周露〔惟澤直隸嘉定縣人吏員〕

武昌府江夏縣將臺驛驛丞王舟〔濟川陝西華州人承差〕
武昌府蒲圻縣官塘驛驛丞王潤〔本德直隸永年縣人承差〕

荆州府監利縣塔市驛驛丞周灝〔仲源福建候官縣人承差〕
punctuated:
武昌左衞左千戸所副千戸孫元〔體仁，直隸定遠縣人〕。

供給官
湖廣等處承宣布政使司照磨所檢校楊梅〔濟川，山東安東衞人，監生〕。
武昌府通判雙桂〔月卿，四川寧川衞人，癸酉貢士〕。

德安府安陸縣知縣李一中〔大本，江西上饒縣人，監生〕。
德安府應山縣知縣王尚用〔賢卿，江西安福縣人，丙子貢士〕。
武昌衞經歷司經歷彭摶〔于漢，江西清江縣人，吏員〕。

武昌府江夏縣縣丞任山〔汝壽，直隸頴州人，吏員〕。
辰州府溆浦縣龍潭巡檢司巡檢周露〔惟澤，直隸嘉定縣人，吏員〕。

武昌府江夏縣魯湖河泊所河泊盛大〔德宏，山東清平縣人，吏員〕。
武昌府江夏縣將臺驛驛丞王舟〔濟川，陝西華州人，承差〕。
武昌府蒲圻縣官塘驛驛丞王潤〔本德，直隸永年縣人，承差〕。
荆州府石首縣調絃驛驛丞郭崇義〔循禮，山東清平縣人，承差〕。
荆州府監利縣塔市驛驛丞周灝〔仲源，福建候官縣人，承差〕。
translation_en:
Sun Yuan, Vice Commander of the Left Battalion of Wuchang Left Guard, had the courtesy name Tiren and was from Dingyuan County, Zhili.

Yang Mei, Examiner in the Records Office of the Huguang Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Jichuan and was from Andong Guard, Shandong. He was an Imperial University student.

Shuang Gui, Assistant Prefect of Wuchang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yueqing and was from Ningchuan Guard [?], Sichuan. He was a tribute student of the guiyou year.

Ye Zongjie, Magistrate of Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Qiancai and was from Lingchuan County, Guangxi. He was a tribute student of the yimao year [?; apparently jimao].

Li Yizhong, Magistrate of Anlu County, De’an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Daben and was from Shangrao County, Jiangxi. He was an Imperial University student.

Wang Shangyong, Magistrate of Yingshan County, De’an Prefecture, had the courtesy name Xianqing and was from Anfu County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute student of the bingzi year.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
志於道據於德依於仁游於藝
郊社之禮所以事上帝也宗廟之禮所以
祀乎其先也
使天下仕者皆欲立於王之朝耕者皆欲
耕於王之野商賈皆欲藏於王之市行
旅皆欲出於王之途
易
===
牝馬地類行地无疆柔順利貞君子攸行
安節之亨承上道也
廣大配天地變通配四時陰陽之義配日
月易簡之善配至德
天地之道貞觀者也日月之道貞明者也
天下之動貞夫一者也
書
無怠無荒四夷來王
股肱惟人良臣惟聖
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
志於道，據於德，依於仁，游於藝。
郊社之禮，所以事上帝也；宗廟之禮，所以祀乎其先也。
使天下仕者皆欲立於王之朝，耕者皆欲耕於王之野，商賈皆欲藏於王之市，行旅皆欲出於王之途。

易
牝馬地類，行地无疆，柔順利貞，君子攸行。
安節之亨，承上道也。
廣大配天地，變通配四時，陰陽之義配日月，易簡之善配至德。
天地之道，貞觀者也；日月之道，貞明者也；天下之動，貞夫一者也。

書
無怠無荒，四夷來王。
股肱惟人，良臣惟聖。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
Set your aspiration on the Way, ground yourself in virtue, cleave to benevolence, and take your recreation in the arts.

The rites of the suburban sacrifice and the altars of soil and grain serve to worship the Lord on High; the rites of the ancestral temple serve to sacrifice to one’s ancestors.

Make all those seeking office under Heaven wish to stand at Your Majesty’s court, all farmers wish to cultivate Your Majesty’s fields, all merchants wish to store their goods in Your Majesty’s markets, and all travelers wish to journey along Your Majesty’s roads.

Book of Changes (Yi)
The mare belongs to the category of earth and travels the earth without limit. Gentle and compliant, beneficial and steadfast: this is the course the noble man follows.

The success of being at ease with restraint comes from following the way of those above.

Its breadth and greatness match Heaven and Earth; its change and adaptation match the four seasons; the significance of its yin and yang matches the sun and moon; the excellence of its ease and simplicity matches the highest virtue.

The way of Heaven and Earth is displayed through constancy; the way of the sun and moon shines through constancy; all movement under Heaven rests on constancy in the One.

Book of Documents (Shu)
Be neither idle nor heedless, and the peoples of the four quarters will come to acknowledge your kingship.

As arms and legs make a person whole, so good ministers make a ruler a sage.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
所寶惟賢則邇人安
不剛不柔厥德允修惟周公克慎厥始惟
君陳克和厥中惟公克成厥終
詩
躋彼公堂稱彼兕觥萬壽無疆
赫赫南仲玁狁于夷
王赫斯怒爰整其旅以按徂旅以篤于周
祜以對于天下
喤喤厥聲肅雝和鳴先祖是聽我客戾止
===
永觀厥成
春秋
冬十有二月祭伯來隱公元年
夏公會齊侯宋公陳侯衞侯曹伯伐鄭圍
新城僖公六年
丁亥楚子入陳宣公十有一年
季孫斯仲孫何忌帥師墮費定公十有二年
禮記
天子祭天下名山大川五嶽視三公四瀆
punctuated:
所寶惟賢，則邇人安。
不剛不柔，厥德允修。惟周公克慎厥始，惟君陳克和厥中，惟公克成厥終。

詩
躋彼公堂，稱彼兕觥，萬壽無疆。
赫赫南仲，玁狁于夷。
王赫斯怒，爰整其旅，以按徂旅，以篤于周祜，以對于天下。
喤喤厥聲，肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。我客戾止，永觀厥成。

春秋
冬十有二月，祭伯來。隱公元年。
夏，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衞侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。僖公六年。
丁亥，楚子入陳。宣公十有一年。
季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。定公十有二年。

禮記
天子祭天下名山大川，五嶽視三公，四瀆
translation_en:
If those you treasure are the worthy, the people nearby will be at peace.
Neither unyielding nor yielding, his virtue is truly cultivated. The Duke of Zhou was able to exercise care at the beginning; Jun Chen was able to bring harmony in the middle; you, my lord, can bring the undertaking to completion at its end.

Book of Odes
Ascend that lordly hall; raise that rhinoceros-horn goblet: may he live ten thousand years, without end!
Illustrious was Nan Zhong; the Xianyun were subdued.
The king blazed with anger and marshalled his troops, to check the advancing host, to strengthen the blessings of Zhou, and to answer to all under Heaven.
Resonant are their sounds, solemn and harmonious their music; the ancestors listen. Our guest has arrived, to behold forever the accomplishment.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In winter, in the twelfth month, the Earl of Zhai came. First year of Duke Yin.
In summer, the duke joined the marquises of Qi, Song, Chen, and Wei and the Earl of Cao in attacking Zheng; they besieged Xincheng. Sixth year of Duke Xi.
On the dinghai day, the Viscount of Chu entered Chen. Eleventh year of Duke Xuan.
Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led troops to demolish the walls of Bi. Twelfth year of Duke Ding.

Book of Rites
The Son of Heaven sacrifices to the renowned mountains and great rivers throughout the realm. The Five Sacred Peaks are treated as equivalent to the Three Dukes; the Four Great Watercourses …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
視諸侯
以正君臣以篤父子以睦兄弟以齊上下
夫婦有所
諸侯以龜為寶以圭為瑞
地氣上齊天氣下降陰陽相摩天地相蕩
鼓之以雷霆奮之以風雨動之以四時
煖之以日月而百化興焉如此則樂者
天地之和也
第貳塲
===
論
孔子聞而知之
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢賜農民今年租稅之半詔文帝十二年
擬唐以馬周為監察御史誥貞觀三年
擬宋頒訓廉謹刑二銘於中外羣臣謝表
淳祐四年
判語五條
信牌
punctuated:
視諸侯。

以正君臣，以篤父子，以睦兄弟，以齊上下，夫婦有所。

諸侯以龜為寶，以圭為瑞。

地氣上齊，天氣下降，陰陽相摩，天地相蕩，鼓之以雷霆，奮之以風雨，動之以四時，煖之以日月，而百化興焉。如此，則樂者，天地之和也。

第貳塲

論
孔子聞而知之。

詔誥表內科一道
擬漢賜農民今年租稅之半詔，文帝十二年。
擬唐以馬周為監察御史誥，貞觀三年。
擬宋頒訓廉謹刑二銘於中外羣臣謝表，淳祐四年。

判語五條
信牌。
translation_en:
…are accorded the same rank as the feudal lords.

Thereby to rectify relations between ruler and minister, deepen affection between father and son, foster harmony between brothers, and order relations between superiors and inferiors, so that husband and wife each have their proper place.

The feudal lords regard tortoise shells as treasures and jade tablets as tokens of authority.

The vital energies of earth rise, and those of heaven descend. Yin and yang interact; heaven and earth stir one another. They rouse things with thunder, animate them with wind and rain, move them through the four seasons, and warm them with the sun and moon; thus the myriad transformations arise. Accordingly, music is the harmony of heaven and earth.

Second Session

Discourse
Confucius knew through hearing.

One topic from among imperial edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose an imperial edict in the manner of the Han dynasty granting farmers a remission of half of this year's land tax: twelfth year of Emperor Wen.
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Ma Zhou as Investigating Censor: third year of Zhenguan.
Compose a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song dynasty for the promulgation to officials at court and in the provinces of the two admonitory inscriptions, “Inculcating Integrity” and “Exercising Caution in Punishment”: fourth year of Chunyou.

Five Legal Judgments
Credential tablets.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
匿稅
失儀
越城
誣告
第參塲
策〔五道〕
問自古聖哲之化天下未有不須于內助
者若文王之於太姒武王之於邑姜是
已我
===
太祖高皇帝首御家邦貽謀萬世雖古聖哲之
君殆無以過然而贊元斡化
孝慈高皇后有力焉其嘉言善行載之傳者可
得而聞歟至
仁孝文皇后復廣
高皇后之教為內訓二十篇邇者
章聖慈仁皇太后復製為女訓十二篇其亦皆
有序歟伏覩三書可以仰窺我
列聖脩齊之化矣今天下家傳人誦風化丕行
punctuated:
匿稅。
失儀。
越城。
誣告。

第參塲
策〔五道〕

問：自古聖哲之化天下，未有不須于內助者。若文王之於太姒、武王之於邑姜，是已。我太祖高皇帝首御家邦，貽謀萬世，雖古聖哲之君，殆無以過。然而贊元斡化，孝慈高皇后有力焉。其嘉言善行載之傳者，可得而聞歟？至仁孝文皇后，復廣高皇后之教，為內訓二十篇。邇者，章聖慈仁皇太后復製為女訓十二篇。其亦皆有序歟？伏覩三書，可以仰窺我列聖脩齊之化矣。今天下家傳人誦，風化丕行，
translation_en:
Concealing taxable property.
Breaching ceremonial propriety.
Crossing the city wall.
Making a false accusation.

Third Session
Policy Questions〔Five questions〕

Question: Since antiquity, no sage or wise ruler has transformed All-under-Heaven without needing the assistance of his consort. Such were King Wen’s relationship with Tai Si and King Wu’s with Yi Jiang. Our Emperor Taizu Gao first took command of the imperial house and realm and bequeathed plans for ten thousand generations; even the sage and wise rulers of antiquity could scarcely have surpassed him. Yet Empress Xiaoci Gao contributed greatly to assisting the sovereign and advancing his transforming influence. May we hear of the admirable words and good deeds recorded in her biography? Later, Empress Renxiao Wen further developed Empress Gao’s teachings, composing the Instructions for the Inner Quarters (Neixun) in twenty chapters. Recently, Empress Dowager Zhangsheng Ciren also composed the Instructions for Women (Nüxun) in twelve chapters. Do these works all have prefaces as well? Reverently examining these three books, we may gain a glimpse of the transforming influence exerted by our successive sage rulers through cultivating themselves and regulating their households. Today, throughout All-under-Heaven, these works are passed down in every household and recited by everyone, and their moral influence spreads widely…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
諸士子皆有正家之責者抑嘗習此以
教否乎請敬陳之以觀脩齊之實學
問周禮周公致太平之書也而唐六典則
倣乎是何其間大不同歟周禮無公孤
之職唐乃有三師三公之官此固成王
立公孤之遺意乃若吏部掌天下官吏
選授勳封考課戶部掌天下戶口井田
禮部掌天下禮儀祠祭燕享貢舉兵部
掌天下軍衛武官選授刑部掌天下刑
===
法及徒隸勾覆關禁均有政令焉者其
與周禮立五官之職掌同歟周禮缺冬
官而後人以考工記補之矣唐乃有工
部掌天下百工屯田山澤之政令者何
所據歟此外又有門下中書秘書殿中
四省御史臺太常光祿衛尉太僕大理
鴻臚司農太府諸寺司國子少府將作
諸監左右等衛及太子與親王府國公
主邑司官屬何其多歟意者其唐太宗
punctuated:
諸士子皆有正家之責者，抑嘗習此以教否乎？請敬陳之，以觀脩齊之實學。

問：周禮，周公致太平之書也，而唐六典則倣乎是，何其間大不同歟？周禮無公孤之職，唐乃有三師三公之官，此固成王立公孤之遺意。乃若吏部掌天下官吏選授、勳封、考課，戶部掌天下戶口、井田，禮部掌天下禮儀、祠祭、燕享、貢舉，兵部掌天下軍衛、武官選授，刑部掌天下刑法及徒隸、勾覆、關禁，均有政令焉者，其與周禮立五官之職掌同歟？周禮缺冬官，而後人以考工記補之矣。唐乃有工部掌天下百工、屯田、山澤之政令者，何所據歟？此外又有門下、中書、秘書、殿中四省，御史臺，太常、光祿、衛尉、太僕、大理、鴻臚、司農、太府諸寺司，國子、少府、將作諸監，左右等衛，及太子與親王府國、公主邑司官屬，何其多歟？意者其唐太宗
translation_en:
…You scholars all bear responsibility for setting your households in order. Have you studied these works and used them to instruct your families? Please respectfully set this forth, so that we may observe your practical learning in cultivating yourselves and ordering your households.

Question: The Rites of Zhou is the book through which the Duke of Zhou brought about Great Peace, and the Six Statutes of the Tang took it as a model. Why, then, are there such great differences between them? The Rites of Zhou contains no offices for the Three Dukes and Three Solitaries, yet the Tang had the Three Preceptors and Three Dukes. This certainly preserves the intention behind King Cheng’s establishment of the Dukes and Solitaries. As for the Ministry of Personnel, which administered the selection and appointment of officials throughout the realm, merit titles and enfeoffments, and evaluations of performance; the Ministry of Revenue, which administered households and population and well-field lands throughout the realm; the Ministry of Rites, which administered ritual observances, sacrifices, banquets, and the recommendation and examination of candidates throughout the realm; the Ministry of War, which administered military guards and the selection and appointment of military officers throughout the realm; and the Ministry of Justice, which administered penal law, convict laborers, judicial review, and restrictions at passes throughout the realm—each having its own administrative ordinances—were their responsibilities the same as those assigned to the five offices established in the Rites of Zhou? The Rites of Zhou lacks the Office of Winter, and later scholars supplied the Record of Artificers to fill the gap. Yet the Tang had a Ministry of Works, administering ordinances concerning all crafts, agricultural colonies, mountains, and marshes throughout the realm. On what was this based?

Besides these, there were the four departments—the Chancellery, Secretariat, Palace Library, and Palace Administration—and the Censorate; the Courts of Imperial Sacrifices, Imperial Entertainments, Imperial Regalia, Imperial Stud, Judicial Review, State Ceremonial, the National Granaries, and the Imperial Treasury; the Directorates of Education, Palace Manufactures, and Palace Buildings; the various Left and Right Guards; and the officials attached to the establishments and domains of the Heir Apparent and imperial princes, and to the estate offices of princesses. Why were there so many? Might it be that Emperor Taizong of the Tang…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
觀會通而立政歟願悉言之以探聖人
制作之意與夫後世因時之政
問天心仁愛人君乃出災異以譴告之昔
殷高宗以雊雉興周宣王以旱魃興盖
天於中興之君尤拳拳焉者也我
皇上仁孝誠敬之德通乎神明近年以來黄河
清甘露降天之所以協應者至矣夫何
偶有彗星之見歟我
皇上痛自脩省又
===
勅諭羣臣各加戒飭遂致彗滅是即先王克謹
天戒臣人克有常憲之意也然春秋書
孛者三左氏公羊皆以彗言之矣自後
見者不一載之史冊可攷也漢文宣光
三帝唐太玄憲三宗宋太祖暨太宗仁
宗皆所謂希世之賢君者而彗皆屢見
何歟自古遇彗陳言之臣若申繻高堂
隆之說其誣不言可知若宋吕公著程
頤富弼吕大防吕大鈞邢恕王安禮陳
punctuated:
觀會通而立政歟？願悉言之，以探聖人制作之意與夫後世因時之政。

問：天心仁愛人君，乃出災異以譴告之。昔殷高宗以雊雉興，周宣王以旱魃興，盖天於中興之君尤拳拳焉者也。我皇上仁孝誠敬之德通乎神明，近年以來，黄河清，甘露降，天之所以協應者至矣。夫何偶有彗星之見歟？我皇上痛自脩省，又勅諭羣臣各加戒飭，遂致彗滅，是即先王克謹天戒、臣人克有常憲之意也。然《春秋》書孛者三，左氏、公羊皆以彗言之矣。自後見者不一，載之史冊可攷也。漢文、宣、光三帝，唐太、玄、憲三宗，宋太祖暨太宗、仁宗，皆所謂希世之賢君者，而彗皆屢見，何歟？自古遇彗陳言之臣，若申繻、高堂隆之說，其誣不言可知。若宋吕公著、程頤、富弼、吕大防、吕大鈞、邢恕、王安禮、陳
translation_en:
…survey the interconnections among institutions and establish his government accordingly? Please explain fully, so as to explore the intentions behind the sages’ creation of institutions and the governmental arrangements by which later ages adapted to their times.

Question: Heaven, in its benevolent concern for rulers, sends disasters and anomalies to reprimand and admonish them. In antiquity, Gaozong of Yin achieved a resurgence in response to a crowing pheasant, and King Xuan of Zhou achieved a resurgence in response to drought. Heaven is indeed especially solicitous toward rulers who restore their dynasties. Our Emperor’s virtues of benevolence, filial piety, sincerity, and reverence reach the divine powers. In recent years, the Yellow River has run clear and sweet dew has descended: Heaven’s harmonious responses have been most abundant. Why, then, has a comet unexpectedly appeared? Our Emperor earnestly undertook self-cultivation and self-examination and further issued an edict admonishing all his ministers to exercise greater vigilance and discipline. Consequently, the comet disappeared. This embodies the principle that the former kings scrupulously heeded Heaven’s warnings and their ministers faithfully observed constant standards.

Yet the Spring and Autumn Annals records a “bushy star” three times, and both the Zuo and Gongyang commentaries describe these as comets. There have been numerous subsequent appearances, which can be verified in the historical records. The three Han emperors Wen, Xuan, and Guangwu; the three Tang emperors Taizong, Xuanzong, and Xianzong; and the Song emperors Taizu, Taizong, and Renzong were all what one would call worthy rulers rarely seen in any age. Yet comets repeatedly appeared during all their reigns. Why was this? Among ministers who have offered counsel upon the appearance of comets since antiquity, the falsity of such explanations as those of Shen Xu and Gaotang Long is evident without further discussion. As for the Song ministers Lü Gongzhu, Cheng Yi, Fu Bi, Lü Dafang, Lü Dajun, Xing Shu, Wang Anli, Chen…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
并吕好問王襄諸臣之疏其切要之旨
可為上下交脩之助者願有聞也
問儲蓄國之大計而漕運又儲蓄之所自
也漢唐都關中運道止河渭一路宋都
汴梁運道所至凡四路今其法可得而
言歟至元都燕始通海漕元史謂為一
代良法又謂視河漕之數所得盖多然
則其議倡於何人歟我
朝洪武永樂初猶通海漕至會通河通利始
===
罷自此嵗運充積
京師富盛矣然慮者猶謂海漕亦不可廢其
果然歟夫制用非一端要之利國利民
而已若戍淮南湖蕩之田如魏鄧艾之
計耕京東瀕海之處如元虞集之策墾
監苑牧馬之地如宋熈寧之法抑可以
寛民力省嵗漕否歟事關經國謀貴逺
慮請畫一以告俟
廟堂之上擇焉
punctuated:
并、吕好問、王襄諸臣之疏，其切要之旨，可為上下交脩之助者，願有聞也。
問：儲蓄，國之大計，而漕運又儲蓄之所自也。漢唐都關中，運道止河渭一路；宋都汴梁，運道所至凡四路。今其法可得而言歟？至元都燕，始通海漕。元史謂為一代良法，又謂視河漕之數，所得盖多。然則其議倡於何人歟？我朝洪武、永樂初猶通海漕，至會通河通利始罷。自此嵗運充積，京師富盛矣。然慮者猶謂海漕亦不可廢，其果然歟？夫制用非一端，要之利國利民而已。若戍淮南湖蕩之田，如魏鄧艾之計；耕京東瀕海之處，如元虞集之策；墾監苑牧馬之地，如宋熈寧之法：抑可以寛民力、省嵗漕否歟？事關經國，謀貴逺慮。請畫一以告，俟廟堂之上擇焉。
translation_en:
…Bing, Lü Haowen, Wang Xiang, and the other ministers’ memorials: I wish to hear their essential points that might help rulers and subjects alike cultivate their conduct.
Question: Maintaining reserves is a major concern of state, and grain transport is in turn the means by which those reserves are supplied. The Han and Tang established their capitals in Guanzhong, and their transport route was confined to a single course along the Yellow and Wei Rivers. The Song established its capital at Bianliang, which was served by four transport routes. Can the arrangements for these now be explained? When the Yuan established its capital at Yan, it opened maritime grain transport. The History of the Yuan calls this an excellent institution of that dynasty and also states that the quantity received was considerably greater than that transported by river. Who, then, first advocated this proposal? Our dynasty still used maritime grain transport during the Hongwu reign and the beginning of the Yongle reign; it was discontinued only once the Huitong Canal became freely navigable. Thereafter, annual shipments filled the reserves, and the capital became prosperous and well supplied. Yet those concerned about the matter still maintained that maritime grain transport should not be abandoned. Were they indeed correct?
There is more than one way to regulate expenditure; the essential aim is simply to benefit the state and the people. If we were to establish garrisons on the fields amid the lakes and marshes of Huainan [?], following the plan of Deng Ai of Wei; cultivate the coastal lands of Jingdong, following the proposal of Yu Ji of the Yuan; or reclaim the horse pastures of the imperial pastoral establishments and parks, following the practice of the Song’s Xining reign, could we ease the burden on the people and reduce annual grain shipments? These matters concern the governance of the state, and planning requires foresight. Please set out your proposals point by point, so that the court may choose among them.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
問荆楚天地之要區也其地廣闊五方雜
寓故宜城有梧州之孝子荆州寓高平
之詞人吳興考功留之穀城濟源少保
處于長沙有舉進士第一而自濱州遷
襄州者有為時宰所惡而棄武夷居當
陽者廣漢南軒之家潭州廣信疊山之
徙興國其他若耿介出塵如丁鶴年矜
式學者如龍仁夫邑民敬之如李安國
州里增重如劉凝之茲數人者抑何負
===
於湖哉我
朝自
國初以至今日荆楚之民固晏如也夫何流
民之聚者乃成客戶凌主之勢或假繼
贅而奪之產或誘借貸而取其貲或駕
虛詞而重其禍其將何以生生歟伊欲
俾居者安来者撫其道果安在歟諸士
生長是邦必有能言之者幸以告我
punctuated: 問：荆楚，天地之要區也。其地廣闊，五方雜寓，故宜城有梧州之孝子，荆州寓高平之詞人，吳興考功留之穀城，濟源少保處于長沙。有舉進士第一而自濱州遷襄州者，有為時宰所惡而棄武夷居當陽者。廣漢南軒之家潭州，廣信疊山之徙興國，其他若耿介出塵如丁鶴年，矜式學者如龍仁夫，邑民敬之如李安國，州里增重如劉凝之，茲數人者，抑何負於湖哉？我朝自國初以至今日，荆楚之民固晏如也。夫何流民之聚者，乃成客戶凌主之勢？或假繼贅而奪之產，或誘借貸而取其貲，或駕虛詞而重其禍，其將何以生生歟？伊欲俾居者安、来者撫，其道果安在歟？諸士生長是邦，必有能言之者，幸以告我。
translation_en:
Question: Jingchu is a strategically important region under Heaven. Its territory is vast, and people from all quarters dwell together there. Thus Yicheng had a filial son from Wuzhou, and Jingzhou lodged a poet from Gaoping; the official of the Bureau of Merit Evaluation from Wuxing stayed in Gucheng, and the Junior Guardian from Jiyuan lived in Changsha. One man who had placed first in the jinshi examination moved from Binzhou to Xiangzhou; another, hated by the chief minister of his day, left Wuyi to live in Dangyang. Nanxuan of Guanghan made his home in Tanzhou, and Dieshan of Guangxin moved to Xingguo. Among others were Ding Henian, upright and aloof from worldly concerns; Long Renfu, a model for scholars; Li Anguo, respected by the county’s people; and Liu Ningzhi, whose presence brought added distinction to his locality. What harm did these men ever do to Huguang?

From the founding of our dynasty down to the present day, the people of Jingchu have certainly lived in peace. Why, then, have gatherings of displaced people produced a situation in which newcomer households overbear the established inhabitants? Some use adoption as an heir or marriage as a live-in son-in-law as a pretext to seize their property; some entice them into borrowing and take their wealth; some fabricate accusations and compound their misfortunes. How are they to sustain their livelihoods? If we wish to give security to those already settled and provide care for those arriving, where indeed does the proper method lie? You gentlemen were born and raised in this region and must have something to say on the matter. Kindly explain it to me.

聖人論學而序其功也蓋為學有序也知所先
===
後其庶矣乎聖人之意豈不以學也者其序不
可紊而其功不可缺知此者斯善學矣故學莫
先於立志而人倫日用當行者道也道而志之
則尊所聞行所知趨向正而無他岐之惑矣學
尤貴於有守而道得於心者德也德而據焉則
守之貴行之利終始一而有日新之功矣以至
心德之全曰仁仁弗依非學也其必功夫益密
而無終食之違則成性存存何適而非天理之
流行歟若夫藝又至理所寓焉者藝弗游抑非
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

「志於道，據於德，依於仁，游於藝。」

龔卿

同考試官教諭韓批：「簡而文，是復古者。」

同考試官教諭黄批：「雋永自然，可以式矣。」

同考試官教授陳批：「發明孔子論學之㫖無餘。」

考試官行人徐批：「傳明。」

聖人論學而序其功也，蓋為學有序也。知所先後，其庶矣乎！聖人之意，豈不以學也者，其序不可紊，而其功不可缺？知此者，斯善學矣。故學莫先於立志，而人倫日用當行者，道也。道而志之，則尊所聞，行所知，趨向正而無他岐之惑矣。學尤貴於有守，而道得於心者，德也。德而據焉，則守之貴，行之利，終始一而有日新之功矣。以至心德之全曰仁，仁弗依，非學也。其必功夫益密，而無終食之違，則成性存存，何適而非天理之流行歟？若夫藝，又至理所寓焉者，藝弗游，抑非
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Set your resolve upon the Way, hold firmly to virtue, rely upon benevolence, and find recreation in the arts.”

Gong Qing

Associate Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: “Concise yet elegant: this is writing that restores the ancient style.”

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Rich in enduring meaning and natural in expression; it may serve as a model.”

Associate Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “It fully elucidates the purport of Confucius’s discussion of learning.”

Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “Clearly conveyed [?].”

When the Sage discussed learning, he set its efforts in order, for learning has a proper sequence. If one knows what comes first and what comes afterward, one is surely close to the goal! Was not the Sage’s meaning that, in learning, the sequence must not be confused and none of the requisite effort may be omitted? Those who understand this know how to learn well. Thus, nothing in learning precedes establishing one’s resolve. What ought to be practiced in human relationships and everyday life is the Way. If one sets one’s resolve upon the Way, one honors what one has heard and puts into practice what one knows; one’s direction is correct, and one is free from the confusion of divergent paths. Learning especially values steadfast adherence. The Way attained within the heart is virtue. If one holds firmly to virtue, one prizes maintaining it and practices it advantageously [?], remaining consistent from beginning to end and achieving daily renewal.

Furthermore, the completeness of the heart’s virtue is called benevolence. Learning that does not rely upon benevolence is no learning at all. One must make one’s efforts ever more exacting, never departing from benevolence even for the duration of a meal. Then, preserving continually one’s perfected nature, wherever one goes, how could there be anything other than the flowing operation of Heaven’s principle? As for the arts, these too are where ultimate principle resides. If one does not find recreation in the arts, this too is not…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
學也其必朝夕與游以博其義理之趣則以我
物物而心亦何所放哉該本末而不偏合內外
而無間下學之全功盡之矣抑學以求諸內者
也故聖人每教人以務本然何終取於游藝耶
盖不外物以求理而常玩物以養性雖聖賢亦
有不得而廢者故曰有始有卒者其惟聖人乎
噫周孔多藝夫豈無謂也哉
郊社之禮所以事上帝也宗廟之禮所以
祀乎其先也
===
丘柟
同考試官教諭陳批說出達孝意宜錄之為士
子式
考試官行人徐批達於禮者
聖人制祀禮享帝享親者也夫禮莫大於祭祀
聖人制禮皆以義起所以謂達孝也歟中庸十
九章引此明道之費者成周制禮有曰郊社曰
宗廟者以郊社言之冬至有事于圜丘夏至有
事于方澤是禮之所以者以天地大父母也大
punctuated:
學也。其必朝夕與游，以博其義理之趣，則以我物物，而心亦何所放哉？該本末而不偏，合內外而無間，下學之全功盡之矣。抑學以求諸內者也，故聖人每教人以務本。然何終取於游藝耶？盖不外物以求理，而常玩物以養性，雖聖賢亦有不得而廢者。故曰：「有始有卒者，其惟聖人乎！」噫！周孔多藝，夫豈無謂也哉！
郊社之禮，所以事上帝也；宗廟之禮，所以祀乎其先也。
丘柟
同考試官教諭陳批：說出達孝意，宜錄之為士子式。
考試官行人徐批：達於禮者。
聖人制祀禮，享帝享親者也。夫禮莫大於祭祀，聖人制禮，皆以義起，所以謂達孝也歟！中庸十九章引此明道之費者。成周制禮，有曰郊社、曰宗廟者。以郊社言之，冬至有事于圜丘，夏至有事于方澤。是禮之所以者，以天地大父母也。大
translation_en:
…learning either. One must surely engage in the arts morning and evening, broadening one’s appreciation of their moral principles. Then one governs things through oneself: how could the mind stray? Encompassing root and branches without partiality, uniting inner and outer without a gap—this fulfills the entire work of learning through everyday affairs. Yet learning seeks within oneself, and so the sages always taught people to attend to the root. Why, then, did they finally turn to taking one’s recreation in the arts? It is because one does not seek principle apart from things, but constantly contemplates things to nurture one’s nature. Even sages and worthies cannot dispense with this. Thus it is said: “Is it not only the sage who carries things through from beginning to end?” Ah! The Duke of Zhou and Confucius were accomplished in many arts. Surely this was not without purpose!

“The rites of the suburban and soil altars are those by which one serves the Lord on High; the rites of the ancestral temple are those by which one sacrifices to one’s forebears.”

Qiu Nan 丘柟

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “This brings out the meaning of extending filial piety. It should be included as a model for examination candidates.”

Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “One who understands ritual.”

The sage established sacrificial rites to offer worship to the Lord on High and to his parents. Among rites, none is greater than sacrifice. All the rites established by the sage arose from what was right. Is this not why it is called extending filial piety? Chapter nineteen of the Doctrine of the Mean cites this to illuminate the extensive operation of the Way. Among the rites established by the Zhou were those of the suburban and soil altars and those of the ancestral temple. As for the suburban and soil altars, sacrifices were performed at the Round Mound on the winter solstice and at the Square Pool on the summer solstice. The reason for these rites is that Heaven and Earth are the great father and mother. “Great …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
哉乾元萬物資始至哉坤元萬物資生惟大君
為之宗子其必齊祓一心達此精明之德對越
于上下者也故曰祀帝于郊敬之至也以宗廟
言之追始祖所自出而配以始祖舉四時之常
祭而享于群廟是禮之所以者以先王啟邦土
也誕膺天命以撫方夏佑啟後人咸正無缺惟
曾孫既巳大正其必有孚顒若將此觀盥之誠
仰承于祖考者也故曰宗廟之禮仁之至也合
而觀之尊尊親親周道備矣此武王周公其達
===
孝也歟抑夫子嘗曰周之文至矣使成周子孫
世而守之周至今猶存可也何至有韓宣子適
魯之嘆夫子老聃之問也信夫知其說者其如
視諸斯爾夫
使天下仕者皆欲立於王之朝耕者皆欲
耕於王之野商賈皆欲藏於王之市行
旅皆欲出於王之途
傅順
同考試官學正區 批 〔明王道者讀之灑然〕
punctuated:
哉乾元，萬物資始；至哉坤元，萬物資生！惟大君為之宗子，其必齊祓一心，達此精明之德，對越于上下者也。故曰：「祀帝于郊，敬之至也。」以宗廟言之，追始祖所自出而配以始祖，舉四時之常祭而享于群廟。是禮之所以者，以先王啟邦土也。誕膺天命，以撫方夏；佑啟後人，咸正無缺。惟曾孫既巳大正，其必有孚顒若，將此觀盥之誠，仰承于祖考者也。故曰：「宗廟之禮，仁之至也。」合而觀之，尊尊親親，周道備矣。此武王、周公其達孝也歟！抑夫子嘗曰：「周之文至矣！」使成周子孫世而守之，周至今猶存可也。何至有韓宣子適魯之嘆、夫子老聃之問也？信夫，知其說者，其如視諸斯爾夫！

使天下仕者皆欲立於王之朝，耕者皆欲耕於王之野，商賈皆欲藏於王之市，行旅皆欲出於王之途。

傅順

同考試官學正區批：〔明王道者讀之灑然〕
translation_en:
…great is the originating power of Qian: all things depend upon it for their beginning; consummate is the originating power of Kun: all things depend upon it for their birth! The great ruler alone serves as their principal heir. He must therefore purify himself and make his heart single, bringing this luminous virtue to full expression and reverently responding to those above and below. Thus it is said: “Sacrificing to the Lord on High at the suburban altar is the utmost expression of reverence.” As for the ancestral temples, one traces the source from which the founding ancestor sprang and associates that ancestor with it in sacrifice; one performs the regular sacrifices of the four seasons and presents offerings in the several ancestral temples. The reason for these rites is that the former kings opened up the realm. They received Heaven’s mandate in its fullness to bring peace to the lands of Xia; they aided and guided their descendants, setting everything right without omission. Once the descendant has fully established proper order, he must surely possess sincerity and a reverent bearing, offering the sincerity exemplified by the ritual handwashing in the hexagram Guan and reverently continuing the service of his ancestors. Thus it is said: “The rites of the ancestral temples are the utmost expression of benevolence.” Viewed together, honoring the honored and cherishing one’s kin made the Way of Zhou complete. Was this not the far-reaching filial piety of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou?

Yet the Master once said: “The cultural accomplishments of Zhou have reached their utmost!” Had the descendants of Zhou at its flourishing preserved them generation after generation, Zhou might well have survived to the present. How, then, would there have been occasion for Han Xuanzi’s sigh of admiration on visiting Lu, or for the Master’s inquiries of Lao Dan? Truly, one who understood the meaning of these rites would find it as clear as looking at this before him!

“Cause all those under Heaven who seek office to wish to stand at the king’s court, those who farm to wish to cultivate the king’s fields, merchants to wish to store their goods in the king’s markets, and travelers to wish to journey along the king’s roads.”

Fu Shun.

Comment by Associate Examiner Ou, School Instructor: 〔Those who understand the Kingly Way will find this refreshing to read.〕

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教授張批講仁力明白如此者絶少
考試官行人徐批簡古
大賢於齊君啓其見與於天下也夫仁天下莫
不與也齊君其知本哉孟子之意盖謂今王發
政施仁則推恩保民矣惻隱根於一心而趨向
鼓于天下豈但已耶使夫仕與耕者皆欲立于
王之朝焉耕于王之野焉或利用賓王而尚觀
光之志或舍彼穡事而思樂土之歸丕應傒志
固有不約而同者是孰使之然哉惟所欲之在
===
此耳商賈行旅皆欲藏于王之市焉出于王之
途焉或願聚貨於日中而交易得所或願問禁
於國門而即次懷資罔不是孚固有不召而至
者抑豈私於我哉惟民歸於德耳夫仁之感人
其速如此校之以力其難易當自辨之大抵唐
虞無力法三代無力兵豈其智之不桓文若哉
取舍定而功業隨焉否泰分矣噫聖人之情其
可見也夫
易
punctuated:
同考試官教授張批：講仁、力明白如此者絶少。
考試官行人徐批：簡古。
大賢於齊君啓其見與於天下也。夫仁，天下莫不與也，齊君其知本哉！孟子之意盖謂：今王發政施仁，則推恩保民矣。惻隱根於一心，而趨向鼓于天下，豈但已耶？使夫仕與耕者皆欲立于王之朝焉，耕于王之野焉，或利用賓王而尚觀光之志，或舍彼穡事而思樂土之歸，丕應傒志，固有不約而同者。是孰使之然哉？惟所欲之在此耳。商賈行旅皆欲藏于王之市焉，出于王之途焉，或願聚貨於日中而交易得所，或願問禁於國門而即次懷資，罔不是孚，固有不召而至者。抑豈私於我哉？惟民歸於德耳。夫仁之感人，其速如此，校之以力，其難易當自辨之。大抵唐虞無力法，三代無力兵，豈其智之不桓文若哉？取舍定而功業隨焉，否泰分矣。噫！聖人之情，其可見也夫！
易
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “Very few explain benevolence and force as clearly as this.”
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “Concise and antique in style.”
The great worthy enlightened the ruler of Qi about winning the support of all under Heaven. For none under Heaven fail to support benevolence. May the ruler of Qi understand this fundamental principle! Mencius’s meaning was that, if the king now issued policies and practiced benevolent government, he would thereby extend his kindness and protect the people. Compassion takes root in a single heart, yet stirs the inclinations of all under Heaven. How could its effects stop there?
Those who serve in office and those who farm would all wish to stand at the king’s court and cultivate the king’s fields. Some, finding it advantageous to be the king’s guests, would cherish the aspiration to behold the glory of his realm; others would leave their farming there and think of finding a home in this happy land. Responding in great numbers, their aspirations fulfilled [?], they would naturally agree without prior arrangement. Who makes them act thus? It is simply that what they desire is here.
Merchants and travelers would all wish to store their goods in the king’s markets and travel along the king’s roads. Some would wish to gather their goods at midday, finding a suitable place for exchange; others would wish to inquire about prohibitions at the gates of the realm and proceed to their lodgings with their resources. None would fail to place their trust in this, and naturally some would come without being summoned. Could this be mere partiality toward me? It is simply that the people turn toward virtue.
Such is the speed with which benevolence moves people. Compare it with force, and the relative difficulty or ease should become clear of itself. Generally speaking, in the ages of Tang and Yu there were no laws relying on force, and under the Three Dynasties there were no armies relying on force. Could their wisdom have fallen short of that of Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin? Once the choice of what to adopt and reject is settled, achievements follow accordingly, and adversity and prosperity take their separate courses. Ah! Here one may indeed perceive the sage’s true feelings!
Book of Changes

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
牝馬地類行地无疆柔順利貞君子攸行
胡鰲
同考試官教諭徐批說坤之利貞甚善
同考試官教授唐批善言坤德錄之
考試官行人徐批精𦂳
彖傳言坤之利貞徵諸物而歸于人也盖物有
得乎坤道之純者也而君子所行如之利貞於
是乎可見矣且坤德有四文王於利貞而以牝
馬為言者何也盖物各有類也馬雖乾象而形
===
乃坤道所成則為牝矣於稽其類其惟地乎類
各相從也馬雖動物而行乃下麗乎地則為順
矣致逺不禦何有疆乎凡同類者舉相似也以
牝馬觀之是知坤之為德相見者於此致役若
柔而无為也知始者於是代終惟順以承天也
然其遂乎物也賦形有定分各宜焉其成乎物
也實理具足靜而正焉順而且健如此君子法
之必有道矣分所當然即之以為安立不易其
方也義所當從順之以為利履不變其素也夫
punctuated:
牝馬地類，行地无疆，柔順利貞，君子攸行。
胡鰲
同考試官教諭徐批：說坤之利貞甚善。
同考試官教授唐批：善言坤德，錄之。
考試官行人徐批：精𦂳。
彖傳言坤之利貞，徵諸物而歸于人也。盖物有得乎坤道之純者也，而君子所行如之，利貞於是乎可見矣。且坤德有四，文王於利貞而以牝馬為言者何也？盖物各有類也，馬雖乾象，而形乃坤道所成，則為牝矣。於稽其類，其惟地乎？類各相從也，馬雖動物，而行乃下麗乎地，則為順矣。致逺不禦，何有疆乎？凡同類者，舉相似也。以牝馬觀之，是知坤之為德，相見者於此致役，若柔而无為也；知始者於是代終，惟順以承天也。然其遂乎物也，賦形有定，分各宜焉；其成乎物也，實理具足，靜而正焉。順而且健如此，君子法之，必有道矣。分所當然，即之以為安，立不易其方也；義所當從，順之以為利，履不變其素也。夫
translation_en:
“The mare belongs to the same kind as Earth; she travels over the earth without bound. Yielding and compliant, beneficial and steadfast: this is the course the gentleman follows.”
Hu Ao
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “An excellent explanation of Kun’s benefit and steadfastness.”
Associate Examiner Tang, Director of Studies, comments: “Discusses Kun’s virtue well. Include it.”
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “Refined and tightly composed.”
The Commentary on the Judgments explains Kun’s benefit and steadfastness by seeking evidence in things and applying it to human beings. Among things there are those that attain the purity of the Way of Kun; the gentleman follows their example in his conduct. Here benefit and steadfastness become apparent. Now Kun has four virtues: why did King Wen speak of a mare when discussing benefit and steadfastness? Things each have their own kind. Although the horse is an image of Qian, its bodily form is produced by the Way of Kun, and thus the mare is specified. When we examine its kind, is it not of the same kind as Earth? Each kind follows its own kind. Although the horse is a moving creature, in its movement it adheres to the earth beneath it, and thus it is compliant. It reaches far without hindrance: what bounds could there be? All things of the same kind resemble one another. Observing the mare, we thus understand Kun’s virtue: that which brings things into mutual visibility here brings them into service [?], as though yielding and acting without deliberate effort; for that which presides over beginnings, it here carries completion through in its stead, complying alone so as to follow Heaven.
Yet in bringing things to fulfillment, it endows them with determinate forms, each suited to its allotted place. In completing things, it possesses substantial principle in full, being still and correct. Since it is compliant yet vigorous in this way, there must be a way for the gentleman to model himself upon it. He finds repose in accepting what his allotted station requires, standing firm without changing his direction. He finds benefit in following what righteousness demands, conducting himself without changing his original integrity. Now …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
是之為安貞其斯免於過舉乎大抵天下之道
乾坤盡之坤之德常减於乾之半而能配乎乾
以是道也不順則倡始不健則无終是其健者
亦順之常耳此坤德所以為美而妻道臣道所
當知也苟處坤之位而昧其義難矣哉君子慎
之
天地之道貞觀者也日月之道貞明者也
天下之動貞夫一者也
熊鳳儀
===
同考試官教諭徐批能體貼經意
同考試官教授唐批觀於文可以知子之慎動矣
考試官行人徐批明暢
大傳論吉凶貞勝必即造化而推其理之一也
盖天下不一者動至一者理也大傳推諸造化
以明之欲人慎動也夫聖人之意盖曰辯吉凶
者存乎辭生吉凶者存乎動所以一乎動者理
而已且法象莫大乎天地也而其為道體之隱
者不可揜化之顯者無非教雖或時有愆違其
punctuated:
是之為安貞，其斯免於過舉乎？大抵天下之道，乾坤盡之。坤之德常减於乾之半，而能配乎乾，以是道也。不順則倡始，不健則无終，是其健者亦順之常耳。此坤德所以為美，而妻道臣道所當知也。苟處坤之位而昧其義，難矣哉！君子慎之。
天地之道，貞觀者也；日月之道，貞明者也；天下之動，貞夫一者也。
熊鳳儀
同考試官教諭徐批：能體貼經意。
同考試官教授唐批：觀於文，可以知子之慎動矣。
考試官行人徐批：明暢。

translation_en:
…This is what is meant by resting in constancy: might one thereby avoid errors in action? Broadly speaking, Qian and Kun encompass the Way of all under Heaven. Although Kun’s virtue is always less than Qian’s by half, it can nevertheless match Qian through this Way. Without obedience, it would take the initiative; without strength, it could not bring things to completion. Its strength, then, is simply the constant expression of its obedience. This is what makes Kun’s virtue admirable, and what those following the way of a wife or a minister ought to understand. To occupy Kun’s position yet remain ignorant of its meaning would indeed be perilous! The gentleman must be watchful in this.
“The Way of Heaven and Earth is displayed through constancy; the Way of the sun and moon shines through constancy; the movements of all under Heaven find constancy in the One.”
Xiong Fengyi

Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Professor: “From reading your composition, one can tell that you are cautious in your actions.”
Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “Clear and fluent.”
In discussing how good and ill fortune prevail through constancy, the Great Commentary necessarily turns to the processes of creation and transformation to infer the unity of their principle. For what is diverse in all under Heaven is movement; what is supremely unified is principle. The Great Commentary elucidates this by extending its inquiry to creation and transformation, wishing people to be cautious in their actions. The sage’s meaning is, in effect: distinguishing good and ill fortune lies in the statements; producing good and ill fortune lies in movement. What unifies movement is principle alone. Now, among models and images, none are greater than Heaven and Earth. title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
所正而常者觀而已矣懸象莫大於日月也而
其為道陰陽之精互藏其宅晝夜之運相推而
生雖或時有晦蝕其所正而常者明而已矣造
化不違乎貞如此而况於吉凶乎執是而推可
見天下之故性以物感而愛惡之相攻事以情
遷而得失之互見夫何常之有然途雖殊而歸
同慮雖百而致一順之而動則罔不吉所以致
吉者此理也逆之而動則罔不凶所以為凶者
亦此理也不曰貞夫一乎學者審於此焉可以
===
慎動矣雖然天下之事固有貞而凶不貞而吉
者何也此以事論也如其貞而不吉於道實競
吉孰甚焉不貞而不凶於道實疚凶孰甚焉故
君子不以吉凶在外者為虞而以貞於道為貴
書
無怠無荒四夷來王
傅順
同考試官學正區批可為儆戒者法
同考試官教授張批虞廷保治氣象如在目前
punctuated:
所正而常者，觀而已矣。懸象莫大於日月也，而其為道，陰陽之精互藏其宅，晝夜之運相推而生。雖或時有晦蝕，其所正而常者，明而已矣。造化不違乎貞如此，而况於吉凶乎？執是而推，可見天下之故。性以物感，而愛惡之相攻；事以情遷，而得失之互見。夫何常之有？然途雖殊而歸同，慮雖百而致一。順之而動，則罔不吉，所以致吉者，此理也；逆之而動，則罔不凶，所以為凶者，亦此理也。不曰貞夫一乎？學者審於此焉，可以慎動矣。雖然，天下之事固有貞而凶、不貞而吉者，何也？此以事論也。如其貞而不吉，於道實競，吉孰甚焉？不貞而不凶，於道實疚，凶孰甚焉？故君子不以吉凶在外者為虞，而以貞於道為貴。

書
無怠無荒，四夷來王。
傅順

同考試官學正區批：可為儆戒者法。
同考試官教授張批：虞廷保治氣象，如在目前。
translation_en:
…what remains correct and constant in them is simply their visible manifestation [?]. Among the images suspended in the heavens, none are greater than the sun and moon. In the Way they embody, the essences of yin and yang each lodge within the other's dwelling, and the cycles of day and night arise through their mutual succession. Although at times there is obscuration or eclipse, what remains correct and constant in them is simply their brightness. If the workings of creation thus never depart from constancy, how much more must this hold for good and ill fortune? Extending this principle, one can understand the affairs of the world. Human nature is stirred by things, and love and hatred contend; affairs change with circumstances, and gain and loss appear in turn. What constancy can there be? Yet although the paths differ, they reach the same destination; although deliberations are a hundredfold, they converge upon one thing. Act in accordance with it, and all is auspicious: what brings about good fortune is this principle. Act against it, and all is inauspicious: what brings about ill fortune is likewise this principle. Is this not what is meant by constancy in the one? If students examine this carefully, they can act with caution.

Nevertheless, among the world's affairs there are indeed instances of constancy accompanied by ill fortune, and of inconstancy accompanied by good fortune. Why is this? Such judgments concern events alone. If someone is constant yet encounters no good fortune, in relation to the Way he is truly strong [?]: what good fortune could be greater? If someone is inconstant yet encounters no ill fortune, in relation to the Way he is truly afflicted: what ill fortune could be greater? Thus the gentleman does not make external good or ill fortune his concern, but prizes constancy in the Way.

Book of Documents
“Be neither idle nor given to excess, and the barbarians of the four quarters will come to acknowledge your kingship.”
Fu Shun

Comment by Associate Examiner Ou, an Instructor: “This can serve as a model for those offering admonition.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, a Professor: “The atmosphere of preserving good government at the court of Yu [Shun] seems present before our very eyes.”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官行人徐批〔善警〕
勤內治而來遠人大臣警聖君然也盖內治聖
王所自盡者也遠人之來其有所感已夫伯益
警帝舜之意若謂人君守成業而致盛治者其
惟憂勤乎是故儆戒之道有所謂法度逸樂焉
用舍理欲焉帝其念哉曰弗慮胡獲兢兢然極
深以通天下之志曰弗為胡成業業然惟幾以
成天下之務說諸心研諸慮朝夕其戒懼也將
有為將有行內外其交脩也夫是之謂克艱夫
===
是之謂惠迪而治道益隆矣豈惟中國之服從
也哉彼四夷者昔在放勳之朝嘗率服矣今則
復通言語於重譯昔仰於變之休無猾夏矣庶
幾再格干羽于兩階盖重華協帝也而聲名洋
溢莫不尊親帝德光天也而道洽政治罔不咸
賴何有弗來王者耶治至于此無虞者可永保
矣夫自古聖人之於夷狄治之以不治而已彼
之來否何足為中國輕重而益乃揭諸儆戒哉
盖夷狄來而後自治有足徵者聖人志壹動氣
punctuated:
考試官行人徐批〔善警〕

勤內治而來遠人，大臣警聖君然也。盖內治，聖王所自盡者也；遠人之來，其有所感已。夫伯益警帝舜之意，若謂人君守成業而致盛治者，其惟憂勤乎！是故儆戒之道，有所謂法度逸樂焉，用舍理欲焉，帝其念哉！曰弗慮胡獲，兢兢然極深以通天下之志；曰弗為胡成，業業然惟幾以成天下之務。說諸心，研諸慮，朝夕其戒懼也；將有為，將有行，內外其交脩也。夫是之謂克艱，夫是之謂惠迪，而治道益隆矣。豈惟中國之服從也哉！彼四夷者，昔在放勳之朝嘗率服矣，今則復通言語於重譯；昔仰於變之休，無猾夏矣，庶幾再格干羽于兩階。盖重華協帝也，而聲名洋溢，莫不尊親；帝德光天也，而道洽政治，罔不咸賴。何有弗來王者耶？治至于此，無虞者可永保矣。夫自古聖人之於夷狄，治之以不治而已。彼之來否，何足為中國輕重，而益乃揭諸儆戒哉？盖夷狄來，而後自治有足徵者，聖人志壹動氣
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: 〔An effective admonition.〕

To attend diligently to internal government and thereby attract distant peoples: this is how a great minister admonishes a sage ruler. Internal government is where the sage king fully exerts himself; the coming of distant peoples must be a response to something that has moved them. The intent of Boyi’s admonition to Emperor Shun was as if to say: surely it is through anxious diligence that a ruler preserves the undertaking he has inherited and brings government to flourishing perfection! Thus, the way of admonition concerns standards and regulations, ease and pleasure, employment and dismissal, moral principle and desire. Let the emperor give these thought! “Without deliberation, how can there be attainment?” With reverent vigilance, he probes the utmost depths to comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven. “Without action, how can there be accomplishment?” With anxious care, he considers the first stirrings of events so as to accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven. Taking delight in these things in his heart and examining them in his thoughts, he remains watchful and apprehensive morning and evening. Whenever he is about to undertake something or put something into practice, he cultivates both his inner self and his outward conduct. This is what is meant by being equal to the difficulties; this is what is meant by following the right way. The way of government thereby becomes ever more exalted. Would the result be merely the submission of the Central Realm?

Those peoples of the four quarters had already submitted in the court of Fangxun, or Yao; now once again their speech is communicated through successive interpreters. Formerly, they admired the blessed transformation and did not disturb the Xia realm; now one may hope that they will once more be brought to submission by the shield-and-plume dance between the two stairways. For Chonghua, or Shun, matched the former emperor, and his fame spread everywhere: none failed to revere and cherish him. The emperor’s virtue illuminated Heaven, his Way permeated all, and his government was well ordered: none failed to benefit from it. How could any fail to come and acknowledge him as king? When government reaches this point, freedom from anxiety can be preserved forever.

Since antiquity, sages have governed the Yi and Di simply by leaving them ungoverned. Whether they come or not, how could this make the Central Realm more or less consequential? Why, then, did Yi make their coming a prominent part of his admonition? It is because only when the Yi and Di come is there sufficient evidence of the quality of one’s own government. The sage’s concentrated resolve moves the vital energies…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之功於是為大
所寶惟賢則邇人安
李相
同考試官學正區批句句是召公本意
同考試官教授張批融會處無滲漏可語經矣
考試官行人徐批知所寶
惟君一於貴德斯中國寧矣盖賢者中國所恃
以為安也然則君之所寶夫豈徒哉昔召公告
武王意若曰君天下有寶也而物不與焉王之
===
慎德亦惟嚴之好尚無玩人爾夫人有賢者不
珍奇而適於用不異產而瑞於時至矣其為寶
也王惟謹貞度於隆遇之時重耳目於明聽之
寄展親脩職是固有可嘉者則合同姓異姓而
頒德貺焉盡心盡力固亦有當重者乃隨君子
小人而無狎侮焉寶賢如此則志不妄發以害
有益之功諫則必行而有膏澤之益藩垣屏翰
外禦其侮彼蠻夷其弗猾夏矣乎親賢樂利各
得其所我中國其永康矣乎否則功弗成民弗
punctuated:
之功，於是為大。
所寶惟賢，則邇人安。
李相
同考試官學正區批：「句句是召公本意。」
同考試官教授張批：「融會處無滲漏，可語經矣。」
考試官行人徐批：「知所寶。」
惟君一於貴德，斯中國寧矣。盖賢者，中國所恃以為安也。然則君之所寶，夫豈徒哉！昔召公告武王，意若曰：「君天下有寶也，而物不與焉。王之慎德，亦惟嚴之好尚，無玩人爾。夫人有賢者，不珍奇而適於用，不異產而瑞於時，至矣其為寶也！王惟謹貞度於隆遇之時，重耳目於明聽之寄。展親脩職，是固有可嘉者，則合同姓異姓而頒德貺焉；盡心盡力，固亦有當重者，乃隨君子小人而無狎侮焉。寶賢如此，則志不妄發，以害有益之功；諫則必行，而有膏澤之益。藩垣屏翰，外禦其侮，彼蠻夷其弗猾夏矣乎！親賢樂利，各得其所，我中國其永康矣乎！否則功弗成，民弗
translation_en:
…the achievement is thereby made great.

“If those whom he treasures are only the worthy, then the people nearby will be at peace.”

Li Xiang

Associate Examiner Ou, School Instructor, comments: “Every sentence conveys the Duke of Shao’s original meaning.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The synthesis leaves nothing unaccounted for; this writer is fit to discuss the Classics.”
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “He knows what to treasure.”

Only when the ruler is single-minded in esteeming virtue will the Central States be at peace. For the worthy are those upon whom the Central States depend for their security. Can what the ruler treasures, then, be of little consequence? In former times, when the Duke of Shao admonished King Wu, his meaning was as follows: “One who rules all under Heaven has treasures, but material objects do not number among them. In attending carefully to virtue, Your Majesty need only exercise strict care over your preferences and refrain from treating people as playthings. Among men there are worthy persons: though neither precious nor rare, they are suited to service; though not exotic products, they are auspicious signs for their age. How supremely precious they are! Your Majesty should maintain upright standards when receiving them with great favor, and attach importance to those entrusted to serve as your eyes and ears so that you may hear clearly. Those who extend affection to their kin and discharge their duties certainly deserve commendation: therefore, bestow gracious gifts upon those of your own surname and those of other surnames alike. Those who devote their hearts and exert their strength likewise deserve respect: therefore, whether they are men of high or low station, treat none with familiarity that becomes contempt. If you treasure the worthy in this way, your purposes will not be recklessly pursued to the detriment of useful achievements; remonstrances will invariably be acted upon, bringing benefits like nourishing rain. Serving as walls and bulwarks, they will ward off insults from abroad. Will those foreign peoples then not cease to disturb the Chinese states? Cherishing the worthy and delighting in the benefits of good government, everyone will find their proper place. Will our Central States then not enjoy lasting peace? Otherwise, achievements will remain unrealized, and the people will not…”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
足豈但遠人不之格也是以明王慎之抑受獒
細故也而召公懇懇至此何耶盖持衡相勝而
剥復乗之憂危者所必爾也童牛弗牿堅氷晚
矣嗚呼相天下者其毋晚之哉而以蹈悔也
詩
王赫斯怒爰整其旅以按徂旅以篤于周
祜以對于天下
龔卿
同考試官教諭韓批興師之義模寫殆盡
同考試官教諭黃批雅義莊重
同考試官教授陳批聖人不得已之心溢於言表
考試官行人徐批温厚
聖人之行天討而所係者大焉夫王者之師為
天下國家舉也茲其所以為師之貞也歟此詩
言文王伐密之事盖謂維我文王其為德也出
乎天授其用武也奉乎天心是故密人不恭罪
人不可不得也於是乎神武形于獨斷而赫然
一怒焉大邦敢距天憲不容不章也於是乎明
punctuated:
足，豈但遠人不之格也？是以明王慎之。抑受獒，細故也，而召公懇懇至此，何耶？盖持衡相勝，而剥復乗之，憂危者所必爾也。童牛弗牿，堅氷晚矣。嗚呼！相天下者，其毋晚之哉，而以蹈悔也。

詩

王赫斯怒，爰整其旅，以按徂旅，以篤于周祜，以對于天下。

同考試官教諭黃批：雅義莊重。
同考試官教授陳批：聖人不得已之心，溢於言表。

聖人之行天討，而所係者大焉。夫王者之師，為天下國家舉也，茲其所以為師之貞也歟？此詩言文王伐密之事。盖謂維我文王，其為德也出乎天授，其用武也奉乎天心。是故密人不恭，罪人不可不得也，於是乎神武形于獨斷，而赫然一怒焉。大邦敢距，天憲不容不章也，於是乎明
translation_en:
…have enough. How could the consequence be merely that distant peoples failed to come in submission? Thus the enlightened king exercises caution in this matter. Yet accepting a mastiff was a small affair: why, then, was the Duke of Shao so earnest in his admonitions? Because opposing forces hang in the balance and contend for mastery, while decline and renewal follow upon them; one who fears danger must necessarily act thus. If the young bull is not fitted with a restraining bar, it will be too late when solid ice has formed. Alas! Let those who assist in governing the world not delay until it is too late and thereby incur regret.

Book of Odes

“The king blazed with anger; thereupon he ordered his troops, to check the advancing hosts, to strengthen Zhou’s blessings, and to answer the expectations of all under Heaven.”

Gong Qing

Comment by Associate Examiner Han, Instructor: “The meaning of raising an army is portrayed almost exhaustively.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The meaning of the ode is presented with dignity and gravity.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Professor: “The sage’s sense that he has no alternative is manifest beyond the words themselves.”
Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “Gentle and generous.”

When a sage carries out Heaven’s punitive justice, great matters depend upon it. The army of a true king is raised for the sake of all under Heaven and the state. Is this not what makes its undertaking upright? This ode speaks of King Wen’s campaign against Mi. Its meaning is that our King Wen received his virtue from Heaven and, in employing military force, acted in accordance with Heaven’s intent. Thus, because the people of Mi were disrespectful, the guilty had to be apprehended. His wondrous martial power therefore took form in his own decisive judgment, and he blazed forth in anger. A great state dared to resist, and Heaven’s law had to be made manifest. Thereupon his illustrious…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
威將於告勑而爰整三軍焉侵阮者遏之俾不
得虔劉我人民也徂共者止之俾無以憑陵我
疆宇也夫興師以禦外侮非曰一人之慶也盖
宗社之佑也彼斲之我敦之周邦根本如地斯
載矣何孔厚乎行罰而安乎民非曰一人之願
也盖天下之心也民望之王慰之上下交感如
響斯應矣豈缺望乎吁王者一有所舉而兩有
所係如此盖亦因可怒而怒之何甞有所畔援
歆羨也哉甚矣周人之善乎奉天也觀其述祖
===
德也而皆歸于天宅曰帝顧配曰天立對曰天
作心曰帝度至于伐罪則曰帝謂而其要在于求
民之莫而已八百年有道之長孰謂無所自哉
喤喤厥聲肅雝和鳴先祖是聽我客戾止
永觀厥成
陳京
同考試官教諭韓批周人音樂之盛此作盡之
同考試官教諭黃批形容作樂合祖意盡
同考試官教授陳批有始有感喤喤之聲者
punctuated:
威將於告勑，而爰整三軍焉。侵阮者遏之，俾不得虔劉我人民也；徂共者止之，俾無以憑陵我疆宇也。夫興師以禦外侮，非曰一人之慶也，盖宗社之佑也。彼斲之，我敦之，周邦根本如地斯載矣，何孔厚乎！行罰而安乎民，非曰一人之願也，盖天下之心也。民望之，王慰之，上下交感，如響斯應矣，豈缺望乎？吁！王者一有所舉，而兩有所係如此，盖亦因可怒而怒之，何甞有所畔援歆羨也哉！甚矣，周人之善乎奉天也！觀其述祖德也，而皆歸于天：宅曰帝顧，配曰天立，對曰天作，心曰帝度，至于伐罪則曰帝謂，而其要在于求民之莫而已。八百年有道之長，孰謂無所自哉！
喤喤厥聲，肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。我客戾止，永觀厥成。
陳京
同考試官教諭韓批：周人音樂之盛，此作盡之。
同考試官教諭黃批：形容作樂合祖，意盡。
同考試官教授陳批：有始有感喤喤之聲者。
translation_en:
…his authority was conveyed through proclamations and admonitions, and he thereupon marshaled the three armies. He checked those invading Ruan, so that they could not slaughter our people; he halted those advancing upon Gong, so that they had no means of overrunning our territory. To raise an army to repel outside aggression was not merely a blessing for one man: it was protection for the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain. What they hacked away at, we strengthened; the foundations of the Zhou realm bore their burden like the earth itself. How very solid they were! To administer punishment and bring peace to the people was not merely one man’s wish: it was the desire of all under Heaven. The people looked to their king, and he comforted them. Those above and below moved one another, responding as an echo answers a sound. How could their hopes have gone unfulfilled? Ah! Whenever a true king undertakes an action, these two concerns are thus bound up with it. His anger arose only from what deserved anger. When did he ever indulge in willfulness or covetous envy? How consummately the people of Zhou served Heaven! Observe how, in recounting their ancestors’ virtue, they attributed everything to Heaven: of their dwelling place, they said, “The Lord on High looked upon it”; of their consort, “Heaven established her”; of their counterpart, “Heaven made him”; of their heart, “The Lord on High measured it.” When it came to punishing the guilty, they said, “The Lord on High spoke.” Yet the essential purpose was simply to seek peace for the people. Who could say that their eight hundred years of enduring rule in accordance with the Way had no foundation?

“Resounding are their tones;
solemn and harmonious, they sound together.
The ancestors listen to them.
Our guest has arrived,
long to behold their accomplishment.”

Chen Jing.

Associate Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: “This composition fully conveys the splendor of Zhou music.”

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “It describes the performance of music to unite with the ancestors, expressing the meaning fully.”

Associate Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “There is a beginning, and there are those moved by the resounding tones [?].”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官行人徐批〔和平〕
周人合祖之樂其聲盛而其感同焉盖樂以感
神為盛也而且及其人之難感者焉周廟之樂
可知矣此始作樂而合乎祖之詩盖謂我周之
祀乎其先也大禮斯舉大樂備焉堂之上下嘒
嘒焉和聲動盪足以昭祖功也樂之大小喤喤
焉雅韻鏗鏘所以播宗德也雍而弗肅則失之
縱非和也樂其皦如也無有所紊焉肅而弗雍
則失之戾非和也樂其純如也無有所乖焉其
===
和鳴矣乎夫是樂也豈曰奏於明而無關于幽
也哉但見祖之既合也聲之神者有以通其氣
形響既隔宜乎其罔聞矣若有知焉而恍惚其
聽之盖享之者孝而歆之者自速也豈曰格于
親而或間于疎者哉但見我客之来也感其異
者亦以忘其情和奏既闋宜乎其或倦矣若始
作焉而終有以觀之盖可悅者深而可慨者自
失也吁樂足以格祖則其子孫可知足以感客
則其臣庶可知周之德其盛矣乎抑考之易曰
punctuated:
考試官行人徐批〔和平〕

周人合祖之樂，其聲盛而其感同焉。盖樂以感神為盛也，而且及其人之難感者焉，周廟之樂可知矣。此始作樂而合乎祖之詩，盖謂我周之祀乎其先也，大禮斯舉，大樂備焉。堂之上下，嘒嘒焉，和聲動盪，足以昭祖功也；樂之大小，喤喤焉，雅韻鏗鏘，所以播宗德也。雍而弗肅，則失之縱，非和也；樂其皦如也，無有所紊焉。肅而弗雍，則失之戾，非和也；樂其純如也，無有所乖焉。其和鳴矣乎！夫是樂也，豈曰奏於明而無關于幽也哉？但見祖之既合也，聲之神者有以通其氣。形響既隔，宜乎其罔聞矣；若有知焉，而恍惚其聽之。盖享之者孝，而歆之者自速也。豈曰格于親而或間于疎者哉？但見我客之来也，感其異者亦以忘其情。和奏既闋，宜乎其或倦矣；若始作焉，而終有以觀之。盖可悅者深，而可慨者自失也。吁！樂足以格祖，則其子孫可知；足以感客，則其臣庶可知。周之德，其盛矣乎！抑考之《易》曰：
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: 〔Balanced and harmonious.〕

The music with which the people of Zhou brought their ancestors together was magnificent in sound and alike in its power to move those who heard it. Music achieves its highest excellence in moving the spirits; when its influence extends even to people who are difficult to move, the excellence of the music in Zhou’s ancestral temple may be understood. This is a poem about beginning the music and bringing the ancestors together. It says, in effect: When we of Zhou sacrifice to our forebears, the great rites are performed and the full complement of grand music is provided. Above and below the hall, clear notes ring out; harmonious sounds swell and stir, sufficient to make manifest our ancestors’ achievements. From instruments great and small, resounding notes arise; elegant tones ring in concert, spreading abroad the virtue of our forebears. Concord without solemnity lapses into laxity and is no true harmony. The music is distinct in its parts, with nothing confused. Solemnity without concord lapses into harshness and is no true harmony. The music is unified, with nothing discordant. How harmoniously it sounds!

Could one say that this music is performed in the visible world but has no connection with the unseen? We see that, once the ancestors have been brought together, the numinous power of sound enables communication with their vital presence. Since their forms and voices are separated from us, one might suppose that they hear nothing. Yet it is as though they were aware, listening in their shadowy presence. For those who present the offerings are filial, and those who savor them come swiftly of themselves. Could one say that the music reaches close kin but encounters some barrier with those more distant? We see that, when our guest arrives, even one whose feelings are different is moved to forget those feelings. Once the harmonious performance has ended, one might suppose that he has grown weary. Yet it is as though the music had just begun, and he continues to observe it through to its conclusion. For the delight it affords is profound, and grounds for sorrow fade away of themselves.

Ah! If this music can reach the ancestors, its effect on their descendants may be understood; if it can move the guest, its effect on ministers and common people may be understood. How flourishing was the virtue of Zhou! Moreover, examining the Book of Changes, we find it says: …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
雷出地奮豫先王以作樂崇德殷薦上帝以配
祖考夫神非德不足以享此人非德不足以作
此故曰樂由人心生也心和氣和則陰陽和而
萬物得天地位矣況鬼神乎況人乎欲觀成周
之盛當於此求之
春秋
夏公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯伐鄭圍
新城僖公六年
周廷聘
===
同考試官教諭陳批齊桓心事發於此作
考試官行人徐批有斷制
觀伯兵討貳有制而有名也夫有制有名仁義
之兵也春秋得無美之者歟且經書公會齊侯
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯伐鄭圍新城抑何美之耶
盖齊自召陵之後威令幾于改物今合六國僅
討一鄭宜若振槁然圍而不舉者何吾以諒桓
之心矣討亂以平定安集為先不戢將自焚也
殖禮以兼弱攻昧為後志滿族乃離也以故兵
punctuated:
雷出地奮，豫。先王以作樂崇德，殷薦上帝，以配祖考。夫神非德不足以享此，人非德不足以作此。故曰：「樂由人心生也。」心和氣和，則陰陽和，而萬物得、天地位矣，況鬼神乎？況人乎？欲觀成周之盛，當於此求之。
春秋
夏，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。僖公六年。
周廷聘
同考試官教諭陳批：「齊桓心事發於此作。」
考試官行人徐批：「有斷制。」
觀伯兵討貳，有制而有名也。夫有制有名，仁義之兵也，春秋得無美之者歟？且經書「公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城」，抑何美之耶？盖齊自召陵之後，威令幾于改物。今合六國，僅討一鄭，宜若振槁，然圍而不舉者何？吾以諒桓之心矣。討亂以平定安集為先，不戢將自焚也；殖禮以兼弱攻昧為後，志滿族乃離也。以故兵
translation_en:
…Thunder emerges from the earth and stirs: this is Yu, Enthusiasm. The former kings accordingly made music to exalt virtue, offering it in abundance to the Lord on High and associating their ancestors with him in sacrifice. Without virtue, the spirits could not receive such offerings; without virtue, human beings could not make such music. Thus it is said: “Music arises from the human heart.” When the heart and vital energies are harmonious, yin and yang are harmonious, the myriad things attain their proper condition, and Heaven and Earth take their proper places. How much more, then, must this hold for ghosts and spirits, and for human beings! Whoever wishes to understand the flourishing of Zhou should seek it here.
Spring and Autumn Annals
“In summer, the duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao to attack Zheng. They besieged Xincheng.” Sixth year of Duke Xi.
Zhou Tingpin
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The intentions of Duke Huan of Qi are brought to light in this composition.”
Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “It displays decisive judgment.”
Observe how the hegemon’s army punished disloyalty: it exercised restraint and had a legitimate cause. An army possessing restraint and a legitimate cause is an army of benevolence and righteousness. Could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to commend it? Yet when the Classic records, “The duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao to attack Zheng. They besieged Xincheng,” what precisely does it commend?
After the meeting at Shaoling, Qi’s authority and commands had nearly transformed the established order. Now, with six states united against Zheng alone, the task should have been as easy as shaking a withered tree. Why, then, did they besiege the city without taking it? From this I understand Duke Huan’s intentions. In suppressing disorder, he gave priority to pacification, stability, and bringing the people together in security: arms left unchecked would consume their wielder in flames. In fostering ritual propriety, he gave secondary place to annexing the weak and attacking the benighted: once ambition becomes self-satisfied, one’s own kind become estranged. For this reason, the army…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
猶遲巡于新城以用兵之法攻心者為尚使鄭
尚有不寧方來之想桓之心斯已矣又況齊自
首止以來信義被于諸侯今合中國獨遺一鄭
似未渙羣乃伐而復圍者何吾以諒桓之職矣
諸夏親暱不可棄也失同人之義者王法不赦
周室大義所當尊也為下喬之行者連帥必懲
以故師直進止于新城正以九伐之法負固則
侵之使鄭蚤有悔過自新之善桓之職斯已矣
故經直書伐鄭圍新城伐者聲罪之謂也圍者
===
寓遺力之意也可槩見矣雖然王者之兵不試
齊桓之節制終不若湯武之仁義也而況久假
不歸者乎然經所以直予者盖首止葵丘二百
四十餘年不二見也此亦小康之治也歟
丁亥楚子入陳〔宣公十有一年〕
丘枏
同考試官教諭陳批〔善恕楚子〕
考試官行人徐批〔謹嚴〕
春秋於外兵討罪不以利掩義不以過棄功夫
banxin: 湖廣鄉試錄 三十一
punctuated:
猶遲巡于新城，以用兵之法，攻心者為尚，使鄭尚有不寧方來之想，桓之心斯已矣。又況齊自首止以來，信義被于諸侯，今合中國，獨遺一鄭，似未渙羣，乃伐而復圍者何？吾以諒桓之職矣。諸夏親暱，不可棄也；失同人之義者，王法不赦。周室，大義所當尊也；為下喬之行者，連帥必懲。以故師直進止于新城，正以九伐之法，負固則侵之，使鄭蚤有悔過自新之善，桓之職斯已矣。故經直書伐鄭圍新城，伐者聲罪之謂也，圍者寓遺力之意也，可槩見矣。雖然，王者之兵不試，齊桓之節制終不若湯武之仁義也，而況久假不歸者乎？然經所以直予者，盖首止、葵丘，二百四十餘年不二見也。此亦小康之治也歟！
丁亥，楚子入陳。〔宣公十有一年〕
丘枏
同考試官教諭陳批〔善恕楚子〕
考試官行人徐批〔謹嚴〕
春秋於外兵討罪，不以利掩義，不以過棄功。夫
translation_en:
…the troops still lingered [?] at Xincheng. In the methods of warfare, winning hearts is paramount: if Zheng could still entertain the thought of coming over because it was unsettled, Duke Huan’s purpose would be fulfilled. Moreover, since the meeting at Shouzhi, Qi’s trustworthiness and righteousness had extended throughout the feudal lords. Now it had united the central states, leaving out only Zheng, seemingly not yet having dispersed its faction [?]. Why, then, did it attack and subsequently lay siege? Here I understand Duke Huan’s duty. The states of the Xia were close kin and could not be abandoned; royal law would not pardon anyone who violated the principle of fellowship. The house of Zhou was to be honored as a matter of supreme righteousness; the chief of the allied lords must punish anyone who acted like one descending from a lofty tree.
