Thus the army advanced in a just cause and halted at Xincheng, precisely in accordance with the rule among the nine punitive campaigns that those who relied on their strongholds should be invaded. If Zheng could promptly repent its faults and reform itself, Duke Huan’s duty would be fulfilled. Hence the Classic simply records, “attacked Zheng and besieged Xincheng.” “Attacked” means publicly declaring its offenses; “besieged” conveys the intention of holding strength in reserve. The general meaning is thus apparent.
Nevertheless, the army of a true king need never be put to the test. Duke Huan of Qi’s disciplined command ultimately fell short of the benevolence and righteousness of Tang and Wu—how much more so when he merely borrowed them for so long without returning them! Yet the Classic gives him unqualified approval because the meetings at Shouzhi and Kuiqiu had no counterparts in its more than 240 years. Was this not also government that achieved a measure of peace and order?
“On the dinghai day, the Viscount of Chu entered Chen.” 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xuan.〕
Qiu Nan 丘枏
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, an Instructor: 〔Skillfully treats the Viscount of Chu with forbearance.〕
Comment by Examiner Xu, a Messenger: 〔Careful and rigorous.〕
When the Spring and Autumn Annals treats the punishment of wrongdoing by armies from outside the central states, it does not allow self-interest to obscure righteousness, nor does it discard achievements on account of faults. Indeed, …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
正倫經世大典也觀春秋書丁亥楚子入陳有
以哉夫楚莊入陳也討其賊為義取其國為貪
義利之分明矣經先書殺後書入者何盖君子
用人之仁去其貪也楚雖有取陳之惡終不可
沒其正陳之善事起于正陳之善其流則為取
陳之惡是則事有義利交集者而義所當重也
於此使不權先後之書以原其情焉非用人之
仁去其貪之意也奚可哉夫楚莊入陳也雖得
為討罪之舉亦肆彼滅國之暴功過之分審矣
===
經不書取陳而猶書入者何盖君子以義度人
則難為人也縣陳之虐固難儕以存亡興滅之
師栗門之轘實則異夫伐莒攢函之為是則事
有功過相準者而功不可沒也於此使不權輕
重之宜以末減焉是以義度人則難為人之意
也奚可哉然則春秋以恕待人而不求備其在
此也歟雖然道大如天見在乎人聖人之制行
也不制以已曲暢旁通可以入道者皆經世所
不棄也信夫曾子曰夫子之道忠恕而已矣
punctuated: 正倫經世大典也。觀《春秋》書「丁亥，楚子入陳」，有以哉！夫楚莊入陳也，討其賊為義，取其國為貪，義利之分明矣。經先書殺，後書入者，何？盖君子用人之仁，去其貪也。楚雖有取陳之惡，終不可沒其正陳之善。事起于正陳之善，其流則為取陳之惡，是則事有義利交集者，而義所當重也。於此使不權先後之書以原其情焉，非用人之仁、去其貪之意也，奚可哉！夫楚莊入陳也，雖得為討罪之舉，亦肆彼滅國之暴，功過之分審矣。經不書取陳，而猶書入者，何？盖君子以義度人，則難為人也。縣陳之虐，固難儕以存亡興滅之師；栗門之轘，實則異夫伐莒攢函之為。是則事有功過相準者，而功不可沒也。於此使不權輕重之宜以末減焉，是以義度人則難為人之意也，奚可哉！然則《春秋》以恕待人而不求備，其在此也歟！雖然，道大如天，見在乎人。聖人之制行也，不制以已，曲暢旁通，可以入道者，皆經世所不棄也。信夫！曾子曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」
translation_en:
…a great canon for rectifying human relationships and ordering the world. Consider the Spring and Autumn Annals’ entry, “On dinghai, the Viscount of Chu entered Chen”: surely there is a reason for its wording! When King Zhuang of Chu entered Chen, punishing its traitor was righteous, but seizing its territory was grasping. The distinction between righteousness and self-interest is clear. Why does the Classic first record the killing and afterward the entry? Because the gentleman makes use of the benevolence in others and rejects their greed. Although Chu committed the wrong of seizing Chen, its good deed in setting Chen right must never be obscured. The undertaking began with the good of setting Chen right, but developed into the evil of seizing it. Thus righteousness and self-interest may converge in a single undertaking, yet righteousness deserves greater weight. If we failed here to weigh the sequence of the entries in order to discern his underlying intentions, we would miss the purpose of making use of another’s benevolence and rejecting his greed. How could that be acceptable?

When King Zhuang of Chu entered Chen, although his action could count as an expedition to punish wrongdoing, he also unleashed the violence of extinguishing a state. The distinction between merit and fault is evident. Why does the Classic not record that he “seized Chen,” but still say that he “entered” it? Because, if the gentleman measures others by righteousness, it becomes difficult for anyone to meet the standard. The cruelty of making Chen a county certainly cannot rank alongside military campaigns that preserve endangered states and restore extinguished ones. Yet the execution by dismemberment at the Li Gate was indeed different from the actions involved in attacking Ju and Zanhan [?]. Thus there are undertakings in which merit and fault counterbalance one another, and the merit must not be obscured. If we failed here to weigh their relative gravity appropriately and grant some mitigation, this would amount to measuring others by righteousness so strictly that they could scarcely meet the standard. How could that be acceptable? Is this, then, not an instance of the Spring and Autumn Annals treating others with sympathetic understanding rather than demanding perfection?

Nevertheless, the Way is as vast as Heaven; its manifestation depends upon human beings. When the sage sets standards for conduct, he does not make himself the sole measure [?]. He develops their implications in every particular and extends their application in every direction: whatever can lead people into the Way is not discarded in ordering the world. How true it is! Master Zeng said, “The Master’s Way consists simply of doing one’s utmost for others and sympathetic understanding.”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
禮記
天子祭天下名山大川五嶽視三公四瀆
視諸侯
蔡完
同考試官學正劉批望祀儀節甚明深於禮者
考試官行人徐批不浮
王者祭地之望而所秩有定分焉夫山川者地
之望也秩而祭之斯所以嚴其分也歟王者之
制分以禮而定禮以稱為善天子者天下之主
===
也有天下者祭百神地示之下非山川邪盖祭
以禮神能成其變化者皆曰神而當禮祭以報
功能資其財用者皆曰有功而當報是非夫山
而皆祭也天下之名山乃其宗矣祭之者於吾
身有所統也亦非百川而皆祭也天下之大川
乃其會矣祭之者於吾身有攸主也天子之望
徧于天下如此禮豈混而無別者哉山之至高
者為嶽五嶽其名山也望秩之禮則視三公焉
川之獨達者為瀆四瀆其大川也望秩之儀則
punctuated:
禮記

天子祭天下名山大川，五嶽視三公，四瀆視諸侯。

蔡完

同考試官學正劉批：望祀儀節甚明，深於禮者。
考試官行人徐批：不浮。

王者祭地之望，而所秩有定分焉。夫山川者，地之望也。秩而祭之，斯所以嚴其分也歟！王者之制分以禮，而定禮以稱為善。天子者，天下之主也。有天下者祭百神，地示之下，非山川邪？盖祭以禮神，能成其變化者，皆曰神而當禮；祭以報功，能資其財用者，皆曰有功而當報。是非夫山而皆祭也，天下之名山乃其宗矣。祭之者，於吾身有所統也。亦非百川而皆祭也，天下之大川乃其會矣。祭之者，於吾身有攸主也。天子之望徧于天下如此，禮豈混而無別者哉！山之至高者為嶽，五嶽其名山也，望秩之禮則視三公焉。川之獨達者為瀆，四瀆其大川也，望秩之儀則
translation_en:
Record of Rites

“The Son of Heaven sacrifices to the renowned mountains and great rivers of all under Heaven. The Five Sacred Peaks are treated as equivalent to the Three Dukes, and the Four Watercourses as equivalent to the regional lords.”

Cai Wan

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “The ceremonial procedures for sacrifices from afar are explained very clearly. Here is someone deeply versed in ritual.”
Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “Not superficial.”

The king sacrifices to the eminent features of the earth, and the ranks assigned to them have fixed distinctions. Mountains and rivers are the eminent features of the earth. To rank them and offer sacrifices accordingly—is this not how their distinctions are strictly maintained? The king establishes distinctions through ritual, and in determining ritual, appropriateness is the measure of excellence. The Son of Heaven is the lord of all under Heaven. He who possesses all under Heaven sacrifices to the hundred spirits; among the earthly spirits, are there not those of mountains and rivers?

Sacrifice serves to honor spirits: all that can accomplish their transformations are called spirits and deserve honor. Sacrifice serves to recompense meritorious service: all that can provide material resources are deemed meritorious and deserve recompense. Thus, it is not every mountain that receives sacrifice; the renowned mountains of all under Heaven are their foremost representatives. In sacrificing to them, I exercise authority over what falls within my rule. Nor does every river receive sacrifice; the great rivers of all under Heaven are where the waters converge. In sacrificing to them, I exercise my lordship over them. The Son of Heaven’s sacrifices from afar thus extend throughout all under Heaven. How could their rites be indiscriminately alike, without distinctions?

The loftiest mountains are called sacred peaks. The Five Sacred Peaks are the renowned mountains, and the ranked rites of sacrifice from afar accord them treatment equivalent to that of the Three Dukes. Rivers that reach the sea independently are called watercourses. The Four Watercourses are the great rivers, and the ranked ceremonial procedures for sacrifice from afar accordingly…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
視諸侯焉服用毳冕從其類矣然獻而貍之者
乃公之桓圭牢數則九也豆數十六也其在嶽
者猶其在三公歟籍用席蒲取其象矣獻而沈
之者乃侯之信圭牢數則七也豆數十二也其
在川者猶其在諸侯歟吁先王制禮其為天下
之防也至矣雖然人存而政舉禮廢而防決不
務民義而徼福于鬼神斯有僭旅而崇川者矣
盖制不存而分不明故也有志於天下者惟辨
上下而定民志
===
地氣上齊天氣下降陰陽相摩天地相蕩
鼓之以雷霆奮之以風雨動之以四時
煖之以日月而百化興焉如此則樂者
天地之和也
丘柟
同考試官學正劉批樂法天地之和子又能法作樂之和矣
考試官行人徐批雅淡
記樂者推造化之功而著其為效法之本焉盖
天地有自然之樂也聖人法之樂斯作矣夫樂
punctuated:
視諸侯焉。服用毳冕，從其類矣。然獻而貍之者，乃公之桓圭；牢數則九也，豆數十六也。其在嶽者，猶其在三公歟？籍用席蒲，取其象矣。獻而沈之者，乃侯之信圭；牢數則七也，豆數十二也。其在川者，猶其在諸侯歟？吁！先王制禮，其為天下之防也至矣！雖然，人存而政舉，禮廢而防決。不務民義而徼福于鬼神，斯有僭旅而崇川者矣。盖制不存而分不明故也。有志於天下者，惟辨上下而定民志。

地氣上齊，天氣下降，陰陽相摩，天地相蕩，鼓之以雷霆，奮之以風雨，動之以四時，煖之以日月，而百化興焉。如此，則樂者天地之和也。
丘柟
同考試官學正劉批：樂法天地之和，子又能法作樂之和矣。
考試官行人徐批：雅淡。

記樂者推造化之功，而著其為效法之本焉。盖天地有自然之樂也，聖人法之，樂斯作矣。夫樂
translation_en:
…are accorded the rank of the feudal lords. The ritual dress is the down-embroidered robe and its ceremonial cap, following the corresponding category. Yet what is presented and then buried is the duke’s huan jade tablet; the number of sets of sacrificial animals is nine, and the number of offering stands is sixteen. Is the treatment of the Sacred Peaks not like that of the Three Dukes? Cattail mats are used beneath the offerings, adopting their symbolism. What is presented and then sunk is the marquis’s xin jade tablet; the number of sets of sacrificial animals is seven, and the number of offering stands is twelve. Is the treatment of the rivers not like that of the feudal lords? Ah! The former kings’ institution of ritual provided the most complete safeguards for all under Heaven! Nevertheless, when the right people are present, government is carried out; when ritual is abandoned, the safeguards give way. If people do not attend to their proper duties but seek blessings from ghosts and spirits, there will be those who presumptuously perform mountain sacrifices and exalt rivers. This is because the institutions no longer survive and distinctions of rank are unclear. Those who aspire to govern all under Heaven must distinguish higher from lower and thereby settle the people’s purposes.

“The earth’s vital force rises; Heaven’s vital force descends. Yin and yang interact; Heaven and earth stir one another. They rouse things with thunder and thunderclaps, stir them with wind and rain, move them through the four seasons, and warm them with the sun and moon; thus the myriad transformations arise. Accordingly, music is the harmony of Heaven and earth.”
Qiu Nan 丘柟
Associate Examiner Liu, School Instructor, comments: “Music takes the harmony of Heaven and earth as its model; you, in turn, can take as your model the harmony involved in creating music.”
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “Elegant and restrained.”

The writer of the Record of Music traces the workings of creation and transformation, making clear that they constitute the foundation to be emulated. For Heaven and earth possess a music that arises naturally; the sages take it as their model, and music is thereby created. Now, music…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
也者人心之動也何假於外哉然所本則在乎
天地爾彼地位乎下也承天而行氣則上齊矣
天位乎上也有隕自天氣則下降矣動而陽靜
而陰相摩之不已焉乾以君坤以藏相盪之不
息焉陰閉而陽之在內者不能出則摶而為雷
矣相激而甚乃霆之大者也陰凝而陽之在外
者不能入則旋而為風矣相畜而解乃雨之潤
者也一寒一暑之互推四時之序有以動之也
或晝或夜之迭見日月之烜有以煖之也由是
===
天地絪縕合同而化萬物其有不醇者乎樂之
見於天地者如此聖人作樂蓋有取焉吾知樂
之興也生於感物變以成方以宣吾和也而生
氣之和亦以之而合矣以達吾順也而順氣之
應亦於是而肇矣清明者天也廣大者地也雷
霆非有聲者乎終始者四時也周還者風雨也
日月非有光者乎樂為天地之和者如此聖人
作樂豈無本歟大抵禮樂固皆不可去身也然
禮序而樂和禮先而樂後知和而不以禮節之
punctuated:
也者，人心之動也，何假於外哉？然所本則在乎天地爾。彼地位乎下也，承天而行氣，則上齊矣；天位乎上也，有隕自天，氣則下降矣。動而陽，靜而陰，相摩之不已焉；乾以君，坤以藏，相盪之不息焉。陰閉而陽之在內者不能出，則摶而為雷矣；相激而甚，乃霆之大者也。陰凝而陽之在外者不能入，則旋而為風矣；相畜而解，乃雨之潤者也。一寒一暑之互推，四時之序有以動之也；或晝或夜之迭見，日月之烜有以煖之也。由是天地絪縕，合同而化，萬物其有不醇者乎？樂之見於天地者如此，聖人作樂蓋有取焉。
吾知樂之興也，生於感物，變以成方。以宣吾和也，而生氣之和亦以之而合矣；以達吾順也，而順氣之應亦於是而肇矣。清明者天也，廣大者地也，雷霆非有聲者乎？終始者四時也，周還者風雨也，日月非有光者乎？樂為天地之和者如此，聖人作樂豈無本歟？大抵禮樂固皆不可去身也，然禮序而樂和，禮先而樂後。知和而不以禮節之，
translation_en:
…is the stirring of the human heart; what need has it to borrow from outside? Yet its foundation lies in Heaven and Earth. Earth occupies the position below: receiving Heaven’s influence and circulating vital energy, it reaches upward. Heaven occupies the position above: things fall from Heaven, and its vital energy descends. In movement there is yang, and in stillness yin; they rub against one another without cease. Qian governs and Kun stores; they stir one another without rest. When yin closes in and the yang within cannot emerge, it gathers into thunder; when their mutual clash grows intense, it becomes the mighty thunderclap. When yin congeals and the yang outside cannot enter, it swirls into wind; when their accumulated forces are released, there is the moistening of rain. Cold and heat impel one another in alternation: the ordered succession of the four seasons sets things in motion. Day and night appear in turn: the radiance of sun and moon warms them. Thus Heaven and Earth intermingle, joining together to bring about transformation. Could any of the myriad things fail to attain their full vitality? Such is music as manifested in Heaven and Earth; surely the sages drew upon it in creating music.
I understand that the arising of music originates in being moved by things, and that its variations form ordered patterns. It gives expression to our harmony, and through it the harmony of life-giving energy likewise comes into accord. It communicates our accord, and thereby the response of harmonious vital energy also begins. What is clear and bright is Heaven; what is broad and great is Earth. Do thunder and thunderclaps not possess sound? What end and begin anew are the four seasons; what circulate and return are wind and rain. Do sun and moon not possess light? Such is music as the harmony of Heaven and Earth. Could the sages’ creation of music have been without a foundation? In general, ritual and music must both remain inseparable from one’s person. Yet ritual establishes order, while music brings harmony; ritual comes first, and music follows. To know harmony but fail to regulate it through ritual…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
亦不可行矣是禮尤成始而成終者也有志于
樂者宜以禮為質
第貳塲
論
孔子聞而知之
傅順
同考試官學正區批孔子聞道之妙此作悉之
同考試官教授張批善言道統者
考試官行人徐批知孔子者
===
論曰天下有至悟焉惟聖人神之夫道天之秘
也而命之聖人聖人者不數出於是乎有至悟
焉故因而啓者達諸天也有所據而覺者明諸
人也因而非因據而非據而悟焉者聖人之神
也神也者不以其時之久而弗值不以其幾之
寂而弗章天以時啓之動其幾使自覺之聖人
之心洞然協天人一古今而道弗藏其秘矣此
孔子之聞知所謂至悟而神者也夫繼善成性
天道寤矣五百餘年而聖人生焉氣之寤也於
punctuated:
亦不可行矣。是禮尤成始而成終者也。有志于樂者，宜以禮為質。

第貳塲

論

孔子聞而知之

傅順

同考試官學正區批：孔子聞道之妙，此作悉之。

同考試官教授張批：善言道統者。

考試官行人徐批：知孔子者。

論曰：天下有至悟焉，惟聖人神之。夫道，天之秘也，而命之聖人。聖人者不數出，於是乎有至悟焉。故因而啓者，達諸天也；有所據而覺者，明諸人也；因而非因，據而非據，而悟焉者，聖人之神也。神也者，不以其時之久而弗值，不以其幾之寂而弗章。天以時啓之，動其幾，使自覺之。聖人之心洞然，協天人，一古今，而道弗藏其秘矣。此孔子之聞知，所謂至悟而神者也。夫繼善成性，天道寤矣；五百餘年而聖人生焉，氣之寤也。於
translation_en:
… it likewise cannot be put into practice. Thus ritual, above all, brings both the beginning and the completion to fulfillment. Those devoted to music should take ritual as its substance.

Second Session

Discourse

“Confucius Knew It through Hearing”

Fu Shun

Comment by Associate Examiner Ou, Instructor: “This composition fully explains the subtlety of Confucius’s hearing the Way.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Professor: “One who speaks well of the transmission of the Way.”

Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “One who understands Confucius.”

The discourse reads: There is an utmost awakening in the world; only the sage gives it spiritual efficacy. The Way is Heaven’s secret, entrusted to the sage. Sages do not appear frequently; hence there is this utmost awakening. Those who are enlightened through what they encounter attain understanding through Heaven; those who awaken with something to rely upon attain illumination through other people. But to awaken through something yet without depending upon it, to have a basis yet without relying upon it—this is the sage’s spiritual power. Such spiritual power does not fail to encounter the Way because of the long interval of time, nor fail to manifest it because its incipient workings are silent. Heaven enlightens the sage at the proper time, stirs those incipient workings, and enables him to awaken for himself. The sage’s mind becomes utterly clear, harmonizing Heaven and humanity and uniting past and present; the Way then no longer conceals its secret. This is Confucius’s knowing through hearing: what is called utmost awakening endowed with spiritual efficacy.

What continues the Way is goodness, and what brings it to completion is human nature: this is the awakening of Heaven’s Way. After more than five hundred years, a sage is born: this is the awakening of vital energy. At …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
是以其造化之渾然者寄之聖人則亦天之心
大寤也故堯舜達諸天湯達諸堯舜文王達諸
湯而禹皐伊萊吕散明諸堯舜湯文此至悟之
神傳道者有不傳之傳也噫不傳之傳孔子其
神乎盖超古今而無滯者神也歷萬世而無弊
者道也曠數十世而相感者氣也越數百年之
口耳而相孚者心也是故有時焉以俟乎人時
弗至人弗值也有幾焉以觸其蘊幾弗融蘊弗
彰也孔子知悟于聞聞神於悟爾已不然則前
===
之授迥其響後之受不順于聰孰從授之孰從
得之哉其所以得之者亦天以道久斯晦晦弗
傳故凝其會以開聖人之時通其寂以闡聞知
之幾而聖人於道孚之於心感之於氣神而明
之於詩聞緝熈之敬純一之誠焉於書聞懿恭
之德敬忌之心焉於易聞六十四卦之蘊焉於
禮樂而忠信和順之本聞焉於經制而榮辱予
奪之權衡聞焉則孔子之聞有至悟也至悟斯
有知故有擇善固執之訓有克己復禮之教有
banxin: 鄉試錄 五十 趙金
punctuated: 是，以其造化之渾然者寄之聖人，則亦天之心大寤也。故堯舜達諸天，湯達諸堯舜，文王達諸湯，而禹皐伊萊吕散明諸堯舜湯文。此至悟之神，傳道者有不傳之傳也。噫！不傳之傳，孔子其神乎！盖超古今而無滯者，神也；歷萬世而無弊者，道也；曠數十世而相感者，氣也；越數百年之口耳而相孚者，心也。是故有時焉以俟乎人，時弗至，人弗值也；有幾焉以觸其蘊，幾弗融，蘊弗彰也。孔子知悟于聞，聞神於悟爾已。不然，則前之授迥其響，後之受不順于聰，孰從授之？孰從得之哉？其所以得之者，亦天以道久斯晦，晦弗傳，故凝其會以開聖人之時，通其寂以闡聞知之幾，而聖人於道孚之於心，感之於氣，神而明之。於《詩》聞緝熈之敬、純一之誠焉；於《書》聞懿恭之德、敬忌之心焉；於《易》聞六十四卦之蘊焉；於禮樂而忠信和順之本聞焉；於經制而榮辱予奪之權衡聞焉。則孔子之聞有至悟也。至悟斯有知，故有擇善固執之訓，有克己復禮之教，有
translation_en:
…thus, when Heaven entrusts the undivided wholeness of its creative transformations to the sage, this too is a great awakening of Heaven’s heart. Hence Yao and Shun attained understanding through Heaven; Tang attained it through Yao and Shun; King Wen attained it through Tang; and Yu, Gao, Yi, Lai [?], Lü, and San gained illumination through Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wen. Such is the spiritual efficacy of consummate awakening: those who transmit the Way possess a transmission that occurs without transmission. Ah! In this transmission without transmission, how spiritually wondrous was Confucius! What transcends past and present without impediment is spiritual efficacy; what endures through myriad generations without deterioration is the Way; what brings mutual resonance across dozens of generations is vital force, qi; what establishes mutual accord across several hundred years of oral and aural transmission is the heart. Thus there is a time that awaits the right person: unless that time arrives, the person does not encounter it. There is an incipient impulse that stirs what lies within: unless that impulse becomes unobstructed, what lies within does not become manifest. Confucius’s understanding awakened through hearing, and his hearing became spiritually efficacious through awakening—that is all. Otherwise, if the echoes of earlier instruction were remote [?], and later reception did not reach a receptive ear, from whom could one transmit it, and from whom could one obtain it?

His means of obtaining it likewise lay in Heaven: because the Way becomes obscure over time, and in obscurity ceases to be transmitted, Heaven concentrated the convergence of circumstances to open the sage’s appointed time, and penetrated the stillness to disclose the incipient impulse toward knowledge through hearing. The sage, in turn, accorded with the Way in his heart, resonated with it in his vital force, and understood it through spiritual efficacy. In the Book of Odes he heard reverence cultivated toward ever greater illumination and sincerity that was pure and undivided. In the Book of Documents he heard the virtue of admirable respectfulness and the disposition of reverence and caution. In the Book of Changes he heard the profound meanings of the sixty-four hexagrams. In rites and music he heard their foundation in loyalty, trustworthiness, harmony, and compliance. In canonical institutions he heard the standards for conferring honor and disgrace, granting and withholding. Thus Confucius’s hearing contained consummate awakening. From consummate awakening came knowledge; hence there were his instructions to choose the good and hold firmly to it, his teaching to overcome oneself and return to ritual propriety, and…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
志立不惑知命耳順不踰矩之全功有廣大變
通陰陽易簡之德象有為邦四代之禮樂有春
秋二百四十二年之經制孔子之知至此殆神
矣乎抑豈惟於文王然也達諸湯達諸堯舜而
羣聖人大成集也曰知我其天曰天何言哉天
且弗違而況於列聖乎哉盖道天之道也列聖
之傳也而孔子至悟之神至於斯也雖然見知
者聞知之因後作者之據也孔子亦因之吕散
而有據焉者也彼子貢見而未悟顏曾大而未
===
化孟子之所為嘆者見知者之惜而聞知者之
望也又不但曰列聖之悟達而行孔子之悟窮
而藏已也噫繼往開來以俟後聖於無窮天非
無意于孔子也後有神乎悟孔子者則亦達諸
天而已矣
同前
李相
同考試官學正區批〔意格自別〕
同考試官教授張批〔論有援據錄之〕
punctuated:
志立、不惑、知命、耳順、不踰矩之全功，有廣大變通、陰陽易簡之德象，有為邦四代之禮樂，有《春秋》二百四十二年之經制。孔子之知至此，殆神矣乎！抑豈惟於文王然也？達諸湯，達諸堯舜，而羣聖人大成集也。曰：「知我其天！」曰：「天何言哉！」天且弗違，而況於列聖乎哉！盖道，天之道也，列聖之傳也，而孔子至悟之神至於斯也。雖然，見知者，聞知之因、後作者之據也。孔子亦因之吕散而有據焉者也。彼子貢見而未悟，顏曾大而未化，孟子之所為嘆者，見知者之惜，而聞知者之望也。又不但曰列聖之悟達而行，孔子之悟窮而藏已也。噫！繼往開來，以俟後聖於無窮，天非無意于孔子也。後有神乎悟孔子者，則亦達諸天而已矣。

同前
李相
同考試官學正區批〔意格自別〕
同考試官教授張批〔論有援據，錄之〕
translation_en:
…the complete achievement of establishing his resolve, becoming free from doubt, knowing Heaven’s mandate, having an ear attuned to truth, and never overstepping the bounds; the moral qualities and patterns of vastness and adaptive transformation, of yin and yang, and of ease and simplicity; the rites and music of the four dynasties for governing a state; and the institutions and judgments recorded in the two hundred and forty-two years of the Spring and Autumn Annals. With his understanding reaching this point, was Confucius not almost spirit-like? Yet was this so only in relation to King Wen? He attained an understanding of Tang, and of Yao and Shun, gathering together the consummate achievements of all the sages. He said, “It is Heaven that knows me!” He also said, “What does Heaven say?” Even Heaven did not run counter to him; how much less, then, the succession of sages! For the Way is Heaven’s Way, transmitted by the succession of sages, and the spirit-like quality of Confucius’s ultimate insight reached this extent.

Nevertheless, those who know through seeing provide the basis for those who know through hearing, and the foundation for those who arise afterward. Confucius likewise relied upon them—Lü San [?]—and thereby had a foundation. Zigong saw but had not yet attained insight; Yan Hui and Zeng Shen achieved greatness but had not yet attained transformation. What Mencius lamented expressed regret concerning those who knew through seeing, and hope for those who would know through hearing. Nor is it merely that the successive sages put their insight into practice when they held influence, while Confucius kept his insight concealed when he lacked opportunity. Ah! In carrying forward the past and opening the way for the future, awaiting later sages through ages without end, Heaven was not without a purpose for Confucius. If someone afterward attains a spirit-like understanding of Confucius, that person will likewise attain an understanding of Heaven, and nothing more.

Same topic as above.
Li Xiang.
Associate Examiner Ou, School Instructor, comments: 〔The conception and style are distinctive.〕
Associate Examiner Zhang, Prefectural School Professor, comments: 〔The argument has supporting authorities; select it for inclusion.〕

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官行人徐批〔明顯〕
事有曠百世而相感者大聖承列聖之統者在
是矣夫天下未甞一日無道統其生聖人有期
而不數也故有達而親授於一時窮而神會於
百世要之心同也道同也前夫所見者殆即其
所聞後夫所聞者殆即其所見必其時之至而
精元一會若有機焉而特不得其朕者焉爾知
此則以夫子而上溯文王一旦乃喟然曰文不
在兹乎而道統之傳誠有自來者孟子發為斯
===
論正以明其傳之有在又以俟後聖於無窮也
孔子聞而知之請遂言之吾道流行於天地未
甞一日而有間也聖賢之興值五百載而一見
不常有也其間固有適丁其盛際會於一堂者
有身處其窮垂憲於萬世者語其時皆不可得
而同也然時有先後世有古今而人心之所同
然者一而已苟得其所同然則雖越宇宙若親
炙之者爾自今觀之二帝三王之治本於道二
帝三王之道本於心由堯舜至湯五百有餘歲
punctuated:
考試官行人徐批〔明顯〕

事有曠百世而相感者，大聖承列聖之統者在是矣。夫天下未甞一日無道統，其生聖人有期而不數也。故有達而親授於一時，窮而神會於百世，要之心同也，道同也。前夫所見者，殆即其所聞；後夫所聞者，殆即其所見。必其時之至，而精元一會，若有機焉，而特不得其朕者焉爾。知此，則以夫子而上溯文王，一旦乃喟然曰：「文不在兹乎？」而道統之傳誠有自來者。孟子發為斯論，正以明其傳之有在，又以俟後聖於無窮也。

孔子聞而知之，請遂言之。吾道流行於天地，未甞一日而有間也。聖賢之興，值五百載而一見，不常有也。其間固有適丁其盛，際會於一堂者；有身處其窮，垂憲於萬世者。語其時，皆不可得而同也。然時有先後，世有古今，而人心之所同然者一而已。苟得其所同然，則雖越宇宙，若親炙之者爾。自今觀之，二帝三王之治本於道，二帝三王之道本於心。由堯舜至湯，五百有餘歲。
translation_en:
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: 〔Clear and manifest.〕

There are things that resonate with one another across a hundred generations: herein lies the great sage’s succession to the lineage of the sages before him. The world has never gone a single day without the succession of the Way, but the birth of sages has its appointed times and is infrequent. Thus some, attaining public influence, transmit it personally within their own age; others, confined by adverse circumstances, commune in spirit across a hundred generations. Ultimately, their minds are the same, and their Way is the same. What those before saw was virtually what they heard; what those afterward heard was virtually what they saw. When the appointed time arrives, their essential spirits unite [?], as though some mechanism were at work, though its traces cannot be discerned. Understanding this, we see how the Master traced his lineage back to King Wen and one day sighed, saying, “Does not this cultural heritage reside here in me?” The transmission of the succession of the Way indeed has its source. Mengzi advanced this argument precisely to make clear where that transmission resided, and also to await future sages through ages without end.

“Confucius knew it through hearing”: allow me to elaborate. Our Way flows throughout Heaven and Earth and has never been interrupted for a single day. The rise of sages and worthies occurs once in five hundred years; it is no commonplace event. Among them, some happen to encounter a flourishing age and meet together in one hall; others live amid adversity and bequeath models to ten thousand generations. In terms of their times, their circumstances cannot all be the same. Yet although times are earlier or later, and ages ancient or modern, what human minds alike acknowledge as right is one and the same. If one grasps what they alike acknowledge, then even across the reaches of space and time, it is as though one had personally received their teaching. Viewed from the present, the government of the Two Emperors and Three Kings was rooted in the Way, and their Way was rooted in the mind. From Yao and Shun to Tang there were more than five hundred years.…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
若禹臯陶則見而知之其所以為堯舜者固不
異也湯處其後不得為禹為臯陶也亦豈有異
夫堯舜者哉由湯至於文王五百有餘歲若伊
尹萊朱則見而知之其所以為成湯者固不異
也文王處其後不得為伊尹為萊朱也亦豈有
異夫成湯者哉由文王而至於孔子又適五百
有餘歲是亦堯舜成湯之一大承也太公望散
宜生既見文王之所見夫子其不聞文王之所
聞者乎是以刪詩書也定禮樂也賛周易也脩
===
春秋也有進退存亡者焉有德仁誠敬者焉有
中正和平者焉有感發懲創者焉有用舍予奪
者焉其所以為精一為執中為建中為建極為
純亦不已為種德為一德為平格為迪教無所
不在亦無所不聞也博文約禮同志之義老安
少懷付物之仁委吏攝相屈伸之感志學從心
始卒之地合之為一理散之為萬事放之彌六
合卷之藏於密萬象異形而同體也百王異世
而同神也未有文王無不為夫子也既有夫子
punctuated: 若禹、臯陶，則見而知之，其所以為堯舜者固不異也。湯處其後，不得為禹、為臯陶也，亦豈有異夫堯舜者哉？由湯至於文王，五百有餘歲。若伊尹、萊朱，則見而知之，其所以為成湯者固不異也。文王處其後，不得為伊尹、為萊朱也，亦豈有異夫成湯者哉？由文王而至於孔子，又適五百有餘歲，是亦堯舜、成湯之一大承也。太公望、散宜生既見文王之所見，夫子其不聞文王之所聞者乎？是以刪《詩》《書》也，定禮樂也，賛《周易》也，脩《春秋》也。有進退存亡者焉，有德仁誠敬者焉，有中正和平者焉，有感發懲創者焉，有用舍予奪者焉。其所以為精一、為執中、為建中、為建極、為純亦不已、為種德、為一德、為平格、為迪教，無所不在，亦無所不聞也。博文約禮，同志之義；老安少懷，付物之仁；委吏攝相，屈伸之感；志學從心，始卒之地。合之為一理，散之為萬事，放之彌六合，卷之藏於密。萬象異形而同體也，百王異世而同神也。未有文王無不為夫子也，既有夫子
translation_en:
…As for Yu and Gao Yao, they knew through seeing; that which made them like Yao and Shun was fundamentally no different. Tang lived after them and could not occupy the position of Yu or Gao Yao; yet how could he have differed from Yao and Shun? From Tang to King Wen, more than five hundred years elapsed. As for Yi Yin and Lai Zhu, they knew through seeing; that which made them like Cheng Tang was fundamentally no different. King Wen lived after them and could not occupy the position of Yi Yin or Lai Zhu; yet how could he have differed from Cheng Tang? From King Wen to Confucius, again just over five hundred years elapsed. This too was a great continuation of the legacy of Yao, Shun, and Cheng Tang. Taigong Wang and San Yisheng had seen what King Wen saw; could the Master have failed to hear what King Wen heard?

Thus he edited the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, established rites and music, elucidated the Changes of Zhou, and compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals. These contain advancement and withdrawal, survival and destruction; virtue, benevolence, sincerity, and reverence; centrality, rectitude, harmony, and peace; inspiration and chastening admonition; and employment and dismissal, bestowal and deprivation. The means of being discerning and undivided, holding to the mean, establishing the mean, establishing the supreme standard, remaining pure without cease, cultivating virtue, being constant in virtue, bringing peace and rectification, and guiding through instruction are present everywhere, and everywhere may be learned through hearing.

Broad learning in cultural traditions and restraint through ritual embody the righteousness of shared aspirations; bringing peace to the aged and cherishing the young embody benevolence bestowed upon others. Serving as a granary clerk and acting as chief minister express responsiveness in obscurity and prominence; setting his heart on learning and following his heart mark the stages from beginning to completion. United, these constitute one principle; dispersed, they constitute the myriad affairs. Extended, they fill the six directions; rolled up, they lie concealed in secrecy. The myriad phenomena differ in form but share one substance; the hundred kings belong to different ages but share one spiritual efficacy. There has never been a King Wen who was not wholly the Master [?]; once there was the Master…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
無不為文王也若語其迹而遺其心不足以言
聖人矣惜夫鳳鳥不至河不出圖故不復夢周
公夫子之心亦已矣積其所窮孰知其事功反
有賢於堯舜者是亦不獨聞知於文王焉爾雖
然孟子終篇歷敘羣聖之統正以明其傳之有
在也夫子聞知於文王孟子見知於夫子無有
乎爾之說亦有見其所自任而不得辭者觀夫
七篇之中無非此理故韓子曰孔子傳之孟軻
信夫
===
表
擬宋頒訓廉謹刑二銘於中外羣臣謝表
淳祐四年
胡鰲
同考試官教諭徐批寓規諷於駢儷深得表體
同考試官教授唐批檃括二銘以代巳意可謂表矣
考試官行人徐批典則
淳祐四年正月某日具官臣某等伏蒙
皇上頒賜
punctuated:
無不為文王也。若語其迹而遺其心，不足以言聖人矣。惜夫！鳳鳥不至，河不出圖，故不復夢周公，夫子之心亦已矣。積其所窮，孰知其事功反有賢於堯舜者？是亦不獨聞知於文王焉爾。雖然，孟子終篇歷敘羣聖之統，正以明其傳之有在也。夫子聞知於文王，孟子見知於夫子，「無有乎爾」之說，亦有見其所自任而不得辭者。觀夫七篇之中，無非此理。故韓子曰：「孔子傳之孟軻。」信夫！

表
擬宋頒訓廉謹刑二銘於中外羣臣謝表
淳祐四年
胡鰲

同考試官教諭徐批：寓規諷於駢儷，深得表體。
同考試官教授唐批：檃括二銘以代巳意，可謂表矣。
考試官行人徐批：典則。

淳祐四年正月某日，具官臣某等伏蒙皇上頒賜
translation_en:
…he likewise embodies King Wen in every respect. To speak of the sages’ deeds while overlooking their hearts is inadequate for discussing them. Alas! The phoenix did not arrive, and the Yellow River yielded no diagram; thus Confucius no longer dreamed of the Duke of Zhou, and his hopes, too, came to an end. Amid all the frustrations he endured, who could have known that his achievements would in some respects surpass those of Yao and Shun? Thus his attainment was not confined to knowing King Wen through what he had heard.

Nevertheless, in the concluding passage of his work, Mengzi successively recounts the lineage of the sages precisely to make clear that its transmission has a living bearer. Confucius knew King Wen through hearing of him; Mengzi knew Confucius through seeing him [?]. The words “Is there no one, then?” also reveal the responsibility he assumed for himself and could not decline. Throughout the seven books, there is nothing that does not express this principle. Thus Master Han said, “Confucius transmitted it to Meng Ke.” How true!

Memorial
A Memorial of Thanks, Composed as Though in the Song Dynasty, for the Distribution to Officials at Court and in the Provinces of the Two Admonitory Inscriptions on Integrity and Caution in Punishment
Fourth year of Chunyou
Hu Ao

Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Admonition and remonstrance are conveyed through parallel prose: this thoroughly captures the form of the memorial.”
Associate Examiner Tang, Professor, comments: “He recasts the two inscriptions to express his own meaning [?]. This may indeed be called a memorial.”
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “Classical and exemplary.”

On a certain day of the first month of the fourth year of Chunyou, your servants, so-and-so and others, holding the specified offices, humbly received from Your Majesty the bestowal of…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
御製訓廉謹刑二銘戒飭中外者
德協龍占永戴清寧之治
功垂象典弘施欽卹之仁
敷言用錫於庶民設教允資乎神道羣工滌
垢萬物回春臣等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊
以六計周官循良是厲三章漢約寬大為
先惟義重而利輕必刑平而民服伯夷播
迪探本於直清太史懲姦寄意於食貨慨
簠簋之弗飾厭鞭朴之日繁大肆狠貪而
===
已肥民瘠罔懲鴟義而下虐上欺心易酌
泉法忘畫地此鰥寡為之無告而父母所
當動心者也恭惟
〇〇〇〇
倫合禹文
信孚虞芮政復乾淳之善法章噬嗑之明
本源潔而屢戒誅求
惠愛深而務存忠厚
離明夬決苞苴不行
punctuated:
御製訓廉謹刑二銘，戒飭中外者。
德協龍占，永戴清寧之治；功垂象典，弘施欽卹之仁。敷言用錫於庶民，設教允資乎神道。羣工滌垢，萬物回春。臣等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊以六計周官，循良是厲；三章漢約，寬大為先。惟義重而利輕，必刑平而民服。伯夷播迪，探本於直清；太史懲姦，寄意於食貨。慨簠簋之弗飾，厭鞭朴之日繁。大肆狠貪，而已肥民瘠；罔懲鴟義，而下虐上欺。心易酌泉，法忘畫地。此鰥寡為之無告，而父母所當動心者也。恭惟〇〇〇〇，倫合禹文，信孚虞芮。政復乾淳之善，法章噬嗑之明。本源潔而屢戒誅求，惠愛深而務存忠厚。離明夬決，苞苴不行。
translation_en:
…the two imperially composed inscriptions, Admonition to Integrity and Caution in Punishment, admonishing officials both at court and throughout the realm.

Your virtue accords with the dragon augury; we shall forever uphold your reign of purity and peace. Your achievements endure in the statutes of punishment, and you broadly extend the benevolence of reverent care and compassion. You proclaim your words to bestow them upon the common people; in establishing instruction, you truly draw upon the way of the spirits. All officials cleanse themselves of defilement, and all things return to spring. We, your servants, in utmost fear and trembling, bow our heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtow.

We humbly reflect that the six assessments in the Offices of Zhou encouraged conscientious and upright officials, while the Han covenant of three articles gave precedence to leniency. Only when righteousness is valued and profit held lightly will punishments necessarily be equitable and the people submit. Bo Yi spread instruction, seeking its foundation in uprightness and purity; the Grand Historian censured wrongdoing, conveying his intent through his treatment of food and wealth. We lament officials’ failure to keep their sacrificial vessels unsullied—a figure for integrity in office—and deplore the daily multiplication of floggings. They give free rein to ferocity and greed, fattening themselves while the people grow lean. They fail to restrain their rapacious conduct [?], abusing those below and deceiving those above. Their hearts change as though they had drunk from the Spring of Greed; their administration of law forgets the age when a line drawn on the ground sufficed as a prison. Thus widowers and widows have no one to whom they can appeal: this is what should move the hearts of those who serve as the people’s parents.

We reverently consider that [four circle marks in the text] your moral stature matches that of Yu and King Wen, and your trustworthiness wins confidence as did King Wen’s among the states of Yu and Rui. Your government restores the excellence of the Qiandao and Chunxi eras; your laws manifest the clarity of the hexagram Biting Through. Pure at the source, you repeatedly admonish against oppressive exactions; profound in benevolent care, you strive to preserve loyalty and generosity. With the illumination of the hexagram Li and the resolution of the hexagram Guai, you ensure that bribes find no currency.…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
履泰屯亨瘡痍是憫惟貨利之不殖致黎庶
之潤疎投珠旣挽乎玄機束矢自歸於皇
極猶蒙
睿慮幷渙
宸章盖欲登進乎羔羊且大懷來於鴻鴈朋龜
益下省元吉之弗違山火賁明闡人文而
成化渢渢乎廉頑之志洋洋乎儆位之謨
望塵可以洗心扶杖莫不垂泣臣等謬官
庶列莫稱激揚叨受嘉師空存惻怛花封
===
拙牧顧稍警於四知柳下戇資慙未免於
三黜彼安貞之節方仰法天地之時而赦
宥之恩遽俯承雷雨之解憂深碩鼠患切
積乎臣等敢不克愼厥猷敬明乃罰奉
申命而行事同寅畏以和衷嚴取舍於義利
之從審重輕於出入之用靖恭爾位誓勿
納於官邪康乂我民勉聞由於聖哲庶冠
紳之弗愧而
光命之對揚伏願
punctuated:
履泰屯亨，瘡痍是憫。惟貨利之不殖，致黎庶之潤疎。投珠旣挽乎玄機，束矢自歸於皇極。猶蒙睿慮，幷渙宸章，盖欲登進乎羔羊，且大懷來於鴻鴈。朋龜益下，省元吉之弗違；山火賁明，闡人文而成化。渢渢乎廉頑之志，洋洋乎儆位之謨！望塵可以洗心，扶杖莫不垂泣。
臣等謬官庶列，莫稱激揚；叨受嘉師，空存惻怛。花封拙牧，顧稍警於四知；柳下戇資，慙未免於三黜。彼安貞之節，方仰法天地之時，而赦宥之恩，遽俯承雷雨之解。憂深碩鼠，患切積乎。臣等敢不克愼厥猷，敬明乃罰，奉申命而行事，同寅畏以和衷，嚴取舍於義利之從，審重輕於出入之用，靖恭爾位，誓勿納於官邪，康乂我民，勉聞由於聖哲，庶冠紳之弗愧，而光命之對揚。伏願
translation_en:
…Treading in peace and bringing difficulty through to a successful conclusion, you pity the afflicted. Because wealth and profit have not increased, the benefits reaching the common people are scant. The casting of pearls has already turned back the mysterious mechanism [?], and the bundles of arrows naturally return to the imperial standard. Yet we have further received your sagely consideration and the promulgation of your imperial pronouncement. Surely your purpose is to advance officials of the integrity celebrated in “The Lamb” and generously gather in the distressed people evoked by “The Wild Geese.” As in the Changes, paired tortoise shells signify Increase bestowed upon those below: you consider how supreme good fortune may be attained without deviation. Fire beneath the mountain shines in Grace: you elucidate human culture and thereby transform the people. How far-reaching your resolve to make the avaricious upright! How abundant your counsels admonishing those in office! Merely beholding the dust of your approach can cleanse the heart; among those leaning on their staffs, none fails to shed tears.
We, your servants, undeservedly occupy places among the ranks of officials and cannot adequately fulfill the duty of discouraging evil and promoting good. Unworthily receiving your excellent instruction [?], we retain only our compassionate concern. As inept shepherds of our flower-planted districts, we have nevertheless taken some warning from the “four who know”; with the blunt disposition of Liuxia Hui, we are ashamed that we have not escaped his three dismissals. In maintaining steadfast rectitude, we were just looking upward to model ourselves on the seasons of Heaven and Earth when we suddenly received, from above, the grace of pardon, like the Release brought by thunder and rain. Our anxiety over the “great rats” is profound; our concern over accumulated troubles is acute [?]. How could we, your servants, fail to exercise caution in our plans and reverently make punishments clear? We shall carry out affairs in obedience to your reiterated commands, sharing reverence and awe so as to unite our hearts. We shall strictly distinguish what to accept and reject according to righteousness and profit, and carefully weigh severity and leniency when imposing or remitting penalties. We shall discharge our offices with quiet reverence, vowing never to fall into official wrongdoing. We shall bring peace and good order to our people, striving to hear and follow the teachings of sages and wise men, so that we may prove worthy of our official caps and sashes and fittingly honor and proclaim your glorious command. Prostrate, we pray that…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
恭默為心
好生洽德
導迎和氣
顧畏民畧
清入聖而興四海之淳風
仁如天而啓八荒之壽域
振紀綱於棫樸繩孫子於螽斯臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
===
表稱
謝以
聞
第參塲
策
第一問
傅頤
同考試官學正區批歸美中有期望意忠愛
者如是乎
punctuated:
恭默為心，好生洽德，導迎和氣，顧畏民畧，清入聖而興四海之淳風，仁如天而啓八荒之壽域，振紀綱於棫樸，繩孫子於螽斯。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第參塲
策
第一問
傅頤
同考試官學正區批：歸美中有期望意，忠愛者如是乎？
translation_en:
…may reverence and quietude guide your heart, and your love of life imbue your virtue; may you usher in harmonious influences and regard the people's concerns with apprehension [?]. Through purity, may you attain sagehood and foster unspoiled customs throughout the Four Seas; with benevolence like Heaven's, may you open a realm of longevity throughout the Eight Regions. May you invigorate the guiding principles of government in the spirit of “The Oak Clumps” (Yupu), and perpetuate your descendants in the spirit of “The Locusts” (Zhongsi).
We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty with the utmost fervor and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks and bring them to your hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Fu Yi
Comment by Associate Examiner Ou, Instructor: “Within his attribution of excellence to the sovereign lies an expression of hope for him. Is this not how one loyal to and devoted to his sovereign should write?”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教授張批〔脩齊之學自是不同〕
考試官行人徐批〔條敘森然涵濡而有得者〕
聖人之化自近而遠者也聖人之教自身
而言者也身教焉以建天下國家之極言
教焉以理天下國家之治極建而天下國
家可理也治理而天下國家可化也身教
盡倫者也言教盡制者也兩盡足為天下
極矣近之齊治而放乎均平之遠自創業
而垂繼體無窮之盛聖人之化優優大哉
===
嘗觀之詩矣關雎舉聖德之全體也葛覃
卷耳言志行樛木螽斯美惠及桃夭兎罝
芣苢則家齊而國治之效漢廣汝墳則見
天下有可平之漸麟趾則王者之瑞而關
雎之應也說者曰妻道無成本諸文王詩
人之意固有在夫嘗觀之易矣乾父道也
彖曰大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天坤母道
也彖曰至哉坤元萬物資生乃順承天傳
曰陰陽合德剛柔有體以體天地之撰通
punctuated:
同考試官教授張批〔脩齊之學，自是不同。〕

考試官行人徐批〔條敘森然，涵濡而有得者。〕\n聖人之化，自近而遠者也；聖人之教，自身而言者也。身教焉，以建天下國家之極；言教焉，以理天下國家之治。極建而天下國家可理也，治理而天下國家可化也。身教盡倫者也，言教盡制者也，兩盡足為天下極矣。近之齊治，而放乎均平之遠；自創業，而垂繼體無窮之盛。聖人之化，優優大哉！

嘗觀之《詩》矣。《關雎》舉聖德之全體也，《葛覃》《卷耳》言志行，《樛木》《螽斯》美惠及，《桃夭》《兎罝》《芣苢》則家齊而國治之效，《漢廣》《汝墳》則見天下有可平之漸，《麟趾》則王者之瑞，而《關雎》之應也。說者曰：「妻道無成，本諸文王。」詩人之意，固有在夫！嘗觀之《易》矣。乾，父道也，彖曰：「大哉乾元！萬物資始，乃統天。」坤，母道也，彖曰：「至哉坤元！萬物資生，乃順承天。」傳曰：「陰陽合德，剛柔有體，以體天地之撰，通
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: 〔The learning of self-cultivation and family regulation is indeed of a different order.〕

Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: 〔An imposing, orderly exposition, by someone who has steeped himself in the teachings and gained understanding.〕

The sage’s transforming influence extends from what is near to what is distant; the sage’s teaching proceeds from his own person to his words. Through teaching by personal example, he establishes the supreme standard for all under Heaven, the state, and the family; through verbal teaching, he orders their governance. Once the standard is established, all under Heaven, the state, and the family can be ordered; once governance is properly ordered, they can be transformed. Teaching by personal example fulfills human relationships; verbal teaching perfects institutions. The fulfillment of both suffices to provide the supreme standard for all under Heaven. Beginning nearby with the regulation of the family and the ordering of the state, this influence extends to the distant goal of equity and peace throughout the realm. From the founding of a dynasty, it bequeaths unending flourishing to succeeding rulers. How abundant and great is the sage’s transforming influence!

I have observed this in the Book of Odes. “The Ospreys” (Guanju) presents sagely virtue in its entirety. “The Spreading Kudzu” (Getan) and “The Cocklebur” (Juan’er) speak of aspirations and conduct; “The Drooping Trees” (Jiumu) and “The Locusts” (Zhongsi) praise the extension of kindness. “The Peach Tree” (Taoyao), “The Rabbit Net” (Tuju), and “The Plantain” (Fuyi) show the effects of regulating the family and ordering the state. “The Broad Han River” (Hanguang) and “The Banks of the Ru River” (Rufen) reveal the gradual advance toward bringing peace to all under Heaven. “The Qilin’s Hoofs” (Linzhi) presents an auspicious sign of a true king and the fulfillment of “The Ospreys.” A commentator says: “The wife’s way claims no independent achievement; its foundation lies in King Wen.” The poets surely had a purpose in this!

I have also observed this in the Book of Changes. Qian is the way of the father. Its Commentary on the Judgment says: “Great indeed is the primal power of Qian! All things draw upon it for their beginning, and it governs Heaven.” Kun is the way of the mother. Its Commentary on the Judgment says: “Perfect indeed is the primal power of Kun! All things draw upon it for their birth, and it compliantly receives Heaven.” The Commentary says: “Yin and yang unite their powers; the firm and the yielding have embodied forms, thereby giving embodiment to the workings of Heaven and Earth and communicating …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
神明之德聖人之意其有妙蘊存焉者乎
我
太祖高皇帝修齊之化媲美周南而統天之功
上擬乾道時又得
孝慈高皇后天作之配斡化賛元母儀天下嘉
言善行載之傳者真足以表勵宫壺為法
天下可傳後世矣是故
仁孝文皇后廣其教而為內訓二十篇首德性
次修身慎言謹行勤勵警戒節儉積善遷
===
善崇
聖訓景賢範事父母事君事舅姑奉祭祀母儀
睦親慈幼逮下而終之以待外戚其綱目
炳如也邇者
章聖慈仁皇太后復集大成而為女訓十二篇
首閨訓次修德受命夫婦孝舅姑敬夫愛
妾慈幼姙子教子慎靜而終之以節儉其
條理秩如也噫是道也
高皇后皆已有之姑舉其一二言焉如貞靜端
punctuated:
神明之德。聖人之意，其有妙蘊存焉者乎？

我太祖高皇帝修齊之化，媲美周南，而統天之功，上擬乾道。時又得孝慈高皇后天作之配，斡化賛元，母儀天下。嘉言善行載之傳者，真足以表勵宫壺，為法天下，可傳後世矣。是故仁孝文皇后廣其教而為《內訓》二十篇：首德性，次修身、慎言、謹行、勤勵、警戒、節儉、積善、遷善、崇聖訓、景賢範、事父母、事君、事舅姑、奉祭祀、母儀、睦親、慈幼、逮下，而終之以待外戚。其綱目炳如也。

邇者，章聖慈仁皇太后復集大成而為《女訓》十二篇：首閨訓，次修德、受命、夫婦、孝舅姑、敬夫、愛妾、慈幼、姙子、教子、慎靜，而終之以節儉。其條理秩如也。噫！是道也，高皇后皆已有之。姑舉其一二言焉，如貞靜端
translation_en:
…the potency of the spirits. Surely the sages’ intent contains subtle depths!

Our Emperor Taizu Gao’s transforming influence through cultivating himself and ordering his household rivaled that celebrated in the “Songs of Zhou and the South”; his achievement in bringing all under Heaven into unity emulated above the Way of Qian, the Creative. At that time he also found in Empress Xiaoci Gao a Heaven-made partner. She assisted the work of transformation and the primal creative power, serving as a maternal exemplar for all under Heaven. Her fine words and good deeds, recorded in her biography, truly suffice to exemplify and encourage conduct within the palace’s inner quarters [?], to provide a model throughout the realm, and to be transmitted to later generations. Thus Empress Renxiao Wen extended her teaching by composing the twenty chapters of Instructions for the Inner Quarters (Neixun). Beginning with “Moral Nature,” these proceed through “Cultivating Oneself,” “Care in Speech,” “Caution in Conduct,” “Diligent Effort,” “Vigilance,” “Frugality,” “Accumulating Good Deeds,” “Turning toward Goodness,” “Honoring the Sagely Instructions,” “Revering Worthy Models,” “Serving Parents,” “Serving the Ruler,” “Serving Parents-in-Law,” “Conducting Sacrifices,” “Maternal Exemplarity,” “Harmony with Kin,” “Kindness to the Young,” and “Extending Care to Those Below,” and conclude with “Treatment of Imperial Maternal and Marital Relatives.” Its guiding principles and particulars are luminously clear.

Recently, Empress Dowager Zhangsheng Ciren again brought these teachings together in a comprehensive synthesis, composing the twelve chapters of Instructions for Women (Nüxun). Beginning with “Instructions for the Women’s Quarters,” these proceed through “Cultivating Virtue,” “Receiving Commands,” “Husband and Wife,” “Filial Service to Parents-in-Law,” “Respecting One’s Husband,” “Caring for Concubines,” “Kindness to the Young,” “Pregnancy,” “Teaching Children,” and “Caution and Quietude,” and conclude with “Frugality.” Its arrangement is orderly and coherent. Ah! Empress Gao had already embodied this Way in its entirety. Let me cite just one or two examples, such as her being chaste, tranquil, and upright…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
一孝敬慈惠則所謂德性矣正位中宮益
自勤勵則所謂修身矣其警勵也有曰無
功受福造物所惡當勤女工以報造物其
積善也有曰惟以不殺人為本顛者扶之
危者救之以至念家世之忠厚而曰吾父
平生急於義以不逮事舅姑為恨而當祭
躬治膳羞內訓之道
高皇后身有之者如此不寧惟是如講求古訓
以諭六宮非所謂閨訓乎訪問家法惟取
===
仁厚非所謂修德乎其教子也勉令務學
諄切懇至其節儉也衣服澣濯不喜侈麗
以至撫育李文忠沐英等愛如己出推此
心也慈幼至矣宮人有過執付宮正司議
罪推此心也愛妾周矣女訓之道
高皇后身有之者又如此然則
高皇后非不欲言教也其為言固已寓乎身教
之中矣若
文皇后之身教也則有所謂貞靜純明孝敬仁
punctuated:
一、孝敬慈惠，則所謂德性矣；正位中宮，益自勤勵，則所謂修身矣。其警勵也，有曰：「無功受福，造物所惡，當勤女工以報造物。」其積善也，有曰：「惟以不殺人為本，顛者扶之，危者救之。」以至念家世之忠厚，而曰：「吾父平生急於義。」以不逮事舅姑為恨，而當祭躬治膳羞。《內訓》之道，高皇后身有之者如此。
不寧惟是，如講求古訓以諭六宮，非所謂閨訓乎？訪問家法，惟取仁厚，非所謂修德乎？其教子也，勉令務學，諄切懇至；其節儉也，衣服澣濯，不喜侈麗。以至撫育李文忠、沐英等，愛如己出，推此心也，慈幼至矣；宮人有過，執付宮正司議罪，推此心也，愛妾周矣。《女訓》之道，高皇后身有之者又如此。
然則高皇后非不欲言教也，其為言固已寓乎身教之中矣。若文皇后之身教也，則有所謂貞靜純明、孝敬仁
translation_en:
…single-minded, filial and respectful, compassionate and kind: these exemplify what is called moral character. Having assumed her rightful place as empress, she applied herself still more diligently: this exemplifies what is called self-cultivation. In admonishing and encouraging herself, she said: “To receive blessings without merit is something the Creator abhors. I must diligently undertake women’s work to repay the Creator.” In accumulating good deeds, she said: “Simply take not killing people as the foundation. Support those who stumble and rescue those in peril.” She also recalled her family’s tradition of loyalty and generosity, saying: “Throughout his life, my father was zealous in doing what was right.” She regretted that she had never had the opportunity to serve her parents-in-law, and personally prepared the food and delicacies for sacrifices to them. Such was Empress Gao’s personal embodiment of the Way set forth in Instructions for the Inner Quarters (Neixun).
Nor was this all. She studied ancient teachings to instruct the women of the Six Palaces: was this not what is called instruction for the women’s quarters? She inquired into rules for household conduct, adopting only those marked by benevolence and generosity: was this not what is called cultivating virtue? In teaching her children, she urged them to devote themselves to learning, with earnest admonitions and the utmost sincerity. In practicing frugality, she wore washed clothing and took no pleasure in lavish finery. She also raised Li Wenzhong, Mu Ying, and others, loving them as her own children. In extending this disposition, her kindness to the young reached its fullest expression. When palace women committed offenses, she had them handed over to the Office of Palace Discipline for deliberation on their punishment. In extending this disposition, her loving care for the concubines was comprehensive. Such, too, was Empress Gao’s personal embodiment of the Way set forth in Instructions for Women (Nüxun).
Thus, it was not that Empress Gao was unwilling to teach through words; what she would express in words was already implicit in her teaching through personal example. As for Empress Wen’s teaching through personal example, there were what are called steadfastness and tranquility, purity and discernment, filial devotion and respect, benevolence…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
厚恭勤婦道足範宮闈者矣若
章聖皇太后之身教也則有所謂克配乾元躬
備聖善徽柔恭懿仁順貞慈者矣此身教
脩而倫盡言教行而制盡以
聖佐
聖所以匹休姜姒體德乾坤啓
創業之盛著
守成之美而恢
中興之治者功獨可誣乎哉雖然愚於此有
===
以仰見我
列聖之脩齊矣斥侈靡而絕游幸敦儉朴以先
天下以一夫不得其所自責而聞加惠窮
民之對以化家為國歸美而聞警戒治安
之規我
太祖高皇帝刑于之化周南以後所未聞也恭
儉服澣濯之衣夙興養清爽之氣則
太宗文皇帝之宣重光者也日躋
聖敬之功天授欽明之德則又
punctuated:
厚，恭勤，婦道足範宮闈者矣。若章聖皇太后之身教也，則有所謂克配乾元，躬備聖善，徽柔恭懿，仁順貞慈者矣。此身教脩而倫盡，言教行而制盡，以聖佐聖，所以匹休姜姒，體德乾坤，啓創業之盛，著守成之美，而恢中興之治者，功獨可誣乎哉？

雖然，愚於此有以仰見我列聖之脩齊矣。斥侈靡而絕游幸，敦儉朴以先天下，以一夫不得其所自責，而聞加惠窮民之對；以化家為國歸美，而聞警戒治安之規。我太祖高皇帝刑于之化，周南以後所未聞也。恭儉服澣濯之衣，夙興養清爽之氣，則太宗文皇帝之宣重光者也。日躋聖敬之功，天授欽明之德，則又
translation_en:
…generous, reverent, and diligent, her conduct as a wife sufficient to serve as a model for the palace women. As for the teaching by personal example of Empress Dowager Zhangsheng, she may be described as worthily matching the primal power of Heaven, personally possessing sagely goodness, admirable gentleness, reverence and dignity, benevolence and compliance, constancy and maternal kindness. Through the cultivation of such teaching by example, the duties of human relationships were fully discharged; through the practice of verbal instruction, the prescribed rules were fully realized. Sages thus assisted sages, equaling the glory of Jiang and Si and embodying the virtues of Heaven and Earth. They inaugurated the flourishing of the dynasty’s foundation, manifested the excellence of preserving its achievements, and extended the governance of its restoration. Can their contributions possibly be denied?

Nevertheless, in this I, in my humble judgment, can discern with reverence how our successive sage emperors cultivated themselves and regulated their families. Rejecting extravagance and dispensing with pleasure excursions, the emperor upheld frugality and simplicity to set an example for all under Heaven. He reproached himself if even one man failed to find his proper place, and heard in reply an appeal to extend kindness to the impoverished people. He attributed the credit for transforming the family into a model for the state to his consort, and heard her admonition to remain vigilant even amid peace and good order. The transforming influence of our Emperor Taizu Gao’s example toward his wife was unheard of since the Airs of Zhounan. Reverent and frugal, wearing washed garments, rising early and nurturing a clear and invigorated spirit—these were how Emperor Taizong Wen made the dynasty’s renewed brilliance manifest. Daily advancing in the practice of sagely reverence and endowed by Heaven with the virtue of respectful discernment—these, in turn, were…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
恭睿淵仁寬穆純聖獻皇帝之欽止率
祖者也
三后之身教言教要皆我
列聖有以倡率之云爾否則本之無機風之無
自其何以行化而宣教乎故曰聖人之化
自近而遠者也聖人之教自身而言者也
方今
皇上純孝深仁本於天性雖處深宮無異臨
朝至化刑于宮壼而御於家邦
===
列聖之化在是矣
聖后正位中宮克宣陰教以助理
聖治
三后之教在是矣則夫兆麟趾振螽斯永綿我
國家無疆之福俾斯世斯民訓行以近
天子之光者孰不獻天保而祝華封以仰答吾
君也哉愚敢曰至敬以享
天心至和以迓
天休斯臣子之願足矣謹對
punctuated:
恭睿淵仁寬穆純聖獻皇帝之欽止率祖者也。
三后之身教言教，要皆我列聖有以倡率之云爾。否則，本之無機，風之無自，其何以行化而宣教乎？故曰：聖人之化，自近而遠者也；聖人之教，自身而言者也。
方今皇上純孝深仁，本於天性，雖處深宮，無異臨朝。至化刑于宮壼，而御於家邦，列聖之化在是矣。聖后正位中宮，克宣陰教，以助理聖治，三后之教在是矣。則夫兆麟趾、振螽斯，永綿我國家無疆之福，俾斯世斯民訓行以近天子之光者，孰不獻天保而祝華封，以仰答吾君也哉？愚敢曰：至敬以享天心，至和以迓天休，斯臣子之願足矣。謹對。
translation_en:
…these exemplify Emperor Xian, the Reverent, Sagacious, Profound, Humane, Magnanimous, Majestic, Pure, and Sage, reverently abiding in his proper place and following his ancestors.
The instruction given by the Three Queens through their conduct and their words ultimately depended upon our successive sage emperors taking the lead. Otherwise, if its foundation had no activating impulse and its influence no source, how could moral transformation be effected and instruction spread? Thus it is said: the sage’s transforming influence proceeds from those nearby to those far away; the sage’s instruction proceeds from his own conduct to his words.
Now His Majesty’s pure filial devotion and profound benevolence spring from his innate nature. Even when residing deep within the palace, he acts no differently than when presiding at court. His consummate transforming influence sets the pattern in the inner palace and extends to the ruling of family and state: herein resides the transforming influence of the successive sage emperors. The sagely empress occupies her rightful position in the central palace and effectively spreads the instruction proper to women, thereby assisting His Majesty’s sagely governance: herein resides the instruction of the Three Queens.
Thus, with the auspicious promise of virtuous descendants celebrated in “The Qilin’s Hooves” and the abundant offspring celebrated in “The Locusts,” boundless blessings will endure forever for our dynasty. When the people of this age are enabled to follow instruction and draw near [?] to the radiance of the Son of Heaven, who would fail to offer the wishes of “Heaven Protects” and the blessings of the border warden of Hua, in grateful response to our sovereign? I venture humbly to say: with utmost reverence, please the heart of Heaven; with utmost harmony, welcome Heaven’s blessings. Then the wishes of your subjects will be fulfilled. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第二問
丘橓
同考試官教諭陳批議論滂洽可與講禮者
考試官行人徐批建官之意是如此
立民極者達損益之宜者也究制作之意
者也制作之在聖人也譬大匠之巧也損
益之在後世也譬則倣大匠之規矩準繩
而不必於小大長短之區區也夫宜可變
而通也巧不可驟而得也宜以時言末也
===
巧以蘊言本也禮有本末知所先後立民
極者其庶乎周禮聖人立民極之規矩準
繩也觀其會通行其典禮則後世於大小
長短之度不必於其區區者也若夫聖人
之意固有妙運乎制作之外亦在夫立民
極者之究之爾昔唐太宗甞讀是書撫卷
浩歎愚讀史至此又未甞不撫卷而善夫
太宗之意也何也有成周建官之制斯有
阜成之效倣成周建官之制乃僅止於貞觀
punctuated:
第二問
丘橓
同考試官教諭陳批：議論滂洽，可與講禮者。
考試官行人徐批：建官之意是如此。
立民極者，達損益之宜者也，究制作之意者也。制作之在聖人也，譬大匠之巧也；損益之在後世也，譬則倣大匠之規矩準繩，而不必於小大長短之區區也。夫宜可變而通也，巧不可驟而得也。宜以時言，末也；巧以蘊言，本也。禮有本末，知所先後，立民極者其庶乎！周禮，聖人立民極之規矩準繩也。觀其會通，行其典禮，則後世於大小長短之度，不必於其區區者也。若夫聖人之意，固有妙運乎制作之外，亦在夫立民極者之究之爾。昔唐太宗甞讀是書，撫卷浩歎。愚讀史至此，又未甞不撫卷而善夫太宗之意也。何也？有成周建官之制，斯有阜成之效；倣成周建官之制，乃僅止於貞觀
translation_en:
Second Policy Question

Qiu Shun

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The argument is expansive and comprehensive. Here is someone with whom one may discuss ritual.”

Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “This is indeed the intention behind establishing offices.”

One who establishes the highest standard for the people understands what should appropriately be removed or added and examines the intentions underlying the creation of institutions. The sages’ creation of institutions is like the skill of a master carpenter. Later generations’ removal or addition of provisions is like following the master carpenter’s compass, square, level, and marking line, without insisting upon every petty detail of size and length. What is appropriate can be adapted to changing circumstances, but skill cannot be acquired all at once. Appropriateness, considered in relation to the times, is a secondary matter; skill, considered in relation to its inner substance, is fundamental. Ritual has its fundamentals and its secondary details. If one knows which should come first and which afterward, one may come close to establishing the highest standard for the people!

The Rites of Zhou provides the compass, square, level, and marking line by which the sages established the highest standard for the people. If later generations discern how its provisions connect and work together, and put its prescribed rites into practice, they need not insist upon every petty detail of its measures of size and length. As for the sages’ intentions, these assuredly have a subtle operation beyond the institutions they created. It remains for those who establish the highest standard for the people to investigate them.

Long ago, Emperor Taizong of Tang once read this book and, resting his hand upon the volume, sighed deeply. Whenever I read this passage in the histories, I too cannot help resting my hand upon the volume and approving Taizong’s sentiments. Why is this? With the system of offices established in the fully realized Zhou order, there would be the results of prosperity and settled government; yet imitation of that system of offices attained only the Zhenguan reign’s…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
夷之陋愚寧能以無惑乎試以周禮言之
建官有曰冢宰曰司徒曰宗伯曰司馬曰
司寇之五官其所掌則邦治邦教邦禮邦
政邦禁之不同總衆屬而約之近二萬三
千職焉若冬官則尤為缺典公孤則尚未
及列也以唐制言之建官有曰吏曰户曰
禮曰兵曰刑曰工之六部其所掌則有選
授勳封考課户口井田禮儀祠祭燕享貢
舉軍衛武官選授刑法徒隸勾覆關禁百
===
工屯田山澤之政令此外又有四省諸監
諸寺司各衛及太子親王等官屬焉匪惟
冬官之備三師三公之立而已合而觀之
周或為兼官而唐則存其名位周或相聯
屬而唐則分為特任周或散在列國而唐
則會於全書不可謂唐制盡非古也盖道
有升降事有繁簡故唐虞之惟百視夏商
之官倍不為寡而周之多官視唐虞之惟
百不為冗況唐去周既久又可槩拘以周
punctuated: 夷之陋，愚寧能以無惑乎？試以周禮言之，建官有曰冢宰、曰司徒、曰宗伯、曰司馬、曰司寇之五官，其所掌則邦治、邦教、邦禮、邦政、邦禁之不同，總衆屬而約之，近二萬三千職焉。若冬官，則尤為缺典；公孤，則尚未及列也。以唐制言之，建官有曰吏、曰户、曰禮、曰兵、曰刑、曰工之六部，其所掌則有選授、勳封、考課、户口、井田、禮儀、祠祭、燕享、貢舉、軍衛、武官選授、刑法、徒隸、勾覆、關禁、百工、屯田、山澤之政令。此外，又有四省、諸監、諸寺司、各衛及太子、親王等官屬焉，匪惟冬官之備、三師三公之立而已。合而觀之，周或為兼官，而唐則存其名位；周或相聯屬，而唐則分為特任；周或散在列國，而唐則會於全書。不可謂唐制盡非古也。盖道有升降，事有繁簡，故唐虞之惟百，視夏商之官倍，不為寡；而周之多官，視唐虞之惟百，不為冗。況唐去周既久，又可槩拘以周
translation_en:
…the crudity of the barbarians [?]. How could I remain unperplexed? Consider the Rites of Zhou: its establishment of offices includes five chief officials—the Grand Steward, Minister of Education, Minister of Rites, Minister of War, and Minister of Justice. Their respective responsibilities differ: governance, instruction, ritual, military administration, and prohibitions throughout the realm. Reckoning all their subordinate personnel together yields nearly twenty-three thousand posts. As for the winter offices, their regulations are notably missing; the Three Dukes and Three Solitaries have not even been included in the listing.

Consider the Tang system: its establishment of offices includes six ministries—Personnel, Revenue, Rites, War, Justice, and Works. Their responsibilities encompass ordinances governing selection and appointment, merit distinctions and enfeoffment, performance evaluations, households and population, the well-field system, ceremonial observances, sacrifices, banquets, the presentation and examination of candidates, military guards, the selection and appointment of military officers, penal law, penal laborers and bondservants, scrutiny and review, restrictions at passes, the various crafts, agricultural colonies, and mountains and marshes. Beyond these were the four departments, the various directorates, courts and bureaus, the guards, and the staffs of the heir apparent and imperial princes. It was not merely a matter of providing a full complement of winter offices and establishing the Three Preceptors and Three Dukes.

Viewed together, some offices held concurrently under the Zhou retained their distinct titles and ranks under the Tang; some linked in subordinate relationships under the Zhou were separated into independent charges under the Tang; and some dispersed among the various states under the Zhou were brought together in a comprehensive compilation under the Tang. One cannot say that the Tang system departed entirely from antiquity. The Way rises and declines, and affairs vary in complexity. Thus the mere hundred officials of Tang and Yu were not too few when compared with the doubled number of offices under the Xia and Shang; nor were the many officials of the Zhou excessive when compared with the mere hundred of Tang and Yu. Moreover, since the Tang was already so far removed in time from the Zhou, could it uniformly be constrained by the Zhou…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
制邪執事所謂唐太宗觀會通而立政是
已夫制有迹也有意也太宗之所得者聖
人立民極之迹耳若聖人之意彼胡有得
哉是故愚甞謂讀周禮不可不讀周官何
也周官曰明王立政不惟其官惟其人又
曰官不必備惟其人盖建官在於得人不
在乎其備也若徒取其備則孔子所謂德
薄而位尊知小而謀大力小而任重者其
能免刑渥之羞乎若不主於得人則沈旣
===
濟所謂安行徐言非德空文善書非才累
資積考非勞者寧不乖銓選之法乎是必
有推賢讓能之訓崇功廣業之戒而後可
者故曰讀周禮不可不讀周官夫牧羊無
芻何益於牧建官者豈異此哉是故愚又
甞謂讀周官不可不讀立政何也立政曰
克知厥若丕乃俾亂又曰則克宅之克由
繹之盖有才而不盡用與無才同也惟不
知惟正是乂之道而任之不專斯有如陸
punctuated: 制邪？執事所謂唐太宗觀會通而立政，是已。夫制有迹也，有意也。太宗之所得者，聖人立民極之迹耳；若聖人之意，彼胡有得哉？是故愚甞謂讀《周禮》不可不讀《周官》。何也？《周官》曰：「明王立政，不惟其官，惟其人。」又曰：「官不必備，惟其人。」盖建官在於得人，不在乎其備也。若徒取其備，則孔子所謂「德薄而位尊，知小而謀大，力小而任重」者，其能免刑渥之羞乎？若不主於得人，則沈旣濟所謂「安行徐言非德，空文善書非才，累資積考非勞」者，寧不乖銓選之法乎？是必有推賢讓能之訓、崇功廣業之戒而後可者。故曰讀《周禮》不可不讀《周官》。夫牧羊無芻，何益於牧？建官者豈異此哉？是故愚又甞謂讀《周官》不可不讀《立政》。何也？《立政》曰：「克知厥若，丕乃俾亂。」又曰：「則克宅之，克由繹之。」盖有才而不盡用，與無才同也。惟不知惟正是乂之道，而任之不專，斯有如陸
translation_en: …institutions? This is precisely what you, sir, mean in saying that Emperor Taizong of the Tang established government by discerning how institutions interconnect and adapt to circumstances. Institutions have both outward forms and underlying intentions. What Taizong grasped was merely the outward form through which the sages established the highest standard for the people. How could he have grasped the sages’ intentions? Thus I have ventured to say that anyone reading the Rites of Zhou must also read “The Offices of Zhou” in the Book of Documents. Why? “The Offices of Zhou” says: “When an enlightened king establishes government, his concern is not with the offices but with the men.” It also says: “The offices need not all be filled; what matters is the men.” Establishing offices thus depends on obtaining suitable men, not on filling every position. If one merely seeks to fill them all, then those whom Confucius described as “slight in virtue yet exalted in rank, limited in understanding yet ambitious in their plans, weak in strength yet bearing heavy responsibilities”—can they escape the disgrace of severe punishment [?]? If obtaining suitable men is not the guiding concern, would this not violate the principles of official selection, as expressed by Shen Jiji: “A measured gait and slow speech are not virtue; empty compositions and fine calligraphy are not talent; accumulated seniority and successive evaluations are not meritorious service”? Only with the instruction to advance the worthy and yield to the capable, and the admonition to increase accomplishments and broaden undertakings, can this be done properly. Hence I say that anyone reading the Rites of Zhou must also read “The Offices of Zhou.” If one tends sheep without fodder, what benefit is there in tending them? How is establishing offices any different? Thus I have also ventured to say that anyone reading “The Offices of Zhou” must also read “Establishing Government.” Why? “Establishing Government” says: “He could recognize those who were suited to their tasks, and then fully entrusted government to them.” It also says: “Then he could settle them in their positions and employ them continuously.” Having talented men but failing to employ them fully is the same as having none. It is precisely through failing to understand the principle of governing through upright men, and through failing to give them undivided responsibility, that situations arise such as those described by Lu…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
贄所謂捨僉議而重已權廢公舉而行私
惠居常則求精太過有急則備位不充者
矣惟不知罔兼罔知之說而信之不篤斯
有如司馬光所謂有勤恪之臣悉心致力
以致其職在上疑之同列嫉之在下怨之
朝廷或以衆言而罰之則勤恪無不解體
者矣是以一則戒以勿間憸人一則戒以
勿誤獄慎而其意逺矣故曰讀周官不可
不讀立政也雖然衡鑑或迷妍媸曷辨知
===
恤豈無本哉德者本也周官之祗勤立政
之忱恂實明王建官之精蘊後世不本乎
此其始也定官職之品則防慮之未周頒
爵祿之制則磨礪之未至清入仕之路或
至銓選之未公開推薦之門或至資格之
未恢而建官於是乎無定制其卒也用術
以為知人之明陰察以為核實之功督責
以為勵精之治疑斥以為振起人才之道
而官於是乎為徒建彼唐太宗者雜流鳴
punctuated:
贄所謂「捨僉議而重已權，廢公舉而行私惠，居常則求精太過，有急則備位不充」者矣。惟不知「罔兼罔知」之說，而信之不篤，斯有如司馬光所謂「有勤恪之臣，悉心致力，以致其職，在上疑之，同列嫉之，在下怨之，朝廷或以衆言而罰之，則勤恪無不解體」者矣。是以一則戒以「勿間憸人」，一則戒以「勿誤獄慎」，而其意逺矣。故曰：讀《周官》不可不讀《立政》也。
雖然，衡鑑或迷，妍媸曷辨？知恤豈無本哉？德者，本也。《周官》之祗勤，《立政》之忱恂，實明王建官之精蘊。後世不本乎此，其始也，定官職之品，則防慮之未周；頒爵祿之制，則磨礪之未至；清入仕之路，或至銓選之未公；開推薦之門，或至資格之未恢。而建官於是乎無定制。其卒也，用術以為知人之明，陰察以為核實之功，督責以為勵精之治，疑斥以為振起人才之道，而官於是乎為徒建。彼唐太宗者，雜流鳴
translation_en:
…what Lu Zhi described as “setting aside collective deliberation and giving weight to one’s own authority, abandoning public nomination and dispensing private favors; in ordinary times, demanding perfection to excess, yet in emergencies, having too few men to fill the posts.” Only because rulers fail to understand the teaching of “neither taking everything upon oneself nor seeking to know everything,” and do not trust their officials firmly, does the situation arise that Sima Guang described: “There are diligent and conscientious ministers who devote all their thought and effort to fulfilling their duties, yet their superiors suspect them, their colleagues envy them, and their subordinates resent them. If the court punishes them on the strength of these many voices, none of the diligent and conscientious will fail to lose heart.” Thus, one passage warns, “Do not let petty men intervene,” and another warns, “Do not err in judicial matters; be cautious” [?]. Their meaning reaches far. Hence I say: one cannot read ‘The Officers of Zhou’ (Zhouguan) without also reading ‘Establishing Government’ (Lizheng).
Yet if the scales and mirror of judgment are sometimes unreliable, how can beauty and ugliness be distinguished? Surely discernment and solicitude must have a foundation? Virtue is that foundation. The reverent diligence of ‘The Officers of Zhou’ and the sincerity and trustfulness of ‘Establishing Government’ are indeed the essential principles by which enlightened kings established offices. Later generations did not take these as their foundation. At first, when fixing the grades of offices, they found their precautions insufficiently comprehensive; when promulgating systems of noble rank and official salary, they found the incentives insufficiently effective; when purifying the routes into official service, they might still fall short of impartiality in selection and appointment; when opening the way to recommendations, they might still fail to broaden eligibility. Thus, the establishment of offices came to have no settled system. In the end, they took the use of manipulative techniques for insight into men’s character, covert surveillance for effective verification of actual performance, relentless demands for energetic government, and suspicion and dismissal for a means of invigorating talented men. Offices were thus established in vain. As for Emperor Taizong of the Tang, men of miscellaneous backgrounds wore tinkling…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
玉玷列縉紳讒佞售姦間疏守道况慙德
閨門乏關雎麟趾之意兼行將相又無四
牡采薇之情乃欲取岩壁之殘書為粉飾
太平之具譬則跛匠眇目於持斤而曰規
矩準繩盡在是者可謂巧乎此臺閣之規
模雖定而禮樂終愧于成周郡邑之赤牒
雖省而治理僅止于李唐也記曰為政在
人取人以身修身以道修道以仁此萬世
建官之準則愚敢以為終篇獻
===
第三問
胡鰲
同考試官教諭徐批敬一格天脩省之大者
同考試官教授唐批條對中具見心學
考試官行人徐批古健
對天何以格曰心而已心何以存曰敬而
已敬何以主曰一而已夫一外無敬也敬
外無心也心外無天也凝一以主敬則動
靜合矣篤敬以存心則運用神矣存心以
punctuated:
玉，玷列縉紳；讒佞售姦，間疏守道。况慙德閨門，乏《關雎》《麟趾》之意；兼行將相，又無《四牡》《采薇》之情。乃欲取岩壁之殘書，為粉飾太平之具，譬則跛匠眇目於持斤，而曰：「規矩準繩盡在是。」者，可謂巧乎？此臺閣之規模雖定，而禮樂終愧于成周；郡邑之赤牒雖省，而治理僅止于李唐也。《記》曰：「為政在人，取人以身，修身以道，修道以仁。」此萬世建官之準則，愚敢以為終篇獻。

第三問
胡鰲
同考試官教諭徐批：敬一格天，脩省之大者。
同考試官教授唐批：條對中具見心學。
考試官行人徐批：古健。

對：天何以格？曰：心而已。心何以存？曰：敬而已。敬何以主？曰：一而已。夫一外無敬也，敬外無心也，心外無天也。凝一以主敬，則動靜合矣；篤敬以存心，則運用神矣；存心以
translation_en:
…jade pendants, sullying the ranks of the official elite; slanderers and flatterers carried out their wicked schemes, alienating those who upheld the Way. Moreover, his conduct within his household was shameful, lacking the spirit of “The Ospreys” (Guanju) and “The Qilin’s Hoofs” (Linzhi). In his employment of generals and chief ministers, he likewise lacked the sentiments expressed in “The Four Steeds” (Simu) and “Gathering Ferns” (Caiwei). Yet he wished to take fragmentary writings from rocky walls and use them to embellish the appearance of peace. This was like a lame, one-eyed carpenter wielding an axe and declaring, “The compass, square, level, and marking cord are all here.” Could he be called skillful? Thus, although the organization of the central administration was established, its rites and music remained inferior to those of the perfected Zhou; although the red documents [?] of the prefectures and counties were reduced, its achievements in government went no further than those of the Li house’s Tang dynasty. The Record of Rites says: “Government depends on men. One obtains men through one’s own person, cultivates one’s person through the Way, and cultivates the Way through benevolence.” This is the standard for establishing offices for all ages. I venture to offer it as the conclusion of this essay.

Third Policy Question
Hu Ao
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Reverent single-mindedness reaches Heaven: this is the great task of self-cultivation and self-examination.”
Associate Examiner Tang, Professor, comments: “Throughout his answers to the several points, his learning of the mind is fully evident.”
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “Classical and vigorous.”

Response: By what means does one reach Heaven? The answer is: the mind alone. By what means does one preserve the mind? The answer is: reverence alone. By what means does one maintain reverence? The answer is: single-mindedness alone. For apart from single-mindedness there is no reverence; apart from reverence there is no mind; apart from the mind there is no Heaven. Concentrate on unity to maintain reverence, and activity and stillness become one. Deepen reverence to preserve the mind, and its functioning becomes wondrous. Preserve the mind in order to…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
格天則轉異為祥矣斯道也以觀古今而
進退在我以察上下而彌綸在我以律政
紀而權衡在我以裨化理而參賛在我大
哉要乎其
皇上所自得者乎彗星之異執事為
皇上慮也愚為
皇上喜也夫憂樂而樂憂得無近佞矣乎夫有
所受之也詩曰天監在玆言天也無貳爾
心言心也聖敬日躋言敬也純一不已言
===
一也是故君人者無問其在天者惟守其
在我者盖天之未始不為人而人之未始
不為天也天定能勝人而人定尤能勝天
也天之示人者祥異而已矣君之格天者
敬一而已矣昔者水於唐堯之天未定也
兢兢以格之而啓時雍之治旱於商湯之
天未定也慄慄以格之而垂允殖之休是
豈災之不足懼而憂之可喜哉盖敬一則
心存心存則天格天且弗違而況於人乎
punctuated: 格天，則轉異為祥矣。斯道也，以觀古今而進退在我，以察上下而彌綸在我，以律政紀而權衡在我，以裨化理而參賛在我。大哉！要乎！其皇上所自得者乎！彗星之異，執事為皇上慮也，愚為皇上喜也。夫憂樂而樂憂，得無近佞矣乎？夫有所受之也。詩曰：「天監在玆」，言天也；「無貳爾心」，言心也；「聖敬日躋」，言敬也；「純一不已」，言一也。是故君人者，無問其在天者，惟守其在我者。盖天之未始不為人，而人之未始不為天也。天定能勝人，而人定尤能勝天也。天之示人者，祥異而已矣；君之格天者，敬一而已矣。昔者，水於唐堯之天未定也，兢兢以格之，而啓時雍之治；旱於商湯之天未定也，慄慄以格之，而垂允殖之休。是豈災之不足懼，而憂之可喜哉？盖敬一則心存，心存則天格。天且弗違，而況於人乎？
translation_en:
…to move Heaven, inauspicious portents will be transformed into auspicious ones. Through this Way, when considering past and present, the decision to advance or withdraw rests with oneself; when examining what is above and below, the ability to encompass and order it rests with oneself; when regulating governmental order, the power to weigh and judge rests with oneself; and when assisting moral transformation and good government, the capacity to participate and help rests with oneself. How great it is! How essential! Surely this is what His Majesty has grasped for himself! Concerning the portent of the comet, you gentlemen worry on His Majesty’s behalf, while I, in my humble view, rejoice for him. To grieve at joy and rejoice at grief—does this not verge on flattery? Yet there is an inherited teaching behind it. The Book of Odes says, “Heaven watches over us here”: this speaks of Heaven; “Let there be no duplicity in your heart”: this speaks of the heart; “His sagely reverence daily ascended”: this speaks of reverence; “Pure singleness without cease”: this speaks of singleness.

Thus, one who rules others need not inquire into what rests with Heaven, but should preserve what rests with oneself. For Heaven has never ceased to act for humanity, and humanity has never ceased to act for Heaven. When Heaven is settled, it can prevail over humanity; when humanity is settled, it can all the more prevail over Heaven. What Heaven shows humanity consists only of auspicious signs and anomalous portents; what a ruler uses to move Heaven consists only of reverence and singleness. Formerly, the floods in the time of Tang Yao occurred before Heaven’s course was settled. Through vigilance and awe he moved Heaven, inaugurating an age of harmonious government. The drought in the time of Shang Tang likewise occurred before Heaven’s course was settled. Through trembling reverence he moved Heaven, bequeathing the blessing of enduring prosperity. Does this mean that calamities are insufficient cause for fear, or that grounds for anxiety are cause for rejoicing? Rather, through reverence and singleness the heart is preserved; when the heart is preserved, Heaven is moved. If even Heaven does not oppose him, how much less will human beings! …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
而况於鬼神乎是故高宗之雊雉宣王之
旱魃天於中興之賢君有拳拳焉而其異
也亦甚矣然一則恭默而思道憲天而正
事一則側身而脩行任賢而使能存是心
以格之而天者定矣彗星之異也或見于
漢文宣光三帝或見于唐太玄憲三宗或
見於宋太祖太宗仁宗天於希世之賢君
若數數焉而其異也亦屢矣然數君者玄
默而勵精也恢廓而大度也寬仁而果斷
===
也恭儉而仁恕也存是心以格之而天者
亦定矣以創大業以美中興以光簡冊則
夫譴告之者謂非仁愛之乎即是而觀則
春秋左氏之紀明是道者也申繻高堂隆
之說昧是道者也吕公著程頤富弼吕大
防吕大鈞邢恕王安禮陳禾吕好問王襄
諸臣之疏又皆以扶翼斯道者也此世治
所以隆汙化理所以淳薄立言所以得失
心術所以邪正造物所以從違灼乎判矣
punctuated: 而况於鬼神乎？是故高宗之雊雉、宣王之旱魃，天於中興之賢君有拳拳焉，而其異也亦甚矣。然一則恭默而思道，憲天而正事；一則側身而脩行，任賢而使能。存是心以格之，而天者定矣。彗星之異也，或見于漢文、宣、光三帝，或見于唐太、玄、憲三宗，或見於宋太祖、太宗、仁宗。天於希世之賢君若數數焉，而其異也亦屢矣。然數君者，玄默而勵精也，恢廓而大度也，寬仁而果斷也，恭儉而仁恕也。存是心以格之，而天者亦定矣。以創大業，以美中興，以光簡冊，則夫譴告之者，謂非仁愛之乎？即是而觀，則《春秋左氏》之紀，明是道者也；申繻、高堂隆之說，昧是道者也；吕公著、程頤、富弼、吕大防、吕大鈞、邢恕、王安禮、陳禾、吕好問、王襄諸臣之疏，又皆以扶翼斯道者也。此世治所以隆汙、化理所以淳薄、立言所以得失、心術所以邪正、造物所以從違，灼乎判矣。
translation_en:
…and how much more so the ghosts and spirits? Thus, in the cases of the crowing pheasant under Gaozong and the drought demon under King Xuan, Heaven showed earnest concern for worthy rulers who restored their dynasties, yet its portents were also severe. One ruler remained reverently silent and reflected upon the Way, taking Heaven as his model and setting affairs right; the other humbled himself and cultivated his conduct, appointing the worthy and employing the capable. They preserved this disposition of mind to move Heaven, and Heaven became settled.

As for the portent of comets, these appeared under the three Han emperors Wen, Xuan, and Guangwu; under the three Tang emperors Taizong, Xuanzong, and Xianzong; and under the Song emperors Taizu, Taizong, and Renzong. Heaven seemed repeatedly to admonish these worthy rulers, rare in any age, and its portents likewise appeared frequently. Yet these rulers were inwardly tranquil while striving with full dedication, broad-minded and magnanimous, generous and humane yet decisive, reverent and frugal, benevolent and forgiving. They preserved this disposition of mind to move Heaven, and Heaven likewise became settled. Through this they founded great enterprises, brought distinction to dynastic restorations, and illuminated the historical records. Can one then say that Heaven’s rebukes and warnings were not expressions of benevolent love for them?

Viewed in this light, the accounts in Zuo’s Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals illuminate this Way, while the explanations of Shen Xu and Gaotang Long fail to comprehend it. The memorials of such ministers as Lü Gongzhu, Cheng Yi, Fu Bi, Lü Dafang, Lü Dajun, Xing Shu, Wang Anli, Chen He, Lü Haowen, and Wang Xiang all serve to uphold and assist this Way. Thus the reasons why governance flourishes or declines, why moral transformation and order are substantial or shallow, why pronouncements are sound or mistaken, why the workings of the mind are deviant or upright, and why the Creator accords with or opposes human endeavors stand clearly distinguished.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
君心之外果有天乎果無天乎敬一之外
抑有格乎抑無格乎可監也已我
皇上涖極以來稟英明純粹之資極仁孝誠敬
之德敬一有箴存心至矣五箴有釋主敬
至矣
郊壇
世廟有享格天至矣存神過化天地同流大政
宏綱膾炙千古足以陋漢唐宋于下風矣
由是禱雨而雨零祈雪而雪集甘露降黃
===
河清僉曰吾
君之祥也愚則曰天欲其敬一而已矣又由是
而山川或未寧蝗蝝或未息而彗星偶見
僉曰吾
君之異也愚則曰天欲其敬一而已矣夫敬一
者而豈徒哉喜怒哀樂心之發也用舍予
奪心之則也典章文物心之著也禮樂法
度心之推也弗純則雜雜則二弗嚴則肆
肆則隳惟二與隳非存心也是故存心於
punctuated: 君心之外，果有天乎？果無天乎？敬一之外，抑有格乎？抑無格乎？可監也已。我皇上涖極以來，稟英明純粹之資，極仁孝誠敬之德。敬一有箴，存心至矣；五箴有釋，主敬至矣；郊壇、世廟有享，格天至矣。存神過化，天地同流。大政宏綱，膾炙千古，足以陋漢唐宋于下風矣。由是禱雨而雨零，祈雪而雪集，甘露降，黃河清，僉曰：「吾君之祥也。」愚則曰：「天欲其敬一而已矣。」又由是而山川或未寧，蝗蝝或未息，而彗星偶見，僉曰：「吾君之異也。」愚則曰：「天欲其敬一而已矣。」夫敬一者，而豈徒哉？喜怒哀樂，心之發也；用舍予奪，心之則也；典章文物，心之著也；禮樂法度，心之推也。弗純則雜，雜則二；弗嚴則肆，肆則隳。惟二與隳，非存心也。是故存心於
translation_en:
Beyond the ruler’s heart, does Heaven indeed exist, or does it not? Beyond reverent unity, is there a way to reach Heaven, or is there not? Here indeed is a lesson to heed.

Since Our August Sovereign ascended the throne, he has brought his endowed brilliance and purity to bear and perfected the virtues of benevolence, filial piety, sincerity, and reverence. With his Admonition on Reverent Unity, he has carried preservation of the heart to its utmost; with his explanations of the Five Admonitions, he has carried the cultivation of reverence to its utmost; with offerings at the suburban altar and the Temple of the Imperial Father, he has carried communion with Heaven to its utmost. Wherever he abides, his influence is spiritual; wherever he passes, transformation follows: he moves in the same current as Heaven and Earth. His great policies and broad principles will be celebrated through the ages, sufficient to make the Han, Tang, and Song appear inferior and leave them far behind.

Thus, when he prays for rain, rain falls; when he prays for snow, snow gathers. Sweet dew descends, and the Huang He runs clear. All say, “These are auspicious signs for our ruler.” I, in my ignorance, say, “Heaven wishes only that he maintain reverent unity.” Yet when mountains and rivers are at times unsettled, locusts and their young have not ceased their ravages, and a comet occasionally appears, all say, “These are ominous signs for our ruler.” I, in my ignorance, say, “Heaven wishes only that he maintain reverent unity.”

How could reverent unity be an empty exercise? Joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure are the heart’s expressions; employing or dismissing, granting or taking away, are the heart’s standards in action; institutions and cultural forms are the heart made manifest; rites, music, laws, and regulations are the heart extended into practice. Without purity there is admixture, and admixture brings division; without strictness there is laxity, and laxity brings collapse. Division and collapse are no preservation of the heart. Therefore, preserving the heart in …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
宥密者毋徒克謹之文而已必不蔽不惑
如程頣所謂而後可治本緩末如呂大防
所謂而後可得人省費如呂大鈞所謂而
後可法祖致治如王襄所謂而後可以是
存心殆媲美于商周矣賛佐於
廟廊者不但脩輔之故而已也必内外無乖擾
之失如吕公著之說左右絕朋黨之私如
王安禮之說戒成鍛鍊如邢恕之說戒趨
時迎合如陳并之說以是賛佐追商周而
===
無讓焉愚見內外交脩上下恭敬敬與心
一心與天一天與我一喘息呼吸氣通乎
微闔闢弛張自作元命中庸位育之功大
易裁成之道禮運諸福之祥胥此焉在承
天休而延
寶祚萬世之業也抑何彗之足憂哉故愚願
皇上之敬一也勿以彗為有無勿以祥為敬怠
允執其要惟盡吾事而已昔董仲舒以災
異之来為天心仁愛愚敢以是為
punctuated:
宥密者，毋徒克謹之文而已，必不蔽不惑，如程頣所謂而後可；治本緩末，如呂大防所謂而後可；得人省費，如呂大鈞所謂而後可；法祖致治，如王襄所謂而後可。以是存心，殆媲美于商周矣。賛佐於廟廊者，不但脩輔之故而已也，必内外無乖擾之失，如吕公著之說；左右絕朋黨之私，如王安禮之說；戒成鍛鍊，如邢恕之說；戒趨時迎合，如陳并之說。以是賛佐，追商周而無讓焉。
愚見內外交脩，上下恭敬，敬與心一，心與天一，天與我一，喘息呼吸，氣通乎微；闔闢弛張，自作元命。《中庸》位育之功，《大易》裁成之道，《禮運》諸福之祥，胥此焉在。承天休而延寶祚，萬世之業也。抑何彗之足憂哉？故愚願皇上之敬一也，勿以彗為有無，勿以祥為敬怠，允執其要，惟盡吾事而已。昔董仲舒以災異之来為天心仁愛，愚敢以是為
translation_en:
…those who preserve their minds in profound stillness must not stop at the outward forms of conscientious care. They must be neither blinded nor deluded, as Cheng Yi said; only then will this suffice. They must attend to the root and give secondary matters less urgency, as Lü Dafang said; only then will this suffice. They must obtain worthy men and reduce expenditure, as Lü Dajun said; only then will this suffice. They must emulate their ancestors and achieve good government, as Wang Xiang said; only then will this suffice. Preserving the mind in this way, they may well rival the excellence of the Shang and Zhou. Those who assist at court must likewise do more than follow established practices of cultivating themselves and assisting their ruler. They must ensure that neither within nor outside the court are there failings of discord and disturbance, as Lü Gongzhu urged; eliminate the selfish interests of factions among the ruler’s attendants, as Wang Anli urged; guard against fabricating charges [?], as Xing Shu urged; and guard against following prevailing fashions and ingratiating themselves, as Chen Bing urged. Assisting in this way, they will match the Shang and Zhou without yielding anything to them.
In my humble view, when those within and outside the court cultivate themselves together, and those above and below are respectful and reverent, reverence becomes one with the mind, the mind one with Heaven, and Heaven one with oneself. With every breath, vital energy communicates with the subtlest workings; through opening and closing, relaxation and tension, one fashions one’s own great mandate. The achievement of placing Heaven and Earth in their proper positions and nurturing all things, described in the Doctrine of the Mean; the way of shaping and completing things, described in the Great Book of Changes; and the auspicious signs of manifold blessings described in the “Evolution of Rites”—all are found here. Receiving Heaven’s favor and prolonging the imperial succession constitute an undertaking for ten thousand generations. Why, then, should a comet be cause for concern? Thus I humbly hope that Your Majesty’s reverent singleness of purpose will neither depend on a comet’s presence or absence nor become more diligent or lax according to auspicious signs.
