Truly grasp what is essential, and simply fulfill what falls to us to do. Formerly, Dong Zhongshu regarded the coming of disasters and anomalies as an expression of Heaven’s benevolent love. I venture to take this as…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
今日喜謹對
第四問
蔡完
同考試官學正劉批守
當代之法而能通其變此有據之說
考試官行人徐批識時務
經國者有一定之法法外之意而後享其
利于不窮夫利之不窮法與意為之也法
不定則無執守之素而或至於弊法定矣
===
而不得其意則無通變之宜而或至於拘
斯二者皆過也其可以享利乎是故守常
者洪其源者也通變者續其流者也源洪
而不可塞流續而不可禦久大之業于是
焉在謂非
國家無窮之利也哉漕運一策執事所以謀
國者甚深慮事者甚遠非區區所能測識
者雖然豈敢以終默哉夫天下之法每患
其弗能行而其行也則患其弗能繼非弗
punctuated:
今日喜。謹對。

第四問
蔡完

同考試官學正劉批：守當代之法而能通其變，此有據之說。

考試官行人徐批：識時務。

經國者有一定之法，法外之意，而後享其利于不窮。夫利之不窮，法與意為之也。法不定，則無執守之素，而或至於弊；法定矣，而不得其意，則無通變之宜，而或至於拘。斯二者皆過也，其可以享利乎？是故守常者，洪其源者也；通變者，續其流者也。源洪而不可塞，流續而不可禦，久大之業于是焉在，謂非國家無窮之利也哉？漕運一策，執事所以謀國者甚深，慮事者甚遠，非區區所能測識者。雖然，豈敢以終默哉？夫天下之法，每患其弗能行，而其行也，則患其弗能繼。非弗
translation_en:
…an occasion for joy today. I respectfully submit this reply.

Fourth Question
Cai Wan

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, School Instructor: He upholds the laws of the present dynasty while understanding how to adapt them to changing circumstances. This is a well-grounded argument.

Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: He understands the needs of the times.

Those who administer the state have fixed laws and an understanding that reaches beyond those laws [?]; only then can they enjoy their benefits without end. Such enduring benefits arise from both the laws and their underlying intent. If the laws are not fixed, there is no established basis to uphold, and abuses may result. If the laws are fixed but their intent is not understood, there is no appropriate means of adapting to change, and rigidity may result. Both are errors: how could either yield benefits? Thus, upholding established principles enlarges the source, while adapting to change sustains the flow. When the source is abundant and cannot be blocked, and the flow continues and cannot be checked, an enduring and great undertaking rests upon them. Can this be called anything other than an inexhaustible benefit to the state?

In this policy question on grain transport, your planning for the state is exceedingly profound, and your consideration of affairs exceedingly far-reaching—beyond what someone of my modest abilities can fathom. Nevertheless, how could I dare remain silent throughout? With the laws of the realm, the recurring concern is that they cannot be put into effect; once they are put into effect, the concern is that they cannot be sustained. It is not that they cannot…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
繼也時勢爾也所貴乎君子有通變之意
焉耳易曰制而用之存乎法推而行之存
乎通夫通所以行也法之意也且漕運孰
始乎王者重九年之食而所于起禹貢詳
九州之貢而駸駸乎盛矣然必貢道通而
後田賦入則漕運為儲蓄之自也固宜夫
漢唐都關中三面阻守之地也或悉仰乎
山東或兼仰乎江淮然其路則止於河渭
而已宋都汴梁四通八達之區也或自汴
===
河黃河而來或自惠民廣濟而至要其路
則凡四而已至元都燕獨用海運之法焉
浙米由浙而入海江米由江而入海自是
達于直沽而運者可歲至矣是法也既省
夫兌支之耗且免夫牽輓之勞倡議于伯
顏成事于朱清張瑄而元史謂為一代良
法所得蓋多其有見矣夫海運之便固也
若鄧艾耕淮南湖蕩之田以兼屯守若熈
寧墾坊監空餘之地以理稼政至元虞集
punctuated: 繼也，時勢爾也。所貴乎君子有通變之意焉耳。《易》曰：「制而用之存乎法，推而行之存乎通。」夫通，所以行也，法之意也。且漕運孰始乎？王者重九年之食，而所于起，禹貢詳九州之貢，而駸駸乎盛矣。然必貢道通而後田賦入，則漕運為儲蓄之自也，固宜。夫漢唐都關中，三面阻守之地也，或悉仰乎山東，或兼仰乎江淮，然其路則止於河渭而已。宋都汴梁，四通八達之區也，或自汴河、黃河而來，或自惠民、廣濟而至，要其路則凡四而已。至元都燕，獨用海運之法焉。浙米由浙而入海，江米由江而入海，自是達于直沽，而運者可歲至矣。是法也，既省夫兌支之耗，且免夫牽輓之勞，倡議于伯顏，成事于朱清、張瑄，而《元史》謂為一代良法，所得蓋多，其有見矣。夫海運之便，固也。若鄧艾耕淮南湖蕩之田，以兼屯守；若熈寧墾坊監空餘之地，以理稼政；至元虞集
translation_en:
…continue: it is merely a matter of the circumstances of the times. What is valued in the gentleman is simply his willingness to adapt to change. The Book of Changes says: “Regulating and using it depends on rules; extending and putting it into practice depends on adaptability.” Adaptability makes implementation possible and fulfills the intent of the rules. Moreover, where did grain transport originate? The ancient kings valued a nine-year supply of grain, and it originated from this [?]. The Tribute of Yu details the tribute of the nine provinces, and the practice steadily flourished. Yet only when the tribute routes were open could the land tax come in; it is therefore fitting that grain transport should be the source of stored reserves.

The Han and Tang established their capitals in Guanzhong, a region protected by natural barriers on three sides. They either depended entirely on Shandong or also drew upon Jianghuai, but their transport routes extended only along the Yellow and Wei rivers. The Song established their capital at Bianliang, a place accessible from every direction. Shipments came either along the Bian and Yellow rivers or by the Huimin and Guangji canals; in all, there were just four routes. When the Yuan established their capital at Yan, they relied exclusively on sea transport. Grain from Zhe entered the sea by way of Zhe, and grain from Jiang entered the sea by way of Jiang. From there it reached Zhigu, and shipments could arrive every year. This method reduced losses in the exchange and disbursement of grain and spared the labor of towing. Proposed by Boyan and brought to fruition by Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan, it was described in the History of the Yuan as an excellent system of that dynasty. Its benefits were indeed considerable, and this assessment showed discernment.

The advantages of sea transport are undeniable. There were also such examples as Deng Ai cultivating the lake and marsh lands of Huainan while maintaining garrison defenses, and the reclamation, during the Xining era, of unused lands belonging to the horse pastures and directorates to put agricultural administration in order. By Yuan times, Yu Ji…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
又有海田之法焉取瀕海之地而築堤以
捍潮設世襲之格而分給以行賞由是漸
征而京師之儲可充矣之數法也皆足以
壯朝廷之勢而供兵食之需者也惜其僅
行于一時而不得盡舉于當日所謂寛民
力省漕費者得無遺恨也哉是故法立也
而尤不可無法外意也通其意弗泥其法
因乎時弗窒乎勢天啓其大利者不有待
于
===
今日乎我
祖宗以天授神聖之資定萬世常行之策自永
樂以来罷海舟而漕會通河則水陸安而
所以輸積于
京師者裕如也而漕法精矣定土壤而成賦
稅則財之出於五方者崇如也而賦法精
矣其良法美意度越千古有非歷代之可
及也抑何資於海運諸議乎哉而執事顧
猶拳拳焉者盖以
punctuated:
又有海田之法焉，取瀕海之地而築堤以捍潮，設世襲之格而分給以行賞，由是漸征而京師之儲可充矣。之數法也，皆足以壯朝廷之勢而供兵食之需者也。惜其僅行于一時，而不得盡舉于當日，所謂寛民力、省漕費者，得無遺恨也哉？是故法立也，而尤不可無法外意也。通其意，弗泥其法；因乎時，弗窒乎勢。天啓其大利者，不有待于今日乎？

我祖宗以天授神聖之資，定萬世常行之策。自永樂以来，罷海舟而漕會通河，則水陸安，而所以輸積于京師者裕如也，而漕法精矣；定土壤而成賦稅，則財之出於五方者崇如也，而賦法精矣。其良法美意，度越千古，有非歷代之可及也。抑何資於海運諸議乎哉？而執事顧猶拳拳焉者，盖以
translation_en:
…there was also a method of cultivating coastal lands: take land along the coast and build embankments to hold back the tides, establish rules for hereditary tenure, and distribute the land as rewards. Taxes could then gradually be levied, replenishing the capital’s reserves. These several methods [?] were all sufficient to strengthen the court’s position and meet the army’s need for provisions. It is regrettable that they were implemented only for a time and could not all be put into effect in their day. Regarding the stated aims of easing the people’s burdens and reducing grain-transport expenses, could this fail to leave cause for regret? Thus, when regulations are established, it is especially essential to retain a sense of their purpose beyond their explicit provisions. Grasp their intent without clinging rigidly to their forms; adapt to the times without being hemmed in by circumstances. Have not the great benefits that Heaven would reveal awaited this very day?

Our imperial ancestors, endowed by Heaven with sagely and divine gifts, established policies to be followed perpetually through myriad generations. Since the Yongle reign, seaborne transport has been discontinued and grain shipped along the Huitong Canal. Routes by water and land have thus been secure, and ample supplies have been transported to and stored in the capital: the grain-transport system has been perfected. By classifying soils and establishing tax assessments, abundant revenue has been obtained from all five regions: the taxation system has been perfected. These excellent institutions and benevolent intentions surpass those of all antiquity, reaching heights beyond the attainments of successive dynasties. What need, then, is there to draw upon the various proposals for maritime transport? Yet you, sir, remain deeply concerned with them, presumably because…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
京師猶人身也會通河猶咽喉也咽喉寧保
其無梗乎是故海運不可廢惟
聖明斷自
宸衷見其可也然後經始兩浙自平江劉家港
以至海門開洋以至成山上海以至楊村
皆募人以導之而造船按試焉行之既熟
則雖有不測之虞可以交發而互至而丘
文莊之議是或一道也
京師譬富室也墾田譬附郭也附郭其可以
===
弗穫乎是故墾田不可廢惟
聖明參諸眾論行之當也然後間命守臣自淮
南以及壽頴遼海以及青齊太僕以及監
苑空地皆設官以理之而勸農力穡焉田
之既成則必享豐登之慶足以居安而慮
危而丘文莊之說未必厚誣者矣夫主之
以會通河輔之以海運經之以常賦緯之
以墾田並行不悖以利國而利民也
國家萬世之業其在乎此嗚呼古今勢也推
punctuated:
京師猶人身也，會通河猶咽喉也，咽喉寧保其無梗乎？是故海運不可廢。惟聖明斷自宸衷，見其可也，然後經始兩浙，自平江劉家港以至海門，開洋以至成山，上海以至楊村，皆募人以導之，而造船按試焉。行之既熟，則雖有不測之虞，可以交發而互至，而丘文莊之議，是或一道也。
京師譬富室也，墾田譬附郭也，附郭其可以弗穫乎？是故墾田不可廢。惟聖明參諸眾論，行之當也，然後間命守臣，自淮南以及壽頴，遼海以及青齊，太僕以及監苑空地，皆設官以理之，而勸農力穡焉。田之既成，則必享豐登之慶，足以居安而慮危，而丘文莊之說，未必厚誣者矣。夫主之以會通河，輔之以海運，經之以常賦，緯之以墾田，並行不悖，以利國而利民也。國家萬世之業，其在乎此！嗚呼！古今勢也，推
translation_en:
…the capital is like the human body, and the Huitong Canal is like its throat. Can one guarantee that the throat will never become obstructed? Thus transport by sea must not be abandoned. Only when Your sagely and enlightened Majesty has decided within your imperial heart and judged it practicable should preparations begin in Liangzhe. From Liujiagang in Pingjiang to Haimen, out onto the open sea as far as Chengshan, and from Shanghai to Yangcun [?], men should be recruited throughout to guide the passage, and ships built, inspected, and tested. Once operations are well practiced, even if unforeseen difficulties arise, shipments can depart by alternate routes and arrive in turn. Qiu Wenzhuang’s proposal may thus offer one way forward.
The capital may be compared to a wealthy household, and land reclamation to its fields adjoining the city walls. Can such fields be left unharvested? Thus land reclamation must not be abandoned. Only when Your sagely and enlightened Majesty has considered the various opinions and judged implementation appropriate should orders then be issued from time to time to the officials responsible for these territories. From Huainan to Shou and Ying, from Liaohai to Qing and Qi, and on vacant lands belonging to the Court of the Imperial Stud and the horse-pasture administrations, officials should be appointed to manage the work and encourage farmers to devote their efforts to cultivation. Once the fields have been established, abundant harvests will surely bring blessings, enabling us to prepare for danger while living in security. Qiu Wenzhuang’s argument, then, need not be dismissed as grossly unfounded. Make the Huitong Canal the mainstay and sea transport its supplement; take regular tax revenues as the warp and land reclamation as the weft. Let them operate together without conflict, benefiting both the state and the people. Surely herein lies the foundation of the state’s enterprise for ten thousand generations! Ah! Antiquity and the present have their respective circumstances; carrying forward…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
行時也經常法也變通意也用而利焉通
之爾也是故寒暑推而歲成焉屈伸感而
利生焉天道之利者一通而已矣知周而
道濟焉旁行而不流焉聖人之利者亦通
而已矣變通以宜民鼓舞以盡利非
皇上之至神至聖其孰能與于此而或者謂海
運乃勝國之遺無以彰
盛世而諸議瑣瑣皆李悝緒餘曾若王政之皞
皞也不知天地之氣有開必先何忌于勝
===
國而古篋之良方取其奏效足矣況自古
及今甞行之而既效者乎易曰神而明之
存乎其人芹曝之忱亦惟
廟堂加之意而已
第五問
龔卿
同考試官教諭韓批憂深言切子其悉湖湘
利害者歟
同考試官教諭黃批不泥不疎
punctuated:
行，時也；經常，法也；變通，意也。用而利焉，通之爾也。是故寒暑推而歲成焉，屈伸感而利生焉。天道之利者，一通而已矣。知周而道濟焉，旁行而不流焉。聖人之利者，亦通而已矣。變通以宜民，鼓舞以盡利，非皇上之至神至聖，其孰能與于此？而或者謂海運乃勝國之遺，無以彰盛世，而諸議瑣瑣，皆李悝緒餘，曾若王政之皞皞也？不知天地之氣，有開必先，何忌于勝國？而古篋之良方，取其奏效足矣。況自古及今甞行之而既效者乎？《易》曰：「神而明之，存乎其人。」芹曝之忱，亦惟廟堂加之意而已。
第五問
龔卿
同考試官教諭韓批：「憂深言切，子其悉湖湘利害者歟？」
同考試官教諭黃批：「不泥不疎。」
translation_en:
…implementation depends on timing; established practice supplies the rules; adaptation expresses their intent. That their application brings benefit is simply a matter of making them work through changing circumstances. Thus cold and heat succeed one another, completing the year; contraction and expansion interact, producing benefits. The benefits of the Way of Heaven amount simply to this responsive interchange. With knowledge encompassing all things and the Way bringing aid to all, the sage acts in every direction without going astray. The benefits conferred by the sage likewise amount simply to such adaptability. To adapt institutions to the people's needs and inspire them to realize every benefit—who could accomplish this without Your Majesty's supreme spiritual insight and sagacity?
Some, however, say that maritime transport is a legacy of the vanquished dynasty and cannot glorify our flourishing age; that all these petty proposals are merely remnants of Li Kui's teachings, hardly comparable to the expansive blessings of kingly government. They do not understand that, in the vital workings of Heaven and Earth, every new development has its antecedents. Why shun something because it comes from the vanquished dynasty? A good prescription found in an old chest need only prove effective. How much more does this apply to measures practiced from antiquity to the present whose effectiveness has already been demonstrated! The Book of Changes says: “Making it spiritually efficacious and illuminating it rests with the person.” With the humble sincerity of one offering celery or the warmth of the sun, I ask only that the court give these matters its attention.
Fifth Question
Gong Qing
Associate Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: “Your concern is profound and your words earnest. Surely you are thoroughly acquainted with what benefits and harms Huxiang?”
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Neither rigid nor superficial.”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教授陳批意見超然
考試官行人徐批善區處
君子之均夫民也綏之而已矣制之而已
矣盖人以安居為樂以財足為生不陷於
刑戮為慶是人心所同然也惟爭趨於利
斯强暴譸張者出矣苟吾之所以均之者
泥之乎一定之迹無以綏之制之則不惟
生聚長養未能即遂而斯民之擾擾何由
息乎是不可不加之意也流民雜寓客户
===
凌主今日為政在所必處者執事以此下
詢豈非以愚生長是邦或知居安來撫之
策哉嘗聞醫之於病也必先有以達其致
病之原而後可以施治病之藥病之入人
乘乎其元氣之虛庸醫者不究其五臟之
受疹毒也而悉以急攻卒治之劑决癰疽
而必除之可乎哉治流民者何以異此是
故荆楚天地之要區其地廣濶其利富饒
固宜其五方之雜聚也乃至今日而成凌
punctuated:
同考試官教授陳批：意見超然。
考試官行人徐批：善區處。
君子之均夫民也，綏之而已矣，制之而已矣。盖人以安居為樂，以財足為生，不陷於刑戮為慶，是人心所同然也。惟爭趨於利，斯强暴譸張者出矣。苟吾之所以均之者，泥之乎一定之迹，無以綏之制之，則不惟生聚長養未能即遂，而斯民之擾擾何由息乎？是不可不加之意也。流民雜寓，客户凌主，今日為政在所必處者。執事以此下詢，豈非以愚生長是邦，或知居安來撫之策哉？嘗聞醫之於病也，必先有以達其致病之原，而後可以施治病之藥。病之入人，乘乎其元氣之虛。庸醫者不究其五臟之受疹毒也，而悉以急攻卒治之劑，决癰疽而必除之，可乎哉？治流民者何以異此？是故荆楚，天地之要區，其地廣濶，其利富饒，固宜其五方之雜聚也。乃至今日而成凌
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, an instructor: “An uncommon breadth of vision.”
Comment by Examiner Xu, a messenger: “Skillful in arranging appropriate measures.”
When the gentleman brings order and equity to the people, he need only settle them in peace and regulate them. People take pleasure in a secure home, depend on sufficient wealth for their livelihood, and count themselves fortunate to escape punishment and execution: these feelings are common to all human hearts. It is when people compete in pursuit of profit that the strong, violent, and deceitful emerge. If the means by which we bring order and equity to them are confined to a single fixed pattern, with no means of settling and regulating them, then not only will their livelihood and nurture fail to prosper promptly, but how can their unrest ever cease? This demands careful attention. Displaced people lodging among the inhabitants, and guest households overbearing the established residents, are matters that those governing today must address. In putting this question to me, do you not suppose that, having been born and raised in this region, I might know some policy for securing those already settled and reassuring newcomers?
I have heard that, in treating illness, a physician must first comprehend its source before administering a remedy. Illness enters a person by taking advantage of a weakness in the vital energy. An inept physician does not investigate how the five internal organs have been afflicted by disease and poison, but applies drastic, hasty remedies to every case, lancing abscesses and insisting on removing them. Can this be acceptable? How does dealing with displaced people differ from this?
Thus Jingchu is a strategically important region of the realm. Its lands are extensive and its resources abundant; it is only natural that people from all five directions should gather and mingle there. Yet that today this has developed into a situation in which they overbear …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
主之勢者殆亦仁義之政未足厭服其心
駕馭其力焉耳考之於古丁蘭以孝居於
宜城王粲以詞依於荆州錢徽自考功郎
中而留穀城裴休由太子少保而處長沙
第進士而遷襄陽者胡旦也忤蔡京而居
當陽者胡安國也家潭州而以道學名世
非張栻乎徙興國而為宋室忠臣非謝枋
得乎他如丁鶴年之耿介出塵龍仁夫之
明經式學李安國之孝行邑民矜式劉凝
===
之之仁德鄉里增重又皆彰彰於書黃衡
寶之域之數人者在一邑則一邑重在一
郡則一郡重真無負於湖矣今之流寓乃
至以客凌主何古今人相遠邪自今觀之
假繼贅而奪其產產奪而人之祀絕矣誘
借貸而取其貲貲盡而人之性傷矣至于
駕虛詞以重其禍則一人構訟或結黨於
同鄉各戶斂財或連詞於終歲弗勝其健
反直為曲則又盡貲產而傾之矣可惡孰
punctuated: 主之勢者，殆亦仁義之政未足厭服其心、駕馭其力焉耳。考之於古，丁蘭以孝居於宜城，王粲以詞依於荆州，錢徽自考功郎中而留穀城，裴休由太子少保而處長沙。第進士而遷襄陽者，胡旦也；忤蔡京而居當陽者，胡安國也。家潭州而以道學名世，非張栻乎？徙興國而為宋室忠臣，非謝枋得乎？他如丁鶴年之耿介出塵，龍仁夫之明經式學，李安國之孝行邑民矜式，劉凝之之仁德鄉里增重，又皆彰彰於書。黃衡寶之域之數人者，在一邑則一邑重，在一郡則一郡重，真無負於湖矣。今之流寓乃至以客凌主，何古今人相遠邪？自今觀之，假繼贅而奪其產，產奪而人之祀絕矣；誘借貸而取其貲，貲盡而人之性傷矣。至于駕虛詞以重其禍，則一人構訟，或結黨於同鄉，各戶斂財；或連詞於終歲，弗勝其健，反直為曲，則又盡貲產而傾之矣。可惡孰
translation_en:
…a position of dominance over their hosts has arisen, probably simply because government through benevolence and righteousness has not been sufficient to win over their hearts and direct their energies. Looking to antiquity, Ding Lan lived in Yicheng and was known for filial piety; Wang Can found refuge in Jingzhou through his literary talents; Qian Hui stayed in Gucheng after serving as Director of the Bureau of Merit Evaluation; and Pei Xiu resided in Changsha after serving as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent. It was Hu Dan who moved to Xiangyang after becoming a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), and Hu Anguo who lived in Dangyang after opposing Cai Jing. Was it not Zhang Shi who made his home in Tanzhou and became renowned for his Learning of the Way? Was it not Xie Fangde who moved to Xingguo and was a loyal minister of the Song house? Others include Ding Henian, whose upright integrity rose above worldly concerns; Long Renfu, whose understanding of the Classics set a model for learning; Li Anguo, whose filial conduct the people of his county took as their example; and Liu Ningzhi, whose benevolence and virtue lent distinction to his community. All are clearly recorded in writing. These men of the region of Huang, Heng, and Bao [?] brought distinction to whatever county or prefecture they inhabited. Truly, they did not fail Huguang.

Yet today’s migrants have gone so far as to dominate their hosts while themselves being guests. Why are people of ancient and modern times so far apart? Judging by present circumstances, they use succession by adoption or marriage as a resident son-in-law as a pretext to seize another’s property; once that property is seized, the family’s ancestral sacrifices cease. They entice people into borrowing and take their wealth; once that wealth is exhausted, people’s lives are harmed. They even fabricate allegations to compound their victims’ misfortunes. When one person instigates a lawsuit, they may form a faction among people from their native place and collect money from every household, or prolong litigation throughout the year. Unable to withstand their aggressiveness, the party in the right is made out to be in the wrong, and is then stripped of all wealth and property and ruined. What could be more detestable …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
甚焉嘗聞理道乖方版圖脫漏人如鳥獸
飛走莫制家以之乏國以之貧奸宄漸興
此杜佑之所為慮也不農則不地著不地
著則離鄉輕家民如鳥獸嚴法重刑猶不
能禁則鼂錯之所為憂也流民之患自古
而然猶未至今日之甚者也然為今日之
計亦曰普天皆王土率土皆王臣流民孰
非吾赤子乎當立為通融之法凡置成產
業者名以稅戶之目為人耕佃者曰耕佃
===
戶專於販易傭作者曰營生戶隨其所在
定為版冊肆貪鼓暴而逞計者又重其刑
以禁之而於吾荆湘之民制以恒產使皆
有田可以自養寬其賦役使皆有財可以
自給明其教化使皆不惑不恐於奪攘矯
虔之徒則亦足以保其產守其財而無憂
於告訐矣於此二者處之既得其道又知
與民最親而狎者里胥也慎重其選使之
屬民讀法如周之族師辨施舍行秩叙如
punctuated:
甚焉？嘗聞理道乖方，版圖脫漏，人如鳥獸，飛走莫制，家以之乏，國以之貧，奸宄漸興，此杜佑之所為慮也。不農則不地著，不地著則離鄉輕家，民如鳥獸，嚴法重刑猶不能禁，則鼂錯之所為憂也。流民之患，自古而然，猶未至今日之甚者也。

然為今日之計，亦曰普天皆王土，率土皆王臣，流民孰非吾赤子乎？當立為通融之法，凡置成產業者，名以稅戶之目；為人耕佃者，曰耕佃戶；專於販易傭作者，曰營生戶。隨其所在，定為版冊。肆貪鼓暴而逞計者，又重其刑以禁之。而於吾荆湘之民，制以恒產，使皆有田可以自養；寬其賦役，使皆有財可以自給；明其教化，使皆不惑不恐於奪攘矯虔之徒，則亦足以保其產、守其財，而無憂於告訐矣。

於此二者，處之既得其道，又知與民最親而狎者，里胥也。慎重其選，使之屬民讀法，如周之族師；辨施舍，行秩叙，如
translation_en:
…more detestable than this? I have heard that when the methods of governance go astray and people are omitted from the population and territorial registers, they scatter like birds and beasts, beyond control. Households are thereby impoverished, the state grows poor, and wrongdoing gradually flourishes. This was what concerned Du You. When people do not farm, they do not remain settled on the land; when they are not settled on the land, they leave their native places and think little of their homes. The people become like birds and beasts, whom even stringent laws and heavy punishments cannot restrain. This was what concerned Chao Cuo. The troubles caused by migrants have existed since antiquity, but never reached the severity seen today.

Yet in devising measures for today, we should also say: all land beneath Heaven is the king’s land, and all who dwell upon it are the king’s subjects. Which of these migrants is not one of our own children? We should establish flexible regulations: all who have acquired established property should be designated “taxpaying households”; those who cultivate land as tenants for others, “tenant-farming households”; and those who engage exclusively in trade or hired labor, “livelihood households.” They should be entered in registers wherever they reside. Those who indulge their greed, foment violence, and carry out their schemes should, moreover, face heavier punishments to restrain them. As for our people of Jing and Xiang, provide them with a secure livelihood, so that all have land with which to support themselves; lighten their taxes and labor obligations, so that all have the means to meet their needs; and make moral instruction clear, so that none are deceived or intimidated by those who seize, plunder, cheat, and coerce. These measures would suffice to enable them to preserve their property and safeguard their wealth, without anxiety over malicious accusations.

Having found the proper way to deal with these two groups, we must also recognize that those in the closest and most familiar contact with the people are the village clerks. Select them with care, and have them assemble the people and read out the laws, like the clan masters of the Zhou; distinguish exemptions from service and implement the prescribed order of precedence, like …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
周之胥宰如酇長之趣其耕耨稽其女工
如閭師之任農耕事任圃樹事又如鄰長
之相糾使之有所警而不為惡相受使之
有所勸而必為善守令者復督察之于上
重擾害之禁嚴誣告之法不至如董仲舒
所謂師帥不賢主德不宣而恩澤不流監
司又振飭之於上宣明教化開釋冤滯必
至如陸贄所謂五術省風俗四賦經財實
六德保罷療如是則仁義行而居者安来
===
者撫元氣內固而外邪弗得侵淫矣尚何
民病之足慮哉噫是道也推而行之天下
之民舉安又不但荆楚爾也執事以為何
如
punctuated: 周之胥宰，如酇長之趣其耕耨、稽其女工，如閭師之任農耕事、任圃樹事，又如鄰長之相糾，使之有所警而不為惡；相受，使之有所勸而必為善。守令者復督察之于上，重擾害之禁，嚴誣告之法，不至如董仲舒所謂「師帥不賢，主德不宣，而恩澤不流」。監司又振飭之於上，宣明教化，開釋冤滯，必至如陸贄所謂「五術省風俗，四賦經財實，六德保罷療」。如是則仁義行，而居者安、来者撫，元氣內固，而外邪弗得侵淫矣。尚何民病之足慮哉？噫！是道也，推而行之，天下之民舉安，又不但荆楚爾也。執事以為何如？
translation_en: …the local administrators of Zhou; like the Neighborhood Chiefs, who urged people on in plowing and weeding and inspected women’s textile work; like the Ward Masters, who assigned farmers to cultivation and gardeners to planting; and also like the Group Heads, who had neighbors correct one another, giving them warning so that they would not do evil, and receive one another, giving them encouragement so that they would surely do good. Prefects and magistrates should further supervise them from above, reinforce prohibitions against harassment and injury, and enforce strictly the laws against false accusations. Thus matters would not reach the condition Dong Zhongshu described: “The leaders are unworthy, the ruler’s virtue is not made manifest, and his beneficence does not flow forth.” The surveillance commissioners should likewise impose discipline from above, make moral instruction clear, and release those unjustly detained, necessarily attaining what Lu Zhi described as “examining customs through five methods, regulating material resources through four levies, and protecting the weary and healing them through six virtues” [?]. If this is done, benevolence and righteousness will prevail; those already dwelling here will be secure, and newcomers will be cared for. The vital force will be strengthened within, and harmful influences from outside will be unable to encroach. What suffering of the people would then remain cause for concern? Ah! If this way were extended and put into practice, all the people under Heaven would enjoy security—not merely those of Jingchu. What do you, gentlemen, think?

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
湖廣辛卯鄉試事竣臣克昌
從諸執事後當任楮墨役敢
序諸簡末用告諸士曰楚人
文地也自昔稱天下之竒必
曰楚才無乃造物者啟其機
以肇
===
今日文明之翊邪夫文非機弗
先機非會弗合機會之際有
期焉
聖天子龍飛江漢物覩之餘楚文
彌盛無乃造物者嘉其會以
共成文明之治邪於是乎有
本焉夫極弗建則機弗會會
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序

湖廣辛卯鄉試事竣，臣克昌從諸執事後，當任楮墨役，敢序諸簡末，用告諸士曰：楚，人文地也。自昔稱天下之竒，必曰楚才。無乃造物者啟其機，以肇今日文明之翊邪？夫文非機弗先，機非會弗合，機會之際有期焉。聖天子龍飛江漢，物覩之餘，楚文彌盛。無乃造物者嘉其會，以共成文明之治邪？於是乎有本焉。夫極弗建，則機弗會；會
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

When the Huguang Provincial Examination of the xinmao year (1531) was completed, I, your servant Kechang, serving after the other officials, was charged with the work of paper and ink. I venture to append a postface at the end of the volume, addressing the candidates as follows: Chu is a land of cultural accomplishment. Since ancient times, whenever people have spoken of the outstanding talents of the realm, they have invariably named the talents of Chu. Might the Creator have set their potential in motion to inaugurate the flourishing of culture today [?]? Cultural accomplishment cannot take the lead without an incipient impulse; that impulse cannot come to fruition without a favorable conjunction of circumstances. There is an appointed time when impulse and circumstance meet.

Our sagely Son of Heaven rose like a dragon from the Jiang and Han rivers, revealing himself to all beings; thereafter, the culture of Chu flourished still more. Might the Creator have favored this conjunction so as to bring about, together, a reign of cultural enlightenment? This, then, has a foundation. If the supreme standard is not established, the impulse cannot meet its favorable circumstances; if the conjunction …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
弗協則治弗純此有本之治
唐虞三代所以保世滋大而
無取於叔季之小康也
聖天子天章睿藻為絲為綸文之
華也準古酌今昭物明度文
有用也然而
敬一以宅心
===
仁孝以懋德是為學之樞要致
治之根本真所謂建有極以
嘉厥會者也文不在兹與或
曰吉甫之才文以武屈平之
才文以忠宋玉之才文以雅
茂叔之才文以理楚之良也
楚産者師其人而修其文其
punctuated:
弗協，則治弗純。此有本之治，唐虞三代所以保世滋大，而無取於叔季之小康也。
聖天子天章睿藻，為絲為綸，文之華也；準古酌今，昭物明度，文有用也。然而敬一以宅心，仁孝以懋德，是為學之樞要、致治之根本，真所謂建有極以嘉厥會者也。文不在兹與？
或曰：「吉甫之才，文以武；屈平之才，文以忠；宋玉之才，文以雅；茂叔之才，文以理。楚之良也。楚産者師其人而修其文，其
translation_en:
…if their convergence is not harmonious, governance will not be pure. Such governance, grounded in a foundation, was how the rulers of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties preserved their realms through the generations and made them ever greater, having no use for the modest peace of declining ages.
The sage Son of Heaven’s heavenly compositions and sagacious writings become the silken threads and cords of imperial commands: this is the splendor of literary culture. Taking antiquity as his standard while weighing present circumstances, clarifying things and making standards manifest: this is literary culture put to use. Yet it is through reverent concentration on the One that he settles his mind, and through benevolence and filial devotion that he advances his virtue. These are the essentials of learning and the foundation of good governance. This is truly what is meant by establishing the supreme standard and thereby bringing excellence to the convergence of circumstances. Does not literary culture reside here?
Someone says: “Jifu’s talent joined literary accomplishment with martial prowess; Qu Ping’s joined it with loyalty; Song Yu’s joined it with elegance; Maoshu’s joined it with principle. These were outstanding men of Chu. If those born in Chu take these men as their teachers and cultivate their literary accomplishments, they might…”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
庶幾矣乎是不然君子居其
地不累其俗軼其俗必追其
古是故幹不與角謀笴不與
金錫謀廬不與函謀鑄不與
劔謀器也若夫可秦可粤可
燕可荆可夷可夏天󠄁下之大
器也傳曰五百年必有王者
===
興其間必有名世者今
聖天子堯文思矣舜文明矣湯懋
昭矣文明德矣諸士子感機
以作協會以俟隆古明良之
一期也於是乎師其本而歸
極焉修乎其家而始於親親
施之天下而篤恭是務文武
punctuated: 庶幾矣乎？是不然。君子居其地，不累其俗；軼其俗，必追其古。是故幹不與角謀，笴不與金錫謀，廬不與函謀，鑄不與劔謀，器也。若夫可秦可粤，可燕可荆，可夷可夏，天󠄁下之大器也。傳曰：「五百年必有王者興，其間必有名世者。」今聖天子堯文思矣，舜文明矣，湯懋昭矣，文明德矣。諸士子感機以作，協會以俟，隆古明良之一期也。於是乎師其本而歸極焉，修乎其家而始於親親，施之天下而篤恭是務，文武
translation_en: …would they not come close? This is not so. A gentleman dwells in a place without being encumbered by its customs; to surpass its customs, he must reach back to its antiquity. Thus the maker of bow staves does not consult the worker in horn, nor the maker of arrow shafts the worker in copper and tin, nor the maker of spear shafts [?] the maker of armor, nor the caster the swordsmith: these are specialized capacities. But one who can serve in Qin or Yue, Yan or Jing, among the non-Chinese or among the Chinese, is a great vessel for all under Heaven. The transmitted text says: “Every five hundred years a true king must arise, and in the interval there must be men renowned in their age.” Now our sagely Son of Heaven possesses Yao’s refinement and thoughtfulness, Shun’s cultivation and enlightenment, Tang’s resplendent brilliance, and King Wen’s illustrious virtue. The scholars, stirred by this opportunity, rise to action; joining in this auspicious convergence, they await their time. This is an occasion for a meeting of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers such as occurred in high antiquity. Accordingly, they take the root as their teacher and return to the ultimate standard. They cultivate their households, beginning with affection for their kin; they extend this throughout the world, making earnest reverence their concern. In civil and martial accomplishments…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
焉而不惑忠焉而不過雅焉
而不溺理焉而純聖則洋洋
纚纚皆典謨訓誥其言皇皇
濟濟皆皐夔周召其人不足
以當名世而翊化理矣乎是
不特曰楚之才而已爾
直隸揚州府儒學教授陳克
===
昌謹序
punctuated:
焉而不惑，忠焉而不過，雅焉而不溺，理焉而純聖，則洋洋纚纚皆典謨訓誥其言，皇皇濟濟皆皐夔周召其人，不足以當名世而翊化理矣乎？是不特曰楚之才而已爾。
直隸揚州府儒學教授陳克昌謹序。
translation_en:
…and are not confused; loyal without going to excess; refined without becoming immersed in refinement; guided by principle and wholly sagely. Then their words, flowing abundantly, will all be like the canons, counsels, instructions, and proclamations of the Book of Documents; and these men, august and dignified, will all be like Gao, Kui, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao. Would they not be worthy of renown in their age and capable of assisting moral transformation and good government? They would be more than merely the talented men of Chu.
Preface respectfully written by Chen Kechang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yangzhou Prefecture, in the Directly Administered Region (Zhili).

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄序
嘉靖十年例應鄉試取士禮
部以湖廣考試官請
上命給事中臣王禎行人臣朱隆
禧行矣未幾臣隆禧弗果至
禮部復以請
上命行人臣謙往時盖七月十二
===
日也臣受
命祗懼嚴程以進越十有三日入
湖境則聞臣禎又弗果至矣
益為惕然初湖中但知二臣
者之去而不知臣之来也自
鎮守太監臣潘真巡撫右副
都御史臣凌相以下咸慮焉
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄序

嘉靖十年，例應鄉試取士，禮部以湖廣考試官請，上命給事中臣王禎、行人臣朱隆禧行矣。未幾，臣隆禧弗果至，禮部復以請，上命行人臣謙往，時盖七月十二日也。臣受命祗懼，嚴程以進，越十有三日入湖境，則聞臣禎又弗果至矣，益為惕然。初，湖中但知二臣者之去，而不知臣之来也，自鎮守太監臣潘真、巡撫右副都御史臣凌相以下，咸慮焉。
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

In the tenth year of Jiajing [1531], the Provincial Examination was due to be held according to established practice to select men for service. The Ministry of Rites requested the appointment of Examiners for Huguang. His Majesty ordered his servants Wang Zhen, Supervising Secretary, and Zhu Longxi, Messenger, to proceed there. Before long, however, his servant Longxi proved unable to arrive. The Ministry of Rites submitted another request, and His Majesty ordered me, his servant Qian, a Messenger, to go. It was then the twelfth day of the seventh month.

Having received the command with reverent apprehension, I pressed forward on a strict travelling schedule. Thirteen days later, I entered Huguang, only to hear that his servant Zhen, too, had been unable to arrive. This heightened my anxiety. Initially, those in Huguang knew only that the two officials had set out, and did not know that I was coming. From His Majesty’s servants Pan Zhen, the eunuch serving as Regional Commander, and Ling Xiang, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, downward, all were concerned.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
顯陵督理大工内官監太監臣傅
平工部左侍郎臣黎奭撫治
鄖陽右副都御史臣潘旦巡
撫南贛右副都御史臣陶諧
清戎御史臣陸琳慮亦如之
若郎中臣劉佐臣張淑主事
臣華察行人臣李遂錦衣衛
===
千戶臣李鵬皆奉
命而蒞茲土者亦與厥慮臣至則
皆喜曰來何速哉事其濟乎
其尤深喜者監臨官巡按監
察御史臣組提調官右布政
使臣鐸左參議臣日休監試
官按察使臣峨副使臣錫也
punctuated: 顯陵督理大工内官監太監臣傅平、工部左侍郎臣黎奭、撫治鄖陽右副都御史臣潘旦、巡撫南贛右副都御史臣陶諧、清戎御史臣陸琳，慮亦如之。若郎中臣劉佐、臣張淑，主事臣華察，行人臣李遂，錦衣衛千戶臣李鵬，皆奉命而蒞茲土者，亦與厥慮。臣至，則皆喜曰：「來何速哉！事其濟乎！」其尤深喜者，監臨官巡按監察御史臣組，提調官右布政使臣鐸、左參議臣日休，監試官按察使臣峨、副使臣錫也。
translation_en: …Fu Ping, Grand Eunuch of the Directorate of Palace Domestic Service, supervising the great construction works at Xianling; Li Shi, Left Vice Minister of Works; Pan Dan, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief charged with pacifying and administering Yunyang; Tao Xie, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of southern Jiangxi; and Lu Lin, Censor charged with inspecting military administration—all your servants—shared these concerns. So too did your servants Liu Zuo and Zhang Shu, bureau directors; Hua Cha, a secretary; Li Sui, a messenger; and Li Peng, a battalion commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard, all of whom had come to this region under imperial orders. When your servant arrived, they all rejoiced, saying, “How quickly you have come! Now perhaps the undertaking can succeed!” Particularly delighted were your servants Zu, the Supervising Official and Regional Inspecting Censor; Duo, the Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Rixiu, the Left Administration Assistant Commissioner, serving as Proctors; and E, the Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Xi, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner, serving as examination monitors.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
其叅政臣黃焯臣劉棟叅議
臣胡德臣鄺灝副使臣文明
臣朱珮臣陳卿僉事臣周佐
臣孟居仁臣毛紹元臣陳嘉
言都指揮臣王表臣周邦簡
臣陳曉罔不欣然樂相其事
若副使臣李顯右叅議臣張
===
天性則先期入
賀矣維時先綜理試事巡按監
察御史臣劉濂暨左布政使
今陞太僕寺卿臣盛儀所聘
同考試官教授臣克昌臣嘉
秀臣汶學正臣燦臣登教諭
臣文昌臣河臣畿臣士奎等
punctuated: 其叅政臣黃焯、臣劉棟，叅議臣胡德、臣鄺灝，副使臣文明、臣朱珮、臣陳卿，僉事臣周佐、臣孟居仁、臣毛紹元、臣陳嘉言，都指揮臣王表、臣周邦簡、臣陳曉，罔不欣然樂相其事。若副使臣李顯、右叅議臣張天性，則先期入賀矣。維時，先綜理試事巡按監察御史臣劉濂暨左布政使、今陞太僕寺卿臣盛儀所聘同考試官，教授臣克昌、臣嘉秀、臣汶，學正臣燦、臣登，教諭臣文昌、臣河、臣畿、臣士奎等，
translation_en:
The other officials—your servants Huang Zhuo and Liu Dong, Administration Vice Commissioners; Hu De and Kuang Hao, Administration Assistant Commissioners; Wenming, Zhu Pei, and Chen Qing, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Zhou Zuo, Meng Juren, Mao Shaoyuan, and Chen Jiayan, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and Wang Biao, Zhou Bangjian, and Chen Xiao, Regional Military Commissioners—all gladly assisted in the undertaking. As for your servants Li Xian, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, and Zhang Tianxing, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner, they had already gone to court ahead of time to offer congratulations.

At that time, the Associate Examiners engaged by your servants Liu Lian, Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor, who had previously overseen the examination arrangements, and Sheng Yi, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, now promoted to Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud—your servants Kechang, Jiaxiu, and Wen, prefectural school instructors; Can and Deng, subprefectural school instructors; and Wenchang, He, Ji, and Shikui, county school instructors, among others…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
畢集乃合提學副使臣崔桐
所取士二千七百有奇三試
之遵
制額得士八十五人并錄其文之
優者以
獻臣不佞敢颺言于衆曰湖南
山川之美甲天下然自開闢
以来至于
今日而
大聖人始作何也蓋天地至精至
粹之氣久于積泓于蓄故其
發也昌以大是氣也一鍾之
冀北而堯舜者出以開百有
餘年之帝治再鍾之岐周而
punctuated:
畢集，乃合提學副使臣崔桐所取士二千七百有奇，三試之，遵制額得士八十五人，并錄其文之優者以獻。
臣不佞，敢颺言于衆曰：「湖南山川之美甲天下，然自開闢以来，至于今日，而大聖人始作，何也？蓋天地至精至粹之氣，久于積，泓于蓄，故其發也昌以大。是氣也，一鍾之冀北，而堯舜者出，以開百有餘年之帝治；再鍾之岐周，而
translation_en:
…all assembled. Then the more than 2,700 candidates selected by your servant Cui Tong, Vice Commissioner for Education, were brought together and examined in three sessions. In accordance with the prescribed quota, eighty-five men were selected, and the finest of their compositions were also transcribed for presentation to the throne.
Untalented though I am, I ventured to proclaim to the assembled company: “The beauty of Hunan’s mountains and rivers ranks first under Heaven. Yet from the beginning of creation down to this very day, only now has a great sage arisen. Why is this? The most refined and purest vital energy of Heaven and Earth accumulates over a long time and is stored in deep abundance; thus, when it issues forth, its manifestation is splendid and great. This energy first concentrated in Jibei, and Yao and Shun emerged to inaugurate more than a hundred years of imperial rule. It concentrated a second time in Qizhou, and…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
文武者出以開八百餘年之
王業鍾之淮甸則
聖祖興焉億萬年鴻基茲啓矣鍾
之湖南而我
大聖人作豈非無疆之休乎然其
間亦必有附是間氣而挺生
於若地者為之名世故元凱
===
冀產周召岐英而我
朝開國功臣又皆淮之豪傑也
則夫
今日獨無若人者奮於湖南乎
矧
天降甘露瑞諸物也瑞諸物未有
不瑞諸人者也
punctuated: 文武者出，以開八百餘年之王業；鍾之淮甸，則聖祖興焉，億萬年鴻基茲啓矣；鍾之湖南，而我大聖人作，豈非無疆之休乎？然其間亦必有附是間氣而挺生於若地者，為之名世。故元凱冀產，周召岐英，而我朝開國功臣又皆淮之豪傑也。則夫今日獨無若人者奮於湖南乎？矧天降甘露，瑞諸物也；瑞諸物，未有不瑞諸人者也。
translation_en: …Kings Wen and Wu emerged, thereby inaugurating a royal enterprise lasting more than eight hundred years. When this vital force gathered in the Huai region, the Sagely Founder arose, and the mighty foundation for countless ages was thus laid. When it gathered in Hunan, our Great Sage arose: is this not a blessing without bounds? Yet there must also be men who partake of this exceptional vital force and are born outstanding in such places, becoming renowned figures of their age. Thus the Yuan and Kai—the groups of eight ancient worthies—were natives of Ji; the Dukes of Zhou and Shao were the outstanding men of Qi; and the meritorious founders of our dynasty were likewise all heroes of the Huai region. Could it be that today alone no such men will rise in Hunan? Moreover, Heaven has sent down sweet dew, an auspicious manifestation among things. An auspicious manifestation among things has never failed to be accompanied by one among men.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
天於湖南其亦不靳若人也已維
茲辛卯黃帝之曆伊起也建
酉之月日月會於壽星是蒼
龍宿之首也抑時必有非常
之士應
大聖人求焉求而得非常之士則
曰元凱曰周召者為時庸矣
===
然臣懼以一己目力而欲悉
搜人材於無遺亦殆矣所幸
諸執事者盡心殫力以克成
之諸執事亦曰懼哉閱卷貴
詳校才貴精取士貴當難乎
其庸力也殆益懼哉臣廼喜

translation_en:
Heaven surely will not begrudge Hunan such men. This is the xinmao year, with which the Yellow Emperor’s calendar begins [?]. In the month designated by the earthly branch you, the sun and moon meet in Shouxing, the first of the Azure Dragon’s celestial lodges. Surely at this time exceptional men must appear in response to the great sage emperor’s search. If his search obtains exceptional men, then men like the Yuan and Kai, and the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, will be employed in the service of the age.

Yet I, your servant, fear that to seek out all talented men, overlooking none, through my own powers of discernment alone is a precarious undertaking. title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
志於道據於德依於仁游於藝
郊社之禮所以事上帝也宗廟之禮所以
祀乎其先也
使天下仕者皆欲立於王之朝耕者皆欲
耕於王之野商賈皆欲藏於王之市行
旅皆欲出於王之途
易
===
牝馬地類行地无疆柔順利貞君子攸行
安節之亨承上道也
廣大配天地變通配四時陰陽之義配日
月易簡之善配至德
天地之道貞觀者也日月之道貞明者也
天下之動貞夫一者也
書
無怠無荒四夷來王
股肱惟人良臣惟聖
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

志於道，據於德，依於仁，游於藝。

郊社之禮，所以事上帝也；宗廟之禮，所以祀乎其先也。

使天下仕者皆欲立於王之朝，耕者皆欲耕於王之野，商賈皆欲藏於王之市，行旅皆欲出於王之途。

易

牝馬地類，行地无疆，柔順利貞，君子攸行。

安節之亨，承上道也。

廣大配天地，變通配四時，陰陽之義配日月，易簡之善配至德。

天地之道，貞觀者也；日月之道，貞明者也；天下之動，貞夫一者也。

書

無怠無荒，四夷來王。

股肱惟人，良臣惟聖。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Set your purpose upon the Way, hold firmly to virtue, rely upon humaneness, and take your recreation in the arts.

The rites of sacrifice at the suburban altar and the altar of soil are the means of serving the Lord on High; the rites of the ancestral temple are the means of sacrificing to one’s ancestors.

Cause all those under Heaven who seek office to wish to stand at Your Majesty’s court, all farmers to wish to till Your Majesty’s fields, all merchants to wish to store their goods in Your Majesty’s markets, and all travelers to wish to journey along Your Majesty’s roads.

Book of Changes (Yijing)

The mare belongs to the same category as Earth and travels the earth without limit. Gentle and compliant, beneficial and steadfast: this is the course the gentleman follows.

The success of resting content within limits comes from following the way of those above.

Its breadth and greatness match Heaven and Earth; its changes and adaptations match the four seasons; the significance of its yin and yang matches the sun and moon; the excellence of its ease and simplicity matches the highest virtue.

The way of Heaven and Earth is displayed through constancy; the way of the sun and moon shines through constancy; the movements of all under Heaven are made constant through unity.

Book of Documents (Shu)

Be neither negligent nor given to excess, and the peoples of the four quarters will come to acknowledge you as king.

Arms and legs make a person complete; worthy ministers make a ruler a sage.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
所寶惟賢則邇人安
不剛不柔厥德允修惟周公克慎厥始惟
君陳克和厥中惟公克成厥終
詩
躋彼公堂稱彼兕觥萬壽無疆
赫赫南仲玁狁于夷
王赫斯怒爰整其旅以按徂旅以篤于周
祜以對于天下
喤喤厥聲肅雝和鳴先祖是聽我客戾止
===
永觀厥成
春秋
冬十有二月祭伯來隱公元年
夏公會齊侯宋公陳侯衞侯曹伯伐鄭圍
新城僖公六年
丁亥楚子入陳宣公十有一年
季孫斯仲孫何忌帥師墮費定公十有二年
禮記
天子祭天下名山大川五嶽視三公四瀆
punctuated:
所寶惟賢，則邇人安。
不剛不柔，厥德允修。惟周公克慎厥始，惟君陳克和厥中，惟公克成厥終。

詩
躋彼公堂，稱彼兕觥，萬壽無疆。
赫赫南仲，玁狁于夷。
王赫斯怒，爰整其旅，以按徂旅，以篤于周祜，以對于天下。
喤喤厥聲，肅雝和鳴，先祖是聽。我客戾止，永觀厥成。

春秋
冬十有二月，祭伯來。隱公元年。
夏，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衞侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。僖公六年。
丁亥，楚子入陳。宣公十有一年。
季孫斯、仲孫何忌帥師墮費。定公十有二年。

禮記
天子祭天下名山大川，五嶽視三公，四瀆
translation_en:
When those whom you treasure are the worthy, the people nearby will be at peace.
Neither harsh nor yielding, his virtue is truly cultivated. The Duke of Zhou was able to exercise care at the beginning; Jun Chen was able to maintain harmony in the middle; and you, my lord, are able to bring it to completion at the end.

Book of Odes
Ascend that lordly hall and raise those rhinoceros-horn goblets: may he live ten thousand years without end!
Illustrious was Nan Zhong: the Xianyun were subdued.
The king blazed with anger and thereupon marshalled his troops, to check the advancing host, to make Zhou’s blessings abundant, and to answer to all under Heaven.
Resonant are their sounds; solemnly and harmoniously they ring together. The ancestors listen to them. Our guest has arrived, long to behold their accomplishment.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In winter, in the twelfth month, the Earl of Ji came. First year of Duke Yin.
In summer, the duke joined the marquises of Qi, Song, Chen, and Wei and the Earl of Cao in attacking Zheng; they besieged Xincheng. Sixth year of Duke Xi.
On the dinghai day, the Viscount of Chu entered Chen. Eleventh year of Duke Xuan.
Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji led an army to demolish the walls of Fei. Twelfth year of Duke Ding.

Book of Rites
The Son of Heaven offers sacrifices to the renowned mountains and great rivers throughout the realm. The Five Sacred Peaks are accorded the same rank as the Three Dukes; the Four Great Watercourses …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
視諸侯
以正君臣以篤父子以睦兄弟以齊上下
夫婦有所
諸侯以龜為寶以圭為瑞
地氣上齊天氣下降陰陽相摩天地相蕩
鼓之以雷霆奮之以風雨動之以四時
煖之以日月而百化興焉如此則樂者
天地之和也
第貳場
===
論
孔子聞而知之
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢賜農民今年租稅之半詔文帝十二年
擬唐以馬周為監察御史誥貞觀三年
擬宋頒訓廉謹刑二銘於中外羣臣謝表
淳祐四年
判語五條
信牌
punctuated:
視諸侯。
以正君臣，以篤父子，以睦兄弟，以齊上下，夫婦有所。
諸侯以龜為寶，以圭為瑞。
地氣上齊，天氣下降，陰陽相摩，天地相蕩，鼓之以雷霆，奮之以風雨，動之以四時，煖之以日月，而百化興焉。如此，則樂者天地之和也。
第貳場
論
孔子聞而知之。
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢賜農民今年租稅之半詔，文帝十二年。
擬唐以馬周為監察御史誥，貞觀三年。
擬宋頒訓廉謹刑二銘於中外羣臣謝表，淳祐四年。
判語五條
信牌。
translation_en:
…are ranked with the regional lords.

To set right the relationship between ruler and minister, deepen affection between father and son, promote harmony among brothers, and order relations between superiors and inferiors, so that husband and wife each have their proper place.

The regional lords regard tortoise shells as treasures and jade gui tablets as tokens of investiture.

The vital force of earth rises, and the vital force of heaven descends. Yin and yang interact; heaven and earth stir one another. They rouse things with thunder, quicken them with wind and rain, move them through the four seasons, and warm them with the sun and moon; thus the myriad transformations arise. Accordingly, music is the harmony of heaven and earth.

Second Session

Discourse

Confucius acquired knowledge through hearing.

One topic from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [the selection rubric is doubtful: 科].

Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty granting farmers remission of half this year's land tax. Twelfth year of Emperor Wen's reign.

Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Ma Zhou as Investigating Censor. Third year of Zhenguan.

Compose a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song dynasty for the distribution to officials at court and in the provinces of the two inscriptions, “Admonition to Integrity” and “Caution in Punishment.” Fourth year of Chunyou.

Five Legal Judgments

Authorization tablets.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
匿稅
失儀
越城
誣告
第參塲
策五道
問自古聖哲之化天下未有不須于內助
者若文王之於太姒武王之於邑姜是
已我
===
太祖高皇帝首御家邦貽謀萬世雖古聖哲之
君殆無以過然而賛元斡化
孝慈高皇后有力焉其嘉言善行載之傳者可
得而聞歟至
仁孝文皇后復廣
高皇后之教為內訓二十篇邇者
章聖慈仁皇太后復製為女訓十二篇其亦皆
有序歟伏覩三書可以仰窺我
列聖脩齊之化矣今天下家傳人誦風化丕行
punctuated:
匿稅、失儀、越城、誣告。

第參塲
策五道

問：自古聖哲之化天下，未有不須于內助者，若文王之於太姒、武王之於邑姜是已。我太祖高皇帝首御家邦，貽謀萬世，雖古聖哲之君殆無以過。然而賛元斡化，孝慈高皇后有力焉。其嘉言善行載之傳者，可得而聞歟？至仁孝文皇后，復廣高皇后之教，為《內訓》二十篇。邇者，章聖慈仁皇太后復製為《女訓》十二篇，其亦皆有序歟？伏覩三書，可以仰窺我列聖脩齊之化矣。今天下家傳人誦，風化丕行，
translation_en:
Concealing taxable assets; breaches of ceremonial propriety; crossing the city wall; false accusation.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: Since antiquity, no sage ruler who transformed the realm has done so without the assistance of his consort. Such were King Wen’s reliance on Tai Si and King Wu’s on Yi Jiang. Our Emperor Taizu Gao first took charge of the imperial house and realm and bequeathed plans for ten thousand generations; even the sage rulers of antiquity could scarcely surpass him. Yet in assisting his great undertakings and guiding the work of transformation, Empress Xiaoci Gao made a substantial contribution. May we hear of her admirable sayings and good deeds recorded in her biography? Subsequently, Empress Renxiao Wen further extended Empress Gao’s teachings, composing the Instructions for the Inner Quarters (Neixun) in twenty chapters. Recently, Empress Dowager Zhangsheng Ciren also composed the Instructions for Women (Nüxun) in twelve chapters. Do these works all have prefaces as well? Reverently reading these three books, we may glimpse the transforming influence of our succession of sage rulers through their cultivation of themselves and regulation of their families. Now these works are transmitted in households and recited by individuals throughout the realm, and their moral influence spreads widely…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
諸士子皆有正家之責者抑嘗習此以
教否乎請敬陳之以觀脩齊之實學
問周禮周公致太平之書也而唐六典則
倣乎是何其間大不同歟周禮無公孤
之職唐乃有三師三公之官此固成王
立公孤之遺意乃若吏部掌天下官吏
選授勳封考課戶部掌天下戶口井田
禮部掌天下禮儀祠祭燕享貢舉兵部
掌天下軍衛武官選授刑部掌天下刑
===
法及徒隸勾覆關禁均有政令焉者其
與周禮立五官之職掌同歟周禮缺冬
官而後人以考工記補之矣唐乃有工
部掌天下百工屯田山澤之政令者何
所據歟此外又有門下中書秘書殿中
四省御史臺太常光祿衛尉太僕大理
鴻臚司農太府諸寺司國子少府將作
諸監左右等衛及太子與親王府國公
主邑司官屬何其多歟意者其唐太宗
punctuated:
諸士子皆有正家之責者，抑嘗習此以教否乎？請敬陳之，以觀脩齊之實學。

問：周禮，周公致太平之書也，而唐六典則倣乎是，何其間大不同歟？周禮無公孤之職，唐乃有三師三公之官，此固成王立公孤之遺意。乃若吏部掌天下官吏選授、勳封、考課，戶部掌天下戶口、井田，禮部掌天下禮儀、祠祭、燕享、貢舉，兵部掌天下軍衛、武官選授，刑部掌天下刑法及徒隸、勾覆、關禁，均有政令焉者，其與周禮立五官之職掌同歟？周禮缺冬官，而後人以考工記補之矣。唐乃有工部掌天下百工、屯田、山澤之政令者，何所據歟？此外又有門下、中書、秘書、殿中四省，御史臺，太常、光祿、衛尉、太僕、大理、鴻臚、司農、太府諸寺，司國子、少府、將作諸監，左右等衛，及太子與親王府國、公主邑司官屬，何其多歟？意者其唐太宗
translation_en:
All you candidates bear responsibility for putting your households in order. Have you studied these works and used them to instruct your families? Please set this forth respectfully, so that we may see your practical learning in cultivating yourselves and regulating your families.

Question: The Rites of Zhou is the book through which the Duke of Zhou brought about Great Peace, and the Six Statutes of the Tang took it as its model. Why, then, are there such great differences between them? The Rites of Zhou provides no offices for the Three Dukes and Three Junior Dukes, whereas the Tang had the Three Preceptors and Three Dukes. This certainly preserved the intent behind King Cheng’s establishment of the Three Dukes and Three Junior Dukes. Now, the Ministry of Personnel managed the selection and appointment of officials throughout the realm, merit ranks and enfeoffments, and performance evaluations; the Ministry of Revenue managed households and population, and well-field lands; the Ministry of Rites managed ceremonies, sacrifices, banquets, and the presentation and examination of candidates; the Ministry of War managed military guards and the selection and appointment of military officials; and the Ministry of Justice managed penal law, convict laborers, judicial review, and restrictions at checkpoints. Each possessed administrative ordinances in its sphere. Were their responsibilities the same as those of the five offices established in the Rites of Zhou? The section on the Winter Offices is missing from the Rites of Zhou, and later men supplied the Record of Artificers to fill the gap. Yet the Tang had a Ministry of Works responsible for ordinances governing all the crafts, agricultural colonies, mountains, and marshes throughout the realm. On what basis was this established?

Besides these, there were the four departments—the Chancellery, Secretariat, Palace Library, and Palace Administration—as well as the Censorate; the Courts of Imperial Sacrifices, Imperial Entertainments, Imperial Regalia, Imperial Stud, Judicial Review, State Ceremonial, the Imperial Granaries, and the Imperial Treasury; the directorates for education, palace manufactures, and palace construction [?]; the Left and Right Guards and other guards; and the officials attached to the establishments of the heir apparent, the households and domains of imperial princes, and the estate offices of princesses. Why were there so many? Might it be that Emperor Taizong of the Tang …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
觀會通而立政歟願悉言之以探聖人
制作之意與夫後世因時之政
問天心仁愛人君乃出災異以譴告之昔
殷高宗以雊雉興周宣王以旱魃興盖
天於中興之君尤拳拳焉者也我
皇上仁孝誠敬之德通乎神明近年以來黄河
清甘露降天之所以協應者至矣夫何
偶有彗星之見歟我
皇上痛自脩省又
===
勅諭羣臣各加戒飭遂致彗滅是即先王克謹
天戒臣人克有常憲之意也然春秋書
孛者三左氏公羊皆以彗言之矣自後
見者不一載之史冊可攷也漢文宣光
三帝唐太玄憲三宗宋太祖暨太宗仁
宗皆所謂希世之賢君者而彗皆屢見
何歟自古遇彗陳言之臣若申繻高堂
隆之說其誣不言可知若宋吕公著程
頤富弼吕大防吕大鈞邢恕王安禮陳
punctuated:
觀會通而立政歟？願悉言之，以探聖人制作之意與夫後世因時之政。

問：天心仁愛人君，乃出災異以譴告之。昔殷高宗以雊雉興，周宣王以旱魃興，盖天於中興之君尤拳拳焉者也。我皇上仁孝誠敬之德通乎神明，近年以來，黄河清，甘露降，天之所以協應者至矣。夫何偶有彗星之見歟？我皇上痛自脩省，又勅諭羣臣各加戒飭，遂致彗滅，是即先王克謹天戒、臣人克有常憲之意也。然《春秋》書孛者三，左氏、公羊皆以彗言之矣。自後見者不一，載之史冊可攷也。漢文、宣、光三帝，唐太、玄、憲三宗，宋太祖暨太宗、仁宗，皆所謂希世之賢君者，而彗皆屢見，何歟？自古遇彗陳言之臣，若申繻、高堂隆之說，其誣不言可知。若宋吕公著、程頤、富弼、吕大防、吕大鈞、邢恕、王安禮、陳
translation_en:
…did he establish his government by discerning how institutions interconnect and adapt to changing circumstances? Please explain this fully, to investigate the intentions behind the sages’ institutional arrangements and the governmental measures adopted in later ages in response to their times.

Question: Heaven’s heart benevolently loves the ruler of men, yet sends disasters and anomalies to reprimand and admonish him. In antiquity, Gaozong of Yin brought about a resurgence following the crowing of a pheasant, and King Xuan of Zhou did so following a drought attributed to the drought demon. Heaven is particularly solicitous toward rulers who restore their dynasties. Our emperor’s benevolence, filial piety, sincerity, and reverence reach the spirits. In recent years, the Yellow River has run clear and sweet dew has descended: Heaven’s harmonious response has been consummate. Why, then, has a comet occasionally appeared? Our emperor subjected himself to earnest self-cultivation and scrutiny, and further issued an edict admonishing all his ministers to exercise greater vigilance and discipline. The comet consequently disappeared. This embodies the principle that the former kings were duly attentive to Heaven’s warnings and their ministers faithfully observed constant norms. Yet the Spring and Autumn Annals records three appearances of a “bushy star,” which both the Zuo and Gongyang commentaries describe as comets. There have been numerous appearances since then, recorded in the histories and available for examination. The three Han emperors Wendi, Xuandi, and Guangwudi; the three Tang emperors Taizong, Xuanzong, and Xianzong; and Song Taizu, Taizong, and Renzong were all worthy rulers of a kind rarely seen in any age. Why, then, did comets repeatedly appear during all their reigns? Among ministers who, from antiquity onward, presented advice upon the appearance of a comet, the falsity of such explanations as those of Shen Xu and Gaotang Long is evident without further discussion. As for the Song ministers Lü Gongzhu, Cheng Yi, Fu Bi, Lü Dafang, Lü Dajun, Xing Shu, Wang Anli, Chen…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
并吕好問王襄諸臣之疏其切要之旨
可為上下交脩之助者願有聞也
問儲蓄國之大計而漕運又儲蓄之所自
也漢唐都關中運道止河渭一路宋都
汴梁運道所至凡四路今其法可得而
言歟至元都燕始通海漕元史謂為一
代良法又謂視河漕之數所得盖多然
則其議倡於何人歟我
朝洪武永樂初猶通海漕至會通河通利始
===
罷自此歳運充積
京師富盛矣然慮者猶謂海漕亦不可廢其
果然歟夫制用非一端要之利國利民
而已若戍淮南湖蕩之田如魏鄧艾之
計耕京東瀕海之處如元虞集之策墾
監苑牧馬之地如宋熈寧之法抑可以
寛民力省歳漕否歟事關經國謀貴逺
慮請畫一以告俟
廟堂之上擇焉
punctuated:
并、吕好問、王襄諸臣之疏，其切要之旨，可為上下交脩之助者，願有聞也。

問：儲蓄，國之大計，而漕運又儲蓄之所自也。漢唐都關中，運道止河渭一路；宋都汴梁，運道所至凡四路。今其法可得而言歟？至元都燕，始通海漕。《元史》謂為一代良法，又謂視河漕之數，所得盖多。然則其議倡於何人歟？我朝洪武、永樂初，猶通海漕，至會通河通利始罷。自此歳運充積，京師富盛矣。然慮者猶謂海漕亦不可廢，其果然歟？夫制用非一端，要之利國利民而已。若戍淮南湖蕩之田，如魏鄧艾之計；耕京東瀕海之處，如元虞集之策；墾監苑牧馬之地，如宋熈寧之法：抑可以寛民力、省歳漕否歟？事關經國，謀貴逺慮。請畫一以告，俟廟堂之上擇焉。
translation_en:
…Bing [?], Lü Haowen, Wang Xiang, and the other ministers: I wish to hear the essential points of their memorials that could help those above and below cultivate themselves together.

Question: Maintaining reserves is a great matter of state planning, and grain transport is the means by which those reserves are supplied. The Han and Tang established their capitals in Guanzhong, and their transport followed just one route, along the Yellow and Wei rivers. The Song established its capital at Bianliang, which was reached by four transport routes in all. Can their methods now be explained? When the Yuan established its capital at Yan, it opened maritime grain transport. The History of the Yuan calls this an excellent system of that dynasty and also states that the quantity received was greater than that transported by river. Who, then, first proposed it? In our dynasty, maritime grain transport continued during the Hongwu reign and the beginning of the Yongle reign. It ceased only when the Huitong Canal became readily navigable. Thereafter, annual shipments filled the stores, and the capital became prosperous and amply supplied. Yet those concerned with long-term planning still maintain that maritime grain transport must not be abandoned. Is this indeed so?

There is more than one way to regulate expenditure; the essential aim is simply to benefit the state and the people. If garrisons were established on the lands amid the lakes and marshes of Huainan [?], following Deng Ai’s plan in the Wei; if coastal lands in Jingdong were cultivated, following Yu Ji’s proposal in the Yuan; or if horse-pasture lands administered by the imperial stud establishments were reclaimed, following the practice of the Song’s Xining reign period—might these measures ease the burden on the people and reduce annual grain shipments? These matters concern the governance of the state, and planning requires foresight. Please set out your recommendations point by point, so that the court may choose among them.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
問荆楚天地之要區也其地廣濶五方雜
寓故宜城有梧州之孝子荆州寓高平
之詞人吳興考功留之穀城濟源少保
處于長沙有舉進士第一而自濱州遷
襄州者有為時宰所惡而棄武夷居當
陽者廣漢南軒之家潭州廣信疊山之
徙興國其他若耿介出塵如丁鶴年矜
式學者如龍仁夫邑民敬之如李安國
州里增重如劉凝之茲數人者抑何負
===
於湖哉我
朝自
國初以至今日荆楚之民固晏如也夫何流
民之聚者乃成客戶凌主之勢或假繼
贅而奪之產或誘借貸而取其貲或駕
虛詞而重其禍其將何以生生歟伊欲
俾居者安来者撫其道果安在歟諸士
生長是邦必有能言之者幸以告我
punctuated:
問：荆楚，天地之要區也。其地廣濶，五方雜寓。故宜城有梧州之孝子，荆州寓高平之詞人，吳興考功留之穀城，濟源少保處于長沙。有舉進士第一而自濱州遷襄州者，有為時宰所惡而棄武夷居當陽者。廣漢南軒之家潭州，廣信疊山之徙興國。其他若耿介出塵如丁鶴年，矜式學者如龍仁夫，邑民敬之如李安國，州里增重如劉凝之。茲數人者，抑何負於湖哉？
我朝自國初以至今日，荆楚之民固晏如也。夫何流民之聚者，乃成客戶凌主之勢？或假繼贅而奪之產，或誘借貸而取其貲，或駕虛詞而重其禍，其將何以生生歟？伊欲俾居者安、来者撫，其道果安在歟？諸士生長是邦，必有能言之者，幸以告我。
translation_en:
Question: Jingchu is a vital region of the realm. Its territory is vast, and people from all quarters dwell there together. Thus Yicheng had a filial son from Wuzhou; Jingzhou accommodated a literary man from Gaoping; the Director of the Bureau of Merit Evaluation from Wuxing remained in Gucheng; and the Junior Guardian from Jiyuan resided in Changsha. One man, having placed first in the jinshi examination, moved from Binzhou to Xiangzhou; another, hated by the chief minister of his day, left Wuyi to live in Dangyang. Nanxuan of Guanghan made his home in Tanzhou, and Dieshan of Guangxin moved to Xingguo. Among others were Ding Henian, upright and above worldly concerns; Long Renfu, a model for scholars; Li Anguo, revered by the county’s people; and Liu Ningzhi, whose presence enhanced his locality’s standing. How did these men ever fail Huguang?
Under our dynasty, from its founding down to the present day, the people of Jingchu have certainly lived in peace. Why, then, have gatherings of displaced people brought about a situation in which newcomer households overbear established residents? Some seize their property under the pretext of becoming heirs or marrying into their households; some entice them into borrowing and take their wealth; some fabricate allegations and compound their misfortunes. How are they then to sustain their livelihoods? If we wish to ensure that established residents live securely and newcomers are cared for, where, indeed, does the proper course lie? You scholars grew up in this region; surely some of you can speak to this matter. Kindly explain it to me.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
志於道據於德依於仁游於藝
龔卿
同考試官教諭韓批〔簡而文是復古者〕
同考試官教諭黄批〔雋永自然可以式矣〕
同考試官教授陳批〔發明孔子論學之旨無餘〕
考試官行人徐批〔傳明〕
聖人論學而序其功也盖為學有序也知所先
===
後其庶矣乎聖人之意豈不以學也者其序不
可紊而其功不可缺知此者斯善學矣故學莫
先於立志而人倫日用當行者道也道而志之
則尊所聞行所知趨向正而無他岐之惑矣學
尤貴於有守而道得於心者德也德而據焉則
守之貴行之利終始一而有日新之功矣以至
心德之全曰仁仁弗依非學也其必功夫益密
而無終食之違則成性存存何適而非天理之
流行歟若夫藝又至理所寓焉者藝弗游抑非
punctuated:
第壹塲
四書
「志於道，據於德，依於仁，游於藝。」
龔卿
同考試官教諭韓批〔簡而文，是復古者。〕
同考試官教諭黄批〔雋永自然，可以式矣。〕
同考試官教授陳批〔發明孔子論學之旨無餘。〕
考試官行人徐批〔傳明。〕
聖人論學而序其功也，盖為學有序也，知所先後，其庶矣乎！聖人之意，豈不以學也者，其序不可紊，而其功不可缺，知此者斯善學矣。故學莫先於立志，而人倫日用當行者，道也。道而志之，則尊所聞，行所知，趨向正而無他岐之惑矣。學尤貴於有守，而道得於心者，德也。德而據焉，則守之貴，行之利，終始一而有日新之功矣。以至心德之全曰仁，仁弗依，非學也。其必功夫益密，而無終食之違，則成性存存，何適而非天理之流行歟！若夫藝，又至理所寓焉者。藝弗游，抑非
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
“Set your resolve on the Way, hold firmly to virtue, rely upon humaneness, and range freely among the arts.”
Gong Qing
Associate Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: 〔Concise yet elegant: this is a writer who restores the ancient style.〕
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Rich in lasting meaning and natural in expression; it may serve as a model.〕
Associate Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: 〔It fully elucidates the meaning of Confucius’s discussion of learning.〕
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: 〔The exposition is clear [?].〕
In discussing learning, the Sage set out the sequence of its endeavors. Learning indeed has an order: knowing what comes first and what follows, one is surely close to the goal! Was not the Sage’s meaning that, in learning, its sequence must not be confused and none of its endeavors may be omitted? Those who understand this know how to learn well.
Thus, in learning, nothing comes before establishing one’s resolve. What ought to be practiced in human relationships and daily life is the Way. If one sets one’s resolve upon the Way, one honors what one has heard and practices what one knows; one’s direction is correct, without the confusion of divergent paths. Learning particularly prizes holding steadfastly to something. The Way apprehended in the heart is virtue. If one holds firmly to virtue, one prizes keeping to it [?] and practices it smoothly, remaining consistent from beginning to end and making progress in daily renewal.
Furthermore, the completeness of the heart’s virtue is called humaneness. Learning without relying upon humaneness is no learning at all. One must make one’s efforts ever more meticulous, never departing from it even for the duration of a meal. Then one continually preserves one’s perfected nature: wherever one goes, is this not the flowing operation of Heaven’s principle? As for the arts, they too are where the highest principle resides. If one does not range freely among the arts, this likewise is not…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
學也其必朝夕與游以博其義理之趣則以我
物物而心亦何所放哉該本末而不偏合內外
而無間下學之全功盡之矣抑學以求諸內者
也故聖人每教人以務本然何終取於游藝耶
盖不外物以求理而常玩物以養性雖聖賢亦
有不得而廢者故曰有始有卒者其惟聖人乎
噫周孔多藝夫豈無謂也哉
郊社之禮所以事上帝也宗廟之禮所以
祀乎其先也
===
丘柟
同考試官教諭陳 批 說出達孝意宜錄之為士
子式
考試官行人徐 批 達於禮者
聖人制祀禮享帝享親者也夫禮莫大於祭祀
聖人制禮皆以義起所以謂達孝也歟中庸十
九章引此明道之費者成周制禮有曰郊社曰
宗廟者以郊社言之冬至有事于圜丘夏至有
事于方澤是禮之所以者以天地大父母也大
punctuated:
學也。其必朝夕與游，以博其義理之趣，則以我物物，而心亦何所放哉？該本末而不偏，合內外而無間，下學之全功盡之矣。抑學以求諸內者也，故聖人每教人以務本，然何終取於游藝耶？盖不外物以求理，而常玩物以養性，雖聖賢亦有不得而廢者，故曰：「有始有卒者，其惟聖人乎！」噫！周孔多藝，夫豈無謂也哉！

郊社之禮，所以事上帝也；宗廟之禮，所以祀乎其先也。

丘柟

同考試官教諭陳批：說出達孝意，宜錄之為士子式。

考試官行人徐批：達於禮者。

聖人制祀禮，享帝享親者也。夫禮莫大於祭祀，聖人制禮，皆以義起，所以謂達孝也歟？中庸十九章引此明道之費者。成周制禮，有曰郊社、曰宗廟者。以郊社言之，冬至有事于圜丘，夏至有事于方澤，是禮之所以者，以天地大父母也。大
translation_en:
…learning either. One must surely engage in the arts morning and evening, thereby broadening one’s appreciation of their moral principles. Then one will govern things through oneself: where could the mind stray? Encompassing both root and branches without partiality, uniting inner and outer without any gap, this fulfills the entire work of learning through ordinary affairs. Yet learning seeks within oneself; hence the sage always teaches people to attend to the root. Why, then, does he finally turn to finding recreation in the arts? It is because one does not seek principle apart from things, but constantly contemplates things to nourish one’s nature. Even sages and worthies cannot dispense with this. Thus it is said: “To have both a beginning and a completion—surely only the sage can do this!” Ah! The Duke of Zhou and Confucius were skilled in many arts. Could this have been without purpose?

“The rites of the suburban and soil altars are the means by which one serves the Lord on High; the rites of the ancestral temple are the means by which one sacrifices to one’s ancestors.”

Qiu Nan 丘柟

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “It brings out the meaning of fully realized filial piety. It should be recorded as a model for examination candidates.”

Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “One who understands ritual.”

The sage established sacrificial rites to offer worship to the Lord on High and to his parents. Among rites, none is greater than sacrifice. In establishing rites, the sage invariably proceeded from what was right. Is this not why it is called fully realized filial piety? Chapter nineteen of the Doctrine of the Mean cites this to illuminate the extensive reach of the Way. Among the rites established by the Zhou were those called the suburban and soil sacrifices and those called the ancestral temple sacrifices. Speaking of the suburban and soil sacrifices, ceremonies are performed at the Round Mound on the winter solstice and at the Square Pool on the summer solstice. The reason for these rites is that Heaven and Earth are the great father and mother. “Great…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
哉乾元萬物資始至哉坤元萬物資生惟大君
為之宗子其必齊祓一心達此精明之德對越
于上下者也故曰祀帝于郊敬之至也以宗廟
言之追始祖所自出而配以始祖舉四時之常
祭而享于群廟是禮之所以者以先王啓邦土
也誕膺天命以撫方夏佑啓後人咸正無缺惟
曾孫旣已大正其必有孚顒若將此觀盥之誠
仰承于祖考者也故曰宗廟之禮仁之至也合
而觀之尊尊親親周道備矣此武王周公其達
===
孝也歟抑夫子嘗曰周之文至矣使成周子孫
世而守之周至今猶存可也何至有韓宣子適
魯之嘆夫子老聃之問也信夫知其說者其如
視諸斯爾夫
使天下仕者皆欲立於王之朝耕者皆欲
耕於王之野商賈皆欲藏於王之市行
旅皆欲出於王之途
傅順
同考試官學正區批明王道者讀之灑然
punctuated:
哉，乾元，萬物資始！至哉，坤元，萬物資生！惟大君為之宗子，其必齊祓一心，達此精明之德，對越于上下者也。故曰：「祀帝于郊，敬之至也。」以宗廟言之，追始祖所自出而配以始祖，舉四時之常祭而享于群廟。是禮之所以者，以先王啓邦土也。誕膺天命，以撫方夏，佑啓後人，咸正無缺。惟曾孫旣已大正，其必有孚顒若，將此觀盥之誠，仰承于祖考者也。故曰：「宗廟之禮，仁之至也。」合而觀之，尊尊親親，周道備矣。此武王、周公其達孝也歟！抑夫子嘗曰：「周之文至矣！」使成周子孫世而守之，周至今猶存可也。何至有韓宣子適魯之嘆、夫子老聃之問也？信夫，知其說者，其如視諸斯爾夫！
使天下仕者皆欲立於王之朝，耕者皆欲耕於王之野，商賈皆欲藏於王之市，行旅皆欲出於王之途。
傅順
同考試官學正區批：明王道者，讀之灑然。
translation_en:
…great indeed is the primal power of Qian: all things depend upon it for their beginning! Consummate indeed is the primal power of Kun: all things depend upon it for their birth! The sovereign alone serves as their principal lineage heir. He must purify himself and unify his mind, bringing this lucid spiritual potency to full expression and reverently responding to those above and below. Thus it is said: “Sacrificing to the Lord on High at the suburban altar is the utmost expression of reverence.” As for the ancestral temples, one traces the source from which the founding ancestor issued and associates the founding ancestor with it in sacrifice; one performs the regular sacrifices of the four seasons and presents offerings in the various temples. The reason for these rites is that the former kings opened up the realm. They received Heaven’s great mandate to bring peace to the lands of Xia, protecting and guiding their descendants so that all might be rightly ordered, with nothing lacking. Once the descendant has firmly established proper order, he must surely possess sincerity and reverence, offering up to his forebears the sincerity expressed in the ritual washing of the hexagram Guan, Contemplation. Thus it is said: “The rites of the ancestral temples are the utmost expression of benevolence.” Taken together, honoring the honored and cherishing one’s kin embody the completeness of the Way of Zhou. Was this not the consummate filial piety of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou?
Moreover, the Master once said: “The cultural refinement of Zhou has reached perfection!” Had the descendants of Zhou preserved it generation after generation, Zhou could have survived even to the present. How, then, could there have been occasion for Han Xuanzi’s exclamation when visiting Lu, or for the Master’s inquiries of Lao Dan? Truly, for one who understood the meaning of these rites, governing would be as plain as looking at this spot here!
“Cause all those under Heaven who seek office to wish to stand at Your Majesty’s court; all who farm to wish to till Your Majesty’s fields; all merchants to wish to store their goods in Your Majesty’s markets; and all travelers to wish to journey along Your Majesty’s roads.”
Fu Shun
Comment by Associate Examiner Ou, Instructor: “One who understands the Kingly Way will find this refreshing to read.”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎授張批講仁力明白如此者絕少
考試官行人徐批簡古
大賢於齊君啓其見與於天下也夫仁天下莫
不與也齊君其知本哉孟子之意盖謂今王發
政施仁則推恩保民矣惻隱根於一心而趨向
鼓于天下豈但已耶使夫仕與耕者皆欲立于
王之朝焉耕于王之野焉或利用賓王而尚觀
光之志或舍彼穡事而思樂土之歸丕應傒志
固有不約而同者是孰使之然哉惟所欲之在
===
此耳商賈行旅皆欲藏于王之市焉出于王之
途焉或願聚貨於日中而交易得所或願問禁
於國門而即次懷資罔不是孚固有不召而至
者抑豈私於我哉惟民歸於德耳夫仁之感人
其速如此校之以力其難易當自辯之大抵唐
虞無力法三代無力兵豈其智之不桓文若哉
取舍定而功業隨焉否泰分矣噫聖人之情其
可見也夫
易
punctuated:
同考試官敎授張批：講仁力明白如此者絕少。
考試官行人徐批：簡古。
大賢於齊君啓其見與於天下也。夫仁，天下莫不與也，齊君其知本哉！孟子之意盖謂：今王發政施仁，則推恩保民矣。惻隱根於一心，而趨向鼓于天下，豈但已耶？使夫仕與耕者，皆欲立于王之朝焉，耕于王之野焉。或利用賓王，而尚觀光之志；或舍彼穡事，而思樂土之歸。丕應傒志，固有不約而同者，是孰使之然哉？惟所欲之在此耳。商賈行旅，皆欲藏于王之市焉，出于王之途焉。或願聚貨於日中，而交易得所；或願問禁於國門，而即次懷資。罔不是孚，固有不召而至者，抑豈私於我哉？惟民歸於德耳。夫仁之感人，其速如此，校之以力，其難易當自辯之。大抵唐虞無力法，三代無力兵，豈其智之不桓文若哉？取舍定而功業隨焉，否泰分矣。噫！聖人之情，其可見也夫！
易
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhang, an Instructor, comments: “Expositions of benevolence and force as clear as this are exceedingly rare.”
Examiner Xu, a Messenger, comments: “Concise and antique in style.”
The great worthy showed the ruler of Qi how to gain the allegiance of all under Heaven. For when one practices benevolence, none under Heaven will fail to give their allegiance. May the ruler of Qi recognize this fundamental principle! Mencius’s meaning was, presumably: if Your Majesty now issues policies and practices benevolence, you will extend your favor and protect the people. Compassion takes root in a single heart, yet stirs the inclinations of all under Heaven. Could its effects stop there?
It would make those who serve in office and those who farm all wish to stand at Your Majesty’s court and cultivate Your Majesty’s fields. Some, finding it advantageous to become the king’s guests, would cherish the ambition to behold the splendor of his realm; others would abandon their farming elsewhere and long to make their home in this happy land. Responding abundantly and fulfilling their hopes [?], they would of themselves agree without prior arrangement. Who would make them do so? It is simply that what they desire is here.
Merchants and travelers would all wish to store their goods in Your Majesty’s markets and journey along Your Majesty’s roads. Some would wish to gather their goods at midday, finding a suitable place to trade; others would wish to inquire about prohibitions at the gates of the realm, then take up lodging with their possessions. None would fail to place their trust in this; they would of themselves arrive without being summoned. Could this be personal partiality toward me? It is simply that the people turn toward virtue.
Such is the speed with which benevolence moves people. Compare it with force, and one should discern for oneself which is difficult and which is easy. Broadly speaking, the ages of Tang and Yu had no methods founded on force, and the Three Dynasties had no armies founded on force. Could it be that their wisdom fell short of that of Dukes Huan and Wen? Once the choice of what to adopt and what to reject is settled, achievements follow accordingly, and the paths of adversity and prosperity diverge. Ah! Here we may indeed perceive the sage’s true intent!
Book of Changes

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
牝馬地類行地无疆柔順利貞君子攸行
胡鰲
同考試官教諭徐批說坤之利貞甚善
同考試官教授唐批善言坤德錄之
考試官行人徐批精潔
彖傳言坤之利貞徵諸物而歸于人也盖物有
得乎坤道之純者也而君子所行如之利貞於
是乎可見矣且坤德有四文王於利貞而以牝
馬為言者何也盖物各有類也馬雖乾象而形
===
乃坤道所成則為牝矣於稽其類其惟地乎類
各相從也馬雖動物而行乃下麗乎地則為順
矣致遠不禦何有疆乎凡同類者舉相似也以
牝馬觀之是知坤之為德相見者於此致役若
柔而无為也知始者於是代終惟順以承天也
然其遂乎物也賦形有定分各宜焉其成乎物
也實理具足靜而正焉順而且健如此君子法
之必有道矣分所當然即之以為安立不易其
方也義所當從順之以為利履不變其素也夫
punctuated:
牝馬地類，行地无疆，柔順利貞，君子攸行。
胡鰲
同考試官教諭徐批：說坤之利貞甚善。
同考試官教授唐批：善言坤德，錄之。
考試官行人徐批：精潔。
彖傳言坤之利貞，徵諸物而歸于人也。盖物有得乎坤道之純者也，而君子所行如之，利貞於是乎可見矣。且坤德有四，文王於利貞而以牝馬為言者，何也？盖物各有類也，馬雖乾象，而形乃坤道所成，則為牝矣。於稽其類，其惟地乎？類各相從也，馬雖動物，而行乃下麗乎地，則為順矣。致遠不禦，何有疆乎？凡同類者，舉相似也。以牝馬觀之，是知坤之為德，相見者於此致役，若柔而无為也；知始者於是代終，惟順以承天也。然其遂乎物也，賦形有定，分各宜焉；其成乎物也，實理具足，靜而正焉。順而且健如此，君子法之，必有道矣。分所當然，即之以為安，立不易其方也；義所當從，順之以為利，履不變其素也。夫
translation_en:
“The mare belongs to the same category as earth; she travels over the earth without limit. Gentle and compliant, beneficial and steadfast: this is the course the gentleman follows.”
Hu Ao
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of Kun’s benefit and steadfastness is excellent.”
Associate Examiner Tang, Professor, comments: “It speaks well of Kun’s virtue. Select it.”
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “Refined and clean.”
The Commentary on the Judgments discusses Kun’s benefit and steadfastness by seeking evidence among things and bringing it back to human beings. For among things there are those that possess the purity of Kun’s Way; the gentleman follows a similar course, and through this its benefit and steadfastness can be seen. Now Kun has four virtues. Why, when speaking of benefit and steadfastness, did King Wen speak of a mare? All things have their respective categories. Although the horse is an image of Qian, its bodily form is brought to completion through Kun’s Way; hence it is represented as female. If we examine its category [?], does it not belong with earth? Each category follows its own kind. Although the horse is a moving creature, in its movement it remains attached to the earth below; hence it is compliant. It reaches far without being checked: what boundary could there be?
All things of the same category resemble one another. Looking at the mare, we thus understand Kun’s virtue: the things that meet one another here are brought into service, as though Kun were gentle and did not act; what the power presiding over beginnings initiates, Kun brings to completion in its stead, complying alone in order to receive Heaven’s influence. Yet in fostering things, it gives them definite forms, each with its appropriate allotted place; in completing things, it fully endows them with substantial principle, still and correct. Since it is both compliant and vigorous in this way, the gentleman must have a way of taking it as his model. He accepts what his allotted station requires and finds repose in it, standing firm without changing his direction. He follows what righteousness requires and finds benefit in it, conducting himself without altering his enduring principles. Now …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
是之為安貞其斯免於過舉乎大抵天下之道
乾坤盡之坤之德常減於乾之半而能配乎乾
以是道也不順則倡始不健則无終是其健者
亦順之常耳此坤德所以為美而妻道臣道所
當知也苟處坤之位而昧其義難矣哉君子慎
之
天地之道貞觀者也日月之道貞明者也
天下之動貞夫一者也
熊鳳儀
===
同考試官教諭徐批能體貼經意
同考試官教授唐批觀於文可以知子之慎動矣
考試官行人徐批明暢
大傳論吉凶貞勝必即造化而推其理之一也
盖天下不一者動至一者理也大傳推諸造化
以明之欲人慎動也夫聖人之意盖曰辯吉凶
者存乎辭生吉凶者存乎動所以一乎動者理
而已且法象莫大乎天地也而其為道體之隱
者不可揜化之顯者無非教雖或時有愆違其
punctuated:
是之為安貞，其斯免於過舉乎？大抵天下之道，乾坤盡之。坤之德常減於乾之半，而能配乎乾，以是道也。不順則倡始，不健則无終，是其健者亦順之常耳。此坤德所以為美，而妻道臣道所當知也。苟處坤之位而昧其義，難矣哉！君子慎之。
天地之道，貞觀者也；日月之道，貞明者也；天下之動，貞夫一者也。
熊鳳儀
同考試官教諭徐批：能體貼經意。
同考試官教授唐批：觀於文，可以知子之慎動矣。
考試官行人徐批：明暢。
大傳論吉凶貞勝，必即造化而推其理之一也。盖天下不一者動，至一者理也。大傳推諸造化以明之，欲人慎動也。夫聖人之意盖曰：辯吉凶者存乎辭，生吉凶者存乎動，所以一乎動者理而已。且法象莫大乎天地也，而其為道，體之隱者不可揜，化之顯者無非教。雖或時有愆違，其
translation_en:
…This is what is meant by resting securely in correctness. Would one not thereby avoid errors in action? Broadly speaking, Qian and Kun encompass the Way of all under Heaven. Kun’s virtue is always half that of Qian, yet it can complement Qian by following this Way. Without compliance, it would take the initiative; without vigor, it would fail to carry things through. Its vigor, then, is simply the constancy of its compliance. This is what makes Kun’s virtue admirable, and what those following the way of a wife or a minister ought to understand. To occupy Kun’s position yet remain ignorant of its meaning would indeed be perilous! The gentleman must take care in this.
“The Way of Heaven and Earth is constantly displayed; the Way of the sun and moon is constantly bright; the movements of all under Heaven are held constant by the one.”
Xiong Fengyi
Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “Able to enter sympathetically into the meaning of the Classic.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Professor: “From this composition, one can see your care in taking action.”
Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “Clear and fluent.”
When the Great Commentary discusses how good and ill fortune prevail through constancy, it necessarily turns to the creative transformations of nature to infer the unity of their underlying principle. For what is diverse under Heaven is movement; what is supremely one is principle. The Great Commentary elucidates this by extending its inquiry to the creative transformations of nature, wishing people to act with care. The sage’s meaning is, in effect: distinguishing good and ill fortune rests with the statements; producing good and ill fortune rests with movement; what unifies movement is principle alone. Moreover, among models and images, none are greater than Heaven and Earth. title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
所正而常者觀而已矣懸象莫大於日月也而
其為道陰陽之精互藏其宅晝夜之運相推而
生雖或時有晦蝕其所正而常者明而已矣造
化不違乎貞如此而况於吉凶乎執是而推可
見天下之故性以物感而愛惡之相攻事以情
遷而得失之互見夫何常之有然途雖殊而歸
同慮雖百而致一順之而動則罔不吉所以致
吉者此理也逆之而動則罔不凶所以為凶者
亦此理也不曰貞夫一乎學者審於此焉可以
===
慎動矣雖然天下之事固有貞而凶不貞而吉
者何也此以事論也如其貞而不吉於道實競
吉孰甚焉不貞而不凶於道實疚凶孰甚焉故
君子不以吉凶在外者為虞而以貞於道為貴
書
無怠無荒四夷來王
傅順
同考試官學正區 批 可為儆戒者法
同考試官教授張 批 虞廷保治氣象如在目前
punctuated:
所正而常者，觀而已矣。懸象莫大於日月也，而其為道，陰陽之精互藏其宅，晝夜之運相推而生。雖或時有晦蝕，其所正而常者，明而已矣。造化不違乎貞如此，而况於吉凶乎？執是而推，可見天下之故。性以物感，而愛惡之相攻；事以情遷，而得失之互見。夫何常之有？然途雖殊而歸同，慮雖百而致一。順之而動，則罔不吉，所以致吉者，此理也；逆之而動，則罔不凶，所以為凶者，亦此理也。不曰貞夫一乎？學者審於此焉，可以慎動矣。雖然，天下之事固有貞而凶、不貞而吉者，何也？此以事論也。如其貞而不吉，於道實競，吉孰甚焉？不貞而不凶，於道實疚，凶孰甚焉？故君子不以吉凶在外者為虞，而以貞於道為貴。

書
無怠無荒，四夷來王。
傅順
同考試官學正區批：可為儆戒者法。
同考試官教授張批：虞廷保治氣象，如在目前。
translation_en:
…what is correct and constant in them is simply their manifestation to view [?]. Among the images suspended above, none are greater than the sun and moon. In their operation, the essences of yin and yang each lie hidden in their respective abodes, while the cycles of day and night arise through their mutual succession. Though there may sometimes be darkness or eclipses, what is correct and constant in them is simply their brightness. If the processes of creation and transformation adhere to constancy in this way, how much more must good and ill fortune do so? By taking this as a basis and extending the reasoning, one can understand the workings of the world. Human nature is stirred by things, and love and hatred contend with one another; affairs shift with circumstances, and gain and loss appear in turn. What constancy is there in these? Yet although the paths differ, their destination is the same; although deliberations are a hundredfold, their ultimate end is one. If one acts in accordance with this principle, nothing fails to be auspicious: what brings about good fortune is this principle. If one acts against it, nothing fails to be inauspicious: what brings about ill fortune is also this principle. Is this not what is meant by being constant in the one? Scholars who examine this closely can act with caution.

Nevertheless, in the affairs of the world there certainly are those who remain correct yet encounter ill fortune, and those who fail to remain correct yet encounter good fortune. Why is this? Such judgments concern only events. If someone remains correct yet encounters no good fortune, he is in truth strong in relation to the Way; what greater good fortune could there be? If someone fails to remain correct yet encounters no ill fortune, he is in truth afflicted in relation to the Way; what greater ill fortune could there be? Thus the gentleman does not worry about good or ill fortune in external circumstances, but prizes steadfast correctness in the Way.

Book of Documents
“Be neither idle nor neglectful, and the peoples of the four quarters will come to acknowledge your kingship.”
Fu Shun
Associate Examiner Ou, School Instructor, comments: “This can serve as a model for those offering admonition.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “The atmosphere of preserving good government at the court of Shun seems present before our very eyes.”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官行人徐批善警
勤內治而來遠人大臣警聖君然也盖內治聖
王所自盡者也遠人之來其有所感已夫伯益
警帝舜之意若謂人君守成業而致盛治者其
惟憂勤乎是故儆戒之道有所謂法度逸樂焉
用舍理欲焉帝其念哉曰弗慮胡獲兢兢然極
深以通天下之志曰弗為胡成業業然惟幾以
成天下之務說諸心研諸慮朝夕其戒懼也將
有為將有行內外其交脩也夫是之謂克艱夫
===
是之謂惠迪而治道益隆矣豈惟中國之服從
也哉彼四夷者昔在放勳之朝嘗率服矣今則
復通言語於重譯昔仰於變之休無猾夏矣庶
幾再格干羽于兩階盖重華協帝也而聲名洋
溢莫不尊親帝德光天也而道洽政治罔不咸
賴何有弗來王者耶治至于此無虞者可永保
矣夫自古聖人之於夷狄治之以不治而已彼
之來否何足為中國輕重而益乃揭諸儆戒哉
盖夷狄來而後自治有足徵者聖人志壹動氣
punctuated:
考試官行人徐批：善警。

勤內治而來遠人，大臣警聖君然也。盖內治，聖王所自盡者也；遠人之來，其有所感已。夫伯益警帝舜之意，若謂人君守成業而致盛治者，其惟憂勤乎！是故儆戒之道，有所謂法度逸樂焉，用舍理欲焉，帝其念哉！曰：「弗慮胡獲？」兢兢然極深，以通天下之志；曰：「弗為胡成？」業業然惟幾，以成天下之務。說諸心，研諸慮，朝夕其戒懼也；將有為，將有行，內外其交脩也。夫是之謂克艱，夫是之謂惠迪，而治道益隆矣。豈惟中國之服從也哉！彼四夷者，昔在放勳之朝，嘗率服矣，今則復通言語於重譯；昔仰於變之休，無猾夏矣，庶幾再格干羽于兩階。盖重華協帝也，而聲名洋溢，莫不尊親；帝德光天也，而道洽政治，罔不咸賴。何有弗來王者耶？治至于此，無虞者可永保矣。夫自古聖人之於夷狄，治之以不治而已。彼之來否，何足為中國輕重，而益乃揭諸儆戒哉？盖夷狄來，而後自治有足徵者，聖人志壹動氣
translation_en:
Examiner Xu, a Messenger, comments: “An effective admonition.”

Be diligent in governing within, and bring distant peoples to court: such is a great minister’s admonition to a sage ruler. For internal government is where the sage king fully exerts himself; when distant peoples come, something must have moved them to do so. The intent of Bo Yi’s admonition to Emperor Shun was, it seems, to say: if a ruler is to preserve an established achievement and bring government to flourishing perfection, must it not be through anxious diligence? Thus the way of admonition concerns laws and standards, ease and pleasure, employment and dismissal, moral principle and desire. Let the emperor reflect upon these!

He says, “Without deliberation, how can there be attainment?” With fearful vigilance, probe the utmost depths to comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven. He says, “Without action, how can there be accomplishment?” With reverent care, attend to the first stirrings of events to accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven. Take these teachings to heart with delight and examine them in thought, maintaining vigilance and apprehension morning and evening. Whenever undertaking or carrying out anything, cultivate both the inward and the outward together. This is what is called mastering difficulty; this is what is called following the right way. The way of government will thereby flourish ever more. Would it be only the people of the Central Lands who submit?

Those peoples of the four quarters had already submitted in the court of Fangxun [Yao]; now once again they communicate through successive interpreters. Formerly they looked up to the blessings of transformation and did not disturb the Central Lands; now one may hope that they will once more be won over by the shield-and-plume dances between the two stairways. For Chonghua [Shun] matched the former emperor, and his fame spread far and wide: none failed to honor and cherish him. The emperor’s virtue illuminated Heaven, his Way pervaded the realm, and government was well ordered: none failed to benefit. How could any fail to come and acknowledge him as king? When government reaches this point, freedom from troubles can be preserved forever.

From antiquity, sages have governed the peoples beyond the borders simply by leaving them ungoverned. Whether those peoples come or not, how could this add to or detract from the standing of the Central Lands? Why, then, did Yi highlight it in his admonition? Because only when those peoples come is there sufficient evidence of the success of one’s own government. The sage’s achievement in making the will single-minded so that it moves the vital force …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之功於是為大
所寳惟賢則邇人安
李相
同考試官學正區批句句是召公本意
同考試官教授張批融會處無滲漏可語經矣
考試官行人徐批知所寳
惟君一於貴德斯中國寧矣盖賢者中國所恃
以為安也然則君之所寳夫豈徒哉昔召公告
