武王意若曰君天下有寳也而物不與焉王之
===
慎德亦惟嚴之好尚無玩人爾夫人有賢者不
珍竒而適於用不異産而瑞於時至矣其為寳
也王惟謹貞度於隆遇之時重耳目於明聴之
寄展親脩職是固有可嘉者則合同姓異姓而
頒德貺焉盡心盡力固亦有當重者乃隨君子
小人而無狎侮焉寳賢如此則志不妄發以害
有益之功諫則必行而有膏澤之益藩垣屏翰
外禦其侮彼蠻夷其弗猾夏矣乎親賢樂利各
得其所我中國其永康矣乎否則功弗成民弗
punctuated:
之功，於是為大。

所寳惟賢則邇人安

李相

同考試官學正區批：句句是召公本意。
同考試官教授張批：融會處無滲漏，可語經矣。
考試官行人徐批：知所寳。

惟君一於貴德，斯中國寧矣。盖賢者，中國所恃以為安也。然則君之所寳，夫豈徒哉！昔召公告武王，意若曰：君天下有寳也，而物不與焉。王之慎德，亦惟嚴之好尚，無玩人爾。夫人有賢者，不珍竒而適於用，不異産而瑞於時，至矣其為寳也！王惟謹貞度於隆遇之時，重耳目於明聴之寄。展親脩職，是固有可嘉者，則合同姓異姓而頒德貺焉；盡心盡力，固亦有當重者，乃隨君子小人而無狎侮焉。寳賢如此，則志不妄發以害有益之功，諫則必行而有膏澤之益。藩垣屏翰，外禦其侮，彼蠻夷其弗猾夏矣乎？親賢樂利，各得其所，我中國其永康矣乎？否則功弗成，民弗
translation_en:
…the achievement of concentrating one’s resolve and thereby moving the vital energies is thus all the greater.

“When Those Treasured Are the Worthy, the People Nearby Are at Peace”

Li Xiang

Associate Examiner Ou, School Instructor, comments: “Every sentence conveys the Duke of Shao’s original intent.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “His integrated understanding leaves nothing unaccounted for; one may discuss the Classics with him.”
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “He knows what to treasure.”

Only when the ruler is single-minded in esteeming virtue will the Central States be tranquil. For the worthy are those upon whom the Central States depend for their peace. Can the ruler’s treasuring them, then, be without consequence? When the Duke of Shao admonished King Wu in former times, his meaning was as follows: A ruler of all under Heaven has his treasures, but material objects do not number among them. The king’s care for virtue consists simply in being exacting about his preferences and not treating people as playthings. Among men there are the worthy: they are no precious curiosities, yet they are suited to practical service; they are no exotic products, yet they are auspicious blessings for their age. Supreme indeed is their value as treasures!

The king should maintain correct standards when bestowing generous favor, and value those who serve as his eyes and ears when entrusting them with keeping him clearly informed. Those who show affection for their kin and discharge their duties certainly deserve praise; therefore, he should bring together those of his own surname and those of other surnames and distribute gracious gifts among them. Those who devote their whole hearts and strength likewise deserve esteem; accordingly, whether they are men of high or low station, he should treat none with disrespect or contempt.

If he treasures the worthy in this way, his intentions will not issue rashly and impair beneficial achievements; remonstrance will assuredly be acted upon, bringing the benefits of his beneficence. As enclosing walls and protective bulwarks, the worthy ward off aggression from without: surely those foreign peoples will then cease disturbing the Central States? Loving the worthy and delighting in the benefits of good rule, everyone will find their proper place: surely our Central States will then enjoy lasting peace? Otherwise, achievements will remain unfulfilled, and the people will not …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
足豈但遠人不之格也是以明王慎之抑受獒
細故也而召公懇懇至此何耶蓋持衡相勝而
剥復乗之憂危者所必爾也童牛弗牿堅氷晚
矣嗚呼相天下者其毋忽之哉而以蹈悔也
詩
王赫斯怒爰整其旅以按徂旅以篤于周
祜以對于天下
龔卿
同考試官教諭韓批興師之義模寫殆盡
===
同考試官教諭黃批雅義莊重
同考試官教授陳批聖人不得已之心溢於言表
考試官行人徐批温厚
聖人之行天討而所係者大焉夫王者之師為
天下國家舉也茲其所以為師之貞也歟此詩
言文王伐密之事蓋謂維我文王其為德也出
乎天授其用武也奉乎天心是故密人不恭罪
人不可不得也於是乎神武形于獨斷而赫然
一怒焉大邦敢距天憲不容不章也於是乎明
punctuated:
足，豈但遠人不之格也？是以明王慎之。抑受獒，細故也，而召公懇懇至此，何耶？蓋持衡相勝，而剥復乗之，憂危者所必爾也。童牛弗牿，堅氷晚矣。嗚呼！相天下者，其毋忽之哉，而以蹈悔也！

詩
王赫斯怒，爰整其旅，以按徂旅，以篤于周祜，以對于天下。
龔卿
同考試官教諭韓批：興師之義，模寫殆盡。
同考試官教諭黃批：雅義莊重。
同考試官教授陳批：聖人不得已之心，溢於言表。
考試官行人徐批：温厚。

聖人之行天討，而所係者大焉。夫王者之師，為天下國家舉也，茲其所以為師之貞也歟？此詩言文王伐密之事，蓋謂維我文王，其為德也出乎天授，其用武也奉乎天心。是故密人不恭，罪人不可不得也，於是乎神武形于獨斷，而赫然一怒焉。大邦敢距，天憲不容不章也，於是乎明
translation_en:
…sufficient. How could the consequence be merely that distant peoples failed to come into allegiance? Therefore the enlightened king treats this cautiously. Yet accepting a mastiff was a minor matter: why, then, did the Duke of Shao admonish him so earnestly? Because the opposing forces hang in the balance and contend for ascendancy, while decline and recovery follow upon them; those who fear danger must act thus. If the young bull is not fitted with a horn restraint, it will be too late when solid ice has formed. Alas! Those who assist in governing the world must not neglect this and thereby incur regret!

Book of Odes
“The king blazed with anger; then he marshaled his troops, to check the advancing host, to strengthen Zhou’s blessings, and to answer the expectations of all under Heaven.”
By Gong Qing.
Associate Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of raising an army is depicted almost exhaustively.”
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “The refined meaning is solemn and dignified.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “The sage’s sense of having no alternative is abundantly evident beyond the words.”
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “Gentle and generous.”

When a sage carries out Heaven’s punishment, matters of great consequence are at stake. The army of a true king is raised for the sake of all under Heaven and the state. Is this not what makes the army’s undertaking upright? This ode speaks of King Wen’s campaign against Mi. Its meaning is that our King Wen received his virtue from Heaven and, in employing military force, obeyed Heaven’s will. Thus, when the people of Mi acted disrespectfully, the guilty could not be left uncaptured. His divine martial power then manifested itself in his sole decision, and he blazed forth in anger. Since a great state dared to resist, Heaven’s law could not remain unproclaimed. Thereupon his illustrious…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
威將於告勅而爰整三軍焉侵阮者遏之俾不
得虔劉我人民也徂共者止之俾無以憑陵我
疆宇也夫興師以禦外侮非曰一人之慶也盖
宗社之佑也彼斵之我敦之周邦根本如地斯
載矣何孔厚乎行罰而安乎民非曰一人之願
也盖天下之心也民望之王慰之上下交感如
響斯應矣豈缺望乎吁王者一有所舉而兩有
所係如此盖亦因可怒而怒之何甞有所畔援
歆羨也哉甚矣周人之善乎奉天也觀其述祖
===
德也而皆歸于天宅曰帝顧配曰天立對曰天
作心曰帝度至于伐罪則曰帝謂而其要在求
民之莫而已八百年有道之長孰謂無所自哉
嘷嘷厥聲肅雝和鳴先祖是聽我客戾止
永觀厥成
陳京
同考試官教諭韓批周人音樂之盛此作盡之
同考試官教諭黃批形容作樂合祖意盡
同考試官教授陳批予殆有感嘷嘷之聲者
punctuated:
威將於告勅，而爰整三軍焉。侵阮者遏之，俾不得虔劉我人民也；徂共者止之，俾無以憑陵我疆宇也。夫興師以禦外侮，非曰一人之慶也，盖宗社之佑也。彼斵之，我敦之，周邦根本如地斯載矣，何孔厚乎！行罰而安乎民，非曰一人之願也，盖天下之心也。民望之，王慰之，上下交感，如響斯應矣，豈缺望乎？吁！王者一有所舉，而兩有所係如此，盖亦因可怒而怒之，何甞有所畔援歆羨也哉！甚矣，周人之善乎奉天也！觀其述祖德也，而皆歸于天：宅曰「帝顧」，配曰「天立」，對曰「天作」，心曰「帝度」，至于伐罪則曰「帝謂」，而其要在求民之莫而已。八百年有道之長，孰謂無所自哉！

嘷嘷厥聲，肅雝和鳴。先祖是聽。我客戾止，永觀厥成。

陳京

同考試官教諭韓批：周人音樂之盛，此作盡之。
同考試官教諭黃批：形容作樂合祖，意盡。
同考試官教授陳批：予殆有感嘷嘷之聲者。
translation_en:
…his manifest might was conveyed in proclamations and commands, and he thereupon marshaled the three armies. He checked those invading Ruan, so that they could not slaughter our people; he stopped those advancing upon Gong, so that they could not overrun our territory. Raising an army to repel foreign aggression was not a blessing for one man alone: it protected the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain. What they hacked away, we strengthened. The foundations of the Zhou state were sustained as though borne by the earth itself—how very firm they were! Inflicting punishment to bring peace to the people was not the wish of one man alone: it was the desire of all under Heaven. The people looked to their king, and he fulfilled their hopes. Those above and below moved one another, responding as an echo answers a sound. How could their hopes have been disappointed? Ah! A single undertaking by a true king had these two great concerns bound up with it. His anger arose only from what deserved anger. When did he ever act from vacillation or covetous desire?

How consummately the people of Zhou served Heaven! Observe how, in recounting their ancestor’s virtue, they attributed everything to Heaven. Of his dwelling they said, “The Lord on High looked upon it”; of his consort, “Heaven established her”; of his counterpart, “Heaven made him”; and of his heart, “The Lord on High measured it.” When it came to punishing the guilty, they said, “The Lord on High spoke.” Yet the essential purpose was simply to seek repose for the people. Who could say that their eight hundred years of enduring rule in accordance with the Way had no source?

“Resounding are their sounds,
Reverent, harmonious, sounding in concord.
The ancestors listen.
Our guest has arrived,
Long to behold their accomplishment.”

Chen Jing

Comment by Associate Examiner Han, an Instructor: “This composition fully conveys the splendor of Zhou music.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, an Instructor: “Its depiction of performing music to unite with the ancestors fully expresses the meaning.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, a Professor: “I myself seem to have been moved by those resounding sounds.”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官行人徐批和平
周人合祖之樂其聲盛而其感同焉盖樂以感
神為盛也而且及其人之難感者焉周廟之樂
可知矣此始作樂而合乎祖之詩盖謂我周之
祀乎其先也大禮斯舉大樂備焉堂之上下嘒
嘒焉和聲動盪足以昭祖功也樂之大小喤喤
焉雅韻鏗鏘所以播宗德也雍而弗肅則失之
縱非和也樂其皦如也無有所紊焉肅而弗雍
則失之戾非和也樂其純如也無有所乖焉其
===
和鳴矣乎夫是樂也豈曰奏於明而無闗于幽
也哉但見祖之既合也聲之神者有以通其氣
形響既隔宜乎其罔聞矣若有知焉而恍惚其
聽之盖享之者孝而歆之者自速也豈曰格于
親而或間于疎者哉但見我客之来也感其異
者亦以忘其情和奏既闋宜乎其或倦矣若始
作焉而終有以觀之盖可悅者深而可慨者自
失也吁樂足以格祖則其子孫可知足以感客
則其臣庶可知周之德其盛矣乎抑考之易曰
punctuated:
考試官行人徐批：和平。

周人合祖之樂，其聲盛而其感同焉。盖樂以感神為盛也，而且及其人之難感者焉，周廟之樂可知矣。此始作樂而合乎祖之詩，盖謂我周之祀乎其先也，大禮斯舉，大樂備焉。堂之上下，嘒嘒焉，和聲動盪，足以昭祖功也；樂之大小，喤喤焉，雅韻鏗鏘，所以播宗德也。雍而弗肅，則失之縱，非和也；樂其皦如也，無有所紊焉。肅而弗雍，則失之戾，非和也；樂其純如也，無有所乖焉。其和鳴矣乎！夫是樂也，豈曰奏於明而無闗于幽也哉？但見祖之既合也，聲之神者有以通其氣。形響既隔，宜乎其罔聞矣；若有知焉，而恍惚其聽之。盖享之者孝，而歆之者自速也。豈曰格于親而或間于疎者哉？但見我客之来也，感其異者亦以忘其情。和奏既闋，宜乎其或倦矣；若始作焉，而終有以觀之。盖可悅者深，而可慨者自失也。吁！樂足以格祖，則其子孫可知；足以感客，則其臣庶可知。周之德，其盛矣乎！抑考之《易》曰：
translation_en:
Examiner Xu, a Messenger, comments: “Harmonious and serene.”

The music with which the people of Zhou brought their ancestors together was magnificent in sound and moved all alike. Music attains its highest excellence by moving the spirits; when it also reaches those among the living who are difficult to move, the quality of the music in Zhou’s ancestral temples can be understood. This is a poem about beginning the music and bringing the ancestors together. It says, in effect: when we of Zhou sacrifice to our forebears, the great rites are performed and the great music is fully prepared. Above and below the hall, clear notes ring out; harmonious sounds resound and swell, sufficient to display our ancestors’ achievements. The instruments, large and small, sound forth grandly; their elegant tones ring out, spreading the virtue of our forebears. Harmony without solemnity lapses into license and is no true harmony. The music is distinct and clear, with nothing confused. Solemnity without harmony lapses into harshness and is no true harmony. The music blends as one, with nothing discordant. How harmoniously it sounds!

Can it be said that this music is performed in the visible world but has no connection with the unseen? We see that, once the ancestors have been brought together, the spiritual potency of the sound communicates with their vital essences. Separated from bodily forms and sounds, they would seem unable to hear; yet it is as though they were conscious and, in their shadowy presence, listened. This is because those presenting the offerings are filial, and those savoring them come of their own accord. Can it be said that the music reaches those bound by kinship but leaves a barrier between itself and those more distant? We see that, when our guest arrives, even one moved by the difference between us forgets his own feelings. Once the harmonious performance has ended, one might expect him to be weary; yet it is as though the music had only just begun, and he watches it through to its completion. This is because the pleasure it affords is profound, while the feelings that might prompt lamentation fade of themselves.

Ah! If the music is sufficient to reach the ancestors, its effect upon their descendants can be understood; if it is sufficient to move the guest, its effect upon ministers and common people can be understood. How abundant was Zhou’s virtue! Furthermore, examining the Book of Changes, we find it says: …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
雷出地奮豫先王以作樂崇德殷薦上帝以配
祖考夫神非德不足以享此人非德不足以作
此故曰樂由人心生也心和氣和則陰陽和而
萬物得天地位矣況鬼神乎況人乎欲觀成周
之盛當於此求之
春秋
夏公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯伐鄭圍
新城僖公六年
周廷聘
===
同考試官教諭陳批齊桓心事發於此作
考試官行人徐批有斷制
觀伯兵討貳有制而有名也夫有制有名仁義
之兵也春秋得無美之者歟且經書公會齊侯
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯伐鄭圍新城抑何美之耶
盖齊自召陵之後威令幾于改物今合六國僅
討一鄭宜若振槁然圍而不舉者何吾以諒桓
之心矣討亂以平定安集為先不戢將自焚也
殖禮以兼弱攻昧為後志滿族乃離也以故兵
punctuated:
雷出地奮，豫。先王以作樂崇德，殷薦上帝，以配祖考。夫神非德不足以享此，人非德不足以作此。故曰：「樂由人心生也。」心和氣和，則陰陽和，而萬物得、天地位矣。況鬼神乎？況人乎？欲觀成周之盛，當於此求之。

春秋

夏，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。僖公六年。

周廷聘

同考試官教諭陳批：「齊桓心事，發於此作。」
考試官行人徐批：「有斷制。」

觀伯兵討貳，有制而有名也。夫有制有名，仁義之兵也，春秋得無美之者歟？且經書公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城，抑何美之耶？盖齊自召陵之後，威令幾于改物。今合六國，僅討一鄭，宜若振槁。然圍而不舉者何？吾以諒桓之心矣。討亂以平定安集為先，不戢將自焚也；殖禮以兼弱攻昧為後，志滿族乃離也。以故兵
translation_en:
…“Thunder emerges from the earth and stirs: Enthusiasm. The former kings accordingly made music to exalt virtue, offering it with solemn grandeur to the Lord on High and associating their ancestors with him in sacrifice.” Without virtue, the spirits cannot receive this offering; without virtue, people cannot create this music. Thus it is said: “Music arises from the human heart.” When the heart and vital energies are harmonious, yin and yang are harmonious; the myriad things attain their proper conditions, and Heaven and Earth take their proper places. How much more, then, the spirits? How much more human beings? Whoever wishes to understand the flourishing of the Zhou should seek it here.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“In summer, the Duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao in attacking Zheng and besieging Xincheng.” Sixth year of Duke Xi.

Zhou Tingpin

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, an Instructor: “Duke Huan of Qi’s inner intentions are brought to light in this composition.”
Comment by Examiner Xu, a Messenger: “It displays decisive judgment.”

Consider the hegemon’s army chastising a disloyal state: it acted with restraint and with legitimate grounds. An army possessing restraint and legitimate grounds is an army of benevolence and righteousness. Could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to praise it? Yet the Classic records that the Duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao in attacking Zheng and besieging Xincheng. Wherein does its praise lie?

Since the encounter at Shaoling, Qi’s authority and commands had nearly transformed the established order. Now six states combined to chastise Zheng alone; this should have been as easy as shaking down withered leaves. Why, then, did they besiege the city without taking it? Here I understand Duke Huan’s intentions. In chastising disorder, priority goes to pacification and bringing the people together in security: those who do not restrain their arms will burn themselves. In establishing ritual order, annexing the weak and attacking the benighted must come last: when ambition becomes overweening, one’s kindred fall away. For this reason, the army…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
猶遲巡于新城以用兵之法攻心者為尚使鄭
尚有不寧方來之想桓之心斯巳矣又況齊自
首止以來信義被于諸侯今合中國獨遺一鄭
似未渙羣乃伐而復圍者何吾以諒桓之職矣
諸夏親暱不可棄也失同人之義者王法不赦
周室大義所當尊也為下喬之行者連帥必懲
以故師直進止于新城正以九伐之法負固則
侵之使鄭蚤有悔過自新之善桓之職斯巳矣
故經直書伐鄭圍新城伐者聲罪之謂也圍者
===
寓遺力之意也可槩見矣雖然王者之兵不試
齊桓之節制終不若湯武之仁義也而況乆假
不歸者乎然經所以直予者盖首止葵丘二百
四十餘年不二見也此亦小康之治也歟
丁亥楚子入陳宣公十有一年
丘柟
同考試官教諭陳批善恕楚子
考試官行人徐批謹嚴
春秋於外兵討罪不以利掩義不以過棄功夫
punctuated:
猶遲巡于新城，以用兵之法，攻心者為尚，使鄭尚有不寧方來之想，桓之心斯巳矣。又況齊自首止以來，信義被于諸侯，今合中國，獨遺一鄭，似未渙羣，乃伐而復圍者何？吾以諒桓之職矣。諸夏親暱，不可棄也，失同人之義者，王法不赦；周室大義所當尊也，為下喬之行者，連帥必懲。以故師直進止于新城，正以九伐之法，負固則侵之，使鄭蚤有悔過自新之善，桓之職斯巳矣。故經直書伐鄭圍新城，伐者聲罪之謂也，圍者寓遺力之意也，可槩見矣。雖然，王者之兵不試，齊桓之節制終不若湯武之仁義也，而況乆假不歸者乎？然經所以直予者，盖首止、葵丘，二百四十餘年不二見也。此亦小康之治也歟？
「丁亥，楚子入陳。」宣公十有一年。
丘柟。
同考試官教諭陳批：善恕楚子。
考試官行人徐批：謹嚴。
春秋於外兵討罪，不以利掩義，不以過棄功。夫
translation_en:
…still lingered hesitantly at Xincheng. For in the methods of warfare, winning hearts is held highest: he wished Zheng still to entertain the thought that those not yet at peace should come and submit. This alone was Duke Huan’s intention. Moreover, since the meeting at Shouzhi, Qi’s trustworthiness and righteousness had extended to the feudal lords. Now, in uniting the central states, it left out Zheng alone, seemingly not yet having dissolved factional groupings [?]. Why, then, did it attack and also lay siege? From this I understand Duke Huan’s duty. The states of the Xia were close kin and could not be abandoned: royal law would not pardon anyone who violated the principle of fellowship. The house of Zhou ought to be honored as a matter of supreme righteousness: the regional leader would certainly punish anyone who abandoned the lofty for the low. Thus the army advanced directly and halted at Xincheng, precisely following the rule among the nine punitive expeditions that those who rely on fortified defenses should be invaded. He wished Zheng promptly to repent its faults and reform. This alone was Duke Huan’s duty. Hence the Classic straightforwardly records “attacked Zheng and besieged Xincheng.” “Attacked” means publicly proclaiming its offenses; “besieged” conveys the intention of holding strength in reserve. The general meaning is thus apparent.
Even so, the army of a true king need never be put to the test. Duke Huan of Qi’s discipline and control ultimately fell short of the benevolence and righteousness of Tang and Wu—how much more so when he had long borrowed these virtues without returning them! Yet the Classic accords him unqualified approval because the meetings at Shouzhi and Kuiqiu were not seen a second time in its more than 240 years. Was this not also government attaining a Lesser Peace?
“On the dinghai day, the Viscount of Chu entered Chen.” Eleventh year of Duke Xuan.
Qiu Nan 丘柟.
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “A good, sympathetic assessment of the Viscount of Chu.”
Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “Careful and rigorous.”
When outside armies punish wrongdoing, the Spring and Autumn Annals does not allow profit to obscure righteousness, nor does it discard achievements because of faults. Indeed, …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
正倫經世大典也觀春秋書丁亥楚子入陳有
以哉夫楚莊入陳也討其賊為義取其國為貪
義利之分明矣經先書殺後書入者何盖君子
用人之仁去其貪也楚雖有取陳之惡終不可
沒其正陳之善事起于正陳之善其流則為取
陳之惡是則事有義利交集者而義所當重也
於此使不權先後之書以原其情焉非用人之
仁去其貪之意也奚可哉夫楚莊入陳也雖得
為討罪之舉亦肆彼滅國之暴功過之分審矣
===
經不書取陳而猶書入者何盖君子以義度人
則難為人也縣陳之虐固難儕以存亡興滅之
師栗門之轘實則異夫伐莒攢函之為是則事
有功過相準者而功不可沒也於此使不權輕
重之宜以末減焉是以義度人則難為人之意
也奚可哉然則春秋以恕待人而不求備其在
此也歟雖然道大如天見在乎人聖人之制行
也不制以已曲暢旁通可以入道者皆經世所
不棄也信夫曾子曰夫子之道忠恕而已矣
punctuated:
正倫經世大典也。觀《春秋》書「丁亥，楚子入陳」，有以哉！夫楚莊入陳也，討其賊為義，取其國為貪，義利之分明矣。經先書殺，後書入者何？盖君子用人之仁，去其貪也。楚雖有取陳之惡，終不可沒其正陳之善。事起于正陳之善，其流則為取陳之惡，是則事有義利交集者，而義所當重也。於此使不權先後之書，以原其情焉，非用人之仁、去其貪之意也，奚可哉！夫楚莊入陳也，雖得為討罪之舉，亦肆彼滅國之暴，功過之分審矣。
經不書取陳，而猶書入者何？盖君子以義度人，則難為人也。縣陳之虐，固難儕以存亡興滅之師；栗門之轘，實則異夫伐莒攢函之為。是則事有功過相準者，而功不可沒也。於此使不權輕重之宜，以末減焉，是以義度人，則難為人之意也，奚可哉！然則《春秋》以恕待人，而不求備，其在此也歟！雖然，道大如天，見在乎人。聖人之制行也，不制以已，曲暢旁通，可以入道者，皆經世所不棄也。信夫！曾子曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」
translation_en:
…is a great canon for rectifying human relationships and ordering the world. Consider the Spring and Autumn Annals’ entry, “On dinghai, the Viscount of Chu entered Chen”: surely there is a reason for this wording! When King Zhuang of Chu entered Chen, punishing its regicide was righteous, while seizing its state was avaricious. The distinction between righteousness and self-interest is clear. Why does the Classic first record the killing and then the entry? Because the gentleman gives credit to a person’s benevolence while rejecting his avarice. Although Chu committed the wrong of seizing Chen, its good deed in setting Chen right must not ultimately be obscured. The affair began with the good deed of setting Chen right, but its subsequent course led to the wrong of seizing Chen. Thus, in an affair where righteousness and self-interest converge, righteousness deserves greater weight. If, here, we failed to weigh the order of the entries in order to discern the underlying motives, we would miss the intention of giving credit to a person’s benevolence while rejecting his avarice. How could that be acceptable? Although King Zhuang’s entry into Chen could count as an undertaking to punish wrongdoing, it also gave free rein to his violence in destroying a state. The distinction between merit and fault is evident.
Why does the Classic nevertheless record an “entry,” rather than the “seizure of Chen”? Because, when the gentleman measures others against righteousness, it becomes difficult for them to meet the standard. The cruelty of reducing Chen to a county certainly cannot rank alongside military expeditions that preserve endangered states and restore extinguished ones. Yet the execution by dismemberment at the Li Gate was indeed different from the attack on Ju and the deed at Zanhan [?]. Thus, in an affair where merit and fault counterbalance one another, the merit must not be obscured. If, here, we failed to weigh their relative gravity appropriately and grant mitigation, we would be measuring others against righteousness in a way that makes it difficult for them to meet the standard. How could that be acceptable? Is this not, then, an instance of the Spring and Autumn Annals treating people with sympathetic understanding rather than demanding perfection?
Nevertheless, the Way is as vast as Heaven; its manifestation rests with human beings. In setting standards for conduct, the sage does not make himself the measure. He develops their implications fully and extends their application in every direction: whatever can lead people into the Way is not discarded in ordering the world. How true indeed are Zengzi’s words: “Our Master’s Way consists solely of wholehearted commitment and sympathetic understanding.”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
禮記
天子祭天下名山大川五嶽視三公四瀆
視諸侯
蔡完
同考試官學正劉批望祀儀節甚明深於禮者
考試官行人徐批不浮
王者祭地之望而所秩有定分焉夫山川者地
之望也秩而祭之斯所以嚴其分也歟王者之
制分以禮而定禮以稱為善天子者天下之主
也有天下者祭百神地示之下非山川邪盖祭
以禮神能成其變化者皆曰神而當禮祭以報
功能資其財用者皆曰有功而當報是非夫山
而皆祭也天下之名山乃其宗矣祭之者於吾
身有所統也亦非百川而皆祭也天下之大川
乃其會矣祭之者於吾身有攸主也天子之望
徧于天下如此禮豈混而無別者哉山之至高
者為嶽五嶽其名山也望秩之禮則視三公焉
川之獨遠者為瀆四瀆其大川也望秩之儀則
punctuated:
禮記

天子祭天下名山大川，五嶽視三公，四瀆視諸侯。

蔡完

同考試官學正劉批：「望祀儀節甚明，深於禮者。」

考試官行人徐批：「不浮。」

王者祭地之望，而所秩有定分焉。夫山川者，地之望也。秩而祭之，斯所以嚴其分也歟！王者之制分以禮，而定禮以稱為善。天子者，天下之主也。有天下者祭百神，地示之下，非山川邪？盖祭以禮神，能成其變化者，皆曰神而當禮；祭以報功，能資其財用者，皆曰有功而當報。是非夫山而皆祭也，天下之名山乃其宗矣，祭之者於吾身有所統也；亦非百川而皆祭也，天下之大川乃其會矣，祭之者於吾身有攸主也。天子之望徧于天下如此，禮豈混而無別者哉？山之至高者為嶽，五嶽其名山也，望秩之禮則視三公焉；川之獨遠者為瀆，四瀆其大川也，望秩之儀則
translation_en:
Book of Rites (Liji)

“The Son of Heaven sacrifices to the renowned mountains and great rivers throughout the realm. The Five Sacred Peaks are treated on a par with the Three Dukes, and the Four Waterways on a par with the regional lords.”

Cai Wan

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “The ceremonial procedures for sacrifices performed from afar are very clearly explained: this is someone deeply versed in ritual.”

Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “Not superficial.”

When the true king sacrifices to the earth’s eminent features, the ranks he assigns them have fixed distinctions. Mountains and rivers are the earth’s eminent features. Is not sacrificing to them according to rank precisely how their distinctions are upheld? The true king establishes distinctions through ritual, and in determining ritual, appropriateness is the standard of excellence. The Son of Heaven is the lord of all under Heaven. He who possesses the realm sacrifices to the hundred spirits. Among the earthly spirits, are there not those of mountains and rivers? Sacrifice serves to honor spirits: whatever can bring about transformations is called a spirit and deserves honor. Sacrifice also serves to recompense services: whatever can supply material resources is said to render service and deserves recompense. This does not mean that every mountain receives sacrifice [?]. Rather, the renowned mountains of the realm are the chief among them; in sacrificing to them, I, as sovereign, have that over which to exercise my encompassing authority. Nor does every river receive sacrifice. Rather, the great rivers of the realm are their gathering places; in sacrificing to them, I have that over which to preside. Thus the Son of Heaven’s sacrifices from afar extend throughout the realm. Could their rites be indiscriminate and without distinctions? The loftiest mountains are called sacred peaks: the Five Sacred Peaks are the renowned mountains, and the rites governing their ranked sacrifices from afar treat them on a par with the Three Dukes. Rivers whose courses are exceptionally long are called waterways: the Four Waterways are the great rivers, and the ceremonial procedures governing their ranked sacrifices from afar …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
視諸侯焉服用毳冕從其類矣然獻而薶之者
乃公之桓圭牢數則九也豆數十六也其在嶽
者猶其在三公歟藉用席蒲取其象矣獻而沈
之者乃侯之信圭牢數則七也豆數十二也其
在川者猶其在諸侯歟吁先王制禮其為天下
之防也至矣雖然人存而政舉禮廢而防決不
務民義而徼福于鬼神斯有僭旅而崇川者矣
盖制不存而分不明故也有志於天下者惟辨
上下而定民志
===
地氣上齊天氣下降陰陽相摩天地相蕩
鼓之以雷霆奮之以風雨動之以四時
煖之以日月而百化興焉如此則樂者
天地之和也
丘柟
同考試官學正劉批〔樂法天地之和子又能法作樂之和矣〕
考試官行人徐批〔雅淡〕
記樂者推造化之功而著其為效法之本焉盖
天地有自然之樂也聖人法之樂斯作矣夫樂
punctuated:
視諸侯焉。服用毳冕，從其類矣。然獻而薶之者，乃公之桓圭；牢數則九也，豆數十六也。其在嶽者，猶其在三公歟？藉用席蒲，取其象矣。獻而沈之者，乃侯之信圭；牢數則七也，豆數十二也。其在川者，猶其在諸侯歟？吁！先王制禮，其為天下之防也至矣。雖然，人存而政舉，禮廢而防決。不務民義，而徼福于鬼神，斯有僭旅而崇川者矣。盖制不存而分不明故也。有志於天下者，惟辨上下而定民志。

地氣上齊，天氣下降，陰陽相摩，天地相蕩。鼓之以雷霆，奮之以風雨，動之以四時，煖之以日月，而百化興焉。如此，則樂者，天地之和也。

丘柟

同考試官學正劉批〔樂法天地之和，子又能法作樂之和矣。〕
考試官行人徐批〔雅淡。〕

記樂者，推造化之功，而著其為效法之本焉。盖天地有自然之樂也，聖人法之，樂斯作矣。夫樂
translation_en:
…are accorded the ceremonial rank of the regional lords. The ceremonial dress is the fur-robe ensemble with its crown, following the corresponding category. Yet what is offered and then buried is the duke’s huan jade tablet; the number of sets of sacrificial animals is nine, and the number of stemmed offering vessels is sixteen. Is not the treatment of the sacred peaks like that of the Three Dukes? Rush mats are used beneath the offerings, adopting their symbolic likeness [?]. What is offered and then submerged is the marquis’s xin jade tablet; the number of sets of sacrificial animals is seven, and the number of stemmed offering vessels is twelve. Is not the treatment of the rivers like that of the regional lords? Ah! In establishing ritual, the former kings provided the utmost safeguards for all under Heaven. Even so, when the right men are present, government flourishes; when ritual is abandoned, the safeguards collapse. If one neglects the people’s sense of right and seeks blessings from ghosts and spirits, there will be those who presumptuously perform mountain sacrifices and exalt river worship. This happens because the institutions no longer endure and distinctions of rank are unclear. Those who aspire to govern all under Heaven must distinguish superior from inferior and thereby settle the people’s aspirations.

“The vital force of earth rises; the vital force of Heaven descends. Yin and yang rub against one another; Heaven and earth stir one another. They beat upon things with thunder and thunderbolts, rouse them with wind and rain, move them through the four seasons, and warm them with the sun and moon; thus the myriad transformations arise. Such being the case, music is the harmony of Heaven and earth.”

Qiu Nan 丘柟

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, an Instructor: “Music models itself on the harmony of Heaven and earth; you, in turn, have been able to model yourself on the harmony of making music.”
Comment by Examiner Xu, a Messenger: “Elegant and understated.”

The author of the Record of Music traces the workings of creation and makes clear that they provide the foundation for emulation. For Heaven and earth possess a music that is naturally their own; the sages model themselves upon it, and music is thus created. Now, as for music…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
也者人心之動也何假於外哉然所本則在於
天地爾彼天位乎上也有隤自天氣則下降矣
地位乎下也承天而行氣則上齊矣動而陽靜
而陰相摩之不已焉乾以君坤以藏相盪之不
息焉陰閉而陽之在內者不能出則搏而為雷
矣相激而甚乃霆之大者也陰凝而陽之在外
者不能入則旋而為風矣相畜而解乃雨之潤
者也一寒一暑之互推四時之序有以動之也
或晝或夜之迭見日月之烜有以煖之也由是
===
天地絪縕合同而化萬物其有不醇者乎樂之
見於天地者如此聖人作樂蓋有取焉吾知樂
之興也生於感物變以成方以宣吾和也而生
氣之和亦以之而合矣以達吾順也而順氣之
應亦於是而肇矣清明者天也廣大者地也雷
霆非有聲者乎終始者四時也周還者風雨也
日月非有光者乎樂為天地之和者如此聖人
作樂豈無本歟大抵禮樂固皆不可去身也然
禮序而樂和禮先而樂後知和而不以禮節之
punctuated: 也者，人心之動也，何假於外哉？然所本則在於天地爾。彼天位乎上也，有隤自天，氣則下降矣；地位乎下也，承天而行，氣則上齊矣。動而陽，靜而陰，相摩之不已焉；乾以君，坤以藏，相盪之不息焉。陰閉而陽之在內者不能出，則搏而為雷矣；相激而甚，乃霆之大者也。陰凝而陽之在外者不能入，則旋而為風矣；相畜而解，乃雨之潤者也。一寒一暑之互推，四時之序有以動之也；或晝或夜之迭見，日月之烜有以煖之也。由是天地絪縕，合同而化，萬物其有不醇者乎？樂之見於天地者如此，聖人作樂蓋有取焉。吾知樂之興也，生於感物，變以成方，以宣吾和也，而生氣之和亦以之而合矣；以達吾順也，而順氣之應亦於是而肇矣。清明者天也，廣大者地也，雷霆非有聲者乎？終始者四時也，周還者風雨也，日月非有光者乎？樂為天地之和者如此，聖人作樂豈無本歟？大抵禮樂固皆不可去身也，然禮序而樂和，禮先而樂後，知和而不以禮節之
translation_en:
…is the stirring of the human heart: why need it borrow anything from outside? Yet its foundation lies in Heaven and Earth. Heaven occupies the place above; there is a descent from Heaven [?], and its vital force consequently moves downward. Earth occupies the place below; it acts in obedience to Heaven, and its vital force rises to meet Heaven’s. Movement produces yang and stillness produces yin; they continually press against one another. Qian rules and Kun stores; they ceaselessly stir one another. When yin closes in and the yang within cannot escape, their collision produces thunder; when their mutual agitation becomes intense, it produces mighty thunderclaps. When yin congeals and the yang outside cannot enter, its swirling produces wind; when their accumulated forces are released, they produce nourishing rain. Cold and heat impel one another in alternation: the ordered succession of the four seasons sets things in motion. Day and night appear in turn: the radiance of sun and moon warms things. Thus Heaven and Earth intertwine their vital forces, joining together to bring about transformation. Could any of the myriad things fail to attain fullness? Such is music as it manifests itself in Heaven and Earth; surely the sages drew upon this in making music.

I know that music arises from being moved by things, and through variation takes patterned form. It expresses our harmony, and through it the harmony of life-giving vital force also comes into accord. It gives expression to our concord, and thereby initiates the response of harmonious vital force. What is pure and bright is Heaven; what is broad and great is Earth. Do thunder and thunderclaps not have sound? What ends and begins again is the cycle of the four seasons; what circulates and returns is wind and rain. Do the sun and moon not have light? Such is the way music constitutes the harmony of Heaven and Earth. Could the sages have made music without a foundation?

In general, ritual and music must never be absent from one’s person. Yet ritual establishes order, while music brings harmony; ritual comes first, and music follows. To understand harmony but fail to regulate it through ritual…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
亦不可行矣是禮也成始而成終者也有志于
樂者宜以禮為質
第貳場
論
孔子聞而知之
傅順
同考試官學正區批孔子聞道之妙此作悉之
同考試官教授張批善言道統者
考試官行人徐批知孔子者
===
論曰天下有至悟焉惟聖人神之夫道天之秘
也而命之聖人聖人者不數出於是乎有至悟
焉故因而啓者達諸天也有所據而覺者明諸
人也因而非因據而非據而悟焉者聖人之神
也神也者不以其時之久而弗值不以其幾之
寂而弗章天以時啓之動其幾使自覺之聖人
之心洞然協天人一古今而道弗藏其秘矣此
孔子之聞知所謂至悟而神者也夫繼善成性
天道寤矣五百餘年而聖人生焉氣之寤也於
punctuated:
亦不可行矣。是禮也，成始而成終者也。有志于樂者，宜以禮為質。

第貳場

論

孔子聞而知之

傅順

同考試官學正區批：孔子聞道之妙，此作悉之。
同考試官教授張批：善言道統者。
考試官行人徐批：知孔子者。

論曰：天下有至悟焉，惟聖人神之。夫道，天之秘也，而命之聖人。聖人者不數出，於是乎有至悟焉。故因而啓者，達諸天也；有所據而覺者，明諸人也；因而非因，據而非據而悟焉者，聖人之神也。神也者，不以其時之久而弗值，不以其幾之寂而弗章。天以時啓之，動其幾，使自覺之。聖人之心洞然，協天人，一古今，而道弗藏其秘矣。此孔子之聞知，所謂至悟而神者也。夫繼善成性，天道寤矣。五百餘年而聖人生焉，氣之寤也。於
translation_en:
…cannot be put into practice either. Ritual thus brings both the beginning and the end to fulfillment. Those devoted to music should take ritual as its substance.

Second Session

Discourse

“Confucius Knew It through Hearing”

Fu Shun

Comment by Associate Examiner Ou, School Instructor: “This composition fully explains the subtlety of Confucius’s hearing the Way.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “One who speaks well of the succession of the Way.”
Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “One who understands Confucius.”

The discourse states: There is an ultimate awakening in the world; only the sage realizes it with spiritual efficacy. The Way is Heaven’s secret, entrusted to the sage. Sages do not appear frequently; hence there is this ultimate awakening. Those who are enlightened by following what is given attain understanding through Heaven; those who awaken with something to rely upon gain illumination through other people. But to awaken by following yet not following, relying yet not relying—this is the sage’s spiritual efficacy. Such efficacy does not fail to encounter the Way because of the long lapse of time, nor fail to manifest itself because its incipient workings lie quiet. Heaven enlightens him at the proper time, stirring those incipient workings so that he awakens of himself. The sage’s mind becomes utterly lucid, harmonizing Heaven and humanity and uniting antiquity and the present; the Way then no longer conceals its secret. This is Confucius’s knowing through hearing, what is called ultimate awakening endowed with spiritual efficacy. Now, the continuation of goodness and the completion of human nature constitute the awakening of Heaven’s Way. After more than five hundred years a sage is born: this is the awakening of vital energy. At…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
是以其造化之渾然者寄之聖人則亦天之心
大寤也故堯舜達諸天湯達諸堯舜文王達諸
湯而禹皐伊萊吕散明諸堯舜湯文此至悟之
神傳道者有不傳之傳也噫不傳之傳孔子其
神乎盖超古今而無滯者神也歷萬世而無弊
者道也曠數十世而相感者氣也越數百年之
口耳而相孚者心也是故有時焉以俟乎人時
弗至人弗值也有幾焉以觸其蘊幾弗融蘊弗
彰也孔子知悟于聞聞神於悟爾已不然則前
===
之授迥其響後之受不順于聰孰從授之孰從
得之哉其所以得之者亦天以道久斯晦晦弗
傳故疑其會以開聖人之時通其寂以闡聞知
之幾而聖人於道孚之於心感之於氣神而明
之於詩聞緝熈之敬純一之誠焉於書聞懿恭
之德敬忌之心焉於易聞六十四卦之蘊焉於
禮樂而忠信和順之本聞焉於經制而榮辱予
奪之權衡聞焉則孔子之聞有至悟也至悟斯
有知故有擇善固執之訓有克己復禮之教有
punctuated: 是以其造化之渾然者寄之聖人，則亦天之心大寤也。故堯舜達諸天，湯達諸堯舜，文王達諸湯，而禹皐伊萊吕散明諸堯舜湯文。此至悟之神，傳道者有不傳之傳也。噫！不傳之傳，孔子其神乎！盖超古今而無滯者，神也；歷萬世而無弊者，道也；曠數十世而相感者，氣也；越數百年之口耳而相孚者，心也。是故有時焉以俟乎人，時弗至，人弗值也；有幾焉以觸其蘊，幾弗融，蘊弗彰也。孔子知悟于聞，聞神於悟爾已。不然，則前之授迥其響，後之受不順于聰，孰從授之，孰從得之哉？其所以得之者，亦天以道久斯晦，晦弗傳，故疑其會以開聖人之時，通其寂以闡聞知之幾，而聖人於道孚之於心，感之於氣，神而明之。於詩聞緝熈之敬、純一之誠焉；於書聞懿恭之德、敬忌之心焉；於易聞六十四卦之蘊焉；於禮樂而忠信和順之本聞焉；於經制而榮辱予奪之權衡聞焉。則孔子之聞有至悟也，至悟斯有知。故有擇善固執之訓，有克己復禮之教，有
translation_en:
…Thus Heaven entrusts the undivided wholeness of its creative transformations to the sage: this too is a great awakening of Heaven’s heart. Thus Yao and Shun attained understanding through Heaven, Tang through Yao and Shun, and King Wen through Tang; Yu, Gao, Yi, Lai, Lü, and San [?] gained illumination through Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wen. Such is the spiritual efficacy of consummate awakening: those who transmit the Way have a transmission that occurs without transmission. Ah! In this transmission without transmission, was not Kongzi spiritually wondrous indeed! What transcends past and present without obstruction is spiritual efficacy; what endures through myriad generations without deterioration is the Way; what resonates across a gap of several dozen generations is vital force; what accords across several centuries of oral and aural transmission is the heart. Thus there is a time that awaits the right person: until that time arrives, the person does not encounter it. There is an incipient impulse that stirs what lies within: unless that impulse finds free passage, what lies within does not become manifest. Kongzi’s understanding awakened through hearing, and his hearing became spiritually efficacious through awakening—that is all. Otherwise, if the transmission from those before him had only a distant echo [?], and its reception by those after them did not reach an attentive ear, through whom could it be transmitted, and from whom could it be acquired?

His acquisition of it also came about because Heaven, seeing that the Way becomes obscure over time and, once obscure, ceases to be transmitted, brought its convergence to fruition [?], thereby opening the sage’s appointed time, and penetrated its stillness, thereby revealing the incipient impulse toward knowing through hearing. The sage then accorded with the Way in his heart, resonated with it in his vital force, and illuminated it through spiritual understanding. In the Odes he heard of reverence cultivated to ever greater brilliance and of sincerity that is pure and undivided; in the Documents he heard of admirable and reverent virtue and of a heart that is respectful and wary; in the Changes he heard the profound meanings of the sixty-four hexagrams. In rites and music he heard the foundations of loyalty, trustworthiness, harmony, and accord; in canonical institutions he heard the standards for conferring honor and disgrace, granting and withholding. Thus Kongzi’s hearing contained consummate awakening; with consummate awakening came knowledge. Hence there are his instruction to choose the good and hold firmly to it, his teaching to overcome the self and return to ritual propriety, and…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
志立不惑知命耳順不踰矩之全功有廣大變
通陰陽易簡之德象有為邦四代之禮樂有春
秋二百四十二年之經制孔子之知至此殆神
矣乎抑豈惟於文王然也達諸湯達諸堯舜而
羣聖人大成集也曰知我其天曰天何言哉天
且弗違而況於列聖乎哉盖道天之道也列聖
之傳也而孔子至悟之神至於斯也雖然見知
者聞知之因後作者之據也孔子亦因之吕散
而有據焉者也彼子貢見而未悟顏曾大而未
===
化孟子之所為嘆者見知者之惜而聞知者之
望也又不但曰列聖之悟達而行孔子之悟窮
而藏已也噫繼往開來以俟後聖於無窮天非
無意于孔子也後有神乎悟孔子者則亦達諸
天而已矣
同前
李相
同考試官學正區 批 意格自別
同考試官教授張 批 論有援據錄之
punctuated:
志立、不惑、知命、耳順、不踰矩之全功，有廣大、變通、陰陽、易簡之德象，有為邦四代之禮樂，有《春秋》二百四十二年之經制。孔子之知至此，殆神矣乎！抑豈惟於文王然也？達諸湯，達諸堯舜，而羣聖人大成集也。曰：「知我其天！」曰：「天何言哉！」天且弗違，而況於列聖乎哉！盖道，天之道也，列聖之傳也，而孔子至悟之神至於斯也。雖然，見知者，聞知之因，後作者之據也。孔子亦因之吕散而有據焉者也。彼子貢見而未悟，顏曾大而未化。孟子之所為嘆者，見知者之惜，而聞知者之望也。又不但曰列聖之悟達而行，孔子之悟窮而藏已也。噫！繼往開來，以俟後聖於無窮，天非無意于孔子也。後有神乎悟孔子者，則亦達諸天而已矣。

同前。
李相。

同考試官學正區批：意格自別。
同考試官教授張批：論有援據，錄之。
translation_en:
…the complete accomplishment of setting one’s purpose, standing firm, being free from perplexity, knowing Heaven’s mandate, having an attuned ear, and never overstepping the bounds; the virtues and images of vastness, transformation and continuity, yin and yang, ease and simplicity; the rites and music of the four dynasties for governing a state; and the institutions and regulations recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals over two hundred and forty-two years. Had Confucius’s understanding, reaching this point, not become almost divine? Yet was this so only with respect to King Wen? His understanding reached back to Tang, and to Yao and Shun, bringing together the great accomplishments of all the sages. He said, “It is Heaven that knows me!” He also said, “What does Heaven say?” Even Heaven did not diverge from him; how much less could the successive sages do so! For the Way is Heaven’s Way, transmitted by the successive sages, and the divine quality of Confucius’s consummate realization reached this degree.

Nevertheless, those who know through seeing provide the basis for those who know through hearing, and the evidence upon which later men who arise may rely. Confucius likewise relied on this and thereby had a basis [the words 吕散 are unclear: ?]. Zigong saw but had not yet attained realization; Yan Hui and Zengzi attained greatness but had not yet reached transformation. What Mencius lamented expressed regret concerning those who knew through seeing, and hope for those who would know through hearing. Nor was it merely that the successive sages, having attained realization and found scope for action, put it into practice, while Confucius, having attained realization but finding himself constrained, kept it concealed. Ah! In carrying forward the past and opening the future, awaiting later sages through ages without end, Heaven was not without a purpose for Confucius. If someone should later attain a divine realization of Confucius, that too would be nothing other than reaching an understanding of Heaven.

Same as the preceding.
Li Xiang.

Associate Examiner Ou, School Instructor, comments: “The conception and style are distinctive.”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The argument has supporting authorities. Include it.”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
考試官行人徐批〔明顯〕
事有曠百世而相感者大聖承列聖之統者在
是矣夫天下未甞一日無道統其生聖人有期
而不數也故有達而親授於一時窮而神會於
百世要之心同也道同也前夫所見者殆即其
所聞後夫所聞者殆即其所見必其時之至而
精元一會若有機焉而特不得其朕者焉爾知
此則以夫子而上遡文王一旦乃喟然曰文不
在茲乎而道統之傳誠有自來者孟子發為斯
===
論正以明其傳之有在又以俟後聖於無窮也
孔子聞而知之請遂言之吾道流行於天地未
甞一日而有間也聖賢之興值五百載而一見
不常有也其間固有適丁其盛際會於一堂者
有身處其窮垂憲於萬世者語其時皆不可得
而同也然時有先後世有古今而人心之所同
然者一而已茍得其所同然則雖越宇宙若親
炙之者爾自今觀之二帝三王之治本於道二
帝三王之道本於心由堯舜至湯五百有餘歲
punctuated:
考試官行人徐批〔明顯〕

事有曠百世而相感者，大聖承列聖之統者在是矣。夫天下未甞一日無道統，其生聖人有期而不數也。故有達而親授於一時，窮而神會於百世。要之，心同也，道同也。前夫所見者，殆即其所聞；後夫所聞者，殆即其所見。必其時之至，而精元一會，若有機焉，而特不得其朕者焉爾。知此，則以夫子而上遡文王，一旦乃喟然曰：「文不在茲乎？」而道統之傳誠有自來者。孟子發為斯論，正以明其傳之有在，又以俟後聖於無窮也。

孔子聞而知之，請遂言之。吾道流行於天地，未甞一日而有間也。聖賢之興，值五百載而一見，不常有也。其間固有適丁其盛，際會於一堂者；有身處其窮，垂憲於萬世者。語其時，皆不可得而同也。然時有先後，世有古今，而人心之所同然者，一而已。茍得其所同然，則雖越宇宙，若親炙之者爾。自今觀之，二帝三王之治本於道，二帝三王之道本於心。由堯舜至湯，五百有餘歲。
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Xu, a Messenger: 〔Clear and manifest.〕

There are instances of mutual resonance across a hundred generations: herein lies the great sage’s succession to the lineage of the preceding sages. The world has never gone a single day without the succession of the Way; yet sages are born at appointed times and do not appear frequently. Thus some, attaining public office, receive personal instruction within their own age; others, remaining without office, apprehend it spiritually across a hundred generations. In essence, their hearts are the same, and their Way is the same. What those earlier witnessed was perhaps precisely what they had heard; what those later heard was perhaps precisely what they witnessed. When the proper time arrives, their essential spirits unite [?], as though some activating impulse were at work, though its traces cannot be discerned. Understanding this, we see how the Master traced his lineage back to King Wen and once exclaimed with a sigh: “Does not this culture reside here in me?” The transmission of the succession of the Way indeed had its source. Mengzi advanced this argument precisely to make clear where that transmission resided, and also to await future sages through all ages to come.

“Confucius knew it through hearing”: allow me to elaborate. Our Way circulates throughout Heaven and Earth and has never been interrupted for a single day. The emergence of sages and worthies occurs but once in five hundred years; it is no frequent event. Among them are those who happen to encounter a flourishing age and gather together in one hall; there are also those who live amid adversity and bequeath models to ten thousand generations. As to their circumstances, these cannot all be alike. Yet although times come earlier or later, and ages are ancient or modern, what human hearts alike acknowledge is one and the same. If one grasps what they alike acknowledge, then even across the reaches of space and time, it is as though one had personally received their instruction. Viewed from the present, the government of the Two Emperors and Three Kings was rooted in the Way, and their Way was rooted in the heart. From Yao and Shun to Tang, there were more than five hundred years…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
若禹臯陶則見而知之其所以為堯舜者固不
異也湯處其後不得為禹為臯陶也亦豈有異
夫堯舜者哉由湯至於文王五百有餘歲若伊
尹萊朱則見而知之其所以為成湯者固不異
也文王處其後不得為伊尹為萊朱也亦豈有
異夫成湯者哉由文王而至於孔子又適五百
有餘歲是亦堯舜成湯之一大承也太公望散
宜生既見文王之所見夫子其不聞文王之所
聞者乎是以刪詩書也定禮樂也賛周易也脩
===
春秋也有進退存亡者焉有德仁誠敬者焉有
中正和平者焉有感發懲創者焉有用舍予奪
者焉其所以為精一為執中為建中為建極為
純亦不已為種德為一德為平格為迪教無所
不在亦無所不聞也博文約禮同志之義老安
少懷付物之仁委吏攝相屈伸之感志學從心
始卒之地合之為一理散之為萬事故之彌六
合卷之藏於密萬象異形而同體也百王異世
而同神也未有文王無不為夫子也既有夫子
punctuated: 若禹、臯陶，則見而知之，其所以為堯舜者固不異也。湯處其後，不得為禹、為臯陶也，亦豈有異夫堯舜者哉？由湯至於文王，五百有餘歲。若伊尹、萊朱，則見而知之，其所以為成湯者固不異也。文王處其後，不得為伊尹、為萊朱也，亦豈有異夫成湯者哉？由文王而至於孔子，又適五百有餘歲，是亦堯舜、成湯之一大承也。太公望、散宜生既見文王之所見，夫子其不聞文王之所聞者乎？是以刪《詩》《書》也，定禮樂也，賛《周易》也，脩《春秋》也。有進退存亡者焉，有德仁誠敬者焉，有中正和平者焉，有感發懲創者焉，有用舍予奪者焉。其所以為精一、為執中、為建中、為建極、為純亦不已、為種德、為一德、為平格、為迪教，無所不在，亦無所不聞也。博文約禮，同志之義；老安少懷，付物之仁；委吏攝相，屈伸之感；志學從心，始卒之地。合之為一理，散之為萬事，故之彌六合，卷之藏於密。萬象異形而同體也，百王異世而同神也。未有文王無不為夫子也，既有夫子
translation_en:
…As for Yu and Gao Yao, they knew through seeing; that which made them like Yao and Shun was fundamentally no different. Tang lived after them and could not occupy the position of Yu or Gao Yao; yet how could he have differed from Yao and Shun? From Tang to King Wen there were more than five hundred years. As for Yi Yin and Lai Zhu, they knew through seeing; that which made them like Cheng Tang was fundamentally no different. King Wen lived after them and could not occupy the position of Yi Yin or Lai Zhu; yet how could he have differed from Cheng Tang? From King Wen to Confucius there were again just over five hundred years. This too was a great continuation of the legacy of Yao, Shun, and Cheng Tang. Since Taigong Wang and San Yisheng had seen what King Wen saw, could the Master have failed to hear what King Wen heard?

Thus he edited the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents, established rites and music, elucidated the Changes of Zhou, and revised the Spring and Autumn Annals. In these are advancement and withdrawal, preservation and destruction; virtue, benevolence, sincerity, and reverence; centrality, correctness, harmony, and peace; inspiration and chastening; employment and rejection, bestowal and deprivation. What constitutes refinement and singleness of mind, holding fast to the mean, establishing the mean, establishing the supreme standard, unceasing purity, cultivating virtue, unified virtue, attaining equable order [?], and guiding through instruction is present everywhere in them; nowhere does it go unheard.

Broad learning in cultural matters and restraint through ritual embody the righteousness of sharing a common resolve; giving the aged peace and cherishing the young embody benevolence extended to others. Serving as a storehouse clerk and acting as chief minister express responsiveness in withdrawal and advancement; setting his heart on learning and following his heart mark the beginning and completion of his cultivation. United, these constitute one principle; dispersed, they constitute the myriad affairs. Extended [?], it fills the six directions; rolled up, it lies hidden in secrecy. The myriad phenomena differ in form but share one substance; the hundred kings lived in different ages but shared one spiritual efficacy. There was never a King Wen who was not wholly the Master [?]; once there was the Master…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
無不為文王也若語其迹而遺其心不足以語
聖人矣惜夫鳳鳥不至河不出圖故不復夢周
公夫子之心亦已矣積其所窮孰知其事功反
有賢於堯舜者是亦不獨聞知於文王焉爾雖
然孟子終篇歷叙羣聖之統正以明其傳之有
在也夫子聞知於文王孟子見知於夫子無有
乎爾之說亦有見其所自任而不得辭者觀夫
七篇之中無非此理故韓子曰孔子傳之孟軻
信夫
===
表
擬宋頒訓廉謹刑二銘於中外羣臣謝表〔淳祐四年〕
胡鰲
同考試官教諭徐 批 寓規諷於駢儷深得表體
同考試官教授唐 批 櫽括二銘以代巳意可謂表矣
考試官行人徐 批 典則
淳祐四年正月某日具官臣某等伏蒙
皇上頒賜
punctuated:
無不為文王也。若語其迹而遺其心，不足以語聖人矣。惜夫！鳳鳥不至，河不出圖，故不復夢周公，夫子之心亦已矣。積其所窮，孰知其事功反有賢於堯舜者？是亦不獨聞知於文王焉爾。雖然，孟子終篇歷叙羣聖之統，正以明其傳之有在也。夫子聞知於文王，孟子見知於夫子，「無有乎爾」之說，亦有見其所自任而不得辭者。觀夫七篇之中，無非此理，故韓子曰：「孔子傳之孟軻。」信夫！

表
擬宋頒訓廉謹刑二銘於中外羣臣謝表〔淳祐四年〕
胡鰲
同考試官教諭徐批：寓規諷於駢儷，深得表體。
同考試官教授唐批：櫽括二銘以代巳意，可謂表矣。
考試官行人徐批：典則。

淳祐四年正月某日，具官臣某等伏蒙皇上頒賜
translation_en:
…there was nothing in which he was not King Wen. If one speaks of his outward deeds but overlooks his heart, one cannot adequately speak of the sage. Alas! The phoenix did not arrive, and the Yellow River did not bring forth its chart; thus he no longer dreamed of the Duke of Zhou, and the Master's aspirations, too, came to an end. Through his accumulated adversities [?], who could have known that his achievements would actually surpass those of Yao and Shun? This, too, went beyond merely knowing King Wen through what he had heard.

Nevertheless, at the close of his book, Mencius recounts in succession the lineage of the sages precisely to make clear that its transmission had a living bearer. The Master knew King Wen through hearing of him; Mencius knew the Master through seeing him [?]. The words “Is there no one, then?” likewise reveal the responsibility he assumed for himself and could not decline. Throughout the seven books, there is nothing that does not embody this principle. Thus Master Han said, “Confucius transmitted it to Meng Ke.” How true!

Memorial
Draft memorial of thanks on behalf of the assembled officials at court and in the provinces upon the Song emperor's promulgation of the two inscriptions, “Admonition to Integrity” and “Caution in Punishment.” 〔Fourth year of Chunyou [1244]〕
By Hu Ao.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor: “He embeds admonition and remonstrance in parallel prose, thoroughly capturing the form of the memorial.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Tang, Director of Confucian Schools: “He adapts the two inscriptions to express his own meaning; this may indeed be called a memorial.”
Comment by Examiner Xu, Messenger: “Classical and well regulated.”

On a certain day of the first month in the fourth year of Chunyou, your servants, So-and-so and others, holding their respective offices, humbly received the bestowal by Your Majesty of…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
御製訓廉謹刑二銘戒飭中外者
德協龍占永戴清寧之治
功垂象典弘施欽恤之仁
敷言用錫於庶民設教允資乎神道羣工滌
垢萬物回春臣等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊
以六計周官循良是屬三章漢約寬大為
先惟義重而利輕必刑平而民服伯夷播
迪探本於直清太史懲姦寄意於食貨慨
簠簋之弗飾厭鞭朴之日繁大肆狼貪而
===
已肥民瘠罔懲鴟義而下虐上欺心易酌
泉法忘畫地此鰥寡為之無告而父母所
當動心者也恭惟
〇〇〇〇
倫合禹文
信孚虞芮政復乾淳之善法章噬嗑之明
本源潔而屢戒誅求
惠愛深而務存忠厚
離明夬決苞苴不行
punctuated:
御製訓廉、謹刑二銘，戒飭中外者。
德協龍占，永戴清寧之治；功垂象典，弘施欽恤之仁。敷言用錫於庶民，設教允資乎神道。羣工滌垢，萬物回春。臣等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊以六計周官，循良是屬；三章漢約，寬大為先。惟義重而利輕，必刑平而民服。伯夷播迪，探本於直清；太史懲姦，寄意於食貨。慨簠簋之弗飾，厭鞭朴之日繁。大肆狼貪，而已肥民瘠；罔懲鴟義，而下虐上欺。心易酌泉，法忘畫地。此鰥寡為之無告，而父母所當動心者也。
恭惟〇〇〇〇，倫合禹文，信孚虞芮。政復乾淳之善，法章噬嗑之明。本源潔而屢戒誅求，惠愛深而務存忠厚。離明夬決，苞苴不行。
translation_en:
…the two imperially composed inscriptions, “Admonition to Integrity” and “Caution in Punishments,” admonishing officials within the capital and beyond.
Your virtue accords with the dragon’s auspicious presage; forever we uphold your reign of purity and peace. Your achievement is perpetuated in the penal statutes; far and wide you extend your humane care and compassion in punishment. You promulgate words to bestow blessings upon the common people; in establishing instruction, you truly draw upon the numinous Way. All officials wash away their stains; all things return to spring. We, your servants, in utmost fear and trepidation, bow our heads and knock them upon the ground.
We humbly reflect that the six criteria for assessing officials in the Offices of Zhou favored conscientious and worthy administrators, while the three articles of the Han compact gave precedence to leniency. Only when righteousness is valued and profit held lightly will punishments be equitable and the people submit. Bo Yi spread instruction, tracing its foundations to uprightness and purity; the Grand Historian censured wrongdoing, conveying his intent through his account of food and money. We lament the dishonor brought upon the sacrificial vessels—official corruption—and deplore the daily multiplication of floggings. Officials give free rein to wolfish greed, fattening themselves while the people waste away; unchecked in their owl-like conduct [?], they abuse those below and deceive those above. Their hearts are easily changed by drinking from the spring of greed; in administering the law, they forget the ancient practice of merely drawing a prison upon the ground. Thus widowers and widows have nowhere to appeal: surely those who act as the people’s parents ought to be moved at heart.
We reverently consider that 〇〇〇〇 [an honorific designation is apparently omitted] matches Yu and King Wen in moral conduct, and inspires the trust exemplified by Yu and Rui. Your government restores the excellence of the Qiandao and Chunxi eras; your laws manifest the clarity of the hexagram Biting Through. Pure at the source, you repeatedly forbid extortion; profound in benevolence and love, you strive to preserve loyalty and generosity. With the illumination of the hexagram Li and the resolve of the hexagram Guai, you prevent gifts of bribery from circulating…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
履泰屯亨瘡痍是憫惟貨利之不殖致禁網
之闊疎投珠既挽乎玄機束矢自歸於皇
極猶蒙
睿慮幷渙
宸章盖欲登進乎羔羊且大懷來於鴻鴈朋龜
益下省元吉之弗違山火賁明闡人文而
成化颯颯乎廉頑之志洋洋乎儆位之謨
望塵可以洗心扶杖莫不垂泣臣等謬官
庶列莫稱激揚叨受嘉師空存惻怛花封
===
拙牧顧稍警於四知柳下戇資慙未免於
三黜彼安貞之節方仰法天地之時而赦
宥之恩遽俯承雷雨之解憂深碩鼠患切
豼牙臣等敢不克慎厥猷敬明乃罰奉
申命而行事同寅畏以和衷嚴取舍於義利
之從審重輕於出入之用靖恭爾位誓勿
納於官邪康乂我民勉聞由於聖哲庶𨗳
紳之弗愧而
光命之對揚伏願
punctuated: 履泰屯亨，瘡痍是憫。惟貨利之不殖，致禁網之闊疎。投珠既挽乎玄機，束矢自歸於皇極。猶蒙睿慮，幷渙宸章，盖欲登進乎羔羊，且大懷來於鴻鴈。朋龜益下，省元吉之弗違；山火賁明，闡人文而成化。颯颯乎廉頑之志，洋洋乎儆位之謨！望塵可以洗心，扶杖莫不垂泣。臣等謬官庶列，莫稱激揚；叨受嘉師，空存惻怛。花封拙牧，顧稍警於四知；柳下戇資，慙未免於三黜。彼安貞之節，方仰法天地之時；而赦宥之恩，遽俯承雷雨之解。憂深碩鼠，患切豼牙。臣等敢不克慎厥猷，敬明乃罰，奉申命而行事，同寅畏以和衷，嚴取舍於義利之從，審重輕於出入之用，靖恭爾位，誓勿納於官邪；康乂我民，勉聞由於聖哲。庶𨗳紳之弗愧，而光命之對揚。伏願
translation_en:
…In prosperity and in bringing difficulty through to resolution, You show compassion for those scarred by suffering. Because You do not seek to accumulate wealth and profit, the net of prohibitions has been made loose and broad. Casting aside pearls has already turned back the workings of the mysterious mechanism [?]; the bundles of arrows presented in litigation naturally come under the sovereign standard. Still we receive Your sagacious consideration, together with the wide promulgation of Your imperial pronouncement. Its purpose is surely to advance officials of the integrity celebrated in “Lamb’s Wool,” and generously to draw near the distressed people of “Wild Geese.” As the paired tortoise shells of Increase bring benefit to those below, You consider how supreme good fortune admits no contravention; as fire beneath the mountain shines in Grace, You illuminate human culture and accomplish moral transformation. How stirring the resolve to make the avaricious honest! How abundant the counsels admonishing those in office! At the mere sight of the dust of Your approach, hearts may be cleansed; among those leaning on staffs, none fails to shed tears.

We, Your servants, unworthily hold offices among the many ranks and cannot adequately fulfill the charge of restraining the wicked and promoting the worthy. Undeservedly receiving Your excellent instruction [?], we retain only feelings of compassion. As inept shepherds of the people in our flower-adorned districts, we have nevertheless taken some warning from the “four who know”; with the blunt disposition of Liuxia Hui, we are ashamed that we have not escaped his three dismissals. In maintaining peaceful steadfastness, we were just looking upward to model ourselves on the seasons of Heaven and Earth; now, through Your grace of pardon, we suddenly receive from above the release figured by thunder and rain. Our anxiety over the “great rats” runs deep; our concern over ravening teeth is acute.

How could we, Your servants, dare fail to exercise care in our counsels and reverently make punishments clear? We shall act in obedience to Your reiterated commands, joining in reverent awe and harmony of purpose. We shall be strict in accepting or rejecting according to righteousness or profit, and carefully weigh severity and leniency when imposing or remitting penalties. Peacefully and reverently attending to our posts, we vow never to fall into official wrongdoing. Bringing peace and good order to our people, we shall strive to heed and follow the wisdom of the sage. Thus may we feel no shame as wearers of official caps and sashes, and worthily respond to and proclaim Your glorious command. We humbly wish that…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
恭默為心
好生洽德
導迎和氣
顧畏民碞
清入聖而興四海之淳風
仁如天而啓八荒之壽域
振紀綱於棫樸繩孫子於螽斯臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
===
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄塲
策
第一問
傅順
同考試官學正區批歸美中有期望意忠愛
者如是乎
punctuated:
恭默為心，好生洽德，導迎和氣，顧畏民碞，清入聖而興四海之淳風，仁如天而啓八荒之壽域，振紀綱於《棫樸》，繩孫子於《螽斯》。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叄塲
策
第一問
傅順
同考試官學正區批：「歸美中有期望意，忠愛者如是乎？」
translation_en:
…May reverence and quietude govern Your Majesty’s heart; may love of life pervade your virtue. May you usher in harmonious influences and remain mindful and wary of the people’s formidable power. May your purity attain sagehood and foster an honest ethos throughout the Four Seas; may your benevolence, like Heaven’s, open a realm of longevity throughout the eight distant regions. May you invigorate the guiding principles of government as in the ode “Yu pu,” and perpetuate your descendants as in “Zhong si.” We, your servants, look up to Heaven and revere Your Majesty with the utmost fervor and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks for your hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Fu Shun 傅順
Comment by Associate Examiner Ou, Instructor: “Within his ascription of merit to the sovereign lies an expression of hopes for him. Is this not how one shows loyalty and devotion?”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎授張批脩齊之學自是不同
考試官行人徐批條敘森然涵濡而有得者
聖人之化自近而遠者也聖人之敎自身
而言者也身敎焉以建天下國家之極言
敎焉以理天下國家之治極建而天下國
家可理也治理而天下國家可化也身敎
盡倫者也言敎盡制者也兩盡足為天下
極矣近之齊治而放乎均平之遠自創業
而垂繼體無窮之盛聖人之化優優大哉
===
甞觀之詩矣關雎舉聖德之全體也葛覃
卷耳言志行樛木螽斯美惠及桃夭兎罝
芣苢則家齊而國治之效漢廣汝墳則見
天下有可平之漸麟趾則王者之瑞而關
雎之應也說者曰妻道無成本諸文王詩
人之意固有在夫甞觀之易矣乾父道也
彖曰大哉乾元萬物資始乃統天坤母道
也彖曰至哉坤元萬物資生乃順承天傳
曰陰陽合德剛柔有體以體天地之撰通
punctuated:
同考試官敎授張批：脩齊之學，自是不同。
考試官行人徐批：條敘森然，涵濡而有得者。
聖人之化，自近而遠者也；聖人之敎，自身而言者也。身敎焉，以建天下國家之極；言敎焉，以理天下國家之治。極建而天下國家可理也，治理而天下國家可化也。身敎盡倫者也，言敎盡制者也。兩盡，足為天下極矣。近之齊治，而放乎均平之遠；自創業，而垂繼體無窮之盛。聖人之化，優優大哉！
甞觀之《詩》矣。《關雎》舉聖德之全體也；《葛覃》《卷耳》言志行；《樛木》《螽斯》美惠及；《桃夭》《兎罝》《芣苢》，則家齊而國治之效；《漢廣》《汝墳》，則見天下有可平之漸；《麟趾》，則王者之瑞，而《關雎》之應也。說者曰：「妻道無成，本諸文王。」詩人之意，固有在夫！甞觀之《易》矣。乾，父道也。彖曰：「大哉乾元！萬物資始，乃統天。」坤，母道也。彖曰：「至哉坤元！萬物資生，乃順承天。」傳曰：「陰陽合德，剛柔有體，以體天地之撰，通
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zhang, an Instructor, comments: “His learning in self-cultivation and the regulation of the family is indeed distinctive.”
Examiner Xu, a Messenger, comments: “The exposition is rigorously ordered: this is someone who has steeped himself in learning and gained understanding.”
The sage’s transforming influence proceeds from what is near to what is distant; his teaching proceeds from his own person to his words. Through teaching by personal example, he establishes the highest standard for all under Heaven, the state, and the family; through verbal teaching, he brings order to their government. Once that standard is established, all under Heaven, the state, and the family can be ordered; once their government is ordered, they can be transformed. Teaching by personal example fully realizes human relationships; verbal teaching fully articulates institutions. Fully realizing both suffices to provide the highest standard for all under Heaven. From the nearby tasks of regulating the family and governing the state, this extends to the distant achievement of equitable peace throughout the realm; from the founding of a dynasty, it transmits unending flourishing to succeeding rulers. How ample and great is the sage’s transforming influence!
I have observed this in the Book of Odes. “The Ospreys Cry” (Guan ju) presents the entirety of sagely virtue. “The Spreading Kudzu” (Ge tan) and “The Cocklebur” (Juan er) speak of aspirations and conduct. “The Drooping Trees” (Jiu mu) and “The Locusts” (Zhong si) praise the extension of kindness. “The Peach Tree” (Tao yao), “The Rabbit Net” (Tu ju), and “Plantain” (Fu yi) show the effects of a well-regulated family and a well-governed state. “The Broad Han River” (Han guang) and “The Banks of the Ru” (Ru fen) reveal the gradual advance toward peace throughout all under Heaven. “The Qilin’s Hooves” (Lin zhi) presents the auspicious sign of a true king and the response to “The Ospreys Cry.” A commentator says: “The wife’s Way claims no independent achievement; its foundation lies in King Wen.” The poets surely had a purpose in this!
I have also observed this in the Book of Changes. Qian represents the Way of the father. Its Commentary on the Judgment says: “Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! All things depend on it for their beginning, and it governs Heaven.” Kun represents the Way of the mother. Its Commentary on the Judgment says: “Perfect indeed is the originating power of Kun! All things depend on it for their birth, and it compliantly follows Heaven.” A commentary says: “Yin and yang unite their powers; the firm and the yielding have their embodied forms, thereby embodying the workings of Heaven and Earth and communicating…”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
神明之德聖人之意其有妙蘊存焉者乎
我
太祖高皇帝修齊之化媲美周南而統天之功
上擬乾道時又得
孝慈高皇后天作之配斡化賛元母儀天下嘉
言善行載之傳者真足以表勵宮壼為法
天下可傳後世矣是故
仁孝文皇后廣其教而為內訓二十篇首德性
次修身慎言謹行勤勵警戒節儉積善遷
===
善崇
聖訓景賢範事父母事君事舅姑奉祭祀母儀
睦親慈幼逮下而終之以待外戚其綱目
炳如也邇者
章聖慈仁皇太后復集大成而為女訓十二篇
首閨訓次修德受命夫婦孝舅姑敬夫愛
妾慈幼姙子教子慎靜而終之以節儉其
條理秩如也噫是道也
高皇后皆已有之姑舉其一二言焉如貞靜端
punctuated:
神明之德。聖人之意，其有妙蘊存焉者乎？

我太祖高皇帝修齊之化，媲美周南，而統天之功，上擬乾道。時又得孝慈高皇后天作之配，斡化賛元，母儀天下。嘉言善行載之傳者，真足以表勵宮壼，為法天下，可傳後世矣。

是故仁孝文皇后廣其教，而為《內訓》二十篇：首德性，次修身、慎言、謹行、勤勵、警戒、節儉、積善、遷善、崇聖訓、景賢範、事父母、事君、事舅姑、奉祭祀、母儀、睦親、慈幼、逮下，而終之以待外戚。其綱目炳如也。

邇者章聖慈仁皇太后復集大成，而為《女訓》十二篇：首閨訓，次修德、受命、夫婦、孝舅姑、敬夫、愛妾、慈幼、姙子、教子、慎靜，而終之以節儉。其條理秩如也。

噫！是道也，高皇后皆已有之。姑舉其一二言焉，如貞靜端
translation_en:
…the virtue of spiritual illumination. Might the sages’ intent contain profound subtleties here?

Our Emperor Taizu Gao’s transforming influence through cultivating himself and ordering his household rivaled that celebrated in the “Airs of Zhou and the South,” while his achievement in encompassing Heaven matched the Way of Qian above. At that time he also gained a Heaven-made consort in Empress Xiaoci Gao, who guided transformation, assisted the primal creative power, and served as a maternal exemplar for all under Heaven. Her excellent words and good deeds recorded in her biography were truly sufficient to provide an inspiring example for the palace women, a model for all under Heaven, and a legacy for later generations.

Thus Empress Renxiao Wen expanded upon her teaching and composed the twenty chapters of Instructions for the Inner Quarters (Neixun). They begin with “Moral Nature,” followed by “Self-Cultivation,” “Care in Speech,” “Care in Conduct,” “Diligent Endeavor,” “Vigilance and Admonition,” “Frugality,” “Accumulating Goodness,” “Turning toward Goodness,” “Revering the Sage Instructions,” “Admiring Worthy Exemplars,” “Serving Parents,” “Serving the Ruler,” “Serving Parents-in-Law,” “Attending to Sacrifices,” “Maternal Exemplarity,” “Harmony with Relatives,” “Kindness to the Young,” and “Extending Care to Those Below,” and conclude with “Treatment of the Empress’s Relatives.” Its main principles and subdivisions are brilliantly clear.

Recently, Empress Dowager Zhangsheng Ciren again brought these teachings together into a comprehensive whole, composing the twelve chapters of Instructions for Women (Nüxun). They begin with “Instructions for the Women’s Quarters,” followed by “Cultivating Virtue,” “Receiving Commands,” “Husband and Wife,” “Filial Service to Parents-in-Law,” “Respecting One’s Husband,” “Loving the Concubines,” “Kindness to the Young,” “Pregnancy,” “Teaching Children,” and “Carefulness and Tranquility,” and conclude with “Frugality.” Its arrangement is orderly and coherent.

Ah! Empress Gao already embodied this Way in its entirety. Let me cite just one or two instances: for example, her chastity, tranquility, and upright…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
一孝敬慈惠則所謂德性矣正位中宮益
自勤勵則所謂修身矣其警勵也有曰無
功受福造物所惡當勤女工以報造物其
積善也有曰惟以不殺人為本顛者扶之
危者救之以至念家世之忠厚而曰吾父
平生急於義以不逮事舅姑為恨而當祭
躬治膳羞內訓之道
高皇后身有之者如此不寧惟是如講求古訓
以諭六宮非所謂閨訓乎訪問家法惟取
===
仁厚非所謂修德乎其教子也勉令務學
諄切懇至其節儉也衣服澣濯不喜侈麗
以至撫育李文忠沐英等愛如己出推此
心也慈幼至矣宮人有過執付宮正司議
罪推此心也愛妾周矣女訓之道
高皇后身有之者又如此然則
高皇后非不欲言教也其為言固已寓乎身教
之中矣若
文皇后之身教也則有所謂貞靜純明孝敬仁
punctuated: 一、孝敬慈惠，則所謂德性矣；正位中宮，益自勤勵，則所謂修身矣。其警勵也，有曰：「無功受福，造物所惡，當勤女工以報造物。」其積善也，有曰：「惟以不殺人為本。」顛者扶之，危者救之，以至念家世之忠厚而曰：「吾父平生急於義。」以不逮事舅姑為恨，而當祭躬治膳羞。《內訓》之道，高皇后身有之者如此。不寧惟是，如講求古訓以諭六宮，非所謂閨訓乎？訪問家法，惟取仁厚，非所謂修德乎？其教子也，勉令務學，諄切懇至；其節儉也，衣服澣濯，不喜侈麗。以至撫育李文忠、沐英等，愛如己出，推此心也，慈幼至矣；宮人有過，執付宮正司議罪，推此心也，愛妾周矣。《女訓》之道，高皇后身有之者又如此。然則高皇后非不欲言教也，其為言固已寓乎身教之中矣。若文皇后之身教也，則有所謂貞靜純明、孝敬仁
translation_en:
…steadfastness, filial devotion, reverence, kindness, and generosity: these exemplify what is called “moral character.” Having assumed her rightful position as empress, she became still more diligent and disciplined: this exemplifies what is called “self-cultivation.” In admonishing and encouraging others, she said: “To receive blessings without merit is what the Creator abhors. We should diligently perform women’s work to repay the Creator.” Concerning the accumulation of good deeds, she said: “Simply take not killing people as the foundation.” She supported those who had fallen and rescued those in danger. Recalling her family’s tradition of loyalty and generosity, she said: “Throughout his life, my father was zealous in doing what was right.” She regretted never having had the opportunity to serve her parents-in-law, and personally prepared the food and delicacies for sacrifices to them. Such was Empress Gao’s personal embodiment of the principles in Instructions for the Inner Quarters (Neixun).

Nor was this all. She studied ancient teachings to instruct the women of the Six Palaces: was this not what is called “instruction for the women’s quarters”? She inquired into rules for governing the family, adopting only those grounded in benevolence and generosity: was this not what is called “cultivating virtue”? In teaching her children, she urged them to apply themselves to study, with earnest and heartfelt exhortations. In practicing frugality, she wore washed clothing and disliked extravagance and finery. She even raised Li Wenzhong, Mu Ying, and others, loving them as her own children. In extending this disposition, she brought kindness toward the young to its utmost extent. When palace women committed offenses, she had them taken to the Office of Palace Discipline for deliberation on their punishment. In extending this disposition, she made her care for concubines all-embracing. Such, too, was Empress Gao’s personal embodiment of the principles in Instructions for Women (Nüxun).

Thus, it was not that Empress Gao had no wish to teach through words; her verbal teachings were already embodied in her teaching through personal example. As for Empress Wen’s teaching through personal example, there was what is described as her steadfastness and tranquility, purity and discernment, filial devotion, reverence, and benevolence…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
厚恭勤婦道足範宮闈者矣若
章聖皇太后之身教也則有所謂克配乾元躬
備聖善徽柔恭懿仁順貞慈者矣此身教
脩而倫盡言教行而制盡以
聖佐
聖所以匹休姜姒體德乾坤啓
創業之盛著
守成之美而恢
中興之治者功獨可誣乎哉雖然愚於此有
===
以仰見我
列聖之脩齊矣斥侈靡而絕游幸敦儉朴以先
天下以一夫不得其所自責而聞加惠窮
民之對以化家為國歸美而聞警戒治安
之規我
太祖高皇帝刑于之化周南以後所未聞也恭
儉服澣濯之衣夙興養清爽之氣則
太宗文皇帝之宣重光者也日躋
聖敬之功天授欽明之德則又
punctuated:
厚、恭勤，婦道足範宮闈者矣。若章聖皇太后之身教也，則有所謂克配乾元，躬備聖善，徽柔恭懿，仁順貞慈者矣。此身教脩而倫盡，言教行而制盡，以聖佐聖，所以匹休姜姒，體德乾坤，啓創業之盛，著守成之美，而恢中興之治者，功獨可誣乎哉？雖然，愚於此有以仰見我列聖之脩齊矣。
斥侈靡而絕游幸，敦儉朴以先天下；以一夫不得其所自責，而聞加惠窮民之對；以化家為國歸美，而聞警戒治安之規。我太祖高皇帝刑于之化，周南以後所未聞也。恭儉服澣濯之衣，夙興養清爽之氣，則太宗文皇帝之宣重光者也；日躋聖敬之功，天授欽明之德，則又
translation_en:
…generous, respectful, and diligent, with womanly conduct sufficient to serve as a model for the palace women. As for the personal example of Empress Dowager Zhangsheng, she may be described as a worthy counterpart to the originating power of Heaven, personally possessing sagely goodness, gracious gentleness, reverence and admirable virtue, benevolence, compliance, constancy, and compassion. Through the cultivation of such personal example, the duties of human relationships were fully fulfilled; through the practice of verbal instruction, the prescribed standards were fully realized. With sage virtue assisting sage virtue, these women equaled Jiang and Si in excellence and embodied the virtues of Heaven and Earth. They inaugurated the splendor of the dynasty’s founding, manifested the beauty of preserving its achievements, and enlarged the governance of its restoration. Can their contributions possibly be denied? Yet here I, in my humble view, can also discern with reverence how our succession of sage rulers cultivated themselves and ordered their families.
Rejecting extravagance and putting an end to imperial pleasure excursions, he upheld frugality and simplicity as an example to all under Heaven. When he reproached himself because even one man had not found his proper place, he heard a reply urging greater kindness to the impoverished people. When he accorded her praise for extending the transformation of the household to the state, he heard her admonition to remain vigilant even amid peace and good order. The transforming influence of our Emperor Taizu Gao’s example within his household had not been heard of since the Airs of Zhounan. Respectful and frugal, wearing washed garments, rising early and nurturing a clear and invigorated spirit: thus Emperor Taizong Wen displayed the renewed radiance of his predecessor. Daily advancing in the practice of sagely reverence, endowed by Heaven with the virtues of respectfulness and discernment: this, in turn, was…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
恭睿淵仁寬穆純聖獻皇帝之欽止率
祖者也
三后之身教言教要皆我
列聖有以倡率之云爾否則本之無機風之無
自其何以行化而宣教乎故曰聖人之化
自近而遠者也聖人之教自身而言者也
方今
皇上純孝深仁本於天性雖處深宮無異臨
朝至化刑于宮壼而御於家邦
===
列聖之化在是矣
聖后正位中宮克宣陰教以助理
聖治
三后之教在是矣則夫兆麟趾振螽斯永綿我
國家無疆之福俾斯世斯民訓行以近
天子之光者孰不獻天保而祝華封以仰荅吾
君也哉愚敢曰至敬以享
天心至和以迓
天休斯臣子之願足矣謹對
punctuated:
恭睿淵仁寬穆純聖獻皇帝之欽止率祖者也。三后之身教言教，要皆我列聖有以倡率之云爾。否則，本之無機，風之無自，其何以行化而宣教乎？故曰：聖人之化，自近而遠者也；聖人之教，自身而言者也。

方今皇上純孝深仁，本於天性，雖處深宮，無異臨朝。至化刑于宮壼，而御於家邦，列聖之化在是矣。聖后正位中宮，克宣陰教，以助理聖治，三后之教在是矣。則夫兆麟趾、振螽斯，永綿我國家無疆之福，俾斯世斯民訓行，以近天子之光者，孰不獻天保而祝華封，以仰荅吾君也哉？愚敢曰：至敬以享天心，至和以迓天休，斯臣子之願足矣。謹對。
translation_en:
…was how Emperor Xian, whose honorific titles were Gongrui Yuanren Kuanmu Chunsheng, reverently abided in his proper station and followed his ancestors. The instruction of the three royal consorts, through both personal example and words, was, in essence, something in which our successive sage emperors took the lead. Otherwise, if it had no foundation from which to operate [?] and no source from which its influence could flow, how could they effect moral transformation and spread instruction? Thus it is said: the sage’s transforming influence proceeds from those nearby to those far away; the sage’s instruction proceeds from his own person to his words.

Today, His Majesty’s pure filial devotion and profound benevolence spring from his innate nature. Even when dwelling deep within the palace, he acts no differently than when presiding at court. His consummate transforming influence sets an example within the palace quarters and extends to the governance of the family and the realm: herein lies the transforming influence of the successive sage emperors. The sagely empress occupies her rightful position in the Central Palace and effectively disseminates womanly instruction to assist His Majesty’s sagely rule: herein lies the instruction of the three royal consorts. Thus may the auspicious promise of “The Qilin’s Hooves” be fulfilled and the teeming abundance of “The Locusts” flourish, perpetually extending boundless blessings to our dynasty. When the people of this age follow this instruction and draw near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven, who would not offer the blessings of “Heaven Protects” and the good wishes of the border warden of Hua in grateful response to our sovereign? I venture humbly to say: with utmost reverence, gratify Heaven’s heart; with utmost harmony, welcome Heaven’s blessings. Then the wishes of us, your subjects, will be fulfilled. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
第二問
丘柟
同考試官教諭陳批議論滂洽可與講禮者
考試官行人徐批建官之意是如此
立民極者達損益之宜者也究制作之意
者也制作之在聖人也譬大匠之巧也損
益之在後世也譬則倣大匠之規矩準繩
而不必於小大長短之區區也夫宜可變
而通也巧不可驟而得也宜以時言末也
===
巧以蘊言本也禮有本末知所先後立民
極者其庶乎周禮聖人立民極之規矩準
繩也觀其會通行其典禮則後世於大小
長短之度不必於其區區者也若夫聖人
之意固有妙運乎制作之外亦在夫立民
極者之究之爾昔唐太宗嘗讀是書撫卷
浩歎愚讀史至此又未嘗不撫卷而善夫
太宗之意也何也有成周建官之制斯有
阜成之效倣成周建官之制乃僅止於雜
punctuated:
第二問
丘柟
同考試官教諭陳批：「議論滂洽，可與講禮者。」
考試官行人徐批：「建官之意是如此。」
立民極者，達損益之宜者也，究制作之意者也。制作之在聖人也，譬大匠之巧也；損益之在後世也，譬則倣大匠之規矩準繩，而不必於小大長短之區區也。夫宜可變而通也，巧不可驟而得也。宜以時言，末也；巧以蘊言，本也。禮有本末，知所先後，立民極者其庶乎！《周禮》，聖人立民極之規矩準繩也。觀其會通，行其典禮，則後世於大小長短之度，不必於其區區者也。若夫聖人之意，固有妙運乎制作之外，亦在夫立民極者之究之爾。昔唐太宗嘗讀是書，撫卷浩歎。愚讀史至此，又未嘗不撫卷而善夫太宗之意也。何也？有成周建官之制，斯有阜成之效；倣成周建官之制，乃僅止於雜
translation_en:
Second Question
Qiu Nan
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The argument is ample and comprehensive; this is someone with whom one can discuss ritual.”
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “This is indeed the purpose behind establishing offices.”
One who establishes the highest standard for the people understands what should appropriately be removed or added and probes the intent behind the creation of institutions. The sages’ creation of institutions resembles the skill of a master craftsman. The adjustments made by later generations resemble following that craftsman’s compass, square, level, and ink-line, without insisting upon every petty detail of size and length. What is appropriate can be adapted to changing circumstances; skill cannot be acquired all at once. Appropriateness concerns the circumstances of the time and is a matter of branches; skill concerns what is stored within and is a matter of roots. Ritual has roots and branches. If one knows what comes first and what comes afterward, one is surely close to establishing the highest standard for the people!
The Rites of Zhou supplies the compass, square, level, and ink-line by which the sages established the highest standard for the people. By discerning how its provisions interconnect and implementing its statutes and rites, later generations need not insist upon every petty detail of its prescribed dimensions. As for the sages’ intent, its subtle operation certainly extends beyond the institutions they created. It remains for those who establish the highest standard for the people to investigate it.
In former times, Emperor Taizong of the Tang once read this book and, resting his hand upon the scroll, sighed deeply. Whenever I reach this passage in reading history, I too cannot help resting my hand upon the scroll and approving Taizong’s intention. Why? With the system of offices established in the flourishing Zhou, there were results of prosperity and good order; yet imitation of that system of offices amounted merely to a mixture …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
夷之陋愚寧能以無惑乎試以周禮言之
建官有曰冢宰曰司徒曰宗伯曰司馬曰
司寇之五官其所掌則邦治邦教邦禮邦
政邦禁之不同總衆屬而約之近二萬三
千職焉若冬官則尤為缺典公孤則尚未
及列也以唐制言之建官有曰吏曰戶曰
禮曰兵曰刑曰工之六部其所掌則有選
授勳封考課戶口井田禮儀祠祭燕享貢
舉軍衛武官選授刑法徒隸勾覆關禁百
===
===
工屯田山澤之政令此外又有四省諸監
諸寺司各衛及太子親王等官屬焉匪惟
冬官之備三師三公之立而已合而觀之
周或為兼官而唐則存其名位周或相聯
屬而唐則分為特任周或散在列國而唐
則會於全書不可謂唐制盡非古也蓋道
有升降事有繁簡故唐虞之惟百視夏商
之官倍不為寡而周之多官視唐虞之惟
百不為冗況唐去周既久又可槩拘以周
punctuated: 夷之陋，愚寧能以無惑乎？試以《周禮》言之，建官有曰冢宰、曰司徒、曰宗伯、曰司馬、曰司寇之五官，其所掌則邦治、邦教、邦禮、邦政、邦禁之不同。總衆屬而約之，近二萬三千職焉。若冬官，則尤為缺典；公孤，則尚未及列也。以唐制言之，建官有曰吏、曰戶、曰禮、曰兵、曰刑、曰工之六部，其所掌則有選授、勳封、考課、戶口、井田、禮儀、祠祭、燕享、貢舉、軍衛、武官選授、刑法、徒隸、勾覆、關禁、百工、屯田、山澤之政令。此外又有四省、諸監、諸寺司、各衛及太子、親王等官屬焉，匪惟冬官之備、三師三公之立而已。合而觀之，周或為兼官，而唐則存其名位；周或相聯屬，而唐則分為特任；周或散在列國，而唐則會於全書。不可謂唐制盡非古也。蓋道有升降，事有繁簡，故唐虞之惟百，視夏商之官倍，不為寡；而周之多官，視唐虞之惟百，不為冗。況唐去周既久，又可槩拘以周
translation_en:
…the crudity of barbarian practices: how could I remain unperplexed by this? Consider the Rites of Zhou. In establishing offices, it names five chief officials: the Minister of State, the Minister of Education, the Minister of Rites, the Minister of War, and the Minister of Justice. Their respective responsibilities differ: state administration, instruction, ritual, military affairs, and prohibitions. Counting all their subordinate personnel together gives approximately twenty-three thousand posts. As for the Offices of Winter, their absence is a particularly notable gap in the institutional record; the Three Dukes and Three Solitary Ministers have not even been included in the enumeration.

Turning to the Tang system, its organization of offices comprises six ministries: Personnel, Revenue, Rites, War, Justice, and Works. Their responsibilities encompass regulations and orders concerning selection and appointment, merit titles and enfeoffment, performance evaluations, household registration, the well-field system, ceremonial observances, sacrifices, banquets, the recommendation and examination of candidates, military guards, the selection and appointment of military officers, penal law, convict laborers and bondservants, scrutiny and review, restrictions at passes, the various crafts, agricultural colonies, and mountains and marshes. In addition, there are the four departments, the various directorates, courts and offices, the guards, and the staffs of the heir apparent and imperial princes. It was not merely a matter of providing a complete complement of Offices of Winter and establishing the Three Preceptors and Three Dukes.

Viewed together, some offices held concurrently under the Zhou retained their distinct names and ranks under the Tang; some offices linked in a subordinate relationship under the Zhou were separated into independent commissions under the Tang; and some offices dispersed among the various states under the Zhou were brought together in a comprehensive book under the Tang. One cannot say that the Tang system departed entirely from antiquity. For the Way rises and declines, and affairs become more complex or simpler. Thus, the mere hundred offices under Tang and Yu were not too few when compared with the twice as many offices of the Xia and Shang; nor were the many offices of the Zhou redundant when compared with the mere hundred under Tang and Yu. Moreover, since the Tang was already so far removed in time from the Zhou, could it be uniformly constrained by the Zhou…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
制邪執事所謂唐太宗觀會通而立政是
已夫制有迹也有意也太宗之所得者聖
人立民極之迹耳若聖人之意彼胡有得
哉是故愚甞謂讀周禮不可不讀周官何
也周官曰明王立政不惟其官惟其人又
曰官不必備惟其人盖建官在於得人不
在乎其備也若徒取其備則孔子所謂德
薄而位尊知小而謀大力小而任重者其
能免刑渥之羞乎若不主於得人則沈旣
===
濟所謂安行徐言非德空文善書非才累
資積考非勞者寧不乖銓選之法乎是必
有推賢讓能之訓崇功廣業之戒而後可
者故曰讀周禮不可不讀周官夫牧羊無
芻何益於牧建官者豈異此哉是故愚又
甞謂讀周官不可不讀立政何也立政曰
克知厥若丕乃俾亂又曰則克宅之克由
繹之盖有才而不盡用與無才同也惟不
知惟正是乂之道而任之不專斯有如陸
punctuated: 制邪？執事所謂唐太宗觀會通而立政，是已。夫制有迹也，有意也。太宗之所得者，聖人立民極之迹耳；若聖人之意，彼胡有得哉？是故愚甞謂讀《周禮》不可不讀《周官》。何也？《周官》曰：「明王立政，不惟其官，惟其人。」又曰：「官不必備，惟其人。」盖建官在於得人，不在乎其備也。若徒取其備，則孔子所謂「德薄而位尊，知小而謀大，力小而任重」者，其能免刑渥之羞乎？若不主於得人，則沈旣濟所謂「安行徐言非德，空文善書非才，累資積考非勞」者，寧不乖銓選之法乎？是必有推賢讓能之訓、崇功廣業之戒而後可者。故曰讀《周禮》不可不讀《周官》。夫牧羊無芻，何益於牧？建官者豈異此哉？是故愚又甞謂讀《周官》不可不讀《立政》。何也？《立政》曰：「克知厥若，丕乃俾亂。」又曰：「則克宅之，克由繹之。」盖有才而不盡用，與無才同也。惟不知惟正是乂之道，而任之不專，斯有如陸
translation_en: …institutions? This is precisely what you, sir, mean when you say that Emperor Taizong of the Tang established government by discerning how institutions converged and could be adapted. Institutions have both outward forms and underlying intentions. What Taizong grasped was merely the outward form through which the sages established the supreme standard for the people. How could he have grasped the sages’ intentions? Thus I have often said that one cannot read the Rites of Zhou without also reading “The Offices of Zhou” in the Book of Documents. Why? “The Offices of Zhou” says: “When an enlightened king establishes government, his concern is not with the offices but with the men.” It also says: “Offices need not all be filled; what matters is the men.” Establishing offices therefore depends upon obtaining the right men, not upon filling every position. If one seeks only to fill them all, can those whom Confucius described as “having scant virtue yet occupying exalted positions, little wisdom yet devising great plans, and little strength yet bearing heavy responsibilities” escape the disgrace of severe punishment [?]? If obtaining the right men is not the guiding concern, would this not violate the principles of official selection, as expressed by Shen Jiji: “A measured gait and deliberate speech are not virtue; empty compositions and fine calligraphy are not ability; accumulated seniority and successive evaluations are not meritorious service”? There must first be instruction to recommend the worthy and yield to the capable, and admonitions to enhance achievements and broaden undertakings. Only then will this suffice. Hence I say that one cannot read the Rites of Zhou without also reading “The Offices of Zhou.” If one tends sheep without fodder, what good does tending them do? How is establishing offices any different? Thus I have also often said that one cannot read “The Offices of Zhou” without reading “The Establishment of Government.” Why? “The Establishment of Government” says: “When you can discern their suitability, then fully entrust them with governing.” It also says: “Then you can place them in office, employ them, and continually draw upon them.” To possess talented men yet fail to employ them fully is the same as having none. It is precisely because one does not understand the principle of employing only the upright in government, and does not give them undivided responsibility, that there arise situations such as those described by Lu…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
贄所謂捨僉議而重已權廢公舉而行私
惠居常則求精大過有急則備位不充者
矣惟不知罔兼罔知之說而信之不篤斯
有如司馬光所謂有勤恪之臣悉心致力
以致其職在上疑之同列嫉之在下怨之
朝廷或以衆言而罰之則勤恪無不解體
者矣是以一則戒以勿間憸人一則戒以
勿誤獄慎而其意遠矣故曰讀周官不可
不讀立政也雖然衡鑑或迷妍媸曷辨知
===
恤豈無本哉德者本也周官之祗勤立政
之忱恂實明王建官之精蘊後世不本乎
此其始也定官職之品則防慮之未周頒
爵祿之制則磨礪之未至清入仕之路或
至銓選之未公開推薦之門或至資格之
未恢而建官於是乎無定制其卒也用術
以為知人之明陰察以為核實之功督責
以為勵精之治疑斥以為振起人才之道
而官於是乎為徒建彼唐太宗者雜流嗚
punctuated:
贄所謂「捨僉議而重已權，廢公舉而行私惠；居常則求精大過，有急則備位不充」者矣。惟不知「罔兼罔知」之說，而信之不篤，斯有如司馬光所謂「有勤恪之臣，悉心致力，以致其職，在上疑之，同列嫉之，在下怨之，朝廷或以衆言而罰之，則勤恪無不解體」者矣。是以一則戒以「勿間憸人」，一則戒以「勿誤獄慎」，而其意遠矣。故曰：讀《周官》，不可不讀《立政》也。
雖然，衡鑑或迷，妍媸曷辨？知恤豈無本哉？德者，本也。《周官》之「祗勤」，《立政》之「忱恂」，實明王建官之精蘊。後世不本乎此，其始也，定官職之品，則防慮之未周；頒爵祿之制，則磨礪之未至；清入仕之路，或至銓選之未公；開推薦之門，或至資格之未恢。而建官於是乎無定制。其卒也，用術以為知人之明，陰察以為核實之功，督責以為勵精之治，疑斥以為振起人才之道，而官於是乎為徒建。彼唐太宗者，雜流嗚
translation_en:
…what Lu Zhi described as “setting aside collective deliberation to magnify one’s own authority, abandoning public recommendation to dispense private favors; in ordinary times demanding excellence to excess, yet in emergencies lacking enough men to fill the posts.” Only because rulers fail to understand the teaching “Do not take on their duties or presume to know their affairs,” and do not trust their officials firmly, does the situation arise that Sima Guang described: “There are diligent and conscientious ministers who devote their whole minds and strength to fulfilling their duties, yet their superiors suspect them, their colleagues envy them, and their subordinates resent them.
