If the court punishes them on the strength of these numerous accusations, none of the diligent and conscientious will fail to lose heart.” Thus one chapter warns, “Do not let petty men intervene,” and the other warns, “Do not mishandle judicial matters and affairs requiring care” [?]. Their meaning reaches far indeed. Hence I say: in reading “The Officers of Zhou” (Zhou guan), one must also read “Establishing Government” (Li zheng).
Yet if the scales and mirror of judgment sometimes fail, how can beauty and ugliness be distinguished? Surely understanding and solicitude must have a foundation? Virtue is that foundation. The “reverent diligence” of “The Officers of Zhou” and the “sincerity and trustworthiness” of “Establishing Government” are the very essence of how enlightened kings established offices. Later generations did not take these as their foundation. At first, when fixing the ranks of offices, they worried that their precautions were insufficiently comprehensive; when promulgating systems of noble rank and official salary, they worried that incentives were insufficiently effective. Efforts to purify the routes into office might result in appointments that were still inequitable; opening channels for recommendation might still leave the eligibility requirements too narrow. Thus the establishment of offices came to have no settled system. In the end, rulers treated the use of manipulative techniques as discernment in judging men, covert investigation as achievement in verifying facts, exacting supervision as vigorous government, and suspicion and dismissal as the way to stimulate talented men. Offices were consequently established in vain. As for Emperor Taizong of Tang, men of miscellaneous backgrounds [the following 嗚 is doubtful] …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
玉玷列縉紳讒佞售姦間疏守道況慙德
閨門乏關雎麟趾之意兼行將相又無四
牡采薇之情乃欲取岩壁之殘書為粉飾
太平之具譬則跛匠眇目於持斤而曰規
矩準繩盡在是者可謂巧乎此臺閣之規
模雖定而禮樂終愧于成周郡邑之赤牒
雖省而治理僅止于李唐也記曰為政在
人取人以身修身以道修道以仁此萬世
建官之準則愚敢以為終篇獻
===
第三問
胡鰲
同考試官教諭徐批敬一格天脩省之大者
同考試官教授唐批條對中具見心學
考試官行人徐批古健
對天何以格曰心而已心何以存曰敬而
已敬何以主曰一而已夫一外無敬也敬
外無心也心外無天也凝一以主敬則動
靜合矣篤敬以存心則運用神矣存心以
punctuated:
玉，玷列縉紳；讒佞售姦，間疏守道。況慙德閨門，乏《關雎》《麟趾》之意；兼行將相，又無《四牡》《采薇》之情。乃欲取岩壁之殘書，為粉飾太平之具，譬則跛匠眇目於持斤，而曰：「規矩準繩盡在是。」者，可謂巧乎？此臺閣之規模雖定，而禮樂終愧于成周；郡邑之赤牒雖省，而治理僅止于李唐也。《記》曰：「為政在人，取人以身，修身以道，修道以仁。」此萬世建官之準則，愚敢以為終篇獻。

第三問
胡鰲
同考試官教諭徐批：敬一格天，脩省之大者。
同考試官教授唐批：條對中具見心學。
考試官行人徐批：古健。

對：天何以格？曰：心而已。心何以存？曰：敬而已。敬何以主？曰：一而已。夫一外無敬也，敬外無心也，心外無天也。凝一以主敬，則動靜合矣；篤敬以存心，則運用神矣；存心以
translation_en:
…jade pendants, sullying the ranks of the gentry; slanderers and flatterers carried out their treachery, alienating those who upheld the Way. Moreover, his conduct within the household was shameful, lacking the spirit of “The Ospreys” (Guanju) and “The Qilin’s Hooves” (Linzhi). In employing generals and chief ministers, he likewise lacked the sentiments expressed in “The Four Steeds” (Simu) and “Gathering Ferns” (Caiwei). Yet he wished to take fragmentary writings from rocky walls and use them to embellish an appearance of great peace. This was like a lame carpenter, blind in one eye, wielding an axe and declaring, “Compasses, square, level, and marking line are all here.” Could such a man be called skilled? Thus, although the framework of the central administration was established, its rites and music remained inferior to those of the Zhou; although the red documents of prefectures and counties were reduced [?], its governance reached only the level of the Li house’s Tang dynasty. The Record of Rites says: “Government depends on men. One selects men by the standard of one’s own person, cultivates one’s person through the Way, and cultivates the Way through humaneness.” This is the standard for establishing offices for all ages. I venture to offer it as the conclusion of this essay.

Third Question
Hu Ao
Associate Examiner Xu, Instructor, comments: “Reverence and single-mindedness move Heaven: these are the great essentials of self-cultivation and self-examination.”
Associate Examiner Tang, Instructor, comments: “The learning of the mind is fully evident in these responses to the individual points.”
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “Classical and vigorous.”

Response: How can Heaven be moved? The answer is: through the mind alone. How can the mind be preserved? The answer is: through reverence alone. How can reverence be maintained? The answer is: through single-mindedness alone. Apart from single-mindedness there is no reverence; apart from reverence there is no mind; apart from the mind there is no Heaven. Concentrate on unity to maintain reverence, and activity and stillness will be united. Deepen reverence to preserve the mind, and its functioning will become numinous. Preserve the mind in order to…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
格天則轉異為祥矣斯道也以觀古今而
進退在我以察上下而彌綸在我以律政
紀而權衡在我以禪化理而参賛在我大
哉要乎其
皇上所自得者乎彗星之異執事為
皇上慮也愚為
皇上喜也夫憂樂而樂憂得無近佞矣乎夫有
所受之也詩曰天監在兹言天也無貳爾
心言心也聖敬日躋言敬也純一不已言
===
一也是故君人者無問其在天者惟守其
在我者盖天之未始不為人而人之未始
不為天也天定能勝人而人定尤能勝天
也天之示人者祥異而已矣君之格天者
敬一而已矣昔者水於唐堯之天未定也
兢兢以格之而啓時雍之治旱於商湯之
天未定也慄慄以格之而垂允殖之休是
豈災之不足懼而憂之可喜哉盖敬一則
心存心存則天格天且弗違而況於人乎
punctuated: 格天，則轉異為祥矣。斯道也，以觀古今而進退在我，以察上下而彌綸在我，以律政紀而權衡在我，以禪化理而参賛在我。大哉！要乎！其皇上所自得者乎！彗星之異，執事為皇上慮也，愚為皇上喜也。夫憂樂而樂憂，得無近佞矣乎？夫有所受之也。《詩》曰：「天監在兹」，言天也；「無貳爾心」，言心也；「聖敬日躋」，言敬也；「純一不已」，言一也。是故君人者，無問其在天者，惟守其在我者。盖天之未始不為人，而人之未始不為天也。天定能勝人，而人定尤能勝天也。天之示人者，祥異而已矣；君之格天者，敬一而已矣。昔者，水於唐堯之天未定也，兢兢以格之，而啓時雍之治；旱於商湯之天未定也，慄慄以格之，而垂允殖之休。是豈災之不足懼，而憂之可喜哉？盖敬一則心存，心存則天格。天且弗違，而況於人乎？
translation_en:
…to move Heaven, then anomalies are transformed into auspicious signs. Through this Way, when we survey antiquity and the present, advance and withdrawal lie within our control; when we examine what is above and below, comprehensive ordering lies within our control; when we regulate the principles of government, weighing and balancing lie within our control; when we transmit transformative order [?], participation in and assistance to Heaven’s work lie within our control. How great! How essential! Is this not what His Majesty has grasped for himself? You, gentlemen, worry for His Majesty over the anomalous appearance of a comet; I, in my ignorance, rejoice for His Majesty. To grieve at joy and rejoice at sorrow—does this not come close to flattery? Yet there is an authoritative teaching on which I base this. The Book of Odes says, “Heaven watches over you here”: this speaks of Heaven; “Let your heart not be divided”: this speaks of the heart; “His sagely reverence rose daily”: this speaks of reverence; “Pure singleness without cease”: this speaks of singleness.
Thus, one who rules others should not inquire into what rests with Heaven, but should preserve what rests with himself. For Heaven has never failed to act for humankind, and humankind has never failed to act for Heaven. When Heaven is settled, it can prevail over human beings; when human beings are settled, they can all the more prevail over Heaven. What Heaven shows human beings consists only of auspicious signs and anomalies; what a ruler uses to move Heaven consists only of reverence and singleness. In former times, the floods in the age of Tang Yao occurred when Heaven was not yet settled. Through vigilant awe he moved Heaven and inaugurated an era of harmonious government. The drought in the age of Shang Tang occurred when Heaven was not yet settled. Through trembling reverence he moved Heaven and bequeathed the blessing of abundant growth. Does this mean that calamities are insufficient cause for fear, or that grounds for sorrow can be cause for joy? Rather, through reverence and singleness the heart is preserved; when the heart is preserved, Heaven is moved. If even Heaven does not oppose him, how much less will human beings!…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
而况於鬼神乎是故高宗之雊雉宣王之
旱魃天於中興之賢君有拳拳焉而其異
也亦甚矣然一則恭默而思道憲天而正
事一則側身而脩行任賢而使能存是心
以格之而天者定矣彗星之異也或見于
漢文宣光三帝或見于唐太玄憲三宗或
見於宋太祖太宗仁宗天於希世之賢君
若數數焉而其異也亦屢矣然數君者玄
默而勵精也恢廓而大度也寬仁而果斷
===
也恭儉而仁恕也存是心以格之而天者
亦定矣以創大業以美中興以光簡冊則
夫譴告之者謂非仁愛之乎即是而觀則
春秋左氏之紀明是道者也申繻高堂隆
之說昧是道者也呂公著程頤富弼呂大
防呂大鈞邢恕王安禮陳姀呂好問王襄
諸臣之疏又皆以扶翼斯道者也此世治
所以隆汙化理所以淳薄立言所以得失
心術所以邪正造物所以從違灼乎判矣
punctuated: 而况於鬼神乎？是故高宗之雊雉，宣王之旱魃，天於中興之賢君有拳拳焉，而其異也亦甚矣。然一則恭默而思道，憲天而正事；一則側身而脩行，任賢而使能。存是心以格之，而天者定矣。彗星之異也，或見于漢文宣光三帝，或見于唐太玄憲三宗，或見於宋太祖太宗仁宗。天於希世之賢君若數數焉，而其異也亦屢矣。然數君者，玄默而勵精也，恢廓而大度也，寬仁而果斷也，恭儉而仁恕也。存是心以格之，而天者亦定矣。以創大業，以美中興，以光簡冊，則夫譴告之者，謂非仁愛之乎？即是而觀，則《春秋》左氏之紀，明是道者也；申繻、高堂隆之說，昧是道者也；呂公著、程頤、富弼、呂大防、呂大鈞、邢恕、王安禮、陳姀、呂好問、王襄諸臣之疏，又皆以扶翼斯道者也。此世治所以隆汙、化理所以淳薄、立言所以得失、心術所以邪正、造物所以從違，灼乎判矣。
translation_en:
…and how much more so with ghosts and spirits? Thus, in the cases of the crowing pheasant under Gaozong and the drought demon under King Xuan, Heaven showed earnest concern for worthy rulers who restored their dynasties, yet its portents were also severe. One ruler, however, pondered the Way in reverent silence, modeled himself on Heaven, and rectified affairs; the other humbled himself and cultivated his conduct, appointed the worthy, and employed the capable. By preserving this disposition of mind, they moved Heaven, and Heaven became settled.

As for the portent of a comet, it appeared under the three Han emperors Wen, Xuan, and Guangwu; under the three Tang emperors Taizong, Xuanzong, and Xianzong; and under the Song emperors Taizu, Taizong, and Renzong. Heaven seemed repeatedly to admonish these rarely equaled worthy rulers, and its portents likewise occurred frequently. Yet these rulers applied themselves diligently in profound quietude, were broad-minded and magnanimous, lenient and humane yet decisive, reverent and frugal, benevolent and forbearing. By preserving this disposition of mind, they moved Heaven, and Heaven likewise became settled. Thus they founded great enterprises, brought distinction to dynastic restoration, and lent luster to the historical records. Can it be said that Heaven’s admonitory warnings were not expressions of benevolent love for them?

Viewed in this light, Zuo’s account of the Spring and Autumn Annals elucidates this Way, whereas the explanations of Shen Xu and Gaotang Long fail to comprehend it. The memorials of such ministers as Lü Gongzhu, Cheng Yi, Fu Bi, Lü Dafang, Lü Dajun, Xing Shu, Wang Anli, Chen He 陳姀 [?], Lü Haowen, and Wang Xiang all further support this Way. Here the reasons why governance flourishes or declines, why moral transformation and order are pure or debased, why pronouncements succeed or fail, why the workings of the mind are deviant or upright, and why the power of creation accords with or opposes human endeavors stand clearly distinguished.

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
君心之外果有天乎果無天乎敬一之外
抑有格乎抑無格乎可監也已我
皇上蒞極以来禀英明純粹之資極仁孝誠敬
之德敬一有箴存心至矣五箴有釋主敬
至矣
郊壇
世廟有享格天至矣存神過化天地同流大政
宏綱膾炙千古足以陋漢唐宋于下風矣
由是禱雨而雨零祈雪而雪集甘露降黃
===
河清僉曰吾
君之祥也愚則曰天欲其敬一而已矣又由是
而山川或未寧蝗螟或未息而彗星偶見
僉曰吾
君之異也愚則曰天欲其敬一而已矣夫敬一
者而豈徒哉喜怒哀樂心之發也用舍予
奪心之則也典章文物心之著也禮樂法
度心之推也弗純則雜雜則二弗嚴則肆
肆則隳惟二與隳非存心也是故存心於
punctuated: 君心之外，果有天乎？果無天乎？敬一之外，抑有格乎？抑無格乎？可監也已。我皇上蒞極以来，禀英明純粹之資，極仁孝誠敬之德。敬一有箴，存心至矣；五箴有釋，主敬至矣；郊壇、世廟有享，格天至矣。存神過化，天地同流，大政宏綱，膾炙千古，足以陋漢唐宋于下風矣。由是禱雨而雨零，祈雪而雪集，甘露降，黃河清。僉曰：「吾君之祥也。」愚則曰：「天欲其敬一而已矣。」又由是而山川或未寧，蝗螟或未息，而彗星偶見。僉曰：「吾君之異也。」愚則曰：「天欲其敬一而已矣。」夫敬一者，而豈徒哉？喜怒哀樂，心之發也；用舍予奪，心之則也；典章文物，心之著也；禮樂法度，心之推也。弗純則雜，雜則二；弗嚴則肆，肆則隳。惟二與隳，非存心也。是故存心於
translation_en: Beyond the ruler’s heart, does Heaven indeed exist, or does it not? Apart from reverent unity, is there a way to reach Heaven, or is there not? Here indeed is a lesson to heed. Since ascending the throne, our Emperor, endowed with brilliant intelligence and unalloyed purity, has brought the virtues of benevolence, filial piety, sincerity, and reverence to their utmost. He has composed the Admonition on Reverent Unity, bringing preservation of the heart to its utmost; he has provided explanations of the Five Admonitions, bringing the maintenance of reverence to its utmost; and he has presented offerings at the suburban altar and the Temple of His Imperial Father, bringing communion with Heaven to its utmost. Wherever he passes, he transforms; wherever he abides, his influence is spiritual, flowing together with Heaven and Earth. His great policies and overarching principles will be acclaimed through the ages, sufficient to make the Han, Tang, and Song appear inferior and leave them far behind. Thus, when he prays for rain, rain falls; when he prays for snow, snow gathers. Sweet dew descends, and the Yellow River runs clear. All say, “These are auspicious signs for our ruler.” I, in my humble judgment, say, “Heaven wishes only that he maintain reverent unity.” Yet mountains and rivers may still be unsettled, locusts and grain pests may not yet have ceased, and a comet occasionally appears. All say, “These are anomalous portents for our ruler.” I, in my humble judgment, say, “Heaven wishes only that he maintain reverent unity.” How could reverent unity be an empty practice? Joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure are expressions of the heart; employing and dismissing, granting and withdrawing, are its standards of judgment; institutions and the forms of civilized culture are its manifestations; rites, music, laws, and regulations are its extension into practice. Without purity there is admixture, and admixture produces division; without strictness there is laxity, and laxity produces collapse. Division and collapse are no preservation of the heart. Therefore, preserving the heart in …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
宥密者毋徒克謹之文而已必不蔽不惑
如程頤所謂而後可治本緩末如呂大防
所謂而後可得人省費如呂大鈞所謂而
後可法祖致治如王襄所謂而後可以是
存心殆媲美于商周矣賛佐於
廟廊者不但脩輔之故而已也必内外無乖擾
之失如呂公著之說左右絕朋黨之私如
王安禮之說戒成鍛鍊如邢恕之說戒趨
時迎合如陳并之說以是賛佐追商周而
===
無讓焉愚見内外交脩上下恭敬敬與心
一心與天一天與我一喘息呼吸氣通乎
微闔闢弛張自作元命中庸位育之功大
易裁成之道禮運諸福之祥胥此焉在承
天休而延
寶祚萬世之業也抑何彗之足憂哉故愚願
皇上之敬一也勿以彗為有無勿以祥為敬怠
允執其要惟盡吾事而已昔董仲舒以災
異之来為天心仁愛愚敢以是為
punctuated:
宥密者，毋徒克謹之文而已，必不蔽不惑，如程頤所謂而後可；治本緩末，如呂大防所謂而後可；得人省費，如呂大鈞所謂而後可；法祖致治，如王襄所謂而後可。以是存心，殆媲美于商周矣。賛佐於廟廊者，不但脩輔之故而已也，必内外無乖擾之失，如呂公著之說；左右絕朋黨之私，如王安禮之說；戒成鍛鍊，如邢恕之說；戒趨時迎合，如陳并之說。以是賛佐，追商周而無讓焉。
愚見内外交脩，上下恭敬，敬與心一，心與天一，天與我一，喘息呼吸，氣通乎微；闔闢弛張，自作元命。《中庸》位育之功，《大易》裁成之道，《禮運》諸福之祥，胥此焉在。承天休而延寶祚，萬世之業也，抑何彗之足憂哉？故愚願皇上之敬一也，勿以彗為有無，勿以祥為敬怠，允執其要，惟盡吾事而已。昔董仲舒以災異之来為天心仁愛，愚敢以是為
translation_en:
…in profound, secluded deliberation, one must not merely observe the outward forms of conscientious care. One must be neither blinded nor deluded, as Cheng Yi said; only then will this suffice. One must attend to the roots of government and give lesser urgency to its branches, as Lü Dafang said; only then will this suffice. One must obtain worthy men and reduce expenditure, as Lü Dajun said; only then will this suffice. One must emulate the ancestors and achieve good government, as Wang Xiang said; only then will this suffice. To preserve the mind in this way would surely rival the excellence of the Shang and Zhou. Those who assist in the imperial court must do more than perform the customary duties of support. They must prevent discord and disruption within and without, as Lü Gongzhu said; eliminate the private interests of factions among those attending the ruler, as Wang Anli said; guard against fabricating charges [?], as Xing Shu said; and guard against following prevailing fashions and currying favor, as Chen Bing said. By assisting in this way, they would match the Shang and Zhou without falling short.
In my humble view, when inner and outer cultivation advance together and those above and below are reverent, reverence becomes one with the mind, the mind one with Heaven, and Heaven one with oneself. With every breath, vital energy communicates with the subtlest workings; through opening and closing, relaxing and tightening, one shapes one’s own great destiny. The achievement of establishing Heaven and Earth in their proper places and nurturing all things, described in the Doctrine of the Mean; the way of ordering and completing the processes of nature, described in the great Book of Changes; and the auspicious signs of manifold blessings, described in the Evolution of Rites—all reside in this. Receiving Heaven’s favor and prolonging the imperial succession constitute an undertaking for ten thousand generations. What cause, then, is a comet for anxiety? Thus I humbly wish that Your Majesty’s reverent single-mindedness should neither depend on whether a comet appears nor become more diligent or lax according to auspicious signs. Firmly grasp its essentials and simply fulfill our own responsibilities. In former times, Dong Zhongshu regarded the coming of calamities and anomalies as an expression of Heaven’s benevolent love. I venture to regard this as…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
今日喜謹對
第四問
蔡完
同考試官學正劉批守
當代之法而能通其變此有據之說
考試官行人徐批識時務
經國者有一定之法法外之意而後享其
利于不窮夫利之不窮法與意為之也法
不定則無執守之素而或至於弊法定矣
===
而不得其意則無通變之宜而或至於拘
斯二者皆過也其可以享利乎是故守常
者洪其源者也通變者續其流者也源洪
而不可塞流續而不可禦久大之業于是
焉在謂非
國家無窮之利也哉漕運一策執事所以謀
國者甚深慮事者甚遠非區區所能測識
者雖然豈敢以終默哉夫天下之法每患
其弗能行而其行也則患其弗能繼非弗
punctuated:
今日喜。謹對。

第四問
蔡完

同考試官學正劉批：「守當代之法，而能通其變，此有據之說。」

考試官行人徐批：「識時務。」

經國者有一定之法、法外之意，而後享其利于不窮。夫利之不窮，法與意為之也。法不定，則無執守之素，而或至於弊；法定矣，而不得其意，則無通變之宜，而或至於拘。斯二者皆過也，其可以享利乎？是故守常者，洪其源者也；通變者，續其流者也。源洪而不可塞，流續而不可禦，久大之業于是焉在，謂非國家無窮之利也哉？漕運一策，執事所以謀國者甚深，慮事者甚遠，非區區所能測識者。雖然，豈敢以終默哉？夫天下之法，每患其弗能行，而其行也，則患其弗能繼。非弗
translation_en:
…a cause for rejoicing today. I respectfully submit this reply.

Fourth Question
Cai Wan

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, an Instructor: “He upholds the laws of the present dynasty while adapting them to changing circumstances. This is a well-grounded argument.”

Comment by Examiner Xu, a Messenger: “He understands the affairs of the times.”

Those who govern a state must have established laws and grasp the intent beyond those laws; only then can they enjoy their benefits without end. These unending benefits arise from both the laws and their intent. If laws are not settled, there is no enduring basis to uphold, and harmful practices may result. If laws are settled but their intent is not understood, there is no fitting adaptation to change, and rigidity may result. Both are errors: how could benefits be enjoyed through them? Thus, upholding constant principles enlarges the source; adapting to change sustains the flow. When the source is abundant and cannot be blocked, and the flow continues and cannot be checked, an enduring and great undertaking rests upon them. Could this be anything other than an inexhaustible benefit to the state?

In this policy question on grain transport, you gentlemen have shown profound concern for the state and far-reaching deliberation over its affairs, beyond what someone as insignificant as I can fathom. Nevertheless, how could I dare remain silent throughout? With the laws of the realm, the recurring concern is that they cannot be put into practice; once put into practice, the concern is that they cannot be sustained. It is not that they fail to…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
繼也時勢爾也所貴乎君子有通變之意
焉耳易曰制而用之存乎法推而行之存
乎通夫通所以行也法之意也且漕運孰
始乎王者重九年之食而所于起禹貢詳
九州之貢而駸駸乎盛矣然必貢道通而
後田賦入則漕運為儲蓄之自也固宜夫
漢唐都關中三面阻守之地也或悉仰乎
山東或兼仰乎江淮然其路則止於河渭
而已宋都汴梁四通八達之區也或自汴
===
河黄河而来或自惠民廣濟而至要其路
則凡四而已至元都燕獨用海運之法焉
浙米由浙而入海江米由江而入海自是
達于直沽而運者可歲至矣是法也既省
夫兌支之耗且免夫牽輓之勞倡議于伯
顏成事于朱清張瑄而元史謂為一代良
法所得盖多其有見矣夫海運之便固也
若鄧艾耕淮南湖蕩之田以兼屯守若熈
寧墾坊監空餘之地以理稼政至元虞集
punctuated: 繼也，時勢爾也。所貴乎君子有通變之意焉耳。《易》曰：「制而用之存乎法，推而行之存乎通。」夫通，所以行也，法之意也。且漕運孰始乎？王者重九年之食，而所于起，禹貢詳九州之貢，而駸駸乎盛矣。然必貢道通而後田賦入，則漕運為儲蓄之自也，固宜。夫漢唐都關中，三面阻守之地也，或悉仰乎山東，或兼仰乎江淮，然其路則止於河渭而已。宋都汴梁，四通八達之區也，或自汴河、黄河而来，或自惠民、廣濟而至，要其路則凡四而已。至元都燕，獨用海運之法焉。浙米由浙而入海，江米由江而入海，自是達于直沽，而運者可歲至矣。是法也，既省夫兌支之耗，且免夫牽輓之勞，倡議于伯顏，成事于朱清、張瑄，而《元史》謂為一代良法，所得盖多，其有見矣。夫海運之便固也。若鄧艾耕淮南湖蕩之田，以兼屯守；若熈寧墾坊監空餘之地，以理稼政；至元虞集
translation_en:
…be sustained; it is merely the circumstances of the time. What is valued in the gentleman is his intention to adapt to changing circumstances. The Book of Changes says: “Regulating and employing them depends upon rules; extending and putting them into practice depends upon adaptation.” Adaptation is what makes implementation possible: this is the intent of the rules themselves. Moreover, when did grain transport begin? The ancient kings valued maintaining nine years’ supply of food, and there it began [?]. The “Tribute of Yu” details the tribute of the Nine Regions, and the practice steadily flourished. Yet only when the tribute routes were open could the land taxes come in; thus it was entirely fitting that grain transport should be the source of stored reserves.

The Han and Tang established their capitals in Guanzhong, a region protected by natural barriers on three sides. At times they relied wholly on Shandong, and at times also on the Jiang and Huai regions; their transport routes, however, extended only along the Yellow and Wei rivers. The Song established its capital at Bianliang, a place accessible from every direction. Supplies came by the Bian River and Yellow River, or arrived by the Huimin and Guangji canals: in all, there were just four routes. When the Yuan established its capital at Yan, it relied exclusively on sea transport. Grain from Zhejiang entered the sea by the Zhe River, and grain from the Yangzi region entered the sea by the Yangzi. From there it reached Zhigu, allowing shipments to arrive annually. This method reduced losses in the transfer and disbursement of grain and spared the labor of towing. Proposed by Boyan and brought into effect by Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan, it is described in the History of the Yuan as an excellent system of that dynasty. Its benefits were indeed considerable, and this assessment showed discernment.

The advantages of sea transport are certainly established. There were also such measures as Deng Ai’s cultivation of the lake and marsh lands of Huainan, combining farming with garrison defense; and the reclamation of unused lands of the horse pastures and horse directorates during the Xining reign period, to put agricultural administration in order. Coming to the Yuan dynasty, Yu Ji …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
又有海田之法焉取瀕海之地而築堤以
捍潮設世襲之格而分給以行賞由是漸
征而京師之儲可充矣之數法也皆足以
壯朝廷之勢而供兵食之需者也惜其僅
行于一時而不得盡舉于當日所謂寬民
力省漕費者得無遺恨也哉是故法立也
而尤不可無法外意也通其意弗泥其法
因乎時弗窒乎勢天啓其大利者不有待
于
===
今日乎我
祖宗以天授神聖之資定萬世常行之策自永
樂以來罷海舟而漕會通河則水陸安而
所以輸積于
京師者裕如也而漕法精矣定土壤而成賦
稅則財之出於五方者崇如也而賦法精
矣其良法美意度越千古有非歷代之可
及也抑何資於海運諸議乎哉而執事顧
猶拳拳焉者蓋以
punctuated:
又有海田之法焉：取瀕海之地而築堤以捍潮，設世襲之格而分給以行賞，由是漸征，而京師之儲可充矣。之數法也，皆足以壯朝廷之勢而供兵食之需者也。惜其僅行于一時，而不得盡舉于當日，所謂寬民力、省漕費者，得無遺恨也哉？是故法立也，而尤不可無法外意也。通其意，弗泥其法；因乎時，弗窒乎勢。天啓其大利者，不有待于今日乎？
我祖宗以天授神聖之資，定萬世常行之策。自永樂以來，罷海舟而漕會通河，則水陸安，而所以輸積于京師者裕如也，而漕法精矣；定土壤而成賦稅，則財之出於五方者崇如也，而賦法精矣。其良法美意，度越千古，有非歷代之可及也。抑何資於海運諸議乎哉？而執事顧猶拳拳焉者，蓋以
translation_en:
…there was also a scheme for coastal farmland: take land along the coast and build dikes to keep out the tides; establish provisions for hereditary tenure and distribute the land as rewards. Taxes could then be imposed gradually, filling the capital’s reserves. These several measures [?] were all sufficient to strengthen the court’s position and meet the army’s provisioning needs. Regrettably, they were implemented only for a time, and could not all be put into effect in their day. As regards easing the people’s burdens and reducing grain-transport costs, could this fail to leave grounds for regret? Thus, once a system has been established, it is especially necessary to retain an understanding of the purposes beyond its provisions. Grasp its intent without clinging rigidly to its rules; adapt to the times without being obstructed by circumstances. Have the great benefits that Heaven would open up not awaited this very day?
Our imperial ancestors, endowed by Heaven with sagely and divine capacities, established policies to be followed for ten thousand generations. Since the Yongle reign, seagoing grain vessels have been discontinued and grain transported along the Huitong Canal. Routes by water and land have thereby been secure, and ample supplies have been conveyed to and stored in the capital: thus the grain-transport system has been perfected. By assessing the land and establishing taxes, abundant revenue has been obtained from all five regions: thus the taxation system has been perfected. These excellent institutions and beneficent intentions surpass those of all antiquity, attaining what successive dynasties could not match. What need, then, is there to draw upon the various proposals for maritime grain transport? Yet the reason you gentlemen remain so earnestly concerned with them is presumably that…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
京師猶人身也會通河猶咽喉也咽喉寧保
其無梗乎是故海運不可廢惟
聖明斷自
宸衷見其可也然後經始兩浙自平江劉家港
以至海門開洋以至成山上海以至楊村
皆募人以導之而造船按試焉行之既熟
則雖有不測之虞可以交發而互至而丘
文莊之議是或一道也
京師譬富室也墾田譬附郭也附郭其可以
===
弗穫乎是故墾田不可廢惟
聖明參諸眾論行之當也然後間命守臣自淮
南以及壽頴遼海以及青齊太僕以及監
苑空地皆設官以理之而勸農力穡焉田
之既成則必享豐登之慶足以居安而慮
危而丘文莊之說未必厚誣者矣夫主之
以會通河輔之以海運經之以常賦緯之
以墾田並行不悖以利國而利民也
國家萬世之業其在乎此嗚呼古今勢也推
punctuated:
京師猶人身也，會通河猶咽喉也，咽喉寧保其無梗乎？是故海運不可廢。惟聖明斷自宸衷，見其可也，然後經始兩浙，自平江劉家港以至海門，開洋以至成山，上海以至楊村，皆募人以導之，而造船按試焉。行之既熟，則雖有不測之虞，可以交發而互至，而丘文莊之議，是或一道也。
京師譬富室也，墾田譬附郭也，附郭其可以弗穫乎？是故墾田不可廢。惟聖明參諸眾論，行之當也，然後間命守臣，自淮南以及壽頴，遼海以及青齊，太僕以及監苑空地，皆設官以理之，而勸農力穡焉。田之既成，則必享豐登之慶，足以居安而慮危，而丘文莊之說，未必厚誣者矣。夫主之以會通河，輔之以海運，經之以常賦，緯之以墾田，並行不悖，以利國而利民也。國家萬世之業，其在乎此！嗚呼！古今勢也，推
translation_en:
…the capital is like the human body, and the Huitong Canal like its throat. Can one guarantee that the throat will never become obstructed? Thus maritime transport must not be abandoned. Only after Your sagacious Majesty has decided in your imperial heart and judged it feasible should preparations begin in Liangzhe. From Liujiagang in Pingjiang to Haimen, out onto the open sea as far as Chengshan, and from Shanghai to Yangcun [?], men should be recruited throughout to guide the passage, and ships built, inspected, and tested. Once these operations are well practiced, even should unforeseen trouble threaten, shipments could depart alternately and arrive by either route. Qiu Wenzhuang’s proposal may indeed offer one way forward.
The capital may be compared to a wealthy household, and land reclamation to its fields beside the city walls. Can those fields be left unharvested? Thus land reclamation must not be abandoned. Only after Your sagacious Majesty has weighed the various opinions and determined that implementation is appropriate should you from time to time command the territorial administrators to act. From Huainan to Shou and Ying, from Liaohai to Qing and Qi, and on vacant lands belonging to the Court of the Imperial Stud and the supervisory offices and parks [?], officials should be appointed to administer the work and encourage farmers to labor diligently at cultivation. Once the fields have been established, there will surely be the joy of abundant harvests, sufficient to provide security while preparing for danger. Qiu Wenzhuang’s argument is therefore by no means necessarily a gross misrepresentation. Let the Huitong Canal be the principal means, supplemented by maritime transport; let regular tax revenues supply the warp, and land reclamation the weft. These measures can proceed together without conflict, benefiting both the state and the people. Surely here lies the foundation of the state’s enterprise for ten thousand generations! Ah! Past and present are matters of circumstance; extending…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
行時也經常法也變通意也用而利焉通
之爾也是故寒暑推而歲成焉屈伸感而
利生焉天道之利者一通而已矣知周而
道濟焉旁行而不流焉聖人之利者亦通
而已矣變通以宜民鼓舞以盡利非
皇上之至神至聖其孰能與于此而或者謂海
運乃勝國之遺無以勸
盛世而諸議瑣瑣皆李悝緒餘曾若王政之皞
皞也不知天地之氣有開必先何忌于勝
===
國而古篋之良方取其奏效足矣況自古
及今嘗行之而既效者乎易曰神而明之
存乎其人芹曝之忱亦惟
廟堂加之意而已
第五問
龔箕卿
同考試官教諭韓批憂深言切子其悉湖湘
利害者歟
同考試官教諭黃批不泥不疎
punctuated:
行，時也；經常，法也；變通，意也；用而利焉，通之爾也。是故寒暑推而歲成焉，屈伸感而利生焉。天道之利者，一通而已矣。知周而道濟焉，旁行而不流焉。聖人之利者，亦通而已矣。變通以宜民，鼓舞以盡利，非皇上之至神至聖，其孰能與于此？而或者謂海運乃勝國之遺，無以勸盛世，而諸議瑣瑣，皆李悝緒餘，曾若王政之皞皞也？不知天地之氣，有開必先，何忌于勝國？而古篋之良方，取其奏效足矣。況自古及今，嘗行之而既效者乎？《易》曰：「神而明之，存乎其人。」芹曝之忱，亦惟廟堂加之意而已。
第五問
龔箕卿
同考試官教諭韓批：「憂深言切，子其悉湖湘利害者歟？」
同考試官教諭黃批：「不泥不疎。」
translation_en:
…carrying it out depends on the time; regular practice supplies the rules; adaptation expresses their intent. Putting them to beneficial use is simply a matter of making them work through changing circumstances. Thus cold and heat succeed one another and complete the year; contraction and expansion interact and produce benefits. The benefits of the Way of Heaven come simply from such responsiveness. Understanding encompasses all and the Way brings aid everywhere; it operates in every direction without straying. The benefits bestowed by the sage likewise come simply from such responsiveness. To adapt so as to serve the people appropriately, and to inspire them so as to realize every benefit—who but His Majesty, with his supreme spiritual insight and sagacity, could accomplish this?

Some, however, say that maritime transport is a legacy of the fallen dynasty, offering nothing worthy of commendation to an age of flourishing rule; that these petty proposals are all remnants of Li Kui’s ideas, hardly comparable to the expansive harmony of true kingly government. They do not understand that, in the workings of Heaven and Earth, every new development has its antecedents. Why shun something because it comes from the fallen dynasty? A good prescription from an old chest need only prove effective. How much more so with measures that, from antiquity to the present, have already been tried and proved effective! The Book of Changes says: “Making it spiritually efficacious and illuminating it rests with the person.” With the humble sincerity of one offering celery or the warmth of the sun, I ask only that the court give these proposals its consideration.

Fifth Question

Gong Jiqing

Associate Examiner Han, Instructor, comments: “Your concerns are profound and your words earnest. Surely you are someone thoroughly acquainted with what benefits and harms the Hu-Xiang region?”

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Neither hidebound nor superficial.”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教授陳批意見超然
考試官行人徐批善區處
君子之均夫民也綏之而已矣制之而已
矣盖人以安居為樂以財足為生不陷於
刑戮為慶是人心所同然也惟爭趨於利
斯强暴譸張者出矣苟吾之所以均之者
泥之乎一定之迹無以綏之制之則不惟
生聚長養未能即遂而斯民之擾擾何由
息乎是不可不加之意也流民雜寓客户
===
凌主今日為政在所必處者執事以此下
詢豈非以愚生長是邦或知居安來撫之
策哉嘗聞醫之於病也必先有以達其致
病之原而後可以施治病之藥病之入人
乘乎其元氣之虛庸醫者不究其五臟之
受疹毒也而悉以急攻卒治之劑决癰疽
而必除之可乎哉治流民者何以異此是
故荆楚天地之要區其地廣濶其利富饒
固宜其五方之雜聚也乃至今日而成凌
punctuated:
同考試官教授陳批：意見超然。
考試官行人徐批：善區處。
君子之均夫民也，綏之而已矣，制之而已矣。盖人以安居為樂，以財足為生，不陷於刑戮為慶，是人心所同然也。惟爭趨於利，斯强暴譸張者出矣。苟吾之所以均之者，泥之乎一定之迹，無以綏之制之，則不惟生聚長養未能即遂，而斯民之擾擾何由息乎？是不可不加之意也。流民雜寓，客户凌主，今日為政在所必處者。執事以此下詢，豈非以愚生長是邦，或知居安來撫之策哉？嘗聞醫之於病也，必先有以達其致病之原，而後可以施治病之藥。病之入人，乘乎其元氣之虛。庸醫者不究其五臟之受疹毒也，而悉以急攻卒治之劑，决癰疽而必除之，可乎哉？治流民者何以異此？是故荆楚，天地之要區，其地廣濶，其利富饒，固宜其五方之雜聚也。乃至今日而成凌
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Chen, Professor, comments: “His views rise above the ordinary.”
Examiner Xu, Messenger, comments: “Skillful in devising measures.”
When the gentleman brings equitable order to the people, he does so simply by giving them security and keeping them under control. People take pleasure in living securely, depend on sufficient wealth for their livelihood, and count it a blessing to escape punishment and execution: these sentiments are common to all human hearts. It is only when people compete in pursuit of profit that the violent and deceitful emerge. If our means of bringing equitable order to them remain bound to a fixed course, with no means of giving them security or keeping them under control, then not only will they fail promptly to prosper and flourish, but how can their turmoil ever cease? This demands careful attention. Displaced people settle among the inhabitants, and newcomer households overbear the established residents: these are matters that those governing today must address. By putting this question to me, do you not suppose that, having grown up in this region, I might know a policy for securing those already settled and reassuring those who come?
I have heard that, in treating illness, a physician must first ascertain its underlying cause before administering medicine to cure it. Illness enters a person by taking advantage of a weakness in the vital energy. Would it be acceptable for an incompetent physician, without investigating how the five viscera have been afflicted by disease and poison, to rely entirely on medicines that attack urgently and cure abruptly, lancing abscesses and insisting on removing them? How does dealing with displaced people differ from this?
Jing-Chu is thus a strategic region under Heaven. Its lands are extensive and its resources abundant; it is certainly natural that people from all five regions should gather there. Yet by the present day this has developed into a situation of overbearing…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
主之勢者殆亦仁義之政未足厭服其心
駕馭其力焉耳考之於古丁蘭以孝居於
宜城王粲以詞依於荆州錢徽自考功郎
中而留穀城裴休由太子少保而處長沙
第進士而遷襄陽者胡旦也忤蔡京而居
當陽者胡安國也家潭州而以道學名世
非張栻乎徙興國而為宋室忠臣非謝枋
得乎他如丁鶴年之耿介出塵龍仁夫之
明經式學李安國之孝行邑民矜式劉凝
===
之之仁德鄉里增重又皆彰彰於書黃衡
寶之域之數人者在一邑則一邑重在一
郡則一郡重真無負於湖矣今之流寓乃
至以客凌主何古今人相遠邪自今觀之
假繼贅而奪其産産奪而人之祀絶矣誘
借貸而取其貲貲盡而人之性傷矣至于
駕虚詞以重其禍則一人構訟或結黨於
同鄉各户斂財或連詞於終歲弗勝其健
反直為曲則又盡貲産而傾之矣可惡孰
punctuated: 主之勢者，殆亦仁義之政未足厭服其心、駕馭其力焉耳。考之於古，丁蘭以孝居於宜城，王粲以詞依於荆州，錢徽自考功郎中而留穀城，裴休由太子少保而處長沙。第進士而遷襄陽者，胡旦也；忤蔡京而居當陽者，胡安國也。家潭州而以道學名世，非張栻乎？徙興國而為宋室忠臣，非謝枋得乎？他如丁鶴年之耿介出塵，龍仁夫之明經式學，李安國之孝行，邑民矜式，劉凝之之仁德，鄉里增重，又皆彰彰於書。黃衡寶之域之數人者，在一邑則一邑重，在一郡則一郡重，真無負於湖矣。今之流寓，乃至以客凌主，何古今人相遠邪？自今觀之，假繼贅而奪其産，産奪而人之祀絶矣；誘借貸而取其貲，貲盡而人之性傷矣。至于駕虚詞以重其禍，則一人構訟，或結黨於同鄉，各户斂財；或連詞於終歲，弗勝其健，反直為曲，則又盡貲産而傾之矣。可惡孰
translation_en:
…a position of dominance over the hosts: this is probably simply because government through benevolence and righteousness has not yet sufficed to win their hearts into submission and bring their strength under control. Examining antiquity, we find that Ding Lan, known for filial piety, lived in Yicheng; Wang Can, known for literary composition, took refuge in Jingzhou; Qian Hui settled in Gucheng after serving as Director of the Bureau of Evaluations; and Pei Xiu resided in Changsha after serving as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent. It was Hu Dan who moved to Xiangyang after attaining the jinshi degree, and Hu Anguo who lived in Dangyang after opposing Cai Jing. Was it not Zhang Shi who made his home in Tanzhou and became renowned for the Learning of the Way? Was it not Xie Fangde who moved to Xingguo and was a loyal minister of the Song ruling house? Others include Ding Henian, upright and aloof from worldly concerns; Long Renfu, whose understanding of the Classics set a model for learning; Li Anguo, whose filial conduct the county’s inhabitants revered and emulated; and Liu Ningzhi, whose benevolence and virtue brought distinction to his community. All are conspicuous in written records. These men of the region of Huang, Heng, and Bao [?] brought distinction to whatever county or prefecture they lived in. Truly, they did not fail Huguang.

Yet today’s migrants have gone so far as to dominate their hosts as outsiders. Why are people of ancient and modern times so far apart? Looking at present circumstances, they seize another’s property under the pretext of becoming an heir or a resident son-in-law; once the property is seized, that person’s ancestral sacrifices cease. They entice others into borrowing and take their wealth; once that wealth is exhausted, their lives are harmed. They even fabricate allegations to aggravate their victims’ misfortunes. When one person instigates litigation, they may form a faction among people from the same native place, collecting money from every household; or they may keep filing complaints throughout the year. Unable to withstand their aggressiveness, the victim finds right turned into wrong, and is then stripped of all wealth and property and ruined. What could be more detestable…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
甚焉嘗聞理道乖方版圖脫漏人如鳥獸
飛走莫制家以之乏國以之貧奸宄漸興
此杜佑之所為慮也不農則不地著不地
著則離鄉輕家民如鳥獸嚴法重刑猶不
能禁則鼂錯之所為憂也流民之患自古
而然猶未至今日之甚者也然為今日之
計亦曰普天皆王土率土皆王臣流民孰
非吾赤子乎當立為通融之法凡置成產
業者名以稅戶之目為人耕佃者曰耕佃
===
戶專於販易傭作者曰營生戶隨其所在
定為版冊肆貪鼓暴而逞計者又重其刑
以禁之而於吾荆湘之民制以恒產使皆
有田可以自養寬其賦役使皆有財可以
自給明其教化使皆不惑不恐於奪攘矯
虔之徒則亦足以保其產守其財而無憂
於告訐矣於此二者處之既得其道又知
與民最親而狎者里胥也慎重其選使之
屬民讀法如周之族師辨施舍行秩叙如
punctuated: 甚焉？嘗聞理道乖方，版圖脫漏，人如鳥獸，飛走莫制，家以之乏，國以之貧，奸宄漸興，此杜佑之所為慮也。不農則不地著，不地著則離鄉輕家，民如鳥獸，嚴法重刑猶不能禁，則鼂錯之所為憂也。流民之患，自古而然，猶未至今日之甚者也。然為今日之計，亦曰普天皆王土，率土皆王臣，流民孰非吾赤子乎？當立為通融之法：凡置成產業者，名以稅戶之目；為人耕佃者，曰耕佃戶；專於販易傭作者，曰營生戶。隨其所在，定為版冊。肆貪鼓暴而逞計者，又重其刑以禁之。而於吾荆湘之民，制以恒產，使皆有田可以自養；寬其賦役，使皆有財可以自給；明其教化，使皆不惑不恐於奪攘矯虔之徒，則亦足以保其產、守其財，而無憂於告訐矣。於此二者，處之既得其道，又知與民最親而狎者，里胥也。慎重其選，使之屬民讀法，如周之族師；辨施舍，行秩叙，如
translation_en:
…could be more odious? I have heard that when governance loses its proper course and people slip out of the population and land registers, they scatter like birds and beasts, with none able to restrain them. Households are thereby impoverished, the state is thereby made poor, and wickedness and disorder gradually arise. This was what troubled Du You. When people do not farm, they have no attachment to the land; without such attachment, they leave their native places and think little of their homes. The people become like birds and beasts, whom even strict laws and heavy punishments cannot restrain. This was what worried Chao Cuo. The troubles caused by displaced people have existed since antiquity, yet they have never reached the severity seen today.

In devising measures for the present, we may say: all beneath Heaven is the king’s land, and all within its bounds are the king’s subjects. Which of these displaced people is not one of our own children? Flexible regulations should therefore be established. Those who have acquired established property should be designated taxpaying households; those who cultivate land as tenants for others should be called tenant-farming households; and those who engage exclusively in trade or hired labor should be called livelihood households. They should be entered in registers wherever they reside. Those who indulge their greed, incite violence, and pursue their schemes should be restrained by heavier punishments.

As for the people of our Jing and Xiang regions, secure livelihoods should be provided for them, so that all have land with which to support themselves. Their taxes and labor obligations should be lightened, so that all have the means to meet their own needs. Moral instruction should be made clear to them, so that none are deceived or intimidated by those who seize and plunder through fraud and force. They will then be able to preserve their property and safeguard their wealth, without fear of malicious accusations.

Once these two groups have been dealt with appropriately, we must also recognize that those in the closest and most familiar contact with the people are the village clerks. Great care should be taken in selecting them. Have them assemble the people and read out the laws, like the lineage heads of the Zhou; distinguish those liable for service from those exempt, and put the prescribed order of precedence into effect, like…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
周之胥宰如酇長之趣其耕耨稽其女工
如閭師之任農耕事任圃樹事又如鄰長
之相糾使之有所警而不為惡相受使之
有所勸而必為善守令者復督察之于上
重擾害之禁嚴誣告之法不至如董仲舒
所謂師帥不賢主德不宣而恩澤不流監
司又振飭之於上宣明教化開釋冤滯必
至如陸贄所謂五術省風俗四賦經財實
六德保罷療如是則仁義行而居者安來
===
者撫元氣內固而外邪弗得侵淫矣尚何
民病之足慮哉噫是道也推而行之天下
之民舉安又不但荆楚爾也執事以為何
如
punctuated: 周之胥宰，如酇長之趣其耕耨、稽其女工，如閭師之任農耕事、任圃樹事，又如鄰長之相糾，使之有所警而不為惡；相受，使之有所勸而必為善。守令者復督察之于上，重擾害之禁，嚴誣告之法，不至如董仲舒所謂師帥不賢、主德不宣而恩澤不流。監司又振飭之於上，宣明教化，開釋冤滯，必至如陸贄所謂五術省風俗、四賦經財實、六德保罷療。如是則仁義行，而居者安，來者撫，元氣內固，而外邪弗得侵淫矣。尚何民病之足慮哉！噫！是道也，推而行之，天下之民舉安，又不但荆楚爾也。執事以為何如？
translation_en: …like the xu and zai officers of the Zhou; like the Hamlet Head, who urged people on in plowing and weeding and inspected women’s textile work; like the Village Master, who assigned farmers to cultivation and gardeners to planting; and like the Neighborhood Head, who had neighbors correct one another, so that they would heed warnings and refrain from wrongdoing, and receive and support one another, so that they would be encouraged and surely do good. Prefects and magistrates should in turn supervise them from above, reinforce prohibitions against harassment and injury, and strictly enforce the laws against false accusations. Matters would then not reach the condition described by Dong Zhongshu: “The leaders are unworthy, the ruler’s virtue is not made manifest, and his beneficence does not flow down.” The surveillance commissioners should further invigorate and discipline the administration from above, make moral instruction clear, and resolve cases of injustice left unsettled. They must attain what Lu Zhi described as “using the five methods to examine customs, the four levies to manage material resources, and the six virtues to protect the weary and provide healing” [?]. In this way, benevolence and righteousness would prevail; those already settled would be secure, and newcomers would be cared for. The vital energy would be fortified within, and harmful influences from outside could not penetrate and spread. What suffering among the people would then remain cause for concern? Ah! If this way were extended and put into practice, all the people under Heaven would enjoy security—not merely those of Jingchu. What do you, honored examiners, think?

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
湖廣辛卯鄉試事竣臣克昌
從諸執事後當任楮墨役敢
序諸簡末用告諸士曰楚人
文地也自昔稱天下之奇必
曰楚才無乃造物者啓其機
以肇
===
今日文明之翊邪夫文非機弗
先機非會弗合機會之際有
期焉
聖天子龍飛江漢物覩之餘楚文
彌盛無乃造物者嘉其會以
共成文明之治邪於是乎有
本焉夫極弗建則機弗會會
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序

湖廣辛卯鄉試事竣，臣克昌從諸執事後，當任楮墨役，敢序諸簡末，用告諸士曰：楚，人文地也。自昔稱天下之奇，必曰楚才。無乃造物者啓其機，以肇今日文明之翊邪？夫文非機弗先，機非會弗合，機會之際有期焉。聖天子龍飛江漢，物覩之餘，楚文彌盛。無乃造物者嘉其會，以共成文明之治邪？於是乎有本焉。夫極弗建，則機弗會；會
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

The business of the Huguang Provincial Examination in the xinmao year having concluded, I, your servant Kechang, following behind the officials responsible, was charged with the work of paper and ink. I venture to append a postface at the end of these pages, addressing the candidates as follows: Chu is a land of literary culture. Since ancient times, whenever people have spoken of the outstanding talents of the realm, they have invariably named the talents of Chu. Might the Creator have set their potential in motion to inaugurate their assistance in today’s flourishing of culture? For culture cannot advance without an initiating impulse, and that impulse cannot come to fruition without a fitting conjunction of circumstances. There is an appointed time when impulse and circumstance meet.

Our sagely Son of Heaven rose like a dragon from the region of the Yangzi and Han rivers. Since all creation beheld him, Chu’s literary culture has flourished still more. Might the Creator have blessed this conjunction so that together they might bring about a government of flourishing culture? Yet this has a foundation. If the supreme standard is not established, the initiating impulse cannot meet its occasion; if that conjunction …

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
弗協則治弗純此有本之治
唐虞三代所以保世滋大而
無取於叔季之小康也
聖天子天章睿藻為絲為綸文之
華也準古酌今昭物明度文
有用也然而
敬一以宅心
===
仁孝以懋德是為學之樞要致
治之根本真所謂建有極以
嘉厥會者也文不在兹與或
曰吉甫之才文以武屈平之
才文以忠宋玉之才文以雅
茂叔之才文以理楚之良也
楚産者師其人而修其文其
punctuated:
弗協則治弗純。此有本之治，唐虞三代所以保世滋大，而無取於叔季之小康也。
聖天子天章睿藻，為絲為綸，文之華也；準古酌今，昭物明度，文有用也。然而敬一以宅心，仁孝以懋德，是為學之樞要、致治之根本，真所謂建有極以嘉厥會者也。文不在兹與？或曰：「吉甫之才，文以武；屈平之才，文以忠；宋玉之才，文以雅；茂叔之才，文以理：楚之良也。楚産者師其人而修其文，其
translation_en:
…if they do not harmonize, governance will not be pure. Such governance, grounded in a foundation, was how the rulers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties preserved their realms through the generations and made them ever greater; they had no need of the modest peace of declining ages.
The sagely Son of Heaven’s imperial compositions and discerning literary embellishments become silken threads and cords—the splendor of writing. Taking antiquity as his standard and weighing present circumstances, he illuminates things and clarifies norms—the practical use of writing. Yet it is reverent single-mindedness that anchors his mind, and benevolence and filial piety that advance his virtue. These are the essentials of learning and the foundation of good governance: truly what is meant by establishing the supreme standard so as to bring excellence to the convergence of circumstances. Does not cultural refinement reside here?
Someone says: “Jifu’s talent found literary expression through martial prowess; Qu Ping’s through loyalty; Song Yu’s through elegance; and Maoshu’s through principle. These were the outstanding men of Chu. If those born in Chu take these men as their teachers and cultivate their writing, they may…”

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
庶幾矣乎是不然君子居其
地不累其俗軼其俗必追其
古是故幹不與角謀笴不與
金錫謀廬不與函謀鎛不與
劒謀器也若夫可秦可粤可
燕可荆可夷可夏天下之大
器也傳曰五百年必有王者
===
興其間必有名世者今
聖天子堯文思矣舜文明矣湯懋
昭矣文明德矣諸士子感機
以作協會以俟隆古明良之
一期也於是乎師其本而歸
極焉修乎其家而始於親親
施之天下而篤恭是務文武
punctuated: 庶幾矣乎？是不然。君子居其地，不累其俗；軼其俗，必追其古。是故幹不與角謀，笴不與金錫謀，廬不與函謀，鎛不與劒謀，器也。若夫可秦、可粤、可燕、可荆、可夷、可夏，天下之大器也。傳曰：「五百年必有王者興，其間必有名世者。」今聖天子堯文思矣，舜文明矣，湯懋昭矣，文明德矣。諸士子感機以作，協會以俟，隆古明良之一期也。於是乎師其本而歸極焉，修乎其家而始於親親，施之天下而篤恭是務，文武
translation_en: …might they come close? This is not so. The gentleman dwells in a place without being encumbered by its customs; to surpass its customs, he must pursue its ancient exemplars. Thus the maker of bow staves does not consult with the worker in horn, nor the maker of arrow shafts with the worker in bronze; the spear maker does not consult with the armor maker, nor the bell maker with the sword maker: these are specialized instruments. But one who can serve in Qin, Yue, Yan, or Jing, among the Yi peoples or among the Xia, is a great instrument for all under Heaven. The transmitted text says: “Every five hundred years a true king must arise, and in the interval there must be men renowned in their age.” Now our sagely Son of Heaven possesses Yao’s cultivation and thoughtfulness, Shun’s cultivation and enlightenment, Tang’s diligent manifestation of virtue, and King Wen’s illumination of virtue. The candidates, stirred by this opportunity, rise to action; they join together and await their time. This is an occasion for an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers to meet, as in high antiquity. Accordingly, they take the root as their teacher and return to the supreme standard. They cultivate their households, beginning with affection for their kin; extending this to all under Heaven, they devote themselves to earnest reverence. In their civil and martial accomplishments…

title: 嘉靖十年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
焉而不惑忠焉而不過雅焉
而不溺理焉而純聖則洋洋
纚纚皆典謨訓誥其言皇皇
濟濟皆臯夔周召其人不足
以當名世而翊化理矣乎是
不特曰楚之才而已爾
直隸揚州府儒學教授陳克
===
昌謹序
punctuated:
焉而不惑，忠焉而不過，雅焉而不溺，理焉而純聖，則洋洋纚纚皆典謨訓誥，其言皇皇濟濟皆臯夔周召，其人不足以當名世而翊化理矣乎？是不特曰楚之才而已爾。
直隸揚州府儒學教授陳克昌謹序。
translation_en:
…and are not led astray; loyal without going to excess, refined without becoming immersed in refinement, and principled with the purity of sages. Then, flowing abundantly, their words will all be like the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements of the Book of Documents; august and dignified, these men will all be like Gao Yao, Kui, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao. Would they not be worthy of being renowned in their age and of assisting moral transformation and good government? They would not merely be called men of talent from Chu.
Preface respectfully written by Chen Kechang, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yangzhou Prefecture in the Metropolitan Region.
